I was already feeling bad. Bad that she is alone. Bad that I am a bad son. Sad that one day something may happen to her, God forbid.
zh_text: 回到客廳，她又打開電視，不過還是開口跟我聊天。我把咖啡遞給她。她調整電視的音量，讓她能一邊跟我講話，一邊聽到電視裡的聲音。那些白人又做了一些非常好笑的事情。我在想如果住在我那種公寓的話，他們是能好笑到哪裡去。媽弓身緩緩喝著咖啡，緊緊握著杯子，一副有人要搶她的模樣。喝完之後，我說要幫她洗杯子。她拒絕，自己去洗，然後抱怨。反正她已經在抱怨了，我乾脆故意看了看手錶，裝出一副驚覺時間已經這麼晚了的樣子，然後告訴她我真的該走了。我必須走完在門口親吻她的完整流程。她謝過我的鮮花，讓我保證要常常聯絡，彷彿我是要出國，而不是要回家。我保證會聯絡，而她以一副我這輩子都不會管她的神情看著我。那是她專門讓我感到罪惡的神情，我早就看習慣了。無論如何，這個神情還是讓我罪惡。我本來就覺得很罪惡了。爲了讓她一個人住感到罪惡。爲了我是個壞兒子感到罪惡。爲了某天她可能會出什麼事而感到哀傷，但願不要。

en_text: I wave from the sidewalk but she is already gone. Where would I be without Mom? I don't know and I never want to find out.
zh_text: 我在門前走道上揮手道別，不過她已經回去了。要是沒有媽的話，我現在會流落何方？我不知道，而我從不想知道。

en_text: "Stop the bus," I say, standing up. "You said . . ."
zh_text: 旅程超過四分之三時，我看到了牠。牠就那麼躺在路旁，還有在動。算是。「停車。」我說著站起身來。「你説……」

en_text: "You're the boss, buddy." He stops the bus, and if I really was his buddy he would give me a quarter of my fare back. The swish of the doors as they close behind me, the purring of the motor, the shuddering of heavy metal, and the bus leaves me behind. We're about halfway between town and my apartment. It's a suburb where people who have made poor choices in life live. I rush over the road and crouch next to it. It's mostly white, with a few streaks of ginger through it. Its mouth is slightly open. It's not moving: maybe I made a mistake when I first saw it. When I put my hand on its side, it's still warm. Its eyes open and look at me. It tries to meow but can't. One of its legs sticks out in that same awkward way as Candy's arm.
zh_text: 「你說了算，老兄。」他停車，真要跟我稱兄道弟，他就更應該退我四分之一的車錢。我聽見車門在我身後關閉的聲音、引擎呼嘯聲、沉重金屬震動的聲音、接著公車揚長而去。我快步衝到路旁，蹲在牠的旁邊。牠毛色幾乎純白，微帶幾絲薑黃色的斑紋。牠的嘴角微張，沒有在動；或許剛剛是我看錯了。我伸手觸摸牠的身側，還有體溫。牠張開雙眼，看著我。牠想叫，但是叫不出聲。牠其中一條腿折成像是坎蒂手臂那種奇特角度。

en_text: He stops the bus, and if I really was his buddy he would give me a quarter of my fare back. The swish of the doors as they close behind me, the purring of the motor, the shuddering of heavy metal, and the bus leaves me behind. We're about halfway between town and my apartment. It's a suburb where people who have made poor choices in life live. I rush over the road and crouch next to it. It's mostly white, with a few streaks of ginger through it. Its mouth is slightly open. It's not moving: maybe I made a mistake when I first saw it. When I put my hand on its side, it's still warm. Its eyes open and look at me. It tries to meow but can't. One of its legs sticks out in that same awkward way as Candy's arm. Funny what fate does to us. Two nights ago it wasn't my place in this crazy, mixed-up world to question the fact that animals are used as tools. They're used every single day. Chemicals are tested on them so we can have higher-quality health care, higher-quality shampoos, matching eyeliners, warmer clothes. Others are killed for food. And here's my opportunity to balance the scales for what I did to poor Fluffy.
zh_text: 他停車，真要跟我稱兄道弟，他就更應該退我四分之一的車錢。我聽見車門在我身後關閉的聲音、引擎呼嘯聲、沉重金屬震動的聲音、接著公車揚長而去。我快步衝到路旁，蹲在牠的旁邊。牠毛色幾乎純白，微帶幾絲薑黃色的斑紋。牠的嘴角微張，沒有在動；或許剛剛是我看錯了。我伸手觸摸牠的身側，還有體溫。牠張開雙眼，看著我。牠想叫，但是叫不出聲。牠其中一條腿折成像是坎蒂手臂那種奇特角度。命運真有趣。兩天前，我一點也不質疑在這個瘋狂混亂的世界中拿動物當作工具的事情。牠們每天都被當成工具。人們拿牠們實驗化學藥劑，好讓我們享有品質更好的醫療、品質更好的洗髮精、對稱的眼線、溫暖的衣服。其他動物則被當作食物。而此刻就是我彌補殺害可憐小貓的機會。

en_text: I pick the cat up, careful to keep my hands away from its broken leg. It meows loudly and tries to struggle, but doesn't have the energy to struggle hard. The long graze down the side of its body looks bloody and raw. Its fur is matted. Strange sounds are coming from it. Rather than holding it against my body, I remove the plastic bag that the groceries came in from my briefcase and rest the cat inside. I begin to walk home. After less than half a mile I come across a phone booth. I find the number for an all-night vet and tell them I'm on my way. Then I call a taxi. It takes five minutes to arrive. The driver is foreign and speaks the same amount of English as the cat. I've torn the page from the phone book and I hand it to him. He reads the address and starts driving. The cat is no longer meowing, but it's still alive. I let it out of the bag before stepping through the vet doors.
zh_text: 我撿起那隻貓，小心不去觸碰牠的斷腳。牠喵喵大叫，試圖掙扎，但是沒有體力用力掙扎。牠身側長長的一道擦傷看來血肉模糊。牠的毛蓬亂糾結。牠不斷發出奇怪的聲音。我不想把牠抱在身上，於是自公事包中拿出購物袋，將貓放入其中。我開始走路回家。走不到半公里，我路過一座電話亭。我找出一間半夜有開的獸醫診所，告訴他們我要過去。接著我打電話叫計程車。車子於五分鐘後抵達。司機是個外國人，會說的英文不比那隻貓多。我把剛剛自電話簿中撕下的頁面拿給他看。他記下地址，開始開車。貓不叫了，不過還活著。我在踏入診所大門前將貓取出購物袋。

en_text: Inside a woman about my age waits behind a counter. She has long red hair tied in a ponytail. She wears little makeup and doesn't need it—she's a natural beauty with soft brown eyes and full lips. She's wearing a white medical jacket unbuttoned halfway down, as if she's about to step onto the set of a porn movie. Beneath it is a blue T-shirt. A great set of breasts pushes its way forward. She smiles at me for less than a second before her concern turns to the cat.
zh_text: 裡面有個跟我年紀相仿的女人等在櫃檯後。她將一頭紅髮綁成一條馬尾。她有上薄妝，不過沒有必要——她是個天生的美人，有著淡棕色的眼眸和豐厚的嘴唇。她身穿白色的醫療外套，上半身沒扣釦子，彷彿正要踏入色情片的拍攝現場一樣。外套下是件藍汗衫。高聳的雙峰向前隆起。她對我微笑了不到一秒，注意力隨即轉移到貓的身上。

en_text: "You're the man who just called?" "Yeah."
zh_text: 「你是剛打電話來的人？」「是。」

en_text: "You ran the cat over?" she asks in a soft voice, without managing to sound accusing. "I found him," I say. "I don't have a car, that's why I had to catch a taxi here," I say, and for some reason it's important to me that she believes that.
zh_text: 「你壓過這隻貓？」她輕聲詢問，沒有指責的意味「我發現牠。」我說。「所以我才搭計程車過來。」

en_text: She takes the cat from me without comment then disappears. I'm left standing by myself. I take a quick look around the clinic. Not much to see. Two walls are dedicated to products like leashes, collars, flea powder, bowls, cages, and food. Another wall has a thousand brochures and pamphlets that don't concern me since none of them is about getting away with murder. I take a seat. I should have been in bed by now. Should have been asleep. I stare at a display of bags of cat litter. I know from experience it's twice the price here than at the supermarket.
zh_text: 她不加評論，自我手中接過貓咪，然後離開。我被獨自留在那裡，不明白我為什麼會想解釋真實的情況。我迅速打量診所。沒什麼好看的。兩面牆上展示著鏈條、項圈、除蚤粉、碗、籠子以及食物。另外一面牆上擺滿一千張我沒興趣的傳單跟小冊子，因為沒有一張在教人如何擺脫殺人罪嫌。我找個位子坐下。現在我應該已經上床了才對。應該已經睡著了才對。我望著一包貓沙。根據我的經驗，這玩意兒在這種地方的售價比超級市場貴一倍。

en_text: I sit patiently. Five minutes turn into ten, then into twenty. I pick up a pamphlet on flea control. On the cover is an artist's impression of what a magnified flea would look like if it were wearing sunglasses and a leather jacket and hosting a party in the fur of a cat. On the next page is an actual photograph of a flea, magnified several hundred times. It seems the artist had it completely wrong. I'm halfway through the brochure, thinking about how scary the world would be if fleas were actually several hundred times bigger, when the redhead comes back out. I put the pamphlet down and hold my breath and stand up. "The cat's going to be okay," she says, breaking into a smile.
zh_text: 我耐心等候。五分鐘、十分鐘、二十分鐘。我拿起一份防治跳蚤的小冊子。封面上畫了一隻藝術家眼中的跳蚤——如果牠正戴著太陽眼鏡、穿著皮夾克、在貓的毛皮上開派對的話。下一頁有張放大幾百倍的跳蚤照片。看來藝術家完全畫錯了。看到一半的時候，紅髮女子走了出來。我起身。「貓會好起來。」她說，面露微笑。

en_text: "What a relief," I say, almost too tired to mean it. "Do you know who he belongs to?"
zh_text: 「太好了。」我說，疲憊到語氣聽來不太誠懇。「你知道他的主人是谁嗎？」

en_text: "No." "We're going to need to keep him here for a few days."
zh_text: 「不知道。」「我們需要留牠在這裡幾天。」

en_text: "Sure, sure, that sounds good," I say, thankful for her help. I realize I'm nodding like an idiot. "Umm, what happens if you can't find the owner? I mean, it won't get put down, will it?"
zh_text: 當然，當然，聽起來很好。」我說，感激她的幫助。「呃，如果找不到主人怎麼辦？我是說，你們不會把他安樂死吧？」

en_text: She shrugs, like she doesn't know, but I think she does. I give her my name and phone number, then pay for the medical attention the cat will need using the money Candy no longer needs. She doesn't try to stop my generosity, but she does point it out. She says I'm an incredibly nice man. I see no need to argue. She tells me she will call to let me know of the cat's progress. I ask her if she can call me a taxi, but she says she's about to leave, and offers me a lift home.
zh_text: 她聳肩，好像她不知道，但是我認爲她知道。我留下我的姓名和電話，然後支付那隻貓需要的醫療費用。她沒有阻止我付那麼多錢，不過她有告知我付太多了。她說我是個難得一見的大好人。我看不出來有爭辯這一點的必要。她說她會打電話讓我知道之後的發展。我請她幫我叫計程車，不過她說她要下班了，可以載我回家。

en_text: I glance at my watch. It would be fun to get a ride with her, but where would I dump her body? "I don't want to put you out. A taxi's fine." She seems disappointed, but doesn't strengthen her offer. The taxi driver is a large man whose stomach rests on the steering wheel and toots the horn every time we go over a bump. He drops me off outside my apartment, the potholes in my street making him wake up the neighbors in the process. The trash outside my apartment has been added to by more trash, and I have to bat away a few flies as I make my way inside. I'm struggling to stay awake as I climb my way up to my door. Inside I ignore my fish, making me not quite the nice guy the vet receptionist thought I was, opting to spend some quality time with my bed instead. I lie down and close my eyes and pretty much fall right asleep.
zh_text: 我看了我的錶一眼。坐她的車會很愉快，不過我要在哪裡棄置她的屍體？「我不想太麻煩妳。計程車就好了。」計程車司機是個胖子，肚子頂在方向盤上，車身每次震動都會壓到喇叭。他在我家門口放我下來。我沒管我的魚，直接爬上床，轉眼沉沉睡去。

en_text: Seven thirty my eyes open. Right on time. I don't have to worry about shaking away any dregs of a dream, because I never dream. I guess I don't because half the shit people dream about I actually do. If I did, I suppose it would be of being married to some plumpish woman with poor taste in everything from fashion to sexual positions. I'd be living inside a house with a mortgage that would take a lifetime to pay off, getting nagged by two unfit kids every single day. I'd be taking out trash and mowing lawns. Each Sunday morning as I pulled out of the driveway in my station wagon on my way to church, I'd have to avoid running over the dog. A Goddamn nightmare.
zh_text: 我雙眼於七點半睜開。很準時。我不需要用開任何夢中殘餘的片段，因為我從不做夢。我想之所以不做夢是因為我真的會去做半數人們在夢裡會做的事情。萬一真的做夢，我想我會夢到跟個從時尙感到性愛姿勢通通品味不佳的胖女人結婚。我會住在一間貸款交到死都交不完的房子裡，每天都讓兩個討人厭的孩子煩得要死。我得要倒垃圾，還得給草皮除草。每個禮拜天，當我駕駛休旅車前往教堂時，我都必須小心不要壓到狗。真他媽的惡夢。

en_text: I share my morning routing with a feeling I can't quite shake, like there's bad news I haven't been given yet. It becomes so strong that I have to take a few minutes to sit down on the sofa and take some deep breaths. My eyes blur with tears, and even playing with Pickle and Jehovah can't cheer me up. I think of the cat I saved last night. That can't cheer me up either. Something bad has happened. I think of Mom and hope she's okay.
zh_text: 換衣服的時候，一股不祥的預感突然來襲。那感覺像是一個我還沒收到的壞消息。我不確定是怎麼回事，不過在進行上班前的例行公事期間一直有這種感覺。我的雙眼泛淚，就連跟泡菜還有耶和華玩都沒辦法讓我好過一點。我想著昨晚救的那隻貓。一樣沒能讓我好一點。有壞事發生了。我想到媽，希望她沒事。

en_text: I make myself a quick breakfast before going to work. No need to walk around hungry just because of bad premonitions. I'm running late so have to run for the bus. Mr. Stanley sees me coming and waits. "Almost missed you this morning, Joe," he says, and this time he punches my ticket— perhaps as punishment for putting him thirty seconds off schedule. Despite that, I still like him. He's an okay guy. Now, Mr. Stanley lives my nightmare. He's married with two kids, one of them in a wheelchair. I know all this because I followed him home one day. Not as a potential victim (though everybody has potential, so I learned in school), but just out of curiosity. It's amazing that a guy with a useless kid and an ugly wife and a crappy job can be so friendly every day. Perhaps more suspicious than amazing. I want to ask him what his secret is.
zh_text: 我匆匆吃了早餐，然後去上班。沒必要爲了不祥預感就餓肚子。公車上，史丹利先生剪了我的票，照例跟我嘘寒問暖。我喜歡史丹利先生。他人不錯。好吧，史丹利先生就是活在我的惡夢裡。他結婚了，有兩個小孩，其中之一必須坐輪椅。我知道這些是因為我跟蹤他回家過一次。不是把他當作有潛力的目標（雖然根據我在學校所學，每個人都有潛力），只是爲了滿足我的好奇。我很難想像有個廢物小孩、醜老婆以及爛工作的男人每天怎麼還能如此和善。

en_text: I walk down the aisle. Find a seat behind a couple of businessmen. The two of them are talking loudly about money, mergers, and acquisitions. I wonder who they are trying to impress on this bus. Maybe each other.
zh_text: 我沿著走道走去，坐在兩個生意人後方。他們兩個大聲談論著金錢、併購及獲利之類的事情。我不知道在這輛公車上他們是在講給誰聽。或許是彼此。

en_text: The air shimmers. The day is still. It's classic global warming weather. I wait for two cars to run the red light before I cross the road. Outside the police station the drunks from the night's holding tanks are being let out, their faces scrunched up in the bright autumn sun.
zh_text: 空氣微微閃爍。四周一片沉悶。我等待兩輛汽車闖紅燈，然後才穿越馬路。警局外，昨晚拘留的酒鬼都被放了出來，他們的臉在耀眼陽光下揪成一團。

en_text: "Morning, Joe," she says in the carefully structured, drawn-out way of a woman struggling with the concept of speech. I have to offer my own version of it, because retarded or not, everybody around here expects me to talk like an imbecile.
zh_text: 「早安，喬。」她以一種咬字清晰又拉得很長的語調說話，像個搞不清楚該怎麼講話的女人。我也得裝出這種語調，因為不管是不是白痴，這裡的人都期待我像個低能兒般講話。

en_text: "Hi morning, Sally," I say, and then I smile the big-kid smile with all the teeth, the one that suggests I'm proud to have strung three words together to make a sentence, even if I did fuck it up. "What a beautiful day. Do you like this weather, Joe?"
zh_text: 「嗨早安，莎莉。」我說，像個大男孩般露齒而笑，一副我對自己能夠說出由三個單字組成的句子十分驕傲的模樣，雖然這句話說得怪怪的。「真是美好的一天。你喜歡這種天氣嗎，喬？」

en_text: Actually it's a bit hot for my taste. "I like the warm sun. I like summer." I'm talking like an idiot so Slow Sally can understand me. "I like Christmas even more." "You should join me for lunch by the river," she says, hitting on me and almost making me gag. I can just imagine how much fun that'd be. How much fun I'd have as the other people walk by looking at one person pretending to be retarded while the other pretends to be normal. We could throw bread at the ducks and tell each other which clouds look like pirate ships and which look like the bloated corpses of drowning victims. Damn, does Sally even know she isn't normal? Do their kind know that about themselves?
zh_text: 事實上，我覺得有點熱。「我喜歡溫暖的陽光。我喜歡夏天。」我像白痴般講話，好讓智障莎莉聽懂我在講什麼。今天跟我去河邊午餐吧。」她說，主動搭訕，讓我差點嗆到。我能夠想像那景象有多有趣。看著路過的人欣賞一個假裝白痴的正常人和一個假裝正常的白痴一起吃飯的模樣會多有趣。我們可以丟麵包給鴨子吃，告訴對方哪片雲看起來像海盜船，哪片看起來像浮屍或是溺斃的被害人。可惡，莎莉究竟知不知道自己不正常？她們那種人知道自己與衆不同嗎？

en_text: "You should join me for lunch by the river," she says, hitting on me and almost making me gag. I can just imagine how much fun that'd be. How much fun I'd have as the other people walk by looking at one person pretending to be retarded while the other pretends to be normal. We could throw bread at the ducks and tell each other which clouds look like pirate ships and which look like the bloated corpses of drowning victims. Damn, does Sally even know she isn't normal? Do their kind know that about themselves? The elevator arrives. I'm confused as to whether I should do the gentlemanly thing and let her step in first, or do the retarded thing and push ahead of her? I do the gentlemanly thing, because the retarded thing means I'd have to scream as the elevator goes up a few stories and then pretend to be in awe at how the scenery has changed when the doors open.
zh_text: 今天跟我去河邊午餐吧。」她說，主動搭訕，讓我差點嗆到。我能夠想像那景象有多有趣。看著路過的人欣賞一個假裝白痴的正常人和一個假裝正常的白痴一起吃飯的模樣會多有趣。我們可以丟麵包給鴨子吃，告訴對方哪片雲看起來像海盜船，哪片看起來像浮屍或是溺斃的被害人。可惡，莎莉究竟知不知道自己不正常？她們那種人知道自己與衆不同嗎？電梯到了。我不知道該像個紳士般讓她先進去，還是像個智障般搶先進去？我決定當紳士，因為當智障就表示我得要在電梯上升幾樓後開始尖叫，然後在發現電梯門後景觀不同時做出驚訝的反應。

en_text: "Fourth floor, Joe?" "Sure."
zh_text: 「三樓嗎，喬？」「當然。

en_text: The doors close. "So . . ." she says, then doesn't finish.
zh_text: 門關了。「那麼……」

en_text: "So what'll it be? You want to join me for lunch?" "I like my office, Sally. I like sitting there and looking out the window." "I know you do, Joe. But outside is good for you."
zh_text: 「那麼你覺得呢？你要跟我共進午餐嗎？」「我喜歡我的辦公室，莎莉。我喜歡坐在裡面，看著窗外。」「我知道，喬。但是出去走走對你比較好。」

en_text: "Huh? Sure," I say, and the rate the elevator is moving at makes me think the fourth floor has been raised a few levels. "I guess so." "I can give you a lift sometimes, if you'd like."
zh_text: 「呃？當然，我想是。」「喜歡的話，我可以載你回家。」

en_text: "I can give you a lift sometimes, if you'd like." "I like the bus."
zh_text: 「喜歡的話，我可以載你回家。」「我喜歡公車。」

en_text: She shrugs, gives up on our conversation. "I'll drop off those sandwiches for you soon."
zh_text: 她聳肩，放棄交談。「我過一會兒送三明治給你。」

en_text: "Thanks, Sally. That'll be nice." And it would be nice. Sally may be a dimwit, she may have a crush on me, but she's always been good to me. Always friendly. Nobody else has ever offered me food, or offered me a lift home (though surely she can't drive—she must mean a lift with her mom or something), and I could do a lot worse. Even though I don't like her, I don't not like her as much as I don't like everybody else. In a way that makes her the closest thing I have to a friend. Outside of my goldfish.
zh_text: 「謝謝，莎莉。那樣好。」那樣確實不錯。莎莉或許是個傻瓜，她或許喜歡我，不過她總是對我很好。總是非常親切。沒有別人帶東西給我吃，或是說要送我回家（不過她當然不會開車——她一定是指讓她媽或是誰來載我們一起回家），而我可能會遇上更糟糕的人。儘管我不喜歡她，但是我不喜歡她的程度還沒有到我不喜歡別人那種地步。從某方面而言，她是最接近朋友定義的人。除了我的金魚之外。

en_text: The doors close, and the smile I offer Sally as they do isn't forced, it's natural, and I realize this too late to change it to my big-boy grin. She stares at me with a blank look on her face, then the doors close and Sally is gone, and a moment later she is gone from my thoughts. I head straight to the conference room. "Hi there, Joe."
zh_text: 電梯門關閉時，我向莎莉露出的笑容並不是勉強擠出來的，而是很自然的，當我發現這一點時已經太遲，沒機會換回那個大男孩微笑了。電梯門關了，莎莉離開了，片刻過後，她也遠離我的腦海。我直接走向會議室。「嗨，喬。」

en_text: "Morning, Detective Schroder." I start looking at him as a suspect, trying to picture him killing Walker. It's easy to do. Of course it's easy to picture any of these people killing her, from the photographer to the pathologist. The first thing I need to do is get a list of these people, then begin eliminating them. As suspects, that is.
zh_text: 「早安，施羅德警探。」我開始把他當成嫌犯般打量，試圖想像他殺害沃克的模樣。施羅德身材壯碩，看起來像是由一團批著皮膚的肌肉組成。如果我會被抓的話，我會盡量不讓他抓到。現在我要將所有偵辦此案的人員當成嫌犯，從攝影師到法醫。我要做的第一件事就是弄一份這些人員的名單，然後開始排除他們。排除嫌犯的可能，我是指。

en_text: "How's the in . . . inv . . . invest . . ." I stop. Just long enough for him to think I'm in that small percentile of the population with an extra chromosome. "How's the case going, Detective Schroder? Found the killer yet?" He shakes his head slowly, as if he's trying to line up a few thoughts in there, but not too hard in case some of them get broken. "Not yet, Joe. Getting there."
zh_text: 「那件……那件……」我說到一半停下。剛好久到讓他以爲我就是那百分之零點五多出來一條染色體的人。「那件案子怎麼樣了，施羅德警探？找到兇手沒？」他緩緩搖頭，彷彿試圖在裡面排列一些思緒，但又沒有很用力在排，因為怕弄破它們。「還沒，喬。快找到了。」

en_text: "Any suspects, Detective Schroder?"
zh_text: 「有嫌犯嗎，施羅德警探？」

en_text: "A few. And Joe, you can call me Carl."
zh_text: 「有幾個。還有喬，你可以叫我卡爾。」

en_text: I'm not going to call him Carl. He's asked me before. Anyway, I've already shortened detective inspector to just detective. And as for there being a few suspects—he's lying.
zh_text: 我才不要叫他卡爾。他以前就這樣說過了。反正我已經把偵緝督察簡化爲警探了。

en_text: He stares at the photographs, grimacing, like he does every morning now. Almost as though he's expecting to come in and find one of the victims has reached out from her portrait and written an answer up there for him. In reality he has nothing. He knows it. I know it. Everybody knows it. Especially the media.
zh_text: 他盯著照片，眉頭深鎖，就跟每天早上一樣。那感覺就像是他期待能夠一到警局就發現有個被害人從照片裡跑出來爲他寫下答案一樣。在現實裡，他毫無線索。他知道。我知道。所有人都知道。特別是媒體。

en_text: "Are you sure they've all been killed by the same person, Detective Schroder?" He turns and stares at me, and I regret my question. "Why's that, Joe? Have you been listening in on our conversations?" I shake my head. "No, never," I say. "I would never do that." He doesn't look convinced. "I just thought that maybe seven different people killed them because nobody can be that mean, can they?" I ask.
zh_text: 「你確定他們都是同一個人殺的嗎，施羅德警探？」

en_text: His expression softens, and slowly he shakes his head. "People can be that mean, Joe, and it's probably best you stop trying to think like Sherlock Holmes." I look down. "Umm . . . I was just, you know, curious." "Life is curious, Joe, and to answer your question, all of these murders all related."
zh_text: 怎麼這麼問，喬？你變成夏洛克·福爾摩斯了嗎？我低頭。「呃……沒有，施羅德警探。我只是，你知道，好奇。「人生總是非常奇妙，喬，還有沒錯，這些案子全都有關聯。」

en_text: I lift my head up fast and look over at him, widening my eyes in what hopefully looks like surprise. "They're all sisters, Detective Schroder?" I ought to get a Goddamn Emmy for this performance. "Not related that way, Joe," he sighs, and after a pause of a few seconds he carries on. "I mean they were all killed by the same person." "Oh. But that's good, right? Better to have one killer out there than seven?"
zh_text: 我迅速抬頭，看向他的身後，瞪大雙眼，故作驚訝貌。「她們都是姊妹，施羅德警探？」我的演技應該得艾美獎。不是那種關聯，喬。」他嘆氣，停了將近十秒。「我是說她們都是同一名兇手所殺。」

en_text: He nods. "It doesn't make any difference to them," he says, pointing at the photographs. "But in this case," he says, then pauses, "you're not going to repeat any of this to anybody, are you, Joe? You don't have friends in the media?" I shake my head, trying to keep a similar pace to Schroder's shake a few minutes ago. He thinks I have no friends. He doesn't know about Pickle and Jehovah. "You guys are the only friends I have, Detective Schroder."
zh_text: 「喔。你確定嗎？」「不會把我的話轉述給別人，是吧，喬？你沒有媒體界的朋友吧？」我搖頭，試圖模仿幾分鐘前施羅德警探搖頭的步調。他以爲我沒有朋友。他不知道泡菜和耶和華的事情。「你們就是我唯一的朋友，施羅德警探。」

en_text: "Have you ever heard of a copycat killer, Joe?"
zh_text: 你有聽說過模仿殺人犯嗎，喬？

en_text: I stop shaking my head before whiplash sets in. "Why would somebody kill cats?" There's another long sigh from Schroder, and I realize I might be laying it on a bit thick.
zh_text: 我搖頭搖到快要扭傷脖子才停。「怎麼會有人殺貓？」施羅德警探再度長嘆，我發現我裝得或許太過火了。

en_text: "Not quite, Joe. A copycat killer is somebody who kills to imitate a serial killer." "Why would they do that?" "Because they can. Because they want to. Because they're insane."
zh_text: 不是殺貓，喬。模仿殺人犯是模仿連續殺人犯殺人的人。「他們爲什麼要這麼做？」「因為他們能這麼做。因為他們想這麼做。因為他們瘋了。

en_text: "Oh. Then why are these people out there, Detective Schroder? Why don't they get put in jail?" "That's a good question," he says, and I smile at his praise. "And it comes with a simple answer. The world is screwed up. You know when you turn on the news and some bastard has gone and shot his family and a few of his neighbors?"
zh_text: 「喔。那這種人爲什麼能逍遙法外，施羅德警探？爲什麼不把他們抓起來關？「這是個好問題。」他說，我假裝在他讚揚的語氣下微笑。「答案很簡單。世界亂了。你知道那種打開電視就看到有人槍殺自己家人和鄰居的新聞的感覺？」

en_text: I start nodding. Stab thy neighbor. I'm familiar with it.
zh_text: 我開始點頭。刺死你的鄰居。我很熟悉那種感覺。

en_text: "The family, the other neighbors, they all say what a quiet guy he was. He had a collection of gun magazines and problems. Then we use hindsight as a preventative, even though it's too late by then. There's nothing to prevent, because everybody's already dead. . . . I'm sorry, Joe," he says, sighing. "I'm rambling on a bit. And venting. I shouldn't be burdening you with any of this."
zh_text: 「家人、其他朋友，他們全都宣稱兇手是個安靜的人。他有很多槍械雜誌和問題。我們總是事後才恍然大悟，但是一切都太遲了。我們沒有辦法預防這種事情，因為所有人都已經死了……我很抱歉，喬。」他嘆氣說道。「我在胡言亂語。我不該說這些話給你聽的。「我不介意。」

en_text: "I don't mind." "I just wish we could do more. I mean, we see these guys every day, but can we do anything about it? No. Because they have rights. Just like the rest of us. And until they finally kill somebody—and they often try to— those rights make them untouchable. Do you know what I mean, Joe?"
zh_text: 我只希望有更多我們能做的事情。我是說，我們每天都看到這些人，但是我們能夠做任何事情來預防這種情況嗎？不行。因為他們都有人權。就像我們其他人一樣。除非他們終於動手殺人——而他們通常都會嘗試動手——他們都受到人權保護。你知道我的意思嗎，喬？

en_text: "Kind of, Detective Schroder."
zh_text: 大概吧，施羅德警探。

en_text: He waves his hand at the wall. "A hundred to one we've spoken to this guy at some point in the past. We know he's got either a drug or a mental problem, but we could never do anything about it. Right now he's watching us, mocking us, laughing at us. I guarantee we've wanted to lock this guy up before, but weren't allowed. I guarantee we've had this guy in this building before."
zh_text: 他向牆面揮手。「我敢打賭一賠一百，我們已經跟兇手會過面了。我們知道他要嘛就是有毒癮，不然就是心理有問題，但是我們什麼都不能做。此刻他正在監視我們，愚弄我們，嘲笑我們。我敢說我們絕對曾想要把這傢伙關起來過，只是上面不允許。我敢說我們曾把這傢伙抓進警局過。」

en_text: He's right and wrong, but I can't point this out to him. Can't take a bet on his odds. With all his sermonizing I quickly lose faith in Schroder as an appropriate suspect. "I understand, Detective Schroder."
zh_text: 他說得對也不對，但是我不能爲他指出這一點。我不能跟他對賭一賠一百。這段長篇大論讓我迅速將他排除在嫌犯名單外。「我了解，施羅德警探。」

en_text: "You'd be one of the few if you do, Joe. You want to know something funny?" "Sure."
zh_text: 你是少數能夠了解的人，如果你真的了解的話，喬。想聽件可笑的事情嗎？當然。

en_text: "Serial killers like to stay ahead of the game, and you know how they do that?"
zh_text: 「連續殺人犯喜歡領先警方，你知道他們會怎麼做嗎？」

en_text: Fact is, I do know. They hang around the edges of the investigation. They might come into the station and say they saw something going on. They come in and try to get a feel for the investigation. Some even hang around in cop bars, listening to idle chitchat, even participating in conversation. Or hang out with reporters looking for an inside scoop.
zh_text: 事實上，我還眞的知道。他們會在調查人員旁徘徊。他們可能會跑來警局，宣稱他們見過某些事發經過。他們跑來打探調查的進度。有些人甚至會跑去警察酒吧混，聽他們說長論短，甚至參與討論。或是混在記者之間，試圖探聽內幕。

en_text: "No. How?" He shrugs again. "Sorry, Joe, I shouldn't be chewing your ear off like this."
zh_text: 「不知道。怎麼做？」他再度聳肩。「抱歉，喬，我不該這樣煩你。」

en_text: "So what about the cat killer?" I ask.
zh_text: 「那貓咪殺手怎麼樣？」

en_text: "Some other time," he sighs, and he says it in a way to indicate the conversation is over. I leave him staring silently at the wall of the dead. I reach up and run my finger across the nameplate on my office door. To the sides of it are four small screw holes. There never used to be anything on it until Sally showed up one day with a small sign with my name on it. Inside I swap my thoughts for a mop and bucket, and then go about cleaning the toilets. Before lunch I carry the vacuum cleaner into Detective Superintendent Stevens's office just as he is leaving. Stevens is the guy everybody answers to, even though he doesn't do any of the footwork, groundwork, or thought work that goes into solving this case. Stevens has been flown down from Wellington, and is one of the highestranking detectives in the country, though I can't see why. All he does is sit in his appointed office, ordering people about while demanding answers. Occasionally he walks back and forth, grabbing a pile of papers or a folder, just trying to look as though he has something to do or someplace to be. Most of the time he's a pretty pissed-off guy. I don't like him, but can't do anything about it. Murdering a police superintendent would be like playing with fire.
zh_text: 改天再說吧。他嘆氣，我留他一個人繼續去盯著死者牆壁看。我伸手觸摸我辦公室門上的名牌。邊邊有四個小螺絲孔。從前這塊牌子上寫著維修室，直到有一天莎莉拿了一塊刻有我名字的小名牌過來。我進去拿了抹布和水桶，然後開始打掃廁所。午餐前，我在史帝文斯偵緝督察長出門的同時帶著吸塵器進入他的辦公室。所有人都要向他回報，即使他完全沒有參與此案跑腿、偵辦或是腦力激盪等工作。史帝文斯是從威靈頓空降來的，是全國階級最高的警探之一，不過我看不出他有何能耐。他每天就是坐在上面指定給他的辦公室裡，下達命令，要求答案。偶爾他會走來走去，抓起一疊文件或是文件夾，裝出一副好像他有事要忙或有地方要去的模樣。大部分的時間他都是個脾氣暴躁的傢伙。我不喜歡他，不過束手無策。偵緝督察長遭人殺害會讓這個部門成爲目光焦點，甚至讓人懷疑到我頭上來。

en_text: I reach up and run my finger across the nameplate on my office door. To the sides of it are four small screw holes. There never used to be anything on it until Sally showed up one day with a small sign with my name on it. Inside I swap my thoughts for a mop and bucket, and then go about cleaning the toilets. Before lunch I carry the vacuum cleaner into Detective Superintendent Stevens's office just as he is leaving. Stevens is the guy everybody answers to, even though he doesn't do any of the footwork, groundwork, or thought work that goes into solving this case. Stevens has been flown down from Wellington, and is one of the highestranking detectives in the country, though I can't see why. All he does is sit in his appointed office, ordering people about while demanding answers. Occasionally he walks back and forth, grabbing a pile of papers or a folder, just trying to look as though he has something to do or someplace to be. Most of the time he's a pretty pissed-off guy. I don't like him, but can't do anything about it. Murdering a police superintendent would be like playing with fire. Stevens is in his late fifties, has thinning black hair, and looks like the sort of policeman you wouldn't approach for help. He is just over six feet and solidly built, but has these black eyes that any author would associate with crazed serial killers. He has a long face with wrinkles that run its entire length, like shallow knife wounds. His tanned skin is pitted with old acne scars around his neck. When he talks, he has a deep voice and an accent that sounds Caribbean, but that's probably because of the cigars he's always smoking. He's one of those useless bastards who wear sports jackets with elbow patches sewn into them.
zh_text: 我伸手觸摸我辦公室門上的名牌。邊邊有四個小螺絲孔。從前這塊牌子上寫著維修室，直到有一天莎莉拿了一塊刻有我名字的小名牌過來。我進去拿了抹布和水桶，然後開始打掃廁所。午餐前，我在史帝文斯偵緝督察長出門的同時帶著吸塵器進入他的辦公室。所有人都要向他回報，即使他完全沒有參與此案跑腿、偵辦或是腦力激盪等工作。史帝文斯是從威靈頓空降來的，是全國階級最高的警探之一，不過我看不出他有何能耐。他每天就是坐在上面指定給他的辦公室裡，下達命令，要求答案。偶爾他會走來走去，抓起一疊文件或是文件夾，裝出一副好像他有事要忙或有地方要去的模樣。大部分的時間他都是個脾氣暴躁的傢伙。我不喜歡他，不過束手無策。偵緝督察長遭人殺害會讓這個部門成爲目光焦點，甚至讓人懷疑到我頭上來。年近六十的史帝文斯有著一頭稀疏的黑髮，看起來就像那種你不會考慮找他幫忙的警察。他身高六呎出頭，體格十分結實，不過眼旁的黑眼圈會讓任何作家聯想到連續殺人魔。他長臉之上皺紋滿布，看來很像淺淺的刀傷。頸部的深色皮膚上密密麻麻都是年代久遠的粉刺疤痕。開口說話時聲音低沉，帶有一股加勒比腔調，不過那很可能是因為隨時不離手的雪茄菸的關係。他就是那種身穿手肘處縫有補綴的運動外套的大廢物。

en_text: I wonder if the ballpoint pen that was left behind was his. I look into his black eyes, searching for the evil that fiction suggests should be there, but I can't see any of it. He tells me to do a good job, says he'll be back after lunch. That gives me plenty of time. So it's just me in his office, me and Mr. Vacuum Cleaner. I sweep it around the carpet like it makes a difference, looking left and right for any information that will help. Like the conference room, Stevens's office looks out onto the fourth floor, meaning people can look in if the blinds are open, as they are. Ten minutes of sucking the same piece of carpet go by, and it's not getting any cleaner. I drop a rag behind his desk, bend down, and use the chance to peek into his desk drawers. I rummage through them, finding a roster of everybody involved in the case in the third drawer I check. I slip it into my overalls. Then I start coughing. Yep, Joe the retard needs a drink. I head to the water cooler. On the way back I pass the photocopying room. It's empty, so I step inside and photocopy the roster. Walk back to the office. Place the document back into the folder.
zh_text: 我懷疑留在現場的原子筆是不是他的。我凝望他的黑眼珠，尋找小說裡描述的那種邪惡目光，不過看不出來。他叫我好好打掃，說他吃完午飯就會回來。這表示我時間充裕。只有我在他的辦公室裡，我和吸塵器先生。我在地毯上吸來吸去，好像當眞吸得乾淨一樣，左顧右盼地尋找可能會有用處的線索。跟會議室一樣，史帝文斯的辦公室能夠看見三樓內的景象，也就是說如果百葉窗拉起來的話，外面的人就會看見裡面，而現在百葉窗就是拉起來的。同一塊地毯吸了十分鐘，一點都沒有比較乾淨。我丟了塊抹布到他辦公桌後方，彎下腰去撿，趁機偷看他的抽屜。我拿起最上面的文件夾，打開它。裡面是所有參與此案人員的名冊。我將檔案夾塞入工作服。然後開始咳嗽。沒錯，智障喬需要喝點東西。我走向飲水器。回程時我路過影印室。裡面沒人，於是我走進去影印了一份名冊。走回辦公室。將文件放回文件夾。及時吸完地毯，回去吃午飯。

en_text: Finish vacuuming in time for lunch. The sun is shining through my office window, so I sit in front of it and pretend I'm getting a tan. I'd have to pretend really hard for other people to see it. Sally knocks on my door, then steps in and hands me a small parcel of food. I give her a small thank you in return. She asks me again if I want to join her outside, and I make the mistake of saying maybe next time. She positively beams at this before she leaves. I stare out the window on the chance I might see her out there, but my view doesn't overlook the river so the only people I see are strangers. On the horizon I see something I haven't seen in weeks—rain clouds. They're too far away to tell which direction they're moving. I eat my sandwiches while looking at the list. With over ninety names on it, ninety-four to be exact, it's pretty big. I don't know what I expected —maybe half a dozen or so—but ninety-four suggests a lot of people running around not knowing what's going on. Dozens more officers took statements, but it's only the detectives who work the scene. Only the detectives who see the body.
zh_text: 陽光自我的辦公室窗口灑落，於是我坐在窗前，假裝曬太陽。我必須努力假裝給其他人看。莎莉敲了敲門，然後走進來，給我一小袋食物。我輕聲道謝。她又問我要不要跟她出去吃，我不小心說了或許改天吧。她帶著愉快的微笑離開。我凝望窗外，看看能不能看到她。不過我的窗口看不見河岸，所以我只看到一群陌生人。我邊看名冊，邊吃三明治。名冊上有超過九十個名字，精確來說是九十四個，很長的名單。我不知道原先期待看到多少——或許半打左右——不過九十四個就表示有一大票搞不清楚狀況的人在現場附近出沒。有數十名警員在外面蒐集鄰居證詞，不過只有警探才會處理犯罪現場。只有警探才會看到屍體。

en_text: I begin to panic: this could take me forever. The feeling that this is going to be a big waste of time is creeping deep into my thoughts. But not all of the people on this list would have been to each of the crime scenes, right? Maybe half of them at each one, maybe not even that. The trick is to figure out which of these ninety-four people went to Daniela Walker's house.
zh_text: 我開始慌了：這件事情可能要搞很久。我心裡產生一股很可能會白忙一場的恐懼。不過並非所有這份名單上的人都曾到過所有犯罪現場，是吧？或許只有半數，甚至可能不到。竅門在於弄清楚這九十四個人裡有多少人到過丹妮耶拉·沃克家。排班表。

en_text: Lunch isn't over yet, but I'm too excited to keep eating. I head into the records room and give it a good spring cleaning. I take extra time near the hard copy of the phone records, giving the area around it an extremely thorough polishing. On the night Daniela Walker was killed, fifteen phone calls out of twenty were successfully made. These are the people who showed up. Fifteen people, plus however many officers showed up on the scene to report it.
zh_text: 午餐還沒吃完，不過我已經興奮到吃不下飯了。我前往紀錄室，好好來個大掃除。我在電話紀錄區多花了一點時間，把那附近擦得特別乾淨。丹妮耶拉·沃克遇害當晚，二十通電話中有十五通成功接通。這些就是有前往現場的人。十五個人，加上天知道多少進入現場回報的警員。

en_text: The original phone call made from the victim's husband to police dispatch is here too. I start reading, but find it has little interest.
zh_text: 被害人丈夫報警的電話紀錄也在這裡。我開始閱讀，不過沒什麼好看的。

en_text: Dispatch sent the nearest car to the scene to begin controlling things before the cavalry arrived. Two officers. Their names are on my list. I circle them. I also circle the fifteen called that night—including the pathologist, the photographer, and Detective Superintendent Stevens with the jetblack eyes. This means I've just cut nearly eighty people off my suspect list. The fear I have of this being a waste of time creeps away. I'm down to seventeen people. I doubt the two officers who first responded to the husband's call have anything to do with her death. First of all, they were together for the previous six hours on their shift, and the body was discovered only an hour after she was killed. Second, what are the chances that the person who killed her was the very officer called to the scene? Pretty low, that's what. I cross their names off the list.
zh_text: 勤務中心派遣最近的警車前往現場，在大隊人馬抵達前控制狀況。兩名警員。他們的名字在我的名單上。我把他們圈出來。我同時也圈出了當晚十五通電話通知的人——包括法醫、攝影師，以及雙眼漆黑的史帝文斯偵緝督察長。這表示我自名單中排除了將近八十個人。深怕白忙一場的恐懼緩緩消失了。嫌犯剩下十七個。我懷疑率先抵達現場的兩名警員會跟此案有關。第一，之前六個小時他們都在一起值班。第二，殺害她的兇手剛好就是被派遣到現場的警員的機會有多高？很低，非常低。我將他們的名字劃掉。

en_text: This means I've just cut nearly eighty people off my suspect list. The fear I have of this being a waste of time creeps away. I'm down to seventeen people. I doubt the two officers who first responded to the husband's call have anything to do with her death. First of all, they were together for the previous six hours on their shift, and the body was discovered only an hour after she was killed. Second, what are the chances that the person who killed her was the very officer called to the scene? Pretty low, that's what. I cross their names off the list. Fifteen people.
zh_text: 這表示我自名單中排除了將近八十個人。深怕白忙一場的恐懼緩緩消失了。嫌犯剩下十七個。我懷疑率先抵達現場的兩名警員會跟此案有關。第一，之前六個小時他們都在一起值班。第二，殺害她的兇手剛好就是被派遣到現場的警員的機會有多高？很低，非常低。我將他們的名字劃掉。十五個人。

en_text: I think about the pathologist. He found several differences between this body and the others. Because he works alone, he could have easily manufactured evidence to make the residues and fibers on this victim identical to the others, but he didn't. Who was going to check his work? Nobody. That's who. If he had killed her, the results would be identical to the others. But they're not.
zh_text: 我考慮法醫。他在這具屍體上發現了好幾處跟其他屍體不同之處。由於獨自工作，他可以輕易竄改證據，讓殘留組織和纖維物質吻合其他屍體，但是他沒這麼做。有誰會去檢查他的報告？沒有人。沒人會檢查。如果兇手是他，驗屍結果就會跟其他屍體一樣。但是結果不同。

en_text: So it isn't him.
zh_text: 所以不是他。

en_text: Fourteen people. Could this be any easier?
zh_text: 十四個人。有沒有這麼容易？

en_text: Back in my office the sun is no longer streaming in, instead one of the rain clouds is covering it, but the cloud is still holding onto its payload. I can't remember the last time I saw rain. When I sit and look at the list again, I see something obvious I missed while in the records room. Of the fourteen left, four are women. I cross them off the list. I could have narrowed down the original ninety-four the same way, but it doesn't matter now. Ten people. I write their names onto a fresh piece of paper, then sit there staring at them until four thirty comes along and says hello. I say good-bye to everybody who crosses my path on the way out of the building. Sally isn't among them. On the way to the bus stop I remember the feeling I had this morning that something was wrong with my mother, and I chide myself for being foolish. If something had happened I would have got the bad news by now.
zh_text: 回到辦公室，再度坐下來研究名單時，我發現了在紀錄室裡忽略掉的一個明顯的線索。剩下的十四個人裡，有四個是女人。我劃掉她們的名字。我可以用同樣的方式排除原先的九十四人，不過那已經不重要了。十個人。我將他們的名字寫在一張白紙上，然後坐下來瞪著它們，直到四點半跑來跟我打招呼爲止。我在離開警局的路上跟所有路過的人招呼。沒有遇上莎莉。前往公車站途中，我想起今天早上那種我媽出事了的感覺，隨即責罵自己太愚蠢了。如果出了什麼事，我早就應該收到消息了。

en_text: But what, exactly? She likes to think that it means Joe likes her, that their friendship is moving along the way she wants. Of course, it might have been a fluke. Joe might have been staring off into space as he is apt to do when she is around him.
zh_text: 但到底是什麼樣的火花呢？她希望這表示喬喜歡她，表示兩人的友誼正朝著自己期望的方向發展。當然，那也可能只是碰巧而已。喬或許只是跟以往在她身邊的時候一樣眼神放空而已。

en_text: She likes to think that it means Joe likes her, that their friendship is moving along the way she wants. Of course, it might have been a fluke. Joe might have been staring off into space as he is apt to do when she is around him. Yet there is no denying that it didn't only make him look grown-up, it made him more . . . more . . . attractive? Sadly, the answer is yes. Joe is attractive, and she had never noticed it before. She doesn't want to think about it now, either, because she finds it confusing.
zh_text: 她希望這表示喬喜歡她，表示兩人的友誼正朝著自己期望的方向發展。當然，那也可能只是碰巧而已。喬或許只是跟以往在她身邊的時候一樣眼神放空而已。難以否認的是，這個笑容不但讓他有種長大的感覺，同時還讓他……更加……迷人？不幸的是，答案是肯定的。喬很迷人，而她之前都沒注意到這一點。

en_text: Yet there is no denying that it didn't only make him look grown-up, it made him more . . . more . . . attractive? Sadly, the answer is yes. Joe is attractive, and she had never noticed it before. She doesn't want to think about it now, either, because she finds it confusing. She spends the day at work fixing a section of faulty air-conditioning. It's a job that has taken the last few weeks of her time. It breaks down every year or two, and the government isn't prepared to budget more money for police, let alone make their surroundings slightly more comfortable. So she does what she can—stopgap measures that will keep it working until the day those measures fall short.
zh_text: 難以否認的是，這個笑容不但讓他有種長大的感覺，同時還讓他……更加……迷人？不幸的是，答案是肯定的。喬很迷人，而她之前都沒注意到這一點。她一整天都在修理部分區域的空調。過去幾個禮拜她都在跟空調系統奮戰。空調每隔一兩年就會壞一次，但政府並不打算爲警方編列更多預算，更別提讓他們的工作環境更加舒適。於是她盡力而爲——運用權宜之計維持空調運作，直到所有權宜之計通通失效爲止。

en_text: Yet her mind keeps returning to Joe. She's sure he doesn't know that he's not the only cleaner employed here. After six o'clock every night, well after Joe has gone home, a team of cleaners come through and do their thing. They vacuum, wipe, dust, sanitize the bathrooms, refill the paper towel dispensers, clean and put away the dishes in the coffee rooms, replace dirty towels with clean ones, and empty the trash cans. Some of these things Joe will do once a week, or once every few weeks, but he doesn't know other people are taking care of them every single day. Joe is here during the day to keep things tidy and, she suspects, to keep people happy. Special people like Joe can struggle to find work, and in a world where they must contribute, where they must fend for themselves, sometimes the government must step in and create positions for them. She knows nobody has told Joe he's not alone in his profession here because it might shatter the image he has of his importance. Sweet, sweet Joe. She doesn't see Joe when she leaves work. Only a few people finish at four thirty, and because of her father's illness, she's one of them. She heads down Cashel Mall, a shopping street that runs through the center of town that's a few blocks from the Christchurch Cathedral, the city's most iconic church that's made of stone and was built well over a hundred years ago. She tried once to go inside and sit in the silence, only there wasn't any— too many tourists for that. She doesn't make it as far as the church today, instead she pauses outside shop windows and occasionally goes inside, searching, hunting, trying to find a gift for her dad that he will appreciate. She needs a card too. Something funny. Something that for the briefest of moments will take his mind off his failing body and her late brother. Just what do you buy for the parent who's losing everything?
zh_text: 想起喬就讓她忍不住微笑。她很肯定他不知道他不是警局中唯一的清潔工。每天晚上六點過後，早已過了喬回家的時間，一組清潔隊員就會打掃整棟大樓。他們吸塵、擦拭、除灰、消毒廁所、補充紙巾機、清理並收拾咖啡間、以乾淨的毛巾更換髒的、並且清空垃圾桶。有些事情喬一個禮拜會做一次，或是隔幾個禮拜會做一次，但是他不知道有其他人每天都在處理它們。喬白天待在這裡是爲了維持環境整潔以及，她懷疑，爲了讓大家高興。像喬這種特殊人士要找工作不容易，而在這個他們必須付出、必須自給自足的世界裡，有時候政府必須出面幫他們製造一些工作機會。她知道沒有人告訴喬這個工作還有其他人在做，因爲這樣可能會粉碎他看待自己的價值。甜蜜、甜蜜的喬。她下班時沒看到喬。只有少數人能在四點半下班，而由於父親生病的緣故，她是其中之一。她走向凱歇爾購物中心，在櫥窗前佇足，偶爾走入店內，尋找、搜索、試圖買樣她爸會喜歡的禮物。她也需要買張卡片。有趣的卡片。一張可以短暫讓他忘卻越來越差的身體和她死去弟弟的卡片。失去一切的父親到底會喜歡什麼禮物？

en_text: She carries her purchases back to her car, pausing only to give Henry another small bag of sandwiches. She wonders if a guy like Henry ever tries to save for anything. How hard it must be to have goals in life when you have nothing. It's not like the poor guy can buy a suit and go to a job interview. It's not like he can show up to one dressed the way he is. She thinks she ought to try and help him out there. "Jesus loves you," he reminds her, opening the bag. "Remember that, Sally, and everything will be okay." By the time she reaches her car, she feels like crying. Not even thinking about Joe's smile can cheer her back up.
zh_text: 她將購買的禮物搬到車上，中途只有停下來交給亨利另外一袋三明治。在一無所有的情況下保持人生目標一定是件很難的事情。「耶穌愛妳。」他提醒她，打開袋子。「記住這點，莎莉，一切都會沒事的。」抵達車旁時，她覺得好想哭。就連回想喬的微笑都沒辦法讓她恢復之前的心情。

en_text: I pull out the latest cassette tape from the conference room and listen to the private words falling from the small speaker of my recorder as I pace back and forth. Not just hear, but really listen. I've heard all of the other tapes over the months, but I was only ever listening to see how the investigation was going. Now I have something new to listen for. Detective Taylor is for the theory that they're looking for more than one killer.
zh_text: 我拿出最新的會議室錄音帶，一邊來回踱步，一邊聽著小錄音機喇叭裡傳來的機密交談。不光只是聽，而是用心聽。幾個月來每一卷帶子我都聽過，不過都只是在聽警方有沒有線索而已。如今我有其他東西要聽。泰勒警探認爲理論上兇手不止一人

en_text: Detective Taylor is for the theory that they're looking for more than one killer. So is Detective McCoy, who suspects the killers are working together.
zh_text: 泰勒警探認爲理論上兇手不止一人麥考伊警探也是如此認爲，他懷疑兇手在合作犯案。

en_text: So is Detective McCoy, who suspects the killers are working together. Detective Hutton is still of the opinion that it's one person.
zh_text: 麥考伊警探也是如此認爲，他懷疑兇手在合作犯案。胡頓警探仍然認爲是一人所爲。

en_text: Other theories. Mixed theories. Confused theories. A confused investigation is a messy investigation. Nobody can agree. Nothing gets done. This makes people hard to catch. Makes things good for me.
zh_text: 還有其他理論。雜亂的理論。迷惘的理論。一場迷惘的調查就是亂七八糟的調查。沒有人能取得共識。什麼事都辦不成。這會讓他們難以掌握大局。情況對我有利。

en_text: I make some dinner. Nothing exciting. Instant pasta that cooks quickly in the microwave, and some coffee. Then I change into something more casual—jeans and a shirt. I'm looking pretty good, better than good. I put on a dark jacket. Even better.
zh_text: 我做了點晚餐。不算豐盛。微波完就可以吃的義大利麵，搭配一杯咖啡。接著我換上一套輕便的衣服——牛仔褲和襯衫。我看起來很帥，帥斃了。我穿上一件深色外套。更帥了。

en_text: I'm just about to go out when the phone rings. My first thought is that it's Mom, and then I remember the bad feeling I had this morning, so my next thought is it may not be Mom, but somebody calling about Mom. I have no idea where it comes from, but an image of making funeral arrangements and sausage rolls for the after-funeral party flashes through my mind. I sit to prepare for the shock that will put both my investigation and my life on hold. My heart races as I put my hand out to the receiver. Please, God, don't let it be so. Don't let anything bad happen to my mother. I pick it up and do my best to sound calm. "Hello?"
zh_text: 正當我打算出門時，電話響了。我直覺認爲是媽打來的，接著想起早上那股不祥的預感，我又覺得或許不是媽，而是爲了媽的事情打來的人。我的心中浮現一幅幫媽安排葬禮以及準備儀式後聚餐食物的畫面。我坐下來，準備迎接將會打斷我的調查和人生的震撼消息。我心跳加速，伸手去拿聽筒。拜託，上帝，不要出這種事。不要讓壞事發生在我媽身上。我拿起話筒，盡可能表現冷靜。「哈囉？」

en_text: "Mom, boy, am I glad to hear from you," I say, the words coming out in one long clump. "It's your mother. I've been trying to ring you all day."
zh_text: 「媽，天啊，我真高興聽到妳的聲音。」我說，聲音有點含糊不清「我是你媽。我一整天都在打電話找你。」

en_text: I look at my answering machine. The little light isn't flashing. "You didn't leave any messages."
zh_text: 我看向答錄機。留言燈沒閃。「妳沒有留言。」

en_text: "You know I don't like talking to a machine." This, of course, is a fallacy. Mom will talk to anything if the opportunity is there. "Are you coming to see me tonight, Joe?"
zh_text: 你知道我不喜歡跟機器說話。這當然是睜著眼睛說瞎話。只要有機會，媽會跟任何東西說話。「你今天要來找我嗎，喬？」

en_text: Mom will talk to anything if the opportunity is there. "Are you coming to see me tonight, Joe?" "It's Wednesday."
zh_text: 這當然是睜著眼睛說瞎話。只要有機會，媽會跟任何東西說話。「你今天要來找我嗎，喬？」「今天禮拜三。」

en_text: "I can't. I've got plans." "A girlfriend?"
zh_text: 不行。我今天有事。「女朋友？」

en_text: "No." "Oh. I see. Well, I wish you weren't—" "I'm not gay, Mom."
zh_text: 「不是。」「喔，我知道了。好了，這種事情是不……」「我不是同性戀，媽。」

en_text: "I thought you might want to come and see me after I was sick all night." "Sick?"
zh_text: 我想在我不舒服一整晚後，你或許會想來看看我。

en_text: "More than sick, Joe. I've been up all night sitting on the toilet," she says, and already that's more information than I needed. Before I can stop her or shoot myself she carries on. "I had stomach pains. I've never experienced anything like it. I was squirting water." I look around my room for a security blanket, something to keep me in reality, to stop me from fainting. To kill the imagery. Luckily I'm sitting down. Luckily I was expecting a shock. "The diarrhea was so bad, Joe, I spent an hour running back and forth soiling my nightgown before deciding to spend the whole night in there. I ended up taking a blanket because it was cold, and I took my jigsaw puzzle in with me to stop the boredom. I actually got the other corner done. It's looking good. You should come around and see it."
zh_text: 「很不舒服，喬。我一整晚都坐在馬桶上。我胃痛。我從來沒有那麼痛過。大便都是用噴的。」我環顧四周，尋找提供安全感的東西，讓我能夠保持清醒，不要昏過去的東西。能夠抹除那個畫面的東西。幸好我是坐著。幸好我本來就準備迎接震撼的消息。「拉肚子拉得太厲害了，喬，我在廁所和臥室間來來回回跑了一個小時，睡衣都弄髒了，最後才決定乾脆待在廁所。我拿了條毛毯裹著，因為很冷，然後我拿了拼圖遊戲進去打發時間。我把另外一個角落拼好了。看起來很棒。你該過來看看。」

en_text: "I didn't even need to push, Joe. It was just falling out of me like, well, like water out of a garden hose."
zh_text: 「我甚至不必用大腦，喬。怎麼拼怎麼順。

en_text: "I felt so sick." "I'm sorry, Mom, I'll come over one night soon and help, okay?"
zh_text: 「我好難過。」「抱歉，媽，我改天晚上去找妳，好嗎？」

en_text: "I'm sorry, Mom, I'll come over one night soon and help, okay?" "Okay, Joe, but—" "I've really got to go, Mom. Taxi's waiting. Love you."
zh_text: 「抱歉，媽，我改天晚上去找妳，好嗎？」「好，喬，但是……」「我真的要出門了，媽。計程車在等。愛妳。」

en_text: "Well, okay, Joe, I love—" "Bye, Mom." I hang up. I go to the sink. Gulp down a glass of water. Rinse out my mouth and pour a second glass thinking I need something stronger, then remembering the beers I transferred from the Walker fridge. I grab one and pop it open with the Walker bottle opener. Pictures of my mother sitting on the toilet with a thousand-piece jigsaw puzzle on a board on a stool in front of her and soiled underwear around her ankles are hard to shake. Cottage . . . blue sky . . . flowers . . . trees. I walk over to the sofa and sit down with my fish. I feed them, and a second later, the phone rings. What does she want now? To tell me how many sheets of toilet paper she used? I let the machine get it.
zh_text: 「呃，好吧，喬，我愛……」「再見，媽。」我掛斷。我走到水槽前。倒了一杯水。漱了個口。然後又倒了一杯。我媽坐在馬桶上，面前擺個放有一千片拼圖的板凳，腳踝附近的衣角沾滿大便的畫面實在太難擺脫了。農舍……藍天……鲜花……樹木。我走向沙發，坐在我的魚旁邊。我餵他們，片刻過後，電話響了。這下她又想幹嘛了？告訴我她用了多少張衛生紙？我讓答錄機接聽。

en_text: I finish the beer and say good-bye to my fish and am just heading out the door when I suddenly remember I have done nothing about Candy— haven't made the anonymous call I was supposed to make. I'll wait now until I narrow down my list. It will be easier to watch for Daniela's killer when there are only a few names left. Because the police have no leads, I have no time limit for solving my own case. I can take days or weeks. However, I have this competitive streak inside me. Right now it's ordering me around, telling me to keep focused and sort out this investigation. I want to prove to myself I can do this, and do it well. I want to prove I'm better than the police, not just at eluding them, but at solving their own case. What sort of man doesn't try to better himself? What sort of man doesn't test himself?
zh_text: 我跟魚說再見，走出家門，接著才突然想起我忘了處理坎蒂的事情——還沒撥打計劃中那通匿名線報。現在我打算等到進一步縮小嫌犯名單之後再說。只剩下幾名嫌犯比較容易觀察丹妮耶拉兇手的反應。由於警方沒有線索，我可以在沒有時間壓力的情況下調查此案。要花數天或數週的時間都無所謂。然而我天性愛好競爭。而此刻這股天性正在左右我的行爲，要求我集中精神，完成這個調查。我想要向自己證明我辦得到，而且能夠處理得很好。我想要證明我比警察還強，不光是能逃避法律制裁，還能偵破他們自己的案子。什麼樣的男人不會努力超越自己？什麼樣的男人不會測試自己？

en_text: Another part of me, the more recreational side, is suggesting why not make it harder for the police? Throw in another victim to investigate? When investigations deal with only one victim, the police can take statements from two or three hundred people, even a thousand. They crossreference these statements in an attempt to draw a map of the person's activities that day. Toss in another victim, and the number of statements doubles, and so does the workload. They spend less time with the people from the previous killing, and close to none with the people before that. One trail is fresh while the others get cold. Soon they stop focusing on the evidence, and wait for the next victim, hoping that will be where they catch a break in their case. They become increasingly understaffed and overworked. A stressed detective is a sloppy detective. Kill two people in a row, and all previous statements are tossed into a pile beneath a conference room table in a large box. I vacuum around them every couple of days or so.
zh_text: 另一部分的我，玩世不恭的我，建議何不增加警方辦案的難度？多丟一具屍體去給他們調查？當一件案子裡只有一名死者時，警方需要蒐集兩三百人的證詞、甚至可能超過千人。他們會相互參照這些證詞，試圖拼湊出案發當日死者的活動。多丟一名死者，證詞的數量就會加倍，工作量也一樣。他們不會花那麼多時間在前一件案子的證人身上，而再前一件案子的證人幾乎就會被遺忘。他們會跟緊一件案子，放棄其他案子。沒過多久他們就會忽略證據，等待下一名被害人出現，希望案情能夠有所突破。他們逐漸開始人手不足，工作過量。壓力大的警探就會變得懶散。連續殺害兩人，之前所有的證詞都會被丟到會議室桌下的一個大箱子裡。我每隔兩天就會在那個箱子旁邊吸塵。

en_text: I catch the bus into town. Getting into a police station is easy when you work there and have a swipe card to open one of the side doors. I do just that, and step into a rear stairwell. I know a record is taken each time an ID card is swiped, but there is no reason for the records to ever be checked. If they are, and I get asked, I'll simply say I got confused about the time, or that I came to get my lunchbox. I make my way to the fourth floor, taking the stairs. Less risky this way. I encounter nobody. Detectives, unlike beat patrol officers, work gentlemen's hours. Unless a homicide is reported, or one is in the process of being solved, the detectives work from nine o'clock until five thirty. After that they go home, and the cubicles, the conference room, and the offices are close to empty. I take another look at the conference room wall. The prostitute I killed last night is still to be discovered. Same with the woman I stuffed into the trunk at the long-term parking garage. Not wanting to hang around, I quickly swap the cassette tapes and leave. The microcassette recorder I use has a voice-activated system. This allows the unit to be left on standby mode, where it won't actually start recording until it hears sound. When the sound stops, it stops, so I can leave it on and there will be no wasted tape. I also replace the batteries.
zh_text: 我搭乘公車，進入市區。當你在警局工作並且擁有側門磁卡的時候，想要混進警局就很容易。我執行以上動作，進入後方的樓梯間。我知道每次刷身分磁卡都會留下紀錄，但是沒人會去檢查。如果有人檢查，跑來問我，我只要說我弄錯時間或是回來拿我的午餐盒就好了。我爬樓梯前往三樓。這樣風險比較低。我一個人也沒碰到。警探跟巡邏警員不同，可以正常上下班。除非有人回報兇殺案，或是有件案子快要偵破，警探都是從早上九點上到晚上五點半。五點半過後，他們就會回家，到時候辦公隔間、會議室、辦公室就會幾乎空無一人。我又去看看會議室的牆壁。還沒有人發現昨晚被我殺害的妓女。塞在長期停車場後車廂裡的女人也一樣。由於不想待在會議室裡，我迅速更換錄音帶，然後離開。我使用的微型錄音機具有聲音啓動功能。這讓機器處於一種待命模式，沒聽見聲音就不會錄音。聲音停止，它就停止，所以我可以一直開著，不必擔心浪費錄音帶的問題。我同時也更換了電池。

en_text: I take another look at the conference room wall. The prostitute I killed last night is still to be discovered. Same with the woman I stuffed into the trunk at the long-term parking garage. Not wanting to hang around, I quickly swap the cassette tapes and leave. The microcassette recorder I use has a voice-activated system. This allows the unit to be left on standby mode, where it won't actually start recording until it hears sound. When the sound stops, it stops, so I can leave it on and there will be no wasted tape. I also replace the batteries. Of the ten names on my list, only a few work on this floor. Some of the others don't even work in this building, but have come here from other cities to help with the investigation. The chances are high that it's going to be one of these men—taking the opportunity of killing while away from the wife and family is pretty hard to turn down.
zh_text: 我又去看看會議室的牆壁。還沒有人發現昨晚被我殺害的妓女。塞在長期停車場後車廂裡的女人也一樣。由於不想待在會議室裡，我迅速更換錄音帶，然後離開。我使用的微型錄音機具有聲音啓動功能。這讓機器處於一種待命模式，沒聽見聲音就不會錄音。聲音停止，它就停止，所以我可以一直開著，不必擔心浪費錄音帶的問題。我同時也更換了電池。我名單上的十個名字裡，只有幾個在這一層樓工作。有些人甚至不在這棟大樓裡工作，而是從其他城市調來協助偵辦此案的。真兇是那些人的機率很高——在遠離妻子與家人的時候趁機殺人可是很難抗拒的誘惑。

en_text: I decide to begin with the first name on my list.
zh_text: 我決定從名單中第一個人查起。

en_text: Detective Wilson Hutton has been a detective far, far longer than I've been cleaning, and he has been overeating far, far longer than he's been a detective. He, like the others, likes me. I move down the aisle, glancing at the cubicles to my left and right, double-checking that I'm alone. Most of the ceiling lights have been turned off. Only every fifth one is going, so it's pretty dim, like being outside under a quarter moon. This gives the place a slight look of life, while also saving power. It also enables staff to come here and not knock themselves out on furniture. I can hear the slight humming of the lights. The ticking of the air-conditioning. But I can't hear a single person. The floor has the feeling of an empty house. Like a tomb. No glowing desk lamps, no squeaking office chairs, no shifting of weight, or a cough, or a yawn. Things look tidier in this light. Cleaner. That's because an hour and a half after I leave, a team of cleaners comes in and spends two hours doing all the things they think I'm too stupid to manage. Nobody has ever mentioned it to me. Maybe they think I think a team of magic trash fairies comes in and makes things sparkly and clean.
zh_text: 威爾森·胡頓警探擔任警探的時間遠比我擔任清潔工的時間要長多了，而他暴飲暴食的時間又遠比他擔任警探的時間要長多了。他就像其他人一樣喜歡我。我走過走道，瞄向左右的辦公隔間，確認辦公室裡沒有其他人。大部分天花板上的燈都被關掉了。每隔五盞燈只開一盞，所以光線十分昏暗，感覺就像在弦月時分身處戶外一樣。這種燈光使這地方保有一點生氣，同時又能節約用電。它同時還能讓員工來此加班，偏偏又不會在椅子上睡著。我聽得見燈管發出的細微嗡嗡聲和空調的滴答聲。不過一點人聲都聽不見。這一整層都散發一股空屋的感覺。像是一座陵寢。沒有發亮的桌燈、沒有吱吱作響的辦公椅、沒有人在改變坐姿、咳嗽或打呵欠。在這種燈光下，一切看來井然有序。比較整潔。這是因為我下班一個半小時後，一組清潔人員會跑來花兩個小時去做那些他們認爲我蠢到不會做的工作。沒有人跟我提過此事。也許他們認爲我會以爲是一群魔法仙子跑來讓一切乾乾淨淨、閃閃發光。

en_text: I find Hutton's cubicle and sit down. He's a big guy, and the ass groove in his reinforced office chair reflects this as I try to get comfortable. At forty-eight years old, he's a candidate for a heart attack, and it wouldn't surprise me if he has already had several minor ones. The only exercise I've ever seen him do is chew junk food. I feel nauseous just sitting in his chair. I also feel like I'm putting on weight. I turn on his lamp. Staring at me is a name plaque sitting on his desk, probably a gift from his wife. It says Detective Inspector Wilson Q. Hutton. I don't know what the Q stands for. Probably queer. I look at the photographs of his family that he's pinned to the inside wall. His wife has similar weight issues, but her problems don't end there. The hair on her arms and legs, and the small splashes on her face, look like wool. The couple looks happy together. I cross his name off the list and flick off the lamp. Mr. Doughnut didn't do this. It isn't possible. He would have come close to dying just chasing the victim up those stairs, and I doubt his ability to gain an erection—something the killer repeatedly used. Though he must have used one at least twice: there are two overweight children in the photographs.
zh_text: 我找到胡頓的辦公隔間，在裡面坐了下來。他是個大胖子，強化辦公椅上的屁股印完全反映出這個事實。以一個四十八歲的男人來說，他絕對是心臟病的候選人，就算已經輕微發作過幾次也不會讓我驚訝。我唯一看他做過的運動就是咀嚼垃圾食物。光是坐在他的椅子上就讓我感到一陣作嘔。同時我也覺得自己變胖了。我打開他的桌燈。面前有塊名牌擺在桌上，或許是他老婆送的禮物。名牌上印著「威爾森·Q·胡頓督察。」我不知道這個Q代表什麼。或許是古怪（Queer）的意思。我看著他釘在隔板上的家庭照片。他老婆也有差不多的體重問題，不過她的問題不只如此。手腳上的毛還有臉上的斑點就像羊毛般濃密。這對夫妻看起來十分幸福。我劃掉他的名字，關上他的桌燈。甜甜圈先生不是兇手。不可能是他。他光是追被害人上樓多半就要心臟病發了，而且我也懷疑他有沒有能力勃起——兇手可是有反覆使用那個地方。儘管他肯定起碼用過兩次：照片裡還有兩個過重小孩。

en_text: Nine people left.
zh_text: 剩下九個人。

en_text: I push the chair back into the position it had been in, which isn't hard to find. The carpet is nearly worn through where the casters normally sit. So is the floor beneath it. I move into the opposite cubicle.
zh_text: 我將椅子推回原位，原位並不難找。輪子所在處的地毯幾乎都已經磨破了。其下的地板也樣。我走到對面的辦公隔間。

en_text: Detective Anthony Watts has been with the police department for twenty-five years, a detective for the last twelve. I'm considering him as my next suspect as I sit down and flick on his lamp. There's a photograph here. Watts and his wife sharing a happy moment together. Jesus, these people get happy and some prick has to take a picture as proof.
zh_text: 安東尼·華茲警探任職警局已經二十五年，晉升警探也已十二年。我將他視爲下一個嫌犯，坐下去打開他的桌燈。他桌上也有張照片。華茲和他太太共度美好時光。老天呀，這些人一高興就要照張相來以資證明。

en_text: Once again I begin to see things for what they are. Watts has that wrinkled look that comes with being sixty. He has gray hair, but not a lot of it left. I'm trying to imagine him having the strength to fight Daniela, let alone strangle her, but I can't do it. So I try to imagine him raping her in the way she'd been raped. Can't see him doing that either. Watts just doesn't have it in him. Daniela didn't have him in her. I cross him off the list. Turn off his lamp. Push his chair back into place.
zh_text: 再一次，我開始觀察小細節。華茲臉上布滿六十歲老人該有的皺紋。他一頭灰髮，不過也沒剩多少。我試圖想像他有力氣攻擊丹妮耶拉，並且將她勒斃，但是辦不到。跟著我又試圖想像他以她被法醫證實的攻擊方式強暴她——我也無法想像他能辦到。華茲根本沒有能力這麼做。丹妮耶拉沒有被他插入過。我刪掉他的名字。關上他的桌燈。將他的椅子推回原位。

en_text: The center aisle, once it reaches the end of this floor, branches into a T formation. I go left, directly to Detective Shane O'Connell's cubicle.
zh_text: 中央走道的盡頭是個T型路口。我轉而向左，直接前往蕭恩·歐康納警探的辦公隔間。

en_text: The next stop and two cubicles along for me is Detective Brian Travers. I slip in and flick on his desk lamp. No photographs of family here—all I'm seeing are swimsuit calendars. This year's, last year's, and the year's before that. I can well understand his hesitancy in throwing away the old calendars.
zh_text: 下一站是位於兩個辦公隔間外的布萊恩·崔佛斯警探。我溜進去，打開他的桌燈。沒有家庭照片——我只看到泳裝月曆。今年的、去年的，還有前年的。我看得出來他捨不得丟舊月曆的原因。

en_text: I open the desk drawers and rummage around. Look through files, folders, any scrap piece of paper, but there is nothing here relevant to the case. I find nothing to suggest his guilt. Or his innocence. I listen to his phone messages with the volume turned down low. I tip back the trash can under his desk, but it's empty. Travers is in his midthirties. He has a lean and strong body. Just under six feet, he has the type of casual good looks that easily attract women and could get him off on a rape charge with the He's so clean cut he could have any woman he wanted defense, which juries still fall for. He doesn't have a wife, and if he has a girlfriend, unless she's Miss January, he hasn't put up any pictures of her. I put a question mark next to his name.
zh_text: 我打開辦公桌抽屜，在裡面翻來翻去。翻閱檔案、文件夾、任何小紙張。我沒有找到他有涉案的證據。也沒有東西顯示他是無辜的。我調低音量，聽取他的電話錄音。我拉出他桌下的垃圾桶，空的。崔佛斯三十五歲左右。體格精壯。身高將近六呎，擁有一張俊俏的面孔，能夠輕易吸引女人，並且以「他英俊瀟灑到能夠追到任何想追的女人」那種說詞來洗脫強暴罪嫌——陪審團到現在還是很吃這一套。他沒有老婆，至於女朋友，除非她是一月小姐，不然他沒有擺出任何照片。我在他的名字旁邊畫了個問號。

en_text: Still seven suspects. I continue on my merry way and sit down behind the desk of Detective Lance McCoy. I start out with the same procedure I used in Travers's cubicle. McCoy is in his early forties, married, with two kids. The photograph telling me all this sits in a small frame on his desk, center stage. Other pictures hang on the walls of his cubicle. His wife looks ten years younger than him. His daughter is quite attractive, but his son looks like a moron. McCoy is a dedicated family man, I can tell just by sitting here in his extremely tidy cubicle. Small mottoes are pasted around the place, on coffee cups and notepads and plaques: Work to live not live to work, and Sloppiness leads to a path of depression. I look for but can't find one that says The only good bitch is a dead bitch, so I can't have him as my lead suspect. I can't find any notes that he's made on the case. I put a small question mark next to his name.
zh_text: 還是七名嫌犯。我繼續愉快的行程，坐在蘭斯·麥考伊警探的辦公桌後。我從崔佛斯辦公隔間裡那一套開始。麥考伊今年四十出頭，已婚，有兩個小孩。告訴我這一切的照片位於桌上的小相框中，最顯眼的地方。隔板上還掛了其他照片。他老婆看起來比他年輕十歲。他女兒相貌迷人，不過兒子看起來像個白痴。麥考伊是個將一生奉獻給家庭的男人，我光是坐在這個超級擁擠的辦公隔間裡就可以看出這一點。到處都是處世格言，咖啡杯上、筆記本上，還有白板上：「爲了生活工作，不要爲了工作生活。」以及「懶散會通往沮喪之路」。我找了一找，不過沒看到「唯一的好婊子就是死婊子」，所以我沒辦法把他列爲頭號嫌疑犯。我在他的名字旁邊畫了個小問號。

en_text: Seven suspects. Isn't this supposed to be getting easier? I check my watch. It's nine thirty-five, but my internal clock tells me it is only eight thirty, so something must be out of whack. When I enter Detective Bill Landry's office—yes, an office, not a cubicle—I confirm that my watch spoke the truth. Like Schroder and many of the other detectives, Landry is involved with trying to solve other crimes and finding other killers. A few months ago bodies were found in a lake in a cemetery, making me not the only serial killer in town—which, I have to say, is actually pretty annoying. It would have been great to have been the only one, just as it would have been great to have been the first. Before recently, the country had only ever seen one serial killer, and that was a guy who had a thing for killing prostitutes, and that was twenty years ago, a guy by the name of Jack Hunter who the media called "Jack the Hunter," a cute allusion to Jack the Ripper.
zh_text: 七名嫌犯。這種事不是應該越來越簡單嗎？我看看手錶。九點三十五分，不過我的生理時鐘宣稱現在才八點半，所以一定有什麼不對勁的地方。進入艾力克斯·漢森的辦公室時——沒錯，一間辦公室，不是辦公隔間——我確認手錶的時間沒錯。除了施羅德外，漢森也是本案的主導人員。兩年前他曾參與偵辦全國第一宗連續殺人魔案件。截至目前爲止，我已經注意到大部分的警探都用電腦，除了胡頓和華茲。胡頓太胖了。就算他有辦法拿鍵盤打出連貫的句子，按鍵中間的縫隙多半也會被他嘴角落下的食物碎屑給填滿。華茲純粹是因爲年紀太大。我翻找漢森的檔案，不過沒有什麼值得懷疑的。他認爲這些案子有兩個獨立犯案的兇手。

en_text: Of course being the optimist, I can also see the positive side of there being another serial killer on the loose. It keeps the police busy.
zh_text: 當然，他想得對。

en_text: Landry has been helpful by making a list of notes that point out how different the Walker scene is from the others. He wouldn't do that if he were the killer. In fact his notes have the word copycat at the top of the first page, with a ring around it and a question mark next to it. I cross Landry off my list. Then I head back up the center aisle and directly to Detective Superintendent Dominic Stevens's office. Fumble with the lock. Eight seconds. I close the blinds and use the small flashlight I've brought along with me. Sneaking around in Stevens's office is far more obvious than sneaking around the cubicles. There's a copy of a report he has written for his superiors on his desk. It explains in detail where the investigation is, which, in simple terms, is nowhere. It explains the running theories, while adding his theory that Daniela Walker was killed by somebody different. He recommends a separate investigation into her death. If Stevens is the killer, he sure as hell wouldn't do that. I cross him off the list. Five suspects left, and I'm starting to get the bad feeling I could end up crossing all of them off over the next few days, that I'm overlooking something.
zh_text: 我將漢森自名單中劃掉。他不太可能是兇手，在經歷兩年前那些事情之後不太可能，而且如果是他，他的筆記就應該認定只有一個兇手。我走回中央走道，直接前往多明尼克·史帝文斯偵緝督察長的辦公室。開鎖花了我八秒鐘。我關上百葉窗，打開我帶來的小手電筒。在史帝文斯辦公室裡偷偷摸摸遠比在辦公隔間裡偷偷摸摸要顯眼多了。他桌上有一份寫給上司看的報告副本。報告中鉅細靡遺地解釋調查進度，不過簡單來說，沒有進度。裡面寫了手下各種理論，同時也加入他自己的看法，就是丹妮耶拉·沃克是由另外一名兇手所殺。他建議將此案分開偵辦。如果史帝文斯是兇手，他肯定不會如此建議。我將他劃掉。

en_text: When eleven o'clock rolls around I decide it's time to go. I catch the bus toward home, but get off a half mile or so before my street hoping a walk in the fresh air will help clear my mind. It's a beautiful night. There's a nor'wester blowing like a cure for anybody feeling down. Same nor'wester that irritates everybody else. Weather's great like that.
zh_text: 五名嫌疑犯。將近十一點，該離開了。我搭乘公車回家，不過在距離我家一哩外的地方下車，因為我想要呼吸一點新鮮空氣。美麗的夜晚。西北風如同沮喪之人的解藥。同樣的西北風又讓其他人心生不快，這就是天氣厲害的地方。

en_text: But I'm not interested in making a forecast. Ahead of me are more long days and plenty of late nights, so I hit the sack the moment I get inside. I realize I didn't call Jennifer about the cat, but that can wait. Right now I'm just too busy falling asleep.
zh_text: 不過我不喜歡預知天氣。我面前有許多漫長的白晝與深夜在等待著我，於是我一回到家立刻上床，直接陷入沉睡。

en_text: At two minutes past eight I'm sitting on the edge of my bed covered in sweat. For the first time in years, I've dreamed. Though the sensation wasn't entirely unpleasant, the dream certainly was. I was a policeman, investigating myself for murder. Attempting to coerce a confession, I played good cop, bad cop. Yet I wouldn't give in. Instead I suggested and then mimed a rather lewd act to myself, which was followed by a demand for a lawyer. When a lawyer did arrive, it was Daniela Walker. She looked exactly as she had in her photograph. The bruises around her neck were like a string of black, deformed pearls. She never blinked, not once, her glazed-over eyes staring at me the entire time. Her only words were to tell me to confess to her murder. She repeated them over and over like a mantra. I was confused and confessed to a whole bunch of murders. Then the walls of the interrogation cell slid away as if I were in a game show, revealing a court of law. There was a judge and a jury and a lawyer. I recognized none of them. There was even a band. One of those old swingtime bands with guys dressed in suits. They were holding up freshly polished brass instruments but none of them were playing. Even with a guilty plea on offer, there was still a jury, and the jury found me guilty. So did the judge. The judge sentenced me to death. The band started playing the same song I'd heard on Angela's stereo, and as they played, the two businessmen I saw on the bus yesterday rolled in an electric chair. I woke just after the clamps of the electric chair locked my arms and legs into place.
zh_text: 八點二分，我滿身大汗地坐在我的床緣。幾年來第一次，我做夢了。儘管整體感覺不算全然不快，但夢境本身真的很糟。我在夢裡是名警察，爲了一件謀殺案而調查自己。爲了取得白白，我要了好警察壞警察那一套。不過我不肯屈服。我以言語及手勢辱罵我自己，然後要求律師到場。結果來的律師是丹妮耶拉·沃克。她看起來就跟照片裡一模一樣。頸部的瘀痕就像扭曲的黑珍珠項鍊。她沒有眨眼，一下都沒眨，呆滯的雙眼從頭到尾凝視著我。她唯一說的話就是叫我承認犯下她的謀殺案。她如同唸咒般一再重複這句話。我心煩意亂，坦承了一大堆謀殺案。接著偵訊室的牆壁向後滑開，如同遊戲節目般露出一座法庭。現場有一名法官、一群陪審團，還有一名律師；我一個也不認得。旁邊甚至還有一組樂團（團員都穿西裝的那種）。他們手持亮晶晶的銅管樂器，不過沒人在演奏樂曲。即使提出有罪抗辯，法庭還是找來陪審團，而陪審團判定我有罪。法官也是。法官判我死刑。樂團開始演奏我在安琪拉的音響裡聽見的那首歌，而演奏的同時，我昨天在公車上看到的兩個生意人推了一張電椅進來。我在電椅扣環固定我手腳時驚醒。

en_text: I can smell burning flesh even now as I sit on the edge of my bed. This is the first time my internal alarm clock has ever let me down. I close my eyes and try to push the big buttons inside to reset it. Why did I dream? How is it I've slept in? Because I'm trying to do something good? Could be. I'm trying to give Daniela Walker's family closure, and that doesn't feel right. I must suffer for my humanity.
zh_text: 即使此刻坐在床緣，我依然聞得到焦肉的味道。這是我的生理時鐘第一次讓我失望。我閉上雙眼，試圖按下腦中的重置大按鈕。我爲什麼會做夢？我爲什麼會睡過頭？因爲我想要做好事嗎？可能。我試圖爲丹妮耶拉·沃克的家人伸張正義，而這麼做感覺很不對勁。我必須爲了我的人性受苦。

en_text: I don't want to miss my bus, so I skip breakfast. Can't make myself lunch either, so I toss some fruit into my briefcase, then race out the door. I don't even have time to feed my fish. The day is overcast and muggy. Warm and lethargic. This is worse than a sun-shining-hot day. I'm already sweating by the time Mr. Stanley refuses to punch my ticket. I walk down the aisle and sit behind the same businessmen who were in my dream, making me suspect for a moment that I'm still in it, and I watch the walls of the bus to see if they give way to another court of law and another swing-time band. They don't. The businessmen are already talking loudly. Business this. Money that. I begin to imagine what they do in their spare time. If they're not sleeping with each other, they're probably married to women who are having affairs. I doubt they would have the courage to dump their bitches if they found out they were being cheated on. And I don't mean divorce.
zh_text: 我不想錯過公車，所以我跳過早餐。我也沒時間做午餐，只好丟點水果到公事包裡，然後奪門而出。我甚至沒時間餵我的魚。天氣陰暗悶熱，令人昏昏欲睡。這種天氣比出太陽的大熱天還要糟糕。當史丹利先生拒絕剪票的時候，我已經熱得滿頭大汗了。我走過走道，坐在夢裡那兩個生意人的後面。他們已經在高談闊論。左一句生意，右一句錢。我開始想像他們閒暇之餘做些什麼消遣。如果他們沒有睡在一起，大概就是娶了有外遇的老婆。我懷疑要是發現老婆外遇的話，他們有沒有膽子擺脫他們的婊子。我可不是指離婚。

en_text: Sally is waiting for me outside the police station. No shimmering heat today. Just wet heat, helped by the thick clouds above that are light gray over the city, but black out to sea. Still no signs of rain, though. Sally looks as though she's trying to figure something out, as if she knows me, but can't place exactly who I am. Then her face brightens and she reaches out and touches me on the shoulder. I don't feel the need to pull away. "How are you, Joe? Feeling up to another hard day at work?" "Sure. I like working here. I like the people."
zh_text: 莎莉在警局門口等我。今天沒有超級熱。只是普通熱而已。莎莉看起來一副在苦心思索的模樣，好像她認得我，但又想不起來我是誰。接著她展顏歡笑，伸手碰我肩膀。我沒有想要閃開的衝動。你好嗎，喬？準備好面對一天辛苦的工作了嗎？當然。我喜歡在這裡工作。我喜歡這裡

en_text: She seems about to say something, then closes her mouth and opens it again. She's fighting with something, and ends up losing the battle. Her arm falls back to her side. "I'm sorry, Joe, but I didn't get to make you lunch today." I'm not sure whether she makes the lunch, whether she buys it, or whether her mom makes it for her not knowing it's for me, but when my face sags a little at the news, it's genuine. "Oh. Okay, then," I say, not knowing what I'm going to do. No breakfast. No made lunch. Just some crappy fruit in my briefcase to last me all day. Why the hell did I think two days of her bringing me food was the start of a pattern?
zh_text: 她開口想要說話，跟著又閉了起來，然後再度開口。她在跟某種想法對抗，最後輸了。她的手臂垂回身側。「很抱歉，喬，今天我沒時間做你的午餐。」我不確定她是自己做的午餐、還是買的、還是她媽在不知情的情況下幫我做的，不過當我聽到後臉色一沉時，我是真的有點失望。「喔。那好吧。」我說，也不知道我該怎麼辦。沒早餐。沒做午餐。一整天就得靠公事包裡的爛水果過活。我怎麼會以爲她連續送了兩天午餐給我就表示以後每天都有得吃？

en_text: "It's my dad's birthday today."
zh_text: 「今天是我爸爸生日。」

en_text: "Happy birthday." She smiles. "I'll pass that along."
zh_text: 「生日快樂。」她微笑。「我會跟他說的。」

en_text: The air-conditioning is working in the foyer. One day it does, the next it won't. The old maintenance worker who used to work here must have died: I haven't seen him for a while. Sally used to work for him, doing things like grabbing rags and washing tools. The sort of thing that warms people's hearts, seeing the trolley-pushers of this world given a low-paying, shiteating job that gives them a place in society. "What did you do before you came to clean here, Joe?" she asks.
zh_text: 前廳的空調運作正常。它時好時壞。之前在這裡工作的維修工八成死了：我已經好一陣子沒看到他了。莎莉以前是幫他工作，拿拿抹布、洗洗工具什麼的。就是那種讓正常人在看到智能不足的人得到收入微薄卻能幫助他們融入社會的狗屁工作時能在心中浮現一絲溫暖的事情。你在來這裡打掃前是做什麼的，喬？

en_text: "Ate breakfast." "No, I mean a few years ago, before you started this job."
zh_text: 「吃早餐。」不，我是說幾年前，你開始這份工作前。

en_text: "Somebody like you?" "You know."
zh_text: 「你這種人？」「妳知道的。

en_text: "You know." "You're special, Joe. Remember that."
zh_text: 「妳知道的。「你很特別，喬。記住這一點。」

en_text: I remember that the whole way up to my floor in the elevator, and I keep remembering it as I say good-bye to the woman who didn't bring me any lunch today. Even when I ignore the conference room and go straight to my office I keep thinking about how special I really am. I have to be, right? That's why I'm down to five suspects and the rest of the department is throwing darts at a phone book. Five suspects. Travers, McCoy, and Schroder are the local three. Then there are the two that have come from out of town—Calhoun and Taylor.
zh_text: 在搭乘電梯前往我的樓層途中我都記得這一點，在跟這個沒有幫我帶午餐的女人道別的時候也還記得。就連當我略過會議室，直接前往我的辦公室時，我都一直在想自己究竟有多特別。我一定很特別，是吧？這就是我已經將嫌犯降到五人，而部門裡其他人都還在亂槍打鳥的原因。五名嫌犯。泰勒和卡爾霍恩警探，兩名外派來的傢伙，以及崔佛斯、麥考伊跟施羅德。

en_text: These two are going to be the harder ones to figure out. Calhoun has come from Auckland, and Taylor from Wellington. I'm still doubting Schroder is the guy after the speech from yesterday morning, but I can't be hasty. And I think I have a way to cross Travers off my list. But until then all five of them will have to remain suspects.
zh_text: 我認爲我想到了一個能夠排除崔佛斯的方法，不過首先我得深入了解他一點。卡爾霍恩和泰勒就比較麻煩了一個來自威靈頓，另一個來自奧克蘭。在昨天早上那番話後，我懷疑施羅德是兇手，不過不能妄下定論。這五個人暫時不能洗脫罪嫌。

en_text: The day drags on, the daily routine cometh. I spend it learning nothing I don't already know and not eating the sandwiches Sally didn't make. I clean and mop and vacuum. Live to work. Work to live. McCoy's coffee cup had it wrong. When four thirty comes around, rather than going home, I wait for Travers. He's out in the field interviewing witnesses and doing what he can to find a killer. He's due back around six o'clock, so rather than sitting outside the station, I head off to a nearby food court. I'm absolutely starving, since I've only eaten fruit today. I have Chinese. Flied lice. The guy who serves me is Asian, and must figure I am too, since he speaks to me in his language. I feel a little silly still wearing my overalls as I sit eating my chicken fried rice, the food court full of moms with strollers and school students eating the kind of food that will have many of them fifty pounds overweight by the time they hit their twenties.
zh_text: 時候不早了，我開始每天的例行公事。我沒有查到任何我不知道的事情。我掃地、拖地、吸地。生活是爲了工作。工作是爲了生活。麥考伊的咖啡杯上寫錯了。四點半的時候，我沒有回家，而是留下來等崔佛斯。他跑到外面去拜訪證人，盡其所能地找尋兇手。他預計六點左右回來，所以我沒有坐在警局外面等，而是跑到附近的速食攤位去。由於今天只有吃水果，我實在餓到了極點。我點了中國菜。炒飯。爲我服務的是個亞洲人，而他必定以爲我也是，因爲他用他的語言跟我交談。吃完飯後，我偷了一輛車。我本來想偷新款賓士，可惜你不能偷輛昂貴的歐洲車，然後停在警局外面等人。

en_text: When I'm done I head into the nearest parking building and I steal a car. I consider a late-model Mercedes, but you can't steal expensive European cars and sit around in them outside a police station. I go for a nondescript and hopefully reliable Honda that takes me less than a minute to break into and hotwire. I adjust the seat and open my briefcase and pull out a baseball cap and put it on. When exiting the building I hand over the ticket that was on the dashboard along with some loose change to the guy at the booth on the way out. He hardly notices me.
zh_text: 我偷了一輛毫不顯眼、希望夠可靠的本田汽車，花了不到一分鐘的時間開門發動。我是在立體停車場裡偷的，因爲附近沒什麼人。離開停車場時，我將停車票卡跟一些零錢交給收費亭裡的人。他看都沒有看我一眼。

en_text: It is six sixteen when Travers arrives back. It is another thirty-five minutes before he leaves. I follow him home thinking about the list, the all-important list. He lives in a nice neighborhood. The houses aren't rusting and the gardens are alive. Shiny homes with clean windows and nice cars parked up paved driveways. His house is a single-story place that's probably around thirty years old, aluminum windows, well looked after. I wait outside for an hour before he leaves again. He has changed into red jeans and a yellow polo shirt that looks like casualwear for Ronald McDonald. He tosses a sports bag into the passenger seat and pulls out onto the street. Over the last twenty minutes or so the last of the daylight has gone, and it's almost dark now.
zh_text: 崔佛斯於六點十六分回到警局，又過了三十五分鐘後才離開。我跟蹤他回家。居家環境不錯。房屋沒有生鏽，花園生氣勃勃。醒目的房子，乾淨的窗戶，車道上停的都是好車。他家是棟屋齡約莫三十年的平房，有著保養得很好的鋁窗。我在外面等了一個小時，然後他又出門了。他換上紅色牛仔褲和黃色馬球衫，看起來像是被拉入真實世界的卡通人物。他丟了一個運動包到乘客座上，然後駕車離開

en_text: I knew Travers was going out tonight—I'd heard the message on his answering machine. I follow him through a couple of suburbs until he finally arrives outside an attractive two-story house in Redwood, where the houses are shinier and the cars slightly more expensive. He parks in the driveway, drags out his sports bag, and locks the car. A guy, also in his midthirties, answers the door. When Travers is in, his friend—a fellow with dark brown hair and a small, trimmed mustache— scans the street, like he's looking for something or somebody. If it's me, he doesn't find it. Playing with the collar of his lime silk shirt, he turns and whisks the door closed behind him.
zh_text: 我知道他今天晚上要出門——我聽了他答錄機裡的留言。我跟著他在近郊穿街走巷，最後終於停在紅木區一棟兩層樓建築物前，附近的房屋更加醒目，車子也更昂貴一點。他停在車道上，拿出他的運動包，然後鎖上車門。一名同樣三十五歲左右的男子出來應門。崔佛斯進去時，他的朋友，留著深棕色的頭髮和整齊小鬍子的男人，掃視街道，彷彿他在找尋什麼東西或是某個人。如果是想找我，他沒找到。他一邊摸著萊姆色絲質襯衫的衣領，一邊轉身輕輕關上房門。

en_text: They're having dinner in tonight. I'll have to wait a few hours. I have brought Daniela's crossword magazine to fill the time and to keep my mind ticking over, using a nearby streetlight so I can see. Four down. An omniscient being. Three letters. Middle letter, O. Joe.
zh_text: 他們今晚在家共進晚餐。我得要等上幾個小時。我帶了丹妮耶拉的塡字遊戲來打發時間，維持敏銳的思緒。直排第四題：一種全知的存在。三個字母。中間是「O」。

en_text: Time dribbles. I look for, but can't find, any active life in this well-kept suburb, and I wonder where everybody is. Maybe they're all dead. I polish off a few crosswords before the lights finally come on upstairs in the house and the ones downstairs disappear. I wait another ten minutes until the upstairs lights twinkle off. A smaller and dimmer version replaces them. A bedside lamp is my guess. Travers is still inside. I open my briefcase. Take out the Glock. I stuff the gun into the pocket of my overalls. Ideally I would like to scale a nearby tree to see, unfortunately, what needs seeing. I've seen some pretty strange things in my time, but never this. I suck in a deep breath. Focus on the job at hand. I only have to see it.
zh_text: 時間緩緩過去，街燈亮了。我環顧四周，在這整潔的市郊住宅區內看不到任何活動的跡象，真不知道大家都去哪兒了。或許他們通通死了。我又塡了幾個字，二樓終於亮燈，一樓的燈火熄滅。我又等了十分鐘，直到二樓的燈也關掉，由一盞較爲黯淡的小燈取代。我猜是床頭燈。崔佛斯還在裡面。我打開公事包。拿出葛拉克手槍。我不想對任何人開槍，不過跟被抓比起來，開槍總是更好的選項。我將槍塞入工作服的口袋。理想的狀況是，我爬到附近的樹上去見證要看的景象。我曾經見過不少非常詭異的畫面。但是我從沒看過這種。我深吸一口氣。專注在眼前的工作。我只要看就夠了，我不需要有所行動。我開始開鎖。我的雙手在顫抖。花了十五秒鐘。

en_text: You don't need to do it. It's my mother's voice, coming from nowhere. Fumble with the lock. My hands are shaking. Fifteen seconds. The house is so neat it looks like a show home. I walk softly through the downstairs living area, pausing at the big-screen TV, wishing there was a way I could take it home. I'd like to take the lounge suite too, if I could fit the damn thing in my apartment. The large rug in the middle of the room ties everything together and would tie everything together back at my place too. Everything in here is colorful: the sofas are bright red, the carpet tan brown, the walls a sunburst orange. I realize I'm stalling for time. Gun pointing ahead, I make my way to the stairs and slowly start climbing. I keep my feet near the carpeted edges to minimize any sound and it works well. When I get to the top the grunting I hear means any sound I would have made would have gone unnoticed. I stand still and think of the list. Five names. A simple peek into the bedroom will make it four. The grunting gets louder.
zh_text: 屋內整齊到看起來像是樣品屋。我躡手躡腳穿越樓下的客廳，停在大螢幕電視前，希望我有辦法把它抱回家。我也想帶走那張沙發床，如果我能把那可惡的東西塞進我的公寓。客廳中央的大地毯將所有家具整合在一起。這裡的東西全都色彩鮮豔：亮紅色沙發，棕褐色地毯，牆壁是陽光灑落的橘色。我發現我在拖時間。槍口朝前，我走向樓梯，緩緩上樓。我將腳掌保持在地毯邊緣，盡量降低腳步聲。上樓之後，耳中聽到的喘息聲表示我不管發出什麼聲音都不會有人注意。我站在原地，想想那份名單。五個名字。只要偷看臥房一眼就可以變成四個。喘息聲越來越響亮。

en_text: Gun pointing ahead, I make my way to the stairs and slowly start climbing. I keep my feet near the carpeted edges to minimize any sound and it works well. When I get to the top the grunting I hear means any sound I would have made would have gone unnoticed. I stand still and think of the list. Five names. A simple peek into the bedroom will make it four. The grunting gets louder. The hallway branches into maybe four rooms up here, but it's the closest one I'm concerned with. I reach the master bedroom where the sounds are coming from. It sounds like somebody is having a pillow stuffed down their throat. The door is slightly ajar. Doesn't matter. If it had been closed I could have opened it undetected. If not, I still have my gun. I poke my head forward and try to see through the small gap. All I need to do is take a glimpse, and then I'm out of here. Downstairs and into the night, and my list will be smaller. But I can't see much. The bed isn't in sight. I lean further around until things come into view. Suddenly I feel sick. Nauseous. I pull away, nearly dropping to my knees.
zh_text: 槍口朝前，我走向樓梯，緩緩上樓。我將腳掌保持在地毯邊緣，盡量降低腳步聲。上樓之後，耳中聽到的喘息聲表示我不管發出什麼聲音都不會有人注意。我站在原地，想想那份名單。五個名字。只要偷看臥房一眼就可以變成四個。喘息聲越來越響亮。走廊分別通往或許四個房間，不過我只在乎最接近的那間。我來到發出喘息聲的主臥房外。聽起來像有人把枕頭塞在喉嚨裡一樣。房門微微開啓。無所謂，就算是關著的，我也可以神不知鬼不覺地打開它。萬一打不開，我手上還有槍。我伸長脖子，試圖從門縫中偷看。我只要偷看一眼，然後就可以離開了。下樓去，遁入夜色中，名單又變短了。但是我看不清楚。透過門縫看不到床。我脖子伸得更長，終於看清楚了。
