en_text: I suck in a deep breath and try to control the urge to vomit, but I'm not sure I can. My legs become jelly, and my mind is spinning. I saw what I expected to see, but I didn't count on feeling this way. My stomach is trying to escape up through my throat. I push a hand against it and lean against the wall. More deep breaths, then I hold it for half a minute. The urge to throw up on the carpet slowly fades. I'm down to four suspects, but it doesn't make me feel any better.
zh_text: 我突然感到一陣噁心、想吐。我縮回腦袋，差點癱倒在地。我深吸一口氣，試圖控制嘔吐的衝動，但是我不確定辦不辦得到。我雙腳痠軟，腦中天旋地轉。我看到期待中要看的畫面，卻沒想到會有這種反應。我的胃試圖跳出喉嚨。我伸手壓住嘴，身體靠在牆上。繼續深呼吸，接著我憋氣半分鐘，在地毯上嘔吐的慾望緩緩消失。剩下四名嫌犯，但是我卻沒有感覺好過一點。

en_text: I'm down to four suspects, but it doesn't make me feel any better. I hobble to the stairs and grab hold of the banister to keep myself from tumbling to the ground floor. I pause to think about what I've just seen. I think of my mother and how she keeps asking me if I'm gay. Is this why I feel sick? Because she thinks that what I just saw is the sort of thing I do?
zh_text: 剩下四名嫌犯，但是我卻沒有感覺好過一點。我蹒跚走向樓梯，緊緊握著欄杆，防止自己滾到一樓。我停頓片刻，想著剛剛看到的畫面。我想起我媽一直在問我是不是同性戀。這就是我如此噁心的原因嗎？因為她認爲我剛剛看到的畫面就是我會做的事情？

en_text: Something else is banging around in my thoughts too. Something I can't quite get a firm grip on. I can see the edges of it floating back there, but when I try to haul the damn thing in, I lose my grip on it and it falls completely away. Will it come back if I take another peek? No way in hell am I going to find out.
zh_text: 我腦中還有其他事情在煩。我不確定是什麼事情。我隱約看見它的蹤影，但是當我試圖伸手去抓的時候，那可惡的東西立刻消失，無影無蹤。如果多看一眼，它會自行回來嗎？我他媽的絕對不會去證實這一點。

en_text: I raise my hand to my mouth and bite my knuckle. I can hardly feel a damn thing. My hand tastes of sweat. I wonder if Dad ever thought I was gay. Should I go back and shoot these two men for making me feel this way? I look up at the ceiling and nearly lose balance. My knuckle is still in my mouth. What would Jesus do? It would be rather Christian of me to go in there and shoot them. Abnormal acts like that only mock Him.
zh_text: 我伸手放在嘴前，輕咬我的指節。我幾乎沒有什麼感覺。我的手上都是汗。我在想老爸是否曾以爲我是同性戀。我應該回去殺了那兩個讓我心生這種感覺的傢伙嗎？我抬頭望向天花板，差點失去平衡。我的指節依然咬在口中。耶穌會怎麼做？我體內基督徒的血液教唆我衝進去殺了他們。同性戀這種反常行爲根本就是在嘲弄上帝。

en_text: What would Dad want me to do? I have no idea why I even consider his outlook on this. So now I'm standing here with another dilemma. I'm sure God won't mind if I shoot them, but Dad will. In fact, God's probably urging me to. I'll be doing both Him and humanity a favor. But do I feel like doing God a favor? I try to think of one favor He's done me, but all He's ever done is take away my father and give me my mother. No, I owe Him nothing.
zh_text: 老爸會希望我怎麼做？我不知道我爲什麼會在意他對此事的看法，不過這又讓我面對了另外一個難題：我很肯定上帝不介意我殺了他們，但是老爸會。事實上，上帝或許會慫恿我去殺。我等於是幫祂和全人類一個大忙。但是我想幫上帝嗎？我試圖想出祂曾經幫過我什麼忙，但祂唯一做過的事情就是奪走我父親，把我媽丟給我。不，我什麼都不欠祂。

en_text: That's enough for the night. It's time to focus on the positives. It's time to be Optimistic Joe. When I call in Candy's body tomorrow there will only be four people to watch closely. It's getting late. If I don't get home soon, I might sleep in again tomorrow. I should have been out the damn door by now.
zh_text: 今晚這樣就夠了。明天打匿名電話報案發現坎蒂的屍體時，我只需要仔細觀察四個人的反應。天色已晚。如果不快點回家，明天可能又會睡過頭。我現在應該已經走出那扇可惡的門了。

en_text: Yet is it really their fault?
zh_text: 但這真的算是他們的錯嗎？

en_text: My God! How can I even question this? What sort of person am I becoming? I'm Joe. J is for Joe. J is for judge. I'm strong and I'm in control, and what I decide is my decision—not God's. Not Dad's. I don't care what either of them thinks.
zh_text: 天啊！我幹嘛質疑這一點？我到底變成什麼人了？我是喬。J就是喬（Joe）的意思。J就是法官（Judge）的意思。我力量強大，掌控大局，我決定的事情就是我的決定——不是上帝的。不是老爸的。我不在乎他們兩個怎麼想。

en_text: I make my way to the bedroom. Stop at the door. Point my gun directly ahead. But I'm not pulling the trigger. Instead I'm thinking about the technical side. The ballistics of the bullets will match against one of the victims I shot. The serial killer strikes again, and this will confuse them. It will blind them to any real motive. Why has the killer targeted a gay policeman? But how ideal is it if the other detectives become conscious that somebody is after them? How easily could I go through their houses if I needed to? Or their motel rooms?
zh_text: 我朝向臥房走去。停在門口。槍口直接向前方。但是我不打算扣下扳機。我開始思考技術層面的問題。彈道測試將會跟被我射殺的一名被害人吻合。連續殺人魔再度出擊，這將會對警方造成困擾。這樣會讓他們看不出任何真正的動機。殺人魔為什麼要殺害一名同性戀警察？不過讓其他警探意識到有人在追殺他們不是很完美嗎？知道我能在必要時輕易進入他們家中？或是他們的飯店房間？

en_text: I take a step back just as the grunting from the bedroom gets louder, as if I've given the sound waves more room to travel and amplify. The creaking bedsprings sound like they're screaming in fear. I push my hands against the sides of my head, but it isn't working. I jam the barrel of my Glock into my right ear, and stuff my middle finger into my left, but it doesn't help me think. The sound is still there. And the only way to get rid of it is to either shoot myself, or to shoot them. But I don't have to shoot them. I'm not an animal. I have the ability to think this out. I know right from wrong. I'm not insane. An insane person would jump in there and start firing because they wouldn't be able to control themselves. The interesting thing about insanity is that Insanity is strictly a legal term, not a medical one. Patients like me are not insane—we just plead it if we're caught. The reality is if we really were insane, we wouldn't be trying to evade conviction—we'd be caught at the scene smeared in blood and peanut butter and singing Barry Manilow tunes. I lower my gun. I could kill them just for the hell of it, just because I'm here. In life you take what comes along in this crazy mixed-up world. Other times you need to let it pass you by in case something better comes your way. Life is like a highway with many dirt roads veering off it.
zh_text: 我後退一步，不過喘息聲似乎越來越響亮。床墊彈簧的吱吱聲聽起來像在驚恐尖叫。我伸出雙手遮住雙耳，但是沒有用。我拿槍管抵住右耳，伸出中指抵住左耳，但是這樣無法幫我思考。喘息聲依然在耳。唯一能夠擺脫它們的方法就是槍殺我自己，或是槍殺他們。但是我沒必要槍殺他們。我不是野獸。我有能力釐清狀況。我能夠分辨對錯。瘋子就會跳進臥房，開始開槍，因為他們無法控制他們的行爲。瘋狂完全是個法律上的名詞，而非醫療上的名詞。心理有問題的病患，不管是殺人犯還是強暴犯，都沒發瘋，他們只是宣稱發瘋而已。真正的瘋子根本不知道他們在做什麼。他們不會試圖規避刑責。他們會在現場被人發現，全身塗滿鮮血，高唱巴瑞·曼尼洛的歌曲。只有正常人才有選擇的能力。我壓低槍口。我可以輕易出手殺死他們，只因為我人在這裡。在這個瘋狂混亂的世界裡，你有時要把握機會。其他時候你則必須放過良機，等待更好的事物到來。人生就是一條擁有許多泥濘岔路的高速公路。

en_text: I lower my gun. I could kill them just for the hell of it, just because I'm here. In life you take what comes along in this crazy mixed-up world. Other times you need to let it pass you by in case something better comes your way. Life is like a highway with many dirt roads veering off it. I'm at a junction right now, standing in the hallway of some guy I have never met. A memory in my mind that I can't reach. A headache coming on. Pounding. Sweat running down the sides of my body. Trickling. Grunting filling my ears. Pounding. Do I kill them? Throw a few of those red herrings into the investigation? Or does it only make things worse?
zh_text: 我壓低槍口。我可以輕易出手殺死他們，只因為我人在這裡。在這個瘋狂混亂的世界裡，你有時要把握機會。其他時候你則必須放過良機，等待更好的事物到來。人生就是一條擁有許多泥濘岔路的高速公路。此刻我站在某個陌生人家的走廊上，面臨人生的交叉點。腦中出現一道捉摸不定的回憶。我的頭隱隱作痛。越來越劇烈。汗水沿著身側滴落。細水長流。耳中充斥著喘息聲。頭痛欲裂。要殺他們嗎？這樣會在調查中投入一些轉移焦點的變數？還是讓情況變得更糟？

en_text: I'm at a junction right now, standing in the hallway of some guy I have never met. A memory in my mind that I can't reach. A headache coming on. Pounding. Sweat running down the sides of my body. Trickling. Grunting filling my ears. Pounding. Do I kill them? Throw a few of those red herrings into the investigation? Or does it only make things worse? I make my way downstairs. The kitchen is full of stainless-steel appliances that cost more than I make in a year. I sit at the breakfast bar on a bar stool and rest the Glock in front of me. Tagging Travers for gay was simple—it was the calendars. Overcompensation was the key word there.
zh_text: 此刻我站在某個陌生人家的走廊上，面臨人生的交叉點。腦中出現一道捉摸不定的回憶。我的頭隱隱作痛。越來越劇烈。汗水沿著身側滴落。細水長流。耳中充斥著喘息聲。頭痛欲裂。要殺他們嗎？這樣會在調查中投入一些轉移焦點的變數？還是讓情況變得更糟？我朝向樓下走去。廚房裡擺滿比我一年所得還要昂貴的不鏽鋼器具。我坐在早餐吧台旁的高腳椅上，將葛拉克手槍放在身前。

en_text: Knowing I'll think better on a stomach that isn't so empty, I open up the fridge and rummage around inside for some food. I end up making myself a corned beef sandwich—Travers's boyfriend is an excellent cook. I grab a can of Coke—it's on special after all—to wash it down. The fizz burns away any fantasy I hold that what I am listening to could be anything other than two men having the time of their lives.
zh_text: 看出崔佛斯是同性戀並不困難——看月曆就知道了。關鍵字是「過度補償」。由於我吃飽了思緒比較清楚，所以我打開冰箱，在裡面找點吃的。結果我做了一個鹹牛肉三明治——崔佛斯的男朋友是個頂尖的廚師。我拿了瓶可樂配著吃。氣泡的聲音澆熄了我對於樓上那種聲音可能不是兩個男人在享受生命中最美好時光的幻想。

en_text: Upstairs, the bed is slamming the bedroom wall, like it too wants to have bolted out the front door half an hour ago. I sit down at the bar and start tracing my finger along the edge of it, flicking some of the crumbs from the sandwich while doing my best to dismiss the thought that because I ate from the same food these people ate from that I'm gay now, but of course that's silly, it's silly, but the thought stays with me as I consider what to do next.
zh_text: 樓上，床頭撞擊著臥房牆壁，彷彿它也想在半個小時前就奪門而出。我在吧台旁坐下，手指沿著吧台邊緣緩緩移動。

en_text: The restaurant is full of conversation, nice smells, good people, decent music, and a warm atmosphere. The waitresses all have perfect hair and trim bodies, shown off by tight clothing. Everybody else has gone to a lot of effort to look casual—jeans, tidy T-shirts, smart shoes.
zh_text: 餐廳裡充滿交談聲、香氣、好人、悅耳的音樂，以及溫暖的氣氛。女服務生個個有著完美的髮型，身穿凸顯動人身材的緊身衣物。其他人全都費盡心思作出休閒的打扮——牛仔褲、整齊的T恤、時髦的鞋子。

en_text: Sally's father is working away at a chicken dish, her mother tackling a salad, while Sally pushes a fork back and forth in her tortellini. The day has gone well. For the first time in ages, her father, fifty-five now, looks close to his age rather than several years beyond it. The DVD player went down well; it was no problem for her to install it, and her father spent ten minutes playing with the remote, learning how to drive it. The buttons were difficult to push with his shuddery hands, yet his frustration stayed at a minimum. Whether that will still be the case in another year, or even another few weeks, is anybody's guess. She stabs a few pieces of pasta and puts them into her mouth. She loves pasta. She could live on it quite happily, yet tonight her appetite isn't allowing her to enjoy it. Her mother and father are laughing. She is happy for them, happy that for an hour or two they don't look so empty. When she finishes her meal, the friendly waitress who has been helping them all night comes over and sweeps away their plates, then just as quickly replaces them with dessert menus. She scans through the choices. She doesn't really feel like any of them, and looking at the waitresses, she doubts any of them have touched any type of dessert in their entire lives. She looks up at her dad and identifies the strain in his features as he tries to keep his body under control. He won't be able to hold on much longer, she thinks.
zh_text: 莎莉的父親點了一份烤雞、她母親在吃沙拉，她自己則拿叉子努力叉她的義大利餃。今天過得不錯。多年來第一次，她五十五歲的父親看起來符合他的年紀，而不是像老好幾歲的樣子。DVD播放器還不錯；安裝上沒有問題，她父親花了十分鐘學會如何使用遙控器。顫抖的手不太容易按按鈕，不過他還不至於無法操作。但是沒人知道這種情況可以再維持一年還是幾個禮拜就是了。她又了幾根管麵，塞到嘴裡。她喜歡義大利管麵。她可以開開心心地靠它過活，不過她今晚沒有什麼胃口。她父母在笑。她爲他們感到高興，至少有一兩個小時他們看起來不是那麼空虛。吃完晚餐後，爲他們服務一晚的友善女服務生走過來清理餐盤，然後迅速換上甜點菜單。她看了看選擇。她並不想吃任何菜單上的甜點，看著女服務生的身材，她很懷疑她們這輩子都不曾碰過這些甜點。她抬頭望向父親，發現他在努力克制身體的抖動。他撐不了多久了，她心想。

en_text: Sally is a few bites into a chocolate sundae when she starts to feel guilty about Joe. She hopes he wasn't relying on her for his lunch today. Of course what makes her feel really bad is what he said this morning. Somebody like me. She hadn't been aware till then that Joe knew people were treating him differently, and she was doing so too. Nobody else was making him lunch. Nobody else was pestering him to sit outside on the banks of the Avon River and throw stale bread at the ducks. Two things occur to her then. The first is there's a reason why Joe always has turned down her offer to have lunch together, or to be given a lift home. She has been treating him differently. The second thing is that this sundae isn't going to help her waistline. Anyway, it's starting to taste plain. Just chilled soggy cream. She pushes her spoon around it, making it even more runny. What she needs to do, she realizes, is to make an effort to get to know Joe while pretending she isn't making an effort. She smiles at her parents, glad they are having a good time. Her mother's metal crucifix is hanging outside her blouse, the light from the candles glinting off it. Through everything, her parents still have their faith. Again she thinks that she can use faith to bring herself closer to Joe.
zh_text: 吃了幾口巧克力聖代後，莎莉開始爲喬的事情感到罪惡。她希望他今天沒期待她準備午餐。當然真正讓她心情不好的地方在於今天早上他說的話。「像我這種人。」在那之前她都不知道喬知道人們會以不同的方式對待他，包括她自己在內。沒有其他人幫他做午餐，沒有其他人找他一起坐在河畔餵鴨子吃麵包。她食不知味。聖代在她口中只是一團冰涼潮濕的奶油。她拿湯匙沿著聖代外緣攪拌，把聖代攪得更稀。她發現自己必須在假裝沒有努力的情況下努力認識喬。她向父母微笑，很高興他們玩得盡興。她媽的金屬十字架掛在上衣外，於燭光照耀下閃閃發光。儘管經歷過大風大浪，她父母依然維持信仰。在這瞬間，她再一次認爲自己能夠藉由信仰去接近喬。

Today is day one to become a better person, a more caring person, a thinner person. She pushes her dessert aside and promises herself never to touch one again.

en_text: The bed is no longer banging. It could be broken. The mattress might have worn out. Maybe they've moved to the floor. Maybe they're spent. Thinking about it makes the corned beef sandwich threaten to come back up, and I'm threatening to let it. Problem is, it won't just be the sandwich. It'll be everything I've eaten for the week. I've made my decision. I'm going to let God down by allowing them to live. Hey, I don't owe Him any favors.
zh_text: 床已經不再撞牆了，或許是被撞壞，也可能是床墊磨光了。或許他們轉移陣地到地板。猜測此事讓我有股三明治試圖反胃而出的感覺，而我很想真的把它吐出來。問題在於，吐出來的不會只有三明治。我會把這個禮拜所吃的一切通通吐出來。我下定決心，打算令上帝失望，留下他們的小命嘿，我又不欠祂什麼。

en_text: I leave the empty can on the table and the leftover makings of my sandwich on the bench. I've never been that domesticated. I'm wearing gloves. When Travers finds the can in the morning, I wonder if he will have it tested for a link with the bottles found at Angela's house. It's a big parallel to draw—too big for a policeman, anyway. I don't bother locking the front door behind me. If somebody else happens to break in and kill them, then who am I to interfere with God? I start to laugh at the thought of their faces in the morning when they see they've had a visitor. Laughter is the best medicine for what I've just been through. What will they do? Report it? No. Travers wants his secret kept. I can't imagine him going to work tomorrow and telling everybody what happened. For a while he's going to live in fear. As will his buddy. And so they should—mocking the Bible and humanity with their actions. Mocking me with them.
zh_text: 我把空的可樂罐留在桌上，三明治剩下的材料留在料理台上。我向來不喜歡做家事。我有戴手套。明天一早崔佛斯發現可樂罐時，我不認爲他會拿去化驗，看看吻不吻合安琪拉家的可樂罐。這兩件事情有點風馬牛不相及——至少對個警察而言是這個樣子。我沒有費心鎖上前門。如果剛好有別人闖進去殺了他們，我有什麼資格去干預上帝的安排？我笑著想像明天早上他們發現夜裡有不速之客時的表情。在經歷過剛剛的天人交戰後，笑就是我最好的藥方。他們會怎麼做？報警？不。崔佛斯想要保守自己的秘密。我不認爲他明天去上班時會告訴其他人出了什麼事。他將會有一段時間生活在恐懼之中。他的夥伴也一樣。他們活該——誰叫他們要以行動嘲弄聖經和人類？

en_text: When I get inside, I see two messages waiting for me, both from my mother. I erase them without listening to them, wondering two things at the same time. First, why I love my mom so much, and second, why she can't be deleted just as easily.
zh_text: 回家後，答錄機中有兩通留言等待著我，兩通都是我媽留的。我刪除它們，同時思索著兩件事情。第一，我爲什麼這麼愛我媽；第二，她爲什麼不能像留言一樣輕鬆刪除？

en_text: I sit in front of Pickle and Jehovah and watch them as they swim in their endless cycle of memory loss. They see me, suspect I am about to feed them, so they race over. I haven't fed them all day, so I don't waste any time. I glance at my answering machine. Maybe Mom will call tomorrow. Ask me around for meatloaf. Show me her newest jigsaw puzzle. Give me some Coke. I look forward to it. I feel bad for not having listened to her messages. Before going to bed I dig out an old alarm clock from the bottom of my small closet. Set it to seven thirty-five. This way I give myself a chance to wake up at seven thirty. It's like a test. A test with a backup. I wish my fish good night before going to bed. I close my eyes and try not to think about my mother as I wait for sleep to come and take me away from the pain of what I've seen tonight.
zh_text: 我坐在泡菜和耶和華面前，看著他們在記憶喪失的迴圈中游動。他們看見我，以爲我要餵他們，連忙衝了過來。我一整天都沒餵他們吃東西，所以我也不浪費時間。我望向我的答錄機。或許媽明天還會打來。問我要不要吃烤肉餅。讓我看看她的新拼圖。給我喝點可樂。我期待她打來。上床之前，我從小衣櫥底下拿出一個舊鬧鐘。調到七點三十五分。這樣我還有機會可以在七點半醒來。就像是個測試。備用鬧鐘的測試。我跟我的魚道晚安，然後上床睡覺。我閉上雙眼，努力不去想我母親，同時等待睡眠到來，帶我遠離今晚所見的痛苦景象。

en_text: "Late night, Detective Schroder?" "We found another body."
zh_text: 昨天很晚睡嗎，施羅德警探？「我們又找到一具屍體。」

en_text: What? I start scanning the corkboard. "Was she dead, Detective Schroder?"
zh_text: 什麼？我立刻望向軟木板。「死了嗎，施羅德警探？」

en_text: Christchurch is overcast and gray. No sun. Lots of heat. Wet heat like yesterday. My sleeves are already rolled up. Schroder gives me a look as though I never cease to amaze him with my well of knowledge. I look back at him as if the characters from a Doctor Seuss story are dancing back and forth in my mind, singing songs and holding hands and doing what they can to keep me permanently entertained. "Yeah. She is, Joe."
zh_text: 基督城烏雲密布，天色陰暗。沒出太陽。非常熱。像昨天那種濕熱。我早已捲起衣袖。施羅德看我一眼，好像我的智力始終讓他驚奇不斷。我以一種蘇斯博士筆下的角色在我心中翩翩起舞、手拉著手、齊聲歡唱、盡其所能讓我永遠保持愉快的神情回頭看他。「是。她死了，喬。」

en_text: The photograph of Candy is one of those after shots that make people's passport pictures look good in comparison, especially in this case because it was taken after two days spent in an upstairs bedroom in sweltering heat. Decomposition has not been kind to her. The skin slippage around her hair and face is extensive. Her skin is blotchy purple. Another day or so, it would be blotchy black. Her eyes are milky. Her arm is crooked and bruised. The skin on her hands looks like wet gloves.
zh_text: 坎蒂的照片是張相形之下讓護照相片看起來很棒的死後照片，不過在這個案例中差別更大，因為這張照片是她在悶熱的一樓臥房裡待了兩天後所照的。她的屍體腐爛得很厲害。頭部和臉部出現大範圍的皮膚位移。皮膚呈現布滿屍斑的紫色。再過一兩天就會變成布滿屍斑的黑色。她雙眼混濁，手臂彎曲，有大片瘀青。手掌的皮膚看起來像是濕手套。在適當的環境下，人體可以於短短數天內腐爛成白骨。我是說非常極端的環境，而不是會下陣雨的陰天，偶爾還出一點太陽的天氣。如果附近有些飢餓的小動物也能加速腐爛的過程。

en_text: "Longer than that, Joe. We'll know exactly when later on this morning."
zh_text: 「更早，喬。晚點我們就會得知確實的死亡時間。」

en_text: The pathologist will figure out the day by examining the insect larvae growing around her battered face and torn vagina, and from the compound fracture in her broken arm, where the bone peeped through and said hello. "You know, Joe, you really shouldn't be seeing these sorts of pictures."
zh_text: 法醫可以藉由爛掉的臉和裂開陰道中的蟲卵以及手臂斷骨突出來打招呼的複雜性骨折來判斷死亡時間。「你知道，喬，你眞的不該看這種照片。」

en_text: "They're okay," I tell him. "I just pretend they're not real people."
zh_text: 「沒關係。我只要假裝上面的不是真人就好了。

en_text: "I guess that must be a luxury." "Coffee, Detective Schroder?"
zh_text: 我想那也是一種幸福。「咖啡，施羅德警探？」

en_text: "Not this morning, Joe. Thanks." I wander off to my office. I'm desperately curious about how the body was found, who found it, and who showed up at the scene. Detective Travers certainly hadn't. He was tied up. It was probably the husband, coming home to get his life back on track.
zh_text: 今天不用，喬。謝謝。我晃向我辦公室。我非常好奇怎麼會有人找到屍體，誰找到的，又是誰前往現場。崔佛斯警探肯定沒去。他有事要忙。

en_text: I wander off to my office. I'm desperately curious about how the body was found, who found it, and who showed up at the scene. Detective Travers certainly hadn't. He was tied up. It was probably the husband, coming home to get his life back on track. Wondered what the smell was coming from upstairs. Déjà vu. Whether you breathe through your nose or your mouth, or even if you don't breathe at all, the smell of decaying death will always get to you. It takes on a life in the same way fire does, looking for oxygen to burn to keep it alive, and, like fire, it has a hunger to be fed. A purpose for its survival. I wonder if the husband will ever walk up those stairs again.

en_text: Wondered what the smell was coming from upstairs. Déjà vu. Whether you breathe through your nose or your mouth, or even if you don't breathe at all, the smell of decaying death will always get to you. It takes on a life in the same way fire does, looking for oxygen to burn to keep it alive, and, like fire, it has a hunger to be fed. A purpose for its survival. I wonder if the husband will ever walk up those stairs again. I've heard of cases where old people have lived with their dead spouse for months because they didn't want to part with their loved one. They lay them down in bed or set them in front of the TV watching game shows with their favorite cushion in their lap. Hold conversations with them. Hold their hand, even though the skin is slipping from it in rotted abrasions. For a while after Dad died, I kept checking on Mom to make sure she was home alone—I thought she might break out the superglue to try and piece Dad's ashes together so she could nag the poor bastard to death one last time.
zh_text: 或許是死者丈夫，試圖回家讓人生步入常軌。不知道樓上傳來的是什麼味道。似曾相識。不管是用鼻子還是嘴巴呼吸，就算你根本不呼吸，腐爛的味道都會進入你的體內。那股味道就跟火焰一樣，會找尋氧氣來保持活力，同時也跟火焰一樣有著難以滿足的胃口，這是它生存的目的。Dr. Seuss，美國著名童書作者。我在想死者丈夫此後還敢不敢走上那幾階樓梯我聽說過有些老人會跟配偶的屍體共處數月，因為不願意與愛人分開。他們會讓配偶躺在床上，或是坐在電視前面看遊戲節目，膝蓋上放著他們最愛的座墊；跟他們交談，握著他們的手，儘管皮膚已經腐爛到會滑落手掌的地步。爸剛死的時候，我常常回去看看我媽是不是一個人在家——我以為她會拿強力膠把老爸的骨灰給黏起來，好讓她可以繼續糾纏那個可憐的混蛋。

en_text: I remember a story I once read in a newspaper. Some guy in Germany had died, and although his rotting body stank, none of the neighbors wanted to disturb him. He was there for a couple of months and wasn't found until the landlord wanted his rent. He'd been eaten by his flock of cats, and was mostly bone by that point. Guy probably got more pussy in death than he did in life.
zh_text: 我想起之前在報紙上看過的一篇報導。有個德國人死了，儘管屍體臭得不像話，他的鄰居卻都不願意去打擾他。他待在屋裡兩個月，直到房東要收房租的時候才發現屍體。他被自己養的貓吃掉，發現的時候幾乎只剩白骨。這傢伙死後或許比生前搞過更多貓咪。

en_text: I mop floors. Wipe windows. Get talked to like I'm a moron. Throughout the course of the morning, I eavesdrop enough to learn the footprints at the scene are identical to those at the other scenes. Residue from my gloves. Carpet fibers. Hair. Daniela Walker's husband had come home to get his electric shaver—my electric shaver now—and had found her.
zh_text: 我拖地、擦窗戶、讓人當成智障般招呼。一整個早上，我透過偷聽得知現場的腳印跟其他現場一樣。還有手套的殘餘物質、地毯纖維、頭髮都是。丹妮耶拉·沃克的丈夫回家拿電動刮鬍刀——現在是我的電動刮鬍刀了——結果找到了她。

en_text: Because of the several differences between Lisa the Hooker's death and Daniela the Battered Housewife's death, more detectives have changed over to the theory that they are hunting two killers and not one. Each victim has been killed differently (though I'm repetitious in my day job, I don't like to be with after-hours activities), but at each scene I'm leaving behind similar evidence, be it clothes, fibers, or saliva.
zh_text: 由於麗莎和丹妮耶拉的死法有許多出入，更多警探開始認爲此案共有兩名兇手涉案，而非一名。所有被害人死法不盡相同（雖然我白天的工作是在反覆做著同樣的事情，不過我不喜歡下班之後繼續這個樣子），不過我在每個兇案現場都留下了類似的證物，像是衣服、纖維，或是口水。

en_text: Two killers. It is the general assumption. Nobody who thinks otherwise has any theories as to why the killer returned to the scene with a hooker. Just before lunch I run into the local gay cop and say hello to him. He isn't in a talkative mood and dismisses me with a quick greeting. He looks distracted. He also looks tired.
zh_text: 兩名兇手。大部分警察都如此認爲。不這麼認爲的人都無法解釋爲什麼兇手要帶個妓女重返現場。午餐前，我遇上局裡的同性戀警察，跟他打招呼。他沒有心情說話，只是隨便跟我打聲招呼。他看起來心煩意亂。他看起來疲態畢露。

en_text: I'm left with four men to study. Lunch comes and goes without a visit from Sally, and more importantly, without any of her sandwiches. I make do with the food I have. After lunch, using the computer and personnel files in one of the records rooms upstairs, I reproduce department records for each of the remaining four men for later reading. I'm getting excited at how my list keeps narrowing itself down. What I can't figure out is why I have to eliminate all but one name until I find the killer. Why can't the next person I investigate be the man I want? Why must luck be against me? I decide to start with the two I don't know as well, the two out-of-towners.
zh_text: 我剩下四個有待觀察的嫌犯。午餐時間過去，莎莉沒來找我，更重要的是，她的三明治也沒出現。我只好吃點自己帶的東西。午餐過後，透過樓上某間紀錄室裡的電腦，我印出剩下四名嫌犯的部門紀錄，打算晚點來看。我對於名單越來越短感到十分興奮。我想不透的是爲什麼我必須消除到最後一個嫌犯才能得知兇手是誰。爲什麼兇手不能是我下一個調查的對象？爲什麼我的運氣這麼差？我決定著手調查我不認識的兩個人，那兩個外派過來的傢伙。

en_text: I'm in the records room running the vacuum over a toner-stained piece of carpet when Sally opens the door and steps in. She doesn't look surprised to find me here, which means she must have been keeping an eye on me. Maybe I ought to be keeping more of an eye on her. I turn off the vacuum cleaner. "How's your day going, Joe?" she asks, always asking me the same thing, as if one day I'm going to have an answer different from Fine or Okay.
zh_text: 正當我在紀錄室中拿吸塵器吸一塊撒了碳粉的地毯時，莎莉開門走了進來。她看來似乎並不驚訝會在這裡看到我，這表示她一定有在注意我；或許我也該多多注意她。我關掉吸塵器。「今天過得好嗎，喬？」她問，她總是問我一樣的問題，好像有一天我會回答「很好」或「不錯」以外的答案。

en_text: I decide to liven up her day and mix up the conversation. "It's going real good, Sally. Just like all the other yesterdays. I like my job."
zh_text: 我決定讓她開心一點，故意攪和這段交談。「今天過得超好，莎莉。就像所有昨天一樣。我喜歡我的工作。」

en_text: "I like my job too," she says, and then she lowers her voice even though there is nobody else here to overhear her, "but I must admit I find it a little boring. Don't you ever feel like you want to do something else?" She walks over to the photocopier and leans against it. The records I printed off are safely in my overalls, and the originals back where they belong. "I mean, don't you think there ought to be more to life?" "Like what?" I ask, genuinely curious. I can learn from this woman. If she has low-end goals in this world, I can say I have those same goals if it will help my act. This is what Method actors do.
zh_text: 「我也喜歡我的工作，不過我必須承認，我覺得工作有點無聊。你都不曾想做其他事情嗎？」她走到影印機旁，靠在機器上。我印出來的檔案已經放在工作服裡，原本的檔案則放回該放的地方。「我是說，你不覺得生活裡應該還有其他的東西嗎？」「像什麼？」我問，真的有點好奇。我可以在這個女人身上學到東西。如果連她的人生都有簡單的目標，那麼我也可以在對扮演這個角色有所幫助的時候宣稱我有同樣的目標。

en_text: "Anything. Everything," she says, and maybe it's the smell of the vacuum cleaner, or the window-cleaner fumes getting to me, but for the first time Sally sounds as though she's thinking outside the box, beyond her limitations.
zh_text: 「都可以。什麼都好。」她說，或許是因為吸塵器的味道，或是窗戶洗潔精的香氣，總之這是第一次莎莉讓我覺得她的想法有點創意，超越她的智力限制。

en_text: "I'm sorry," she says. "I'm not making any sense. Don't you have dreams, Joe? If you could be anything in the world, what would you want to be?" The answer is simple. "Joe."
zh_text: 「你沒有夢想嗎，喬？如果你可以變成任何人的話，你會想當什麼人？」「喬。」

en_text: "No, I mean a job. Any job in the world." "A cleaner."
zh_text: 「不，我是說工作。如果你能做世界上任何工作的話。」「清潔工。」

en_text: "Besides that?" "I'm not quer . . . qual . . . fied for anything else."
zh_text: 「除了清潔工呢？「我沒有……資……格做其他工作。」

en_text: "I'm not quer . . . qual . . . fied for anything else." "Do you like the idea of being a fireman? Or a policeman? Or an artist?"
zh_text: 「我沒有……資……格做其他工作。」「你會想當消防隊員嗎？還是警察？或是藝術家？」

en_text: She sighs, and for a moment I think about documentaries on TV where some retarded guy will marry his female equal. Surely these are the conversations they must have during foreplay before trying to make mentally disabled babies. I decide to put an end to it and help her out.
zh_text: 她嘆了口氣，一時之間我想起曾在電視上看過的紀錄片，裡面有個智障男人娶個智障女人的故事。我想這就是他們每天晚上吃過晚飯之後會聊天的內容。我決定結束這段對話，幫幫她的忙。

en_text: Her face beams at my answer. "Really?" "Yeah. Ever since I was a boy," I say, winging it now because even though it isn't my fantasy, it sounds like the kind of thing any man— regardless of IQ—would like to do. "I looked up at the moon and wanted to walk there. I know you can't live there, but I could at least fly there and make snow angels in the moon dirt."
zh_text: 「是啊。打從小時候開始。」我說，伸手擺出翅膀的模樣，因為儘管不是我的夢想，這依然聽起來像是任何男人——不管智商高低——會想做的事情。「我抬頭看到月亮，就想上去走走。我知道人不能住在上面，不過至少我可以飛到月亮上，在上面做個雪天使。」

en_text: "That sounds nice, Joe."
zh_text: 「聽起來不錯，喬。」

en_text: Her smile starts to waver. "You worry about what other people think about you?"
zh_text: 「你會擔心其他人怎麼看待你？」

en_text: "Retarded." "What?"
zh_text: 「智障。「什麼？」

en_text: "It doesn't matter," she says. "What about God?" "God?" I ask, as if I've never heard of the guy. "Do you think he's retarted?"
zh_text: 「沒什麼。那你如何看待上帝？」「上帝？」我問，彷彿我從來沒聽說過這傢伙一樣。「妳覺得祂是智障嗎？」

en_text: "Of course not. But do you ever worry about what He thinks?"
zh_text: 「當然不是。你有擔心過祂怎麼看待你嗎？」

en_text: "I always worry, because God is always watching," I say, and her face lights up again and I realize that if Sally doubled her IQ and halved her weight, she could be the kind of person I'd find myself following home.
zh_text: 「我一直擔心，因為上帝一直都在看。」我說，她聽後眼睛一亮，因為這就是她期待中的答案。

en_text: "You should." "I get confused," I say, looking down while I say it, as if I'm admitting something that makes me feel ashamed of being a God-loving, God-fearing Christian. "I wish I could, but I can never make it all the way through the . . ." The what? The lesson? The sermon? The boredom? I'm not sure of the answer. "You know. The three hours of sitting still and listening. Plus I find some of the things hard to understand. It seems to me that the Bible doesn't really make a whole lot of sense." Which I'm sure is true. I look back up and I smile away the ashamed look I had put on my face. The bigboy grin gives her smile a new lease on life.
zh_text: 「你該去的。」我很惶恐。」我說著低下頭去，彷彿在承認一件會讓一個熱愛上帝又敬畏上帝之人感到十分羞愧的事情。「我希望我能去，但是我絕對沒有辦法度過那一整段……」一整段什麼？上課？佈道？無聊？我不確定該怎麼接。「妳知道。原地坐上三個小時聽人講話。而且我覺得有些話眞的很難聽懂。」我抬起頭來，以微笑取代羞愧的神情。大男孩的笑容爲她的微笑增添一股活力。

The three hours of sitting still and listening. Plus I find some of the things hard to understand. It seems to me that the Bible doesn't really make a whole lot of sense." Which I'm sure is true. I look back up and I smile away the ashamed look I had put on my face. The bigboy grin gives her smile a new lease on life. "I go to church every Sunday," she says, reaching up and touching the crucifix.
zh_text: 我很惶恐。」我說著低下頭去，彷彿在承認一件會讓一個熱愛上帝又敬畏上帝之人感到十分羞愧的事情。「我希望我能去，但是我絕對沒有辦法度過那一整段……」一整段什麼？上課？佈道？無聊？我不確定該怎麼接。「妳知道。原地坐上三個小時聽人講話。而且我覺得有些話眞的很難聽懂。」我抬起頭來，以微笑取代羞愧的神情。大男孩的笑容爲她的微笑增添一股活力。「我每個禮拜天都會去教堂。」她說著伸手摸摸十字架。

en_text: "That's good." "You're welcome to come along. I promise it won't be boring."
zh_text: 「那很好。」歡迎你一起來。我保證不會無聊。

en_text: I have no idea how she can promise something like that unless the priest is planning on breaking at least half the commandments. "I'll think about it." "Do your parents go to church?"
zh_text: 我不知道她如何能夠保證這點，除非牧師打算違反十戒中至少一半的戒律。「我會考慮。」「你父母會上教堂嗎？」

en_text: "No." "It's good that you have faith, Joe."
zh_text: 「不會。」「你有信仰是件好事，喬。」

en_text: "It's good that you have faith, Joe." "The world needs faith," I say, and then Sally prattles on for five minutes, telling me things she has been able to learn from the Bible. I figure that to absorb all that Christian bullshit she must have forgotten other things along the way, which is why she's so incredibly dim.
zh_text: 「你有信仰是件好事，喬。」「世界需要信仰。」我說，接著莎莉嘰嘰喳喳地說了五分鐘，告訴我一堆她從聖經上學到的事情。我想她在吸收那一堆基督教狗屎的過程中必定遺忘了其他事情，像是如何減肥或如何交朋友之類的。

en_text: "The world needs faith," I say, and then Sally prattles on for five minutes, telling me things she has been able to learn from the Bible. I figure that to absorb all that Christian bullshit she must have forgotten other things along the way, which is why she's so incredibly dim. At the end of it all she asks me what I have planned for my weekend. I tell her I have lots of plans, like watching TV and sleeping. I'm worried she might suddenly suggest we do either one of those things together at her place.
zh_text: 「世界需要信仰。」我說，接著莎莉嘰嘰喳喳地說了五分鐘，告訴我一堆她從聖經上學到的事情。我想她在吸收那一堆基督教狗屎的過程中必定遺忘了其他事情，像是如何減肥或如何交朋友之類的。講到最後，她問我週末有什麼計畫。我說我有很多計畫，像是看電視和睡覺。我很擔心她會突然提議要我去她家一起做這兩件事情其中之一。

en_text: But she lets me off the hook. "Have I ever told you about my brother?" she asks.
zh_text: 不過她放我一馬。「我有跟你說過我弟弟的事情嗎？」

en_text: "No." "You remind me of him."
zh_text: 「沒有。」「你讓我想到他。」

en_text: Her brother must have been awesome, but I find it a little sick that she must have wanted to fuck him, too. "That's nice," I guess. "Anyway, I wanted to let you know that if you ever wanted help with anything, or wanted to just do something, like talk or have coffee or something, well, I'm always available."
zh_text: 「那樣很好，我猜。「總而言之，我想要你知道如果你需要任何幫忙的話，或是想做什麼事情，比方說聊天，還是喝咖啡之類的，真的，我隨時有空。」

en_text: I'm sure she is. "Thanks." She reaches into a pocket and pulls out a business card. Her phone number is written on it—she has that same cute, happy handwriting that normal women have. Seeing it there makes me realize she had this whole speech planned out. She hands it over. I turn the card over and see it's one of Detective Schroder's cards. There's also a coffee-colored ring stain on it —she's recycled the card rather than stealing a new one.
zh_text: 我相信她有空。「謝謝。」她伸手到口袋裡，拿出一張小紙條。上面寫了她的電話號碼；她的字跡就像正常女人一樣可愛。看到這張紙讓我了解到剛剛那段話都是早就安排好的。她將紙條遞給我。

en_text: "A phone call away," I say, giving her my big-boy grin and tucking the number into my pocket while the back of my neck breaks out in goose bumps.
zh_text: 「打個電話就好。」我說，露出大男孩的笑容，將紙條塞入口袋。

en_text: Four thirty rolls around. Time to stop working. It's also Friday, so time to stop thinking. Putting in too many extra hours will only stress me out. A stressed cleaner is a sloppy cleaner. Therefore, when I climb off the bus near home, I decide not to continue investigating into the weekend. A stressed detective is a sloppy detective. I will use this weekend to unwind. Try to enjoy myself. Spend some quality time with Joe. Perhaps watch my fish for a while. Perhaps visit Mom. Maybe read another romance novel. I walk up the stairs to my apartment, unlock the door, and push my way inside. A moment later I pull the folders from my briefcase. I'm telling myself not to open them up, not to start reading, but perhaps I'll have a quick browse. . . .
zh_text: 加太多班只會讓我壓力過大。壓力過大的清潔工就會變成懶散的清潔工。因此，在我家附近下公車時，我決定週末不要繼續查案。壓力過大的偵探就會變成懶散的偵探。我要利用這個週末來放鬆一下。試著找點樂子：或許欣賞欣賞我的魚、或許去看看老媽、或許再讀一本言情小說。我上樓回到公寓，打開門鎖，推門進去。片刻過後，我自公事包中取出檔案夾。我告訴自己不要打開它們，不要開始閱讀……但或許我可以迅速瀏覽一下……

en_text: No. Must. Not. Work.
zh_text: 不。絕對。不要。工作。

en_text: I sit down on the sofa. Put down the files. Feed Pickle and Jehovah. While they're eating, I check my answering machine. Mom hasn't called. Odd. I move back to the sofa and look at the files I don't want to read. This must be how some cops become dedicated to solving a crime. Unfortunately, you only let yourself down, not for working so hard, but for working so hard and getting nowhere. You can't stop working, because suddenly nothing else really matters anymore. You become obsessed.
zh_text: 我坐上沙發。放下檔案。餵泡菜和耶和華。趁他們吃東西的時候，我看了看答錄機。媽沒打來。怪了。我回到沙發上，看著我不想看的檔案。某些警察沉迷辦案時大概就是這個樣子。不幸的是，這樣只會讓自己失望，不是因為太努力工作，而是因為努力過後依然一無所獲。你沒有辦法停止工作，因為突然間生活中其他的事物通通變得無關緊要。你成爲問題的焦點。

en_text: I am at that point now. It's like a need, I guess, or a craving. I've opened this investigation. I'm experiencing the exact reason for so many divorces in the police department. Unless I put the folder down right now, I'm going to end up spending my entire weekend sitting on my bed and reading. Working. Stressing. But it is a challenge. . . . I walk over to the sink and splash cold water on my face. Do I want to be this dedicated? Who am I to spend my weekend solving a crime I've no real interest in?
zh_text: 此刻我就位於那個焦點上。那就像是一種需求，我猜，或是渴望。我已經展開調查了。我經歷了導致警局那麼多人離婚的原因。除非我現在就放下檔案夾，不然這整個週末都會坐在床上閱讀它們。工作。壓力。但這是一項挑戰……我走到水槽前，在臉上灑了點水。我想要這麼投入嗎？我有什麼理由把週末花在調查一件我又不是當眞感興趣的案子上？

en_text: Ah, and that's the problem. I am interested. Have been for the entire week. How can I not be? Is this a product of my lack of a life? Must I solve a murder to enjoy myself? And here's the killer blow—I actually am enjoying myself. Sure, all along I've been enjoying narrowing down my suspects, but I've also enjoyed everything about the entire investigation. I like the espionage—the way I feel like James Bond, sneaking into Mr. and Mr. Gay's house, darting into the cubicles and offices at the station. The long hours. The continuous mind drain. The logic and the reality. It's all been a buzz.
zh_text: 啊，這就是問題所在。我確實感興趣。一整個禮拜都很感興趣。我怎麼能不感興趣？這是因為我人生缺乏目標的關係嗎？我必須偵破兇案才能享受人生？最重要的是——我確實很享受這種感覺。當然，我始終很喜歡排除嫌犯名單的樂趣，不過整個辦案過程都讓我十分享受。我喜歡暗中辦案——讓我感覺像是詹姆斯·龐德，潛入同性戀先生的屋子裡，溜進警局裡的辦公隔間。長時間的工作。持續不斷的腦力激盪。邏輯與現實。實在太愉快了。

en_text: The problems are the late nights. The dreams. Not waking on time in the mornings. The disrupted routine. But I don't want my life to be a routine. After this, I might take on another case. The satisfaction of knowing I am better than anybody else at the police department satisfies my ego, but is that enough of a reason to keep doing this?
zh_text: 麻煩的地方在於深夜。做夢。早上無法準時起床。分崩離析的正常生活。不過我不希望日子過得一成不變。這件案子結束後，我或許還要再找件案子來查。知道我的辦案能力強過警局裡任何一個人能夠滿足我的自尊，不過我應該爲了這個理由而繼續查下去嗎？

en_text: I think it just might be. Sometimes killing is all about ego, especially for other people, but I remain comfortable with the knowledge that I'm not like other killers. I know what I do is wrong, but I won't attempt to justify it. I won't say God or Satan made me do it. I won't say they had it coming. Nor will I pretend an abusive childhood sent me spiraling onto this dirt road from the main highway of life. My childhood was normal, at least as normal as it could have been with my crazy mother. She never abused me, never neglected me—though it would have been easier growing up if she had. The abuse would have given me a reason to hate her. The neglect would have given me a reason to love her.
zh_text: 有時候殺人純粹是爲了滿足自尊，特別是對其他人而言，不過我向來自認跟其他殺人魔不同。我知道自己的所作所爲是錯的，但是我不會找理由來爲自己辯護。我不會說是上帝或撒旦強迫我殺人。我不會說他們罪有應得。我也不會假裝童年受虐導致我背離人生大道，轉向這條泥濘小徑。我有個正常的童年，至少在這個瘋子老媽的照顧下還算正常。她從不虐待我，從不忽視我——不過如果她有這麼做的話，或許我的成長過程會比較順遂。虐待能夠提供痛恨她的理由。忽視則能提供愛她的理由。

en_text: If I could point to my childhood and choose one thing that made me the man I am today, it would be the exact opposite of neglect. It would be the constant talking, the constant explaining, the always being there. So no deep-seated reason why I grew up to enjoy killing people, no inner turmoil or conflicts or resentment at the world or at my parents. Neither of them was an alcoholic. Neither of them molested me. I never burned down the school, never set fire to the dog. I was a normal kid. I turn away from the sink and look out my small window onto the city. It's still gray out there. I run some more water over my face, then towel myself down.
zh_text: 如果要我在童年經驗裡找出一個導致自己變成今天這個樣子的理由，我會說是因為她完全沒有忽視我。因為她隨時都在說話，隨時都在解釋，隨時都在我身邊。我這麼享受殺人的感覺並沒有什麼深層的理由，沒有內心騷亂與衝突或是怨恨這個世界或我父母。他們兩個都不是酒鬼。他們兩個都沒有性侵過我。我從未縱火焚燒學校，也沒有燒狗。我只是個正常小孩。我將目光自水槽移開，轉頭透過小窗戶望向城市的景觀。外面依然灰濛濛地。我又在臉上灑了點水，然後拿毛巾擦臉。

en_text: Just how dedicated do I want to be? Dedication is willpower. I squeeze my eyes shut. To work or not to work? That is the question.
zh_text: 我究竟打算投入到什麼地步？投入是一種意志力的表現。我緊閉雙眼。工作還是不工作？就是這個問題。

en_text: Dedication is willpower. I squeeze my eyes shut. To work or not to work? That is the question. The phone rings. It startles me and I look at it expecting to see it rattling on the hook. My first thought is Mom. Has something happened to her? I'm not sure what the statute of limitations on premonitions is, but the one I had yesterday morning must have expired by now. Mom's okay. Mom's always going to be okay. I snatch it up before the answering machine kicks in.
zh_text: 投入是一種意志力的表現。我緊閉雙眼。工作還是不工作？就是這個問題。電話響了。我嚇了一跳，轉過頭去，期待看到話筒在話機上跳動。我最先想到是我媽打來的。難道出了什麼事嗎？我不知道預感這種東西有沒有期限，不過昨天早上的不祥預感應該已經過期了才對。媽沒事。媽每次都沒事。我在答錄機接聽之前抓起電話。

en_text: "Joe? Is that you?" she asks before I even get the chance to say anything.
zh_text: 「喬？是你嗎？」她在我有機會開口之前問道。

en_text: "Mom?"
"Hello, Joe. This is your mother." "Mom . . . why . . . why are you ringing me?"
zh_text: 「哈囉，喬，我是你媽。」「媽……妳……妳爲什麼打給我？」

en_text: "What's this? Do I need an excuse to ring my only child who I thought loved me?" "I do love you, Mom."
zh_text: 「這是什麼意思？打電話給我以爲愛我的獨子還需要理由嗎？」「我是真的愛妳，媽。」

en_text: "You have an odd way of showing it," she says.
zh_text: 「你表现的方式很奇特。」

en_text: "You know I love you, Mom," I say, wanting to add that I wish that for once she could say something positive toward or about me, because if she could it'd make loving her a whole lot easier to do. "That's great, Joe." "Thanks." "You misunderstand," she says. "I'm being sarcastical."
zh_text: 「妳知道我愛妳，媽。」我說，很想補句我希望她偶爾也能對我說點正面的言語。「那很好，喬。」「你誤會了。我是在挖口你。」

en_text: "Sarcastic." "What, Joe?"
zh_text: 「挖苦。」「什麼，喬？」

en_text: "What did you say?" she asks.
zh_text: 「你說什麼？」

en_text: "It sounded like something."
zh_text: 「聽起來有什麼。」

en_text: "I think I have a bad line," I tell her. "What were you saying?" "I said I was being sarcastical. I'm saying that it's great that you now think I'm only imagining you love me. Are you saying I'm supposed to assume that you love your mother? I don't see how I can assume such a thing. You never visit me, and when I call, you complain! Sometimes I just don't know what to do. Your father would be ashamed to see how you treat me, Joe. Ashamed!"
zh_text: 我想電話訊號不好。妳剛剛說什麼？「我說我是在挖口你。你的意思是我應該假設你愛你媽嗎？我不知道要怎麼假設這種事情。你不來看我，我一打電話來，你就抱怨！有時候我真不知道該怎麼做。你爸看到你這樣對我，一定會羞愧到無地自容！無地自容！」

en_text: Part of me wants to cry. Another part wants to scream. I do neither. I sit down and let my head and chest sag down slightly. I wonder what life would be like if Mom had died instead of Dad. "I'm sorry," I say, knowing I can only apologize rather than try to correct her way of thinking. "I promise to be better, Mom. I really do."
zh_text: 部分的我很想哭。部分的我很想尖叫。這兩件事情我都沒做。我坐下來，腦袋和胸口微微下垂。我在想如果死的是我媽而不是我爸的話，我的人生會是什麼樣子。「我很抱歉。」我說，心知這種情況下只能道歉，不能妄想改變她的想法。「我保證會改進的，媽。真的。」

en_text: "Really? That's the Joe I know. The loving, caring son who I knew I could only have had. You truly can be an angel at times, Joe. You make me so proud."
zh_text: 真的？這才是我認識的喬。我一直都知道你是個關懷體貼的好兒子。你有時候眞是天使，喬。你眞令我驕傲。」

en_text: "Really?" I start to smile. "Thanks," I say, praying she isn't being sarcastical.
zh_text: 「真的？」我面露微笑。「謝謝。」我說，希望她不是在「挖口」

en_text: "I went to the doctor today," she says, changing the subject—or more accurately, getting around to the reason she actually called.
zh_text: 「我今天去看醫生。」她改變話題——正確來說，是終於進入打電話來的主題。

en_text: The doctor? Oh Jesus. "What's wrong?" "I must have been sleepwalking last night, Joe. I woke up this morning with my bedroom door open, and I was lying on the floor." "The floor? Oh my God. Are you okay?" "What do you think?"
zh_text: 醫生？喔天啊。「怎麼了？」「我昨晚一定是夢遊了，喬。我今早醒來的時候臥房門是開著的，而我躺在地板上。」「地板？喔天啊。妳沒事吧？」「你以爲呢？」

en_text: "What did the doctor say?" "He said I had an episode. Do you know what an episode is, Joe?" I feel closer to crying than screaming. I think about Fay, Edgar, Karen, and Stewart from Mom's favorite program. Yeah, I know what an episode is.
zh_text: 「醫生怎麼說？」我感覺比較想哭，而不是想叫。我想起媽的電視影集裡的菲、愛德嘉、凱倫和史都華。沒錯，我知道看一集影集是什麼意思。

en_text: "What kind of episode?" "Doctor Costello says it's nothing to be worried about. He has given me some tablets."
zh_text: 「什麼影集？」「卡斯迪洛醫生說沒什麼好擔心的。他開了些藥片給我。

en_text: "What sort of tablets?" "I'm not sure. I'll tell you more when you come over. I'll cook meatloaf. It's your favorite, Joe." "Are you sure you're okay?"
zh_text: 「什麼藥片？」「我不確定。詳情等你過來再告訴你。我會做烤肉餅。你最愛吃的烤肉餅，喬。」「妳確定妳沒事嗎？」

en_text: "Doctor Costello seems to think so. So what time will you be coming over?" Suddenly I'm not so sure there was an episode. In fact I'm almost positive Mom is making all of this up to make me feel guilty. "Do you have to go for more tests?"
zh_text: 「卡斯迪洛醫生似乎這麼認爲。那你幾點過來？」我突然覺得她或許根本沒有病發。事實上，我幾乎可以肯定這一切都是媽爲了激起我的罪惡感而捏造出來的。「妳得去做更多檢查嗎？」

en_text: "No. Around six? Six thirty?" "No tests? Why? What more are they going to do?"
zh_text: 「不用。六點左右如何？六點半？」「不用檢查？爲什麼？他們還有什麼進一步的療法？」

en_text: "I'll be better when you get here."
zh_text: 「你來我就好過多了。」

en_text: I suck in a deep breath. Here we go. "I can't come over, Mom. I'm kind of busy." "You're always busy, no time to spend with your mother. I'm all you have, you know. All you have since your father died. Where will you be when I'm gone?"
zh_text: 我深吸一口氣。來吧。「我不能過去，媽。我有點忙。」「你老是在忙，都沒時間陪你老媽。我是你僅有的一切，你知道。打從你爸死後就是你僅有的一切。我死了以後，你該怎麼辦？」

en_text: In paradise. "I'll come by on Monday, like normal." "I guess we'll find out on Monday." The line suddenly goes dead.
zh_text: 我會彷彿置身天堂。「我禮拜一過去，就像往常一樣。」這點要到禮拜一才知道。電話突然掛斷。

en_text: I stand back up and hang up the phone. Hearing it ring reminds me that I never called the vet back, but being reminded doesn't make me want to do it now. I walk over to my battered sofa. I sit down and throw my feet up onto the scarred coffee table. In the silence of my room I can hear the pump circulating the water around in the fishbowl. I wonder what kind of peace I could find if I was a goldfish with a memory that spanned only the last five seconds of my mother's conversation.
zh_text: 我站起身來，掛上電話。我走到老舊沙發前。我坐下，雙腳翹在破破爛爛的咖啡桌上。在寂靜的房間裡，我能聽見魚缸中幫浦循環水流的聲音。如果我是一條受困於剛剛最後五秒對話的記憶中的金魚，是能寧靜祥和到哪去。

en_text: I look over at the folders containing the printouts of the four men left on my suspect list. If I start looking through them, I'll at least stop thinking about my mother. Meatloaf on Monday. It's a prelude to having her nagging me for not living there, for not having a life, for not owning a BMW. Will reading the files put her out of my mind? I figure it's worth a shot.
zh_text: 我望向檔案夾。現在開始閱讀它們的話，至少我可以不去管我老媽。禮拜一要吃烤肉餅。那是她要唸我不住在家裡、不找個好工作、不買BMW的前奏。閱讀這些檔案可能讓她遠離我的腦海嗎？我覺得值得一試。

en_text: I pick them up and begin looking through them.
zh_text: 我拿起檔案，開始翻閱。

en_text: Detective Harvey Taylor. Forty-three years old. Married. Four kids. Been on the police force for eighteen years. Became a detective in the burglary squad at the age of twenty-eight. Promoted to homicide at the age of thirty-four. Has been assigned to some of the biggest homicide cases New Zealand has ever seen. He's a part of the team tracking the guy who left all the bodies in the cemetery lake—a guy the media are calling the Burial Killer. He's a part of the team trying to track me too.
zh_text: 哈維·泰勒警探。四十三歲。已婚。四名子女。加入警界十八年。二十八歲時在竊盜科晉升警探。三十四歲調升重案組。曾經偵辦過幾件紐西蘭史上最重大的兇殺案。也有參與兩年前紐西蘭第一宗連續殺人魔案。之後被調來偵辦這件案子。跟兩年前一樣，來自威靈頓的警探空降基督城。不同的地方在於，這件案子還在偵辦中。

en_text: I'm reading through Taylor's history, seeing he was a straight-A student at school. Several outstanding sporting achievements. High IQ. The type of guy I hated when I was at school. The type of guy I wanted to be.
zh_text: 根據泰勒的經歷，這傢伙在校的時候是個優良學生。在運動方面也有幾樣傑出的成就。智商極高。就是我在學校的時候很討厭的那種人。我想要成爲的那種人。

en_text: Listed in the folder are results from his school days. Results from the Royal New Zealand Police College. Results from psychological tests. I look through the questions for Have you ever strangled a woman to death after raping her? but it's not there. I figure he would have ticked No. Most of the questions are pretty lame. What is your favorite color? What is your favorite number? Would you steal if you were desperate? Have you ever smoked drugs? Ever killed a pet? Ever beaten anybody up at school? Ever been beaten up? Do you like setting fires?
zh_text: 檔案中還附上了求學時代的在校成績、皇家紐西蘭警察大學的在校成績、心理測試結果。我在心理測試中尋找類似「你可曾強暴女子後將其勒斃？」的問題，不過沒找到。我猜他應該會勾選「沒有」。大部分的心理測驗問題都很爛——你最喜歡的顏色為何？你最喜歡的數字為何？走投無路的時候會偷東西嗎？有沒有吸過毒？有沒有殺過寵物？在學校打過人嗎？被打過嗎？喜歡縱火嗎？

en_text: The yes-or-no questions take up five pages before the tests move on to questions that require written answers instead of ticks in boxes. What should we do with murderers? How did it feel being beaten up at school? What did you do about it? Why this and why that. Big fucking deal this and big fucking deal that. They're designed to make up a psychological profile. Something like "I was beaten up at school, but my favorite color is blue, which means I can't be gay. Right?" Yeah, right.
zh_text: 是非題佔了滿滿五頁，然後才出現直接填寫答案的問題：我們應該如何處置殺人犯？在學校遭人毆打是什麼感覺？你如何處理那種感覺？爲什麼這樣，爲什麼那樣？好像這樣很嚴重，那樣很了不起一樣。這些問題是用來建置心理概況的。像是「我在學校被人扁過，不過我最喜歡的顏色是藍色，這表示我不可能是同性戀。對不對？」是啊，沒錯。

en_text: I stop looking at the questions and go to the results. Taylor was basically rubber-stamped sane. No further explanation than that. The "insane" graduates become parking attendants. I continue reading through his record from officer to detective: the arrests he's made, the cases he's solved. The guy has put in several of his own hours into these cases. You don't get compensated for those hours, but you do gain some respect. They help you get promoted, so you can do even more work that you won't get compensated for. The report indicates the man is dedicated, to his work and to his family. I don't know what the balance is, but so far he still has both.
zh_text: 我跳過問題，直接去看結果。泰勒基本上是個蓋章定案的正常人。沒有任何進一步的註解，被歸類爲「不正常」的人就會淪落爲停車場督導員。我繼續閱讀他的檔案，從警員到警探：他的逮捕紀錄，破案紀錄。這傢伙花了不少私人時間偵辦這些案子。那些時間不會給付加班費，但是會讓你贏得他人的敬意。它們能幫助你晉升，好讓你花更多沒有加班費的私人時間去做更多工作。報告指出此人非常投入他的工作與家庭。我不知道他是如何調適的，不過截至目前爲止，他都還能同時保有工作與家庭。

en_text: This doesn't eliminate him as a suspect. For all I know he's missing his wife so much his imagination and right hand can't accommodate him any longer. Maybe he seeks sexual release with a stranger. I have no way of knowing. All I do know is that besides the burglary cases, which have such an extremely low solution rate it's appalling, Taylor has solved nearly every one of his investigations. That's why he's here. Not that his being here has helped either investigation. The photograph supplied with the file is probably ten years old, taken when he was in his early thirties. Even then Taylor looked ten years older than he was. Now, he looks twenty years older. These days his hair is ash gray with peaks at the corners of his forehead that threaten to see him bald within a few years. He doesn't have the black eyes of a killer. Instead his friendly blue eyes mask an intelligence I don't associate with many detectives. His face is lined with wrinkles from age and from the sun. His skin is weathered and tanned, and it's easy to imagine him on a surfboard in the middle of the ocean.
zh_text: 這些資料並不能排除他涉案的可能。在我看來，他可能想老婆想到性幻想加結繭的手掌也無法滿足自己的地步。或許他想找個陌生人來發洩發洩。我沒有辦法得知確實情況。我唯一知道的事實就是除了破案率極低的竊盜案外，泰勒幾乎偵破了每一件他所經手的案子。那就是他出現在這裡的原因。他是這個團隊中的核心人物。檔案中的照片可能是十年前拍的，照片上的他看來約莫三十出頭。即使在當時，泰勒看起來也像比實際年齡老上十歲的模樣。如今，他看起來像老上二十歲。現在的他滿頭灰髮，額頭髮線微微後退，要不了幾年就會變成禿頭。他沒有殺人犯的黑眼珠，反而有雙親切的藍眼，掩飾著一種鮮少在警探身上看到的智慧。他臉上佈滿年齡與日曬造成的皺紋。他的皮膚久經風霜，呈深褐色，讓人輕易聯想到他在海上衝浪的畫面。

en_text: The picture in the folder is in color and shows the sort of fashions we were all wearing back then. I can only hope no photographs exist of me anywhere wearing similar clothes. I put his folder down. Yawn. Stretch. And glance at my watch. It's already eight o'clock. Somehow I've already been home for nearly three hours. Where does the time go?
zh_text: 檔案照是彩色的，他身上穿的都是十年前流行的打扮。我希望世界上沒有任何我穿成那樣的照片。我放下這份檔案。打呵欠。伸懶腰。看了看手錶。已經八點了。我竟然已經回家三小時了。時間都跑到哪裡去了？

en_text: If only I knew. My internal alarm sure isn't telling me.
zh_text: 我要是知道就好了。我的生理時鐘肯定不會告訴我。

en_text: It's Friday night. Party night. Yet here I am, stuck inside my cramped home, my mind elsewhere and my eyes gliding over information that isn't helping. I knock back my coffee. I can't even remember making it, but it's still warm. Reading all this information must have put me into a fugue. I figure it'd put anybody into one. As I take off my overalls, I pull Sally's phone number from the pocket. I'm about to crunch it up into a tiny little ball when I decide to hang on to it. It's nice having somebody's phone number here other than my mother's and work. I use a magnet that looks like a miniature banana to stick it onto the front of the fridge. It makes me feel as though I have friends, and it isn't such a bad feeling. I take a break. I finally get around to ringing Jennifer at the vet's and I can tell that just hearing my voice has made her day. I ask about the cat. The cat is doing about as well as it can, but is still in bad condition. I ask about the cat's owners. She says there's been no joy there. I ask what they're going to do with the cat if he lives. She says it will go to a shelter. I don't ask what will happen at the shelter. I ask her to keep me updated, and she tells me she will. I head back to the couch to grab a towel hanging over the arm, but end up picking up another folder. I'm naked, my armpits smell like homeless people, yet I sit back on the couch and continue reading.
zh_text: 禮拜五晚上。狂歡的夜晚。結果我卻待在這裡，受困於我的小公寓中，心思飄往別處，盯著一堆毫無幫助的檔案看。我喝光咖啡。我都不記得是什麼時候煮的，不過還有餘溫就是了。閱讀這些檔案必定讓我進入一種神遊天外的狀態。我認爲這些檔案能讓任何人進入這種狀態。正當我脫下工作服，自口袋中取出莎莉的電話號碼，打算揉成一團的時候，我突然決定還是將電話號碼留下來。在家裡放張媽和工作之外的電話號碼感覺也不錯。我用小香蕉磁鐵把它吸在冰箱門上，它給我一種我有朋友的感覺，而這種感覺還不算差。我走回沙發去拿掛在椅臂上的毛巾，結果卻又拿起另外一份檔案。我一絲不掛，腋下聞起來像流浪漢，不過還是坐上沙發，繼續閱讀。

en_text: I head back to the couch to grab a towel hanging over the arm, but end up picking up another folder. I'm naked, my armpits smell like homeless people, yet I sit back on the couch and continue reading. Detective Inspector Robert Calhoun. Fifty-four years old. Married. The photograph was taken a year or so before his son visited the big suicide house in the sky. The report is all here. Timothy Calhoun. Little Timmy. I can't imagine having a cop as a parent. That's probably why he hanged himself in their garage. Or maybe his old man was playing doctor and nurse with him.
zh_text: 我走回沙發去拿掛在椅臂上的毛巾，結果卻又拿起另外一份檔案。我一絲不掛，腋下聞起來像流浪漢，不過還是坐上沙發，繼續閱讀。羅伯特·卡爾霍恩警探。四十四歲。已婚。照片是在他兒子掛掉一年前左右拍的——十四歲就在車庫裡上吊自殺，那是十年前的事了。發現屍體的是卡爾霍恩。這裡有完整的報告。提摩西·卡爾霍恩。小提米。我沒有辦法想像父親是警察的生活。或許這就是他自殺的原因。又或許是他老爸喜歡跟他玩醫生跟護士的遊戲。

en_text: Want to see a magic trick, little Timmy? Calhoun entered the police force at twenty-two and was on the beat ten years before becoming a detective. Originally from Dunedin, he was based in Wellington, spent a few years there, and was then transferred to Auckland. The police force is like that. They'll give you a job, train you up, then separate you from your family and friends by giving you a home anywhere in the country where you don't know anybody.
zh_text: 想要看魔術嗎，小提米？卡爾霍恩二十二歲時進入警界，辛苦十年之後終於成爲警探。他一開始在但尼丁，後來搬到威靈頓，在那裡服務數年，接著調往奧克蘭。警界就是這個樣子。他們會給你一個工作，訓練你，然後活生生地拆散你的家人和朋友，把你丟到國內某處完全陌生的地方。

en_text: Calhoun worked serious assaults, including rape, for twelve years. After that he was given the opportunity to work homicide. There are no dedicated homicide departments in this country. Not yet. When somebody gets killed, they pull experienced detectives from other areas—generally from sexual assaults, sometimes burglary—to investigate. So when these guys have been working homicide for five years or whatever, they're still first and foremost burglary or fraud cops until opportunity knocks. I figure working rape cases and other assaults for twelve years would surely give anybody a few ideas. It could easily be here that Calhoun learned a thing or two about what women really want. I look at his photograph. In the passing years, he has aged three years for every one that's passed. His black hair, full and in the shape of a Godfearing mullet, is gray now and receding. His face is long and he looks tired, his eyes and mouth surrounded by tiny wrinkles. No black eyes here either. Instead his are dark brown. They're sad looking, like the eyes of a lost puppy. He has a narrow jawline that's still the same, except for the gray stubble he always has now.
zh_text: 卡爾霍恩剛開始十二年都在重傷害科，處理的案件包括性侵害。那之後，上面把他調去偵辦兇殺案。這個國家沒有專辦兇殺案的部門。目前還沒有。有人被謀殺時，他們就會從其他領域，一般來說是性侵科，有時候是竊盜科，調派有經驗的警探來偵辦。所以當這些人偵辦兇殺案超過五年之後，他們依然算是竊盜科或詐欺科的警察，直到機會上門爲止。我想處理了十二年性侵與其他傷害案件肯定能在任何人心中燃起想做什麼事情的衝動。卡爾霍恩很可能是透過這些案件學會我所使用的犯案手法。我看著他的照片。過去幾年裡，他都像是一年當作三年在衰老。照片上的他黑髮濃密，剪成嚴肅的鯡魚頭，如今頭髮已經變灰，而且髮線後退。他的臉型很長，神情疲憊，雙眼和嘴角四周都是細紋。他的眼珠也不是黑色，而是深褐色的。狹窄的下巴倒是沒變，只不過現在隨時都有鬍碴。

en_text: What do we have? A dead son. A wife who probably hasn't touched her husband since then. Assaults. A man who sported a mullet. All these rape cases. The reason the tally of rape cases in this country is so high and only getting higher is that the justice system has never placed a big enough deterrent not to commit them. I study Calhoun's psychological profile. Nothing too different from Taylor's. I take a look at his college records. Not brilliant, but pretty good. Top twenty percent of his class, but that also makes him in the bottom eighty percent. He hasn't solved all his cases, but not many people do. There are a large number of unsolved sexual assaults that I'd like to believe Calhoun committed, but know he couldn't have—too risky. If a cop does something like that he needs to ensure that his victim can't identify him afterward, for which only one method is truly guaranteed.
zh_text: 這下是什麼情況？一個死掉的兒子。一個或許打從喪子之後就沒碰過老公的老婆。傷害案件。會剪鯡魚頭的男人。一大堆性侵案件。這個國家性侵案的犯罪率居高不下，而且還在持續攀升的原因就在於司法體系一直沒有做出能夠有效抑止人們犯案的判決。我研究卡爾霍恩的心理概況。跟泰勒的沒有多大不同。我看了看他的大學成績。不是天才，不過也很不錯。班上前百分之二十的學生。他沒有偵破所有經手的案件，不過沒有多少警察做得到這一點。他手頭上有一大堆未偵破的性侵案件，我很希望是卡爾霍恩幹的，但也知道不太可能——風險太高了。如果警察想幹這種事情，他就必須確保被害人不會在事後指證他，而只有一種作法能夠確保此事。

en_text: Time is flying. My head is spinning. I look down at my lap and see the reason for the blood loss to my brain. All this reading about sexual assault has perked me up. I stand up and grab the towel, but suddenly the idea of a cold shower isn't enough to get me through till tomorrow, not when the night has so much to offer. My body is wound tight and my mind even tighter, and as much fun as it's been being a detective, I deserve a reward for all that hard work—and what better reward is there than letting me be myself again? I skip the shower. Thoughts of seizing the night pull me away from the files. I get dressed. I have a closet full of nice clothes that belong to men who now have dead wives. I tuck my Glock into the waistband of my jeans and make sure my leather jacket will cover it. I slip one of my blades into the inside pocket.
zh_text: 時光飛逝。我頭昏眼花。我低頭看向膝蓋，發現腦部缺血的原因。閱讀這些關於性侵的報告令我興奮不已。我站起身來，拿起毛巾，纏在腰上，把「小喬伊」塞在毛巾下。黑夜可以提供許多消遣。浴室裡只有熱水與蒸汽，不過我出來之後依然煥然一新，宛如重生。我的身體緊繃，心理繃得更緊。我超時工作，又沒有獲得報酬。我需要放鬆，我需要發洩。當偵探很有趣，不過當回我自己更有趣。我將葛拉克手槍塞在牛仔褲腰帶上，確保我的皮夾克會遮住它。我把刀放在外套裡。

en_text: Dressed to kill. Essential items only.
zh_text: 做好殺人的打扮。只帶必要的工具。

en_text: Christchurch at night. My city. My playground. Where people who hate you will still call you "buddy." The air is warm, alive with activity, a light breeze coming from the northwest. Not too hot, but muggy. Full of sound as much as moisture. Full of fluorescent light as much as hormones. To the south of the city, on the Port Hills, a million lights twinkle in the distance. In the other directions, just flat landscape with buildings dotted across it. The town itself is full of neon lights—pinks, purples, reds, and greens. All possible colors dazzle the eyes from all possible angles. The red-light district of Christchurch straddles Manchester and Colombo streets, which run parallel through the heart of the city. On any of these corners you can buy a personal party for twenty, sixty, or a hundred bucks. Circling these streets are two types of people. The first are the boys in their teens and twenties, driving with no destination in mind except to be somewhere else, always on the move like a shark. Modified engines that make more noise than a jumbo jet. Mag wheels shiny and fat. Exhaust pipes wide enough to put your fist into. These are the boy-racers. I couldn't really say how they came into being, but they just did, one day thousands of teenagers driving expensive-looking Japanese imported cars, some of the cars have subwoofers installed in the backs with bass as loud as cannon fire, some cars have neon strips stuck along the base of them, some cars are painted so bright they could cause an onlooker to suffer a brain embolism, all of the cars are a burden on society. Windows in the nearby shops vibrate with the sound of them passing by. Some peel rubber at every set of lights as their tweaked motors lurch into action. Kids trying their hardest to be cool in an uncool world, they're winding down their busy week of cashing welfare checks by impressing everybody with their taste in music. At the other end of the spectrum is the second type of people. There are the guys who used to do the same thing ten years ago, only back then they'd only cruise up and down the same street. Now these guys are still driving the same cars; older bigger cars that don't get as much mileage. These are guys who wear tight black jeans and black T-shirts with holes in them and the names of heavy metal bands or whisky brands printed across them. They have long hair or shaved heads, nothing in between. Cigarettes or joints hang from their mouths. Their windows are tinted, the side ones wound down so we can all enjoy their presence. They think women who see them will instantly fall in love, and the crazy part is that some of them do. The sluts who wear the tie-dyed dresses and jars of face paint covering their skin—they wear their hearts on their arms along with colorful but cheap tattoos.
zh_text: 夜間的基督城。我的城市。我的遊樂場。討厭你的人會叫你「老兄」的地方。晚風十分溫暖，充滿活力。西北風。不會太熱，不過有點悶。人聲喧嘩，街道潮濕。到處充滿明亮的燈光和荷爾蒙。基督城南方，波特山上，一百萬盞燈於遠方閃爍。至於其他方向，就只是一望無際的土地，零星散布著些許建築。基督城本身充滿霓虹燈光——粉紅色、紫色、紅色和綠色。所有可能的色彩自所有可能的角度映入眼簾。基督城的紅燈區位於曼徹斯特街和可倫坡街上，兩條平行橫貫市中心的街道。你可以在這個區域裡每一個街角買到二十、六十，或一百元的個人伴遊。可倫坡街上，十幾二十歲的男孩漫無目的地駕車飛奔。熱騰騰的引擎發出的聲音比噴射機還要大。鋁鎂合金的車輪又大又亮。排氣管粗到能把拳頭給塞進去。安裝在車後座的重低音喇叭夾帶如同砲彈發射般的貝斯旋律推動車輛前進。附近商店的窗戶隨著這種聲音震動。每盞紅綠燈下都有福特Escort和福特Cortina在馬達的呼嘯聲中摩擦輪胎。沒有比賽可參加的年輕賽車手試圖藉由他們的音樂品味吸引眾人的目光，來放鬆一週的忙碌生活。身穿緊身黑牛仔褲和上面打洞還印有重金屬樂團或威士忌汗衫的人，他們留著長髮或光頭，沒有其他髮型。香菸和大麻叼在嘴裡。車窗都是有色玻璃，不過總會搖下側窗好讓旁人欣賞他們的英姿。他們以爲看見他們的女人會立刻愛上他們，而瘋狂之處在於真的有女人會這個樣子。濃妝豔抹、身穿連身裙的蕩婦——在衣袖上縫有愛心，在手臂上紋有廉價的彩色刺青。

The Oxford Terrace line of bars and cafés is known as The Strip. It's a meat market where skanky girls tease a few dozen men for every one they end up sleeping with. Seven or eight of these bars are packed tightly within this block, all of them with a riverside view. On the other side of the river and on a slight diagonal, a few hundred feet away from the closest bar, is the police station. On a Friday night the urine-water mix in the Avon is about fifty-fifty. Eels float along belly up. Ducks pick at used condoms left on the banks. Small fish flop from the water figuring they have a better chance in the air than they do breathing in the same stuff they're swimming in. Every ten meters or so somebody has passed out drunk. As I get closer to The Strip, I take the gun from my waistband and zip it inside my jacket pocket, then take off my jacket and carry it. The night isn't as hot as it'd been over the last week, but sweat still trickles down the sides of my body. I've applied enough aftershave and deodorant to hide any smell my body can come up with, though there's more than enough aftershave and perfume already hanging in the air. Walking down this street has me scented for free within seconds.

en_text: The Strip is the highlight of town for most locals. Already the drum 'n' bass, the techno, and the hip-hop deafen me. The only thing I know about hip-hop is that I hate it, and I figure that's all anybody knows about it. We may have evolved from something that crawled out of a swamp and continued to evolve as monkeys became men, but boy-racers and hip-hop music are proof we've hit our peak and are now heading backward. It could take at least thirty minutes to get inside any of these places, so I head deeper into the city, walking down Cashel Mall passing shoe shops and clothing stores in search of another club or bar. Perhaps one that's quieter. I find it eventually—a club with an open front where the music isn't quite so loud and a lot more bearable and there's room to sit. The crowd seems to be made up of people from their midtwenties through to their late thirties. Guess that makes me average.
zh_text: 條紋區對大部分的本地人而言是城內最熱鬧的地方。鼓和貝斯、電音，以及嘻哈音樂震耳欲聾。要進入任何一間俱樂部起碼都得排上三十分鐘，於是我深入城內，走向凱歇爾購物中心，尋找其他俱樂部或酒吧。或許找間比較安靜點的。最後我終於找到了——大門敞開的俱樂部，音樂沒有那麼大聲，而且裡面還有空的座位。顧客的年齡層介於二十五歲到四十歲之間，看來我的年齡適中。

en_text: I make my way inside, sidestepping the bouncer with a smile and without a comment from either of us. There's a sea of people to greet me, but not an ocean. I push my way through, keeping a tight grip on my jacket. At the bar I'm served by a delicious blonde—tight white top, short black skirt, great tits. I order myself a gin and tonic. Expensive, but you can't go into town on a Friday or Saturday night and not expect to spend a small fortune. I could have stayed at home and had the same drink for a quarter of the price, but there would be nobody to watch. I sit at the bar, nurse my drink, and watch the crowd around me. Mostly men wearing expensive clothing they can't afford, attempting to look richer and more impressive than they really are. Caretakers, laborers, plumbers, shop assistants—all dressed to look like lawyers. Whereas the lawyers are at other bars, dressed to look like casual guys. The women, even the fat chicks, dress to look like sluts. Not that I'm complaining. It's here where men flock to get a glance at potential bedtime stories to tell their friends on Monday morning. Women come here to be easy. To be free. From all corners of the club, lights flicker and dance and throb and pulse at my eyes. I finish my drink, order another. I look up at the roof and check for any surveillance cameras covering the bar. Nothing. The music is getting louder. My ears are humming.
zh_text: 我走了進去，橫跨一步，在一言不發的情況下笑著路過保鏢。裡面人山人海，不過還沒到一片汪洋的地步。我在人群中擠來擠去，一手緊握夾克。吧台有位美味可口的金髮女侍爲我服務——緊身白上衣、黑短裙、棒呆了的咪咪。我點了一杯橙味伏特加。很貴，不過想在禮拜五或禮拜六晚上進市區鬼混就得要有花錢的準備。我可以待在家裡，花四分之一的錢享受同樣的飲料，但是這樣就沒人可供欣賞了。我坐在吧台上，慢慢喝著酒，看著四周的人群。大部分的男人都穿著他們負擔不起的昂貴服飾，試圖裝扮出比他們本身有錢有勢的模樣。工友、勞工、水電工、店員——全都打扮成像是律師。真正的律師則都在其他酒吧裡，打扮成像是普通男子的模樣。這裡的女人，包括胖妞在內，全作蕩婦打扮。倒不是說我有什麼好抱怨的。男人就是在這種地方找尋可以在禮拜一早上跟同事炫耀的床邊故事。女人則是來這裡讓人釣的，免費。俱樂部中每個角落傳來的光線都在我的眼中閃爍、飛舞、衝擊、跳動。我喝完飲料，又點了一杯。我抬起頭來，觀察有沒有監視攝影機可以照到吧台。沒有。音樂越來越大聲。我的耳朵嗡嗡作響。

en_text: In a place like this, women only speak to you for one of three reasons: you're either extremely good-looking, you look extremely rich, or they're telling you to get lost and stop bothering them. Tonight I'm wearing expensive clothing. Money's no object when it comes to clothes, because a few of my victims have had husbands my size. I'm also wearing a rather expensive wristwatch—a Tag Heuer that cost victim number three's husband three thousand dollars. It has a sapphire crystal face that can't be scratched and a metal bracelet strap. Not as costly as a Rolex, but Rolexes don't retain a high market value; they're ugly, worn only by old men and Asians. It takes thirty minutes and three drinks for a woman to come up to me. Out of the overalls, I don't look like the simple guy the guys at the station think I am. Clothes make all the difference. She forces her way to the bar and stands next to me. She turns and smiles. Acknowledges my existence. A good start. She orders a drink. Just one.

en_text: "People can't know. People laugh at Joe. Laugh more if they find out." "I have to call the police." She reaches out and grabs hold of the phone. "No!" Joe screams, sitting up and grabbing hold of her hand again, his hand wrapping around her wrist with so much force she's worried he's going to break it. "They'll kill me!" Then, the pain of sitting up hits him, he flops down, his eyes roll back in his head, and he passes out. Sally stares at the phone. What are her obligations here? To help Joe, that's a certainty. Does she do what's best for her patient, or does she follow the patient's wishes? If she makes the call, what happens if Joe is right and people come back to hurt him? The police can only do so much. She puts the phone down. She has made up her mind. God has brought her here to help Joe, not to risk putting him in the path of more violence. She balls up the sheet and puts it on the floor, out of the way. Standing by the side of the bed, peering at the wound, she can't help but think she's invading Joe's privacy, but of course she's a nurse now, a professional. This is what she trained for. This is what she wanted to be.
zh_text: 「不能讓別人知道。別人會笑喬。知道了會笑更大聲。」「我必須報警。」她伸手握住電話。「不！」喬大叫，坐起身來，再度抓住她的手。「他們會殺了我！」用力起身引發了一陣疼痛，他躺回床上，兩眼一翻，昏了過去。莎莉很想打電話，不過有種感覺阻止她打。萬一喬說的是眞的呢？萬一他們跑來把他殺了呢？不，喬有她就夠了。上帝帶她來此是爲了幫助喬，不是讓他承受更多暴行。

en_text: Yes, but a professional would know when she was out of her depth. She would know when to call for an ambulance. That's exactly right. This isn't what she trained for. But a professional making that decision could get Joe killed, if what he said is true. At the very least she'll see what she can do to help him, then reassess the decision. She reaches up to bring the crucifix up to her chin. She holds it there for a few seconds before taking it off and wrapping the chain around Joe's hand so Jesus rests in his palm. Moving back she crouches down to look at the wound from another direction. Joe's penis is lying on an angle, upward across the base of his stomach and pointing at his shoulder. He's placed a piece of duct tape across it, to hold it away from the wound.
zh_text: 她拿起被單，放到旁邊的地板上。站在床邊，看著傷口，她不禁認爲自己是在侵犯喬的隱私，不過此刻她的身分當然是名護士：專業人士。這就是她在學校學的技能，她想要做的工作。沒錯，不過專業人士會知道自己的能力範圍。她會知道什麼時候該叫救護車。這種想法一點也沒錯。她沒有能力處理這種情況。她不知道該怎麼做。「不，妳知道。」她低聲道，伸手將十字架貼緊下巴。她維持這個姿勢幾秒，然後取下十字架，將項鍊纏在喬的手上，讓耶穌待在他的掌心。她彎下腰去，自其他角度打量傷口。喬的陽具躺在他的肚子下方，向上指著他的肩膀。一塊膠布將其固定在那裡，顯然是爲了不要讓它去碰到傷口。

en_text: That's exactly right. This isn't what she trained for. But a professional making that decision could get Joe killed, if what he said is true. At the very least she'll see what she can do to help him, then reassess the decision. She reaches up to bring the crucifix up to her chin. She holds it there for a few seconds before taking it off and wrapping the chain around Joe's hand so Jesus rests in his palm. Moving back she crouches down to look at the wound from another direction. Joe's penis is lying on an angle, upward across the base of his stomach and pointing at his shoulder. He's placed a piece of duct tape across it, to hold it away from the wound. "Poor Joe," she says, almost in tears. The way to continue is with the basics. She tells herself this over and over as she pulls on a pair of latex gloves, and as she does, she notices other pairs lying around the apartment. What does Joe use them for? Cleaning, most likely. She reaches over and pushes down on the side of Joe's thigh, trying to get a better look at the wound without touching it. His testicle has been squeezed, mashed, and destroyed by a tool. Her guess is a pair of pliers, or vise grips.
zh_text: 「不，妳知道。」她低聲道，伸手將十字架貼緊下巴。她維持這個姿勢幾秒，然後取下十字架，將項鍊纏在喬的手上，讓耶穌待在他的掌心。她彎下腰去，自其他角度打量傷口。喬的陽具躺在他的肚子下方，向上指著他的肩膀。一塊膠布將其固定在那裡，顯然是爲了不要讓它去碰到傷口。「可憐的喬。」她說，差點聲淚俱下。處理這種傷口得要從基本做起。她在戴上乳膠手套時一再如此告訴自己，同時她又發現公寓裡還有其他乳膠手套。喬拿這些手套做什麼？最大的可能是用來打掃環境。她伸出手去，壓壓喬的大腿，試圖在不觸碰傷口的情況下觀察傷口。他的睪丸被人拿工具壓扁、打爛、摧毀了。她猜是用鉗子，或是扳手。

en_text: "Mugged," Joe murmurs. His eyes are open again.
zh_text: 「打劫。」喬喃喃說道。他再度張眼。

en_text: "Who mugged you?" He doesn't answer. Just keeps looking straight ahead.
zh_text: 「什麼人幹的？」喬沒回答。只是一直看著前方。

en_text: He doesn't answer. Just keeps looking straight ahead. She continues to assess the wound. The testicle has to be removed. She wishes there were a way around that, but can't see one. There's no doubt it has to go, just as there's no doubt she lacks the qualifications—or even the confidence—to do the procedure.
zh_text: 喬沒回答。只是一直看著前方。她繼續評估傷口。睪丸必須割除。她希望有其他方法，但是看不出來。非割不可，毫無疑問，就像她沒有能力——也沒有自信——動手割除一樣。

en_text: "Can't. They'll come back. Hurt me. Please, can you make it better?" She smiles down at him. "Of course," she says.
zh_text: 不行。他們會回來找我。傷害我。拜託，妳能治好我嗎？「我試試看。」她違背本願說道。

en_text: She pulls out the handle of her scalpel and drops it in the boiling water. The blade is wrapped in foil, already sterile. She unfolds a plastic sheet and tries to roll Joe on his side and slip it beneath him, but he's too heavy. She does know how to move patients, but not a patient with a testicle that has been ripped into shreds. She rocks him slightly to the side and does the best she can. She leaves the tape over his penis. It's a crude job, but effective enough. She soaks a few small pads in iodine, then begins to wipe the area around the wound. The risk of infection is high, but this is the best she can do. "Are you sure you don't want to go to a hospital? Joe?"
zh_text: 她取出手術刀的刀柄，丟到開水裡。刀片已經消毒過了，包在鋁箔裡。她攤開一張塑膠床單，試圖將喬推成側躺，把床單塞到他身體下，可是他太重了。她知道該如何移動傷患，不過不是睪丸被打爛的傷患。她將他扶側一點，然後盡力塞入床單。她沒撕開陽具上的膠帶。那種作法很粗糙，不過固定得很好。她拿些小襯墊沾了碘酒，然後開始擦拭傷口附近。感染的風險很高，不過她也只能做到這樣了。「你確定不要上醫院嗎，喬？」

en_text: Joe is staring at her as if he wasn't expecting her to be here. His eyes move to the goldfish bowl on the table. She hadn't noticed it until now.
zh_text: 喬瞪視著她，彷彿沒想到她會在這裡一樣。他的目光移動到桌上的魚缸。她直到現在才注意到它。

en_text: "Please . . ." He points to the empty bottle of wine. She takes a closer look and realizes it's still about a third full. She reaches out and hands it to him. It will help, she thinks. She also pulls the belt out of his discarded and bloody jeans. The belt will help too.
zh_text: 「麻煩妳……」喬指向空酒瓶。她細看之下，發現裡面還有三分之一的酒。她將酒瓶遞給喬。喝酒會有幫助，她心想。她同時也抽出丟在旁邊的牛仔褲上的皮帶。皮帶也幫得上忙。

en_text: I dream of death and wish I was there. I dream of pain and this is where I live. My teeth bite down on the end of the wine bottle and I start swallowing what I can. I'm lucky I even own wine. I bought it six months ago when it was my mother's birthday. I thought we might celebrate. She accused me of trying to poison her, and I ended up bringing it back home. Normally the smell of wine is enough to make me gag. Now I cling to the feeling it's giving me, a feeling of hope that I might just slip away from all of this. I try to hold my tongue aside so I don't have to taste it, but it doesn't work. I feel like vomiting after a few seconds, but the more I get through, the less concerned I become about the taste, and the more I begin to enjoy the sensation it's giving me. I let my head rest against the pillow, and look at the person crouching in front of my crotch. The person is wearing a surgeon's mask, but I can tell it's a woman. I pray it isn't Melissa. I don't know why she's here. I can't remember calling for help, and I realize I must be hallucinating. Or just lucky. My face is growing numb, and my vision becomes slow. When I turn my head it takes my eyes a second to catch up. The pain starts to flare up again. I look around the room, but the surroundings are familiar, not like they ought to be if I were in a hospital. I try to bite down on the bottle, but find I am already biting down on something else. It's my belt. Not the sort of thing a doctor would use. My hands are shaking, and my entire body feels warm. I don't know how the doctor does it, but she moves so quickly that one moment she'll be holding something sharp in the air, and the next she'll be dabbing something on me. I blink once, she changes position; I blink again, she's somewhere else—I'm slipping in and out of consciousness. Mostly her words are disjointed, but she's trying to reassure me. I watch as she removes pieces of skin and flesh, then I can watch no more.
zh_text: 我夢見死亡，希望自己置身死後世界。我夢見痛苦，而那才是我所生存的地方。我的牙齒緊咬酒瓶瓶口，盡可能開始吞噬酒精。幸虧家裡有酒。那是六個月前我媽生日的時候買的。我想跟她慶祝慶祝。她指控我想毒死她，最後我就把酒帶回家了。正常情況下，光是聞到紅酒的味道我就受不了。如今我擁抱它所帶來的感覺，一種希望我能擺脫這一切的感覺。我試圖縮起舌頭，不去接觸酒味，但是這樣沒用。幾秒鐘後，我開始想吐，不過喝得越多，我就越不在乎酒味。我將腦袋靠在枕頭上，看著在我胯下旁的那個人。那個人戴著外科口罩，不過看得出來是個女人。我希望她不是梅莉莎。我不知道她為何來此。我不記得有打電話找人幫忙，接著我了解這一切都是幻覺。又可能是我運氣好。我的臉越來越麻，視線開始模糊。轉頭之時，我的眼睛要過一會兒才會跟著轉過來。我又開始痛了。我環顧四周，身處環境看來十分熟悉，如果在醫院裡的話應該不會這樣。我試圖緊咬酒瓶，不過卻發現我在咬其他東西。我伸手摸了摸，發現那是我的皮帶。這可不是醫生會用的道具。我的雙手在抖，全身都感到一陣暖意。我不知道醫生是怎麼辦到的，但是她的動作飛快，前一刻手裡還握著某樣尖銳的東西，下一刻她已經在擦拭我的身體。我眨了眨眼，她改變位置；我又眨眼，她又出現在別處——我在意識邊緣遊走。她的話聽來斷斷續續，但是我知道她在安慰我。我看著她割下皮膚和肉塊，接著我再也看不下去了。

en_text: My teeth bite down on the end of the wine bottle and I start swallowing what I can. I'm lucky I even own wine. I bought it six months ago when it was my mother's birthday. I thought we might celebrate. She accused me of trying to poison her, and I ended up bringing it back home. Normally the smell of wine is enough to make me gag. I try talking to my doctor, but I'm not really sure what I'm saying. Is this all a dream? Am I operating on myself?
zh_text: 我的牙齒緊咬酒瓶瓶口，盡可能開始吞噬酒精。幸虧家裡有酒。那是六個月前我媽生日的時候買的。我想跟她慶祝慶祝。她指控我想毒死她，最後我就把酒帶回家了。正常情況下，光是聞到紅酒的味道我就受不了。如今我擁抱它所帶來的感覺，一種希望我能擺脫這一切的感覺。我試圖縮起舌頭，不去接觸酒味，但是這樣沒用。幾秒鐘後，我開始想吐，不過喝得越多，我就越不在乎酒味。我將腦袋靠在枕頭上，看著在我胯下旁的那個人。那個人戴著外科口罩，不過看得出來是個女人。我希望她不是梅莉莎。我不知道她為何來此。我不記得有打電話找人幫忙，接著我了解這一切都是幻覺。又可能是我運氣好。我的臉越來越麻，視線開始模糊。轉頭之時，我的眼睛要過一會兒才會跟著轉過來。我又開始痛了。我環顧四周，身處環境看來十分熟悉，如果在醫院裡的話應該不會這樣。我試圖緊咬酒瓶，不過卻發現我在咬其他東西。我伸手摸了摸，發現那是我的皮帶。這可不是醫生會用的道具。我的雙手在抖，全身都感到一陣暖意。我不知道醫生是怎麼辦到的，但是她的動作飛快，前一刻手裡還握著某樣尖銳的東西，下一刻她已經在擦拭我的身體。我眨了眨眼，她改變位置；我又眨眼，她又出現在別處——我在意識邊緣遊走。她的話聽來斷斷續續，但是我知道她在安慰我。我看著她割下皮膚和肉塊，接著我再也看不下去了。我凝視著天花板。天花板中央有點下沉。我試圖跟醫生交談，不過不太確定我究竟在說些什麼。我是在做夢嗎？我是在給自己開刀嗎？

en_text: I don't know how much time passes, but when I look up again, the doctor is gone. I am all alone, just as my testicle is now all alone. I start to reach down my body, but then think better of it. I'm too scared to see what the damage could be. I close my eyes. Open them again. The doctor is in. I close them. The doctor is out.
zh_text: 我不知道過了多久，不過當我再度抬頭時，醫生已經不在了。我孤零零地，就像我的睪丸一樣孤零零。我開始伸手去摸下體，不過想想還是不要這麼做比較好。我不敢去看底下的慘狀。我閉上雙眼。再度睜開。醫生回來了。我閉上雙眼。醫生又消失了。

en_text: What is happening to me?
zh_text: 我到底怎麼了？

en_text: Am I dying?
zh_text: 我要死了嗎？

en_text: I stare at the ceiling and hope that I am.
zh_text: 我凝望天花板，希望我真的快要死了。

en_text: Sally sits on the couch and stares at the goldfish bowl. When she reaches out and sprinkles in some food, the two fish inside quickly head toward the surface and begin eating. The surgery, if she can call it that, has gone well. She suspects the chances of infection are slim. She has neatly removed the damage done by the pliers, and used dissolvable stitches internally and normal stitches externally. Of course only time will tell. Now that she's finished, she's hung the crucifix back around her neck.
zh_text: 莎莉坐在沙發上，看著金魚缸。當她伸手丟入一些飼料時，裡面的兩條魚立刻游到水面來大快朵頤。那場手術，如果可以稱爲手術的話，進行得不錯。她認爲感染的機率很低。她順利移除了鉗子造成的傷害，用可溶式縫線縫合內部，用正常縫線縫合外傷。當然會不會感染有待時間證明。如今完工了，她又將十字架掛回脖子上。她認爲手術過程中喬比較需要它。

en_text: She had figured Joe needed it more during that time. She's decided that as much as she wants to call the police, she won't do it. She wants Joe to be healed professionally, and she wants the people who did this to be caught and convicted, but she'll wait until she can discuss it with him. There isn't room out on the streets for people who can commit such an evil act. She thinks about the Christchurch Carver, about the hell he's been putting women through. It's true that the devil can walk among us.
zh_text: 她想打電話報警。她希望喬能有專業的醫療照顧，而且她希望犯案的人被逮捕定罪。世界上絕對容不下有能力做出這等邪惡之舉的人。她想到基督城屠夫，想到他讓女人經歷過的地獄。魔鬼真的會行走人間。

en_text: Joe's life is different enough, and she doesn't blame him for not wanting to be the mentally challenged man who was deprived of his money and his dignity. She respects Joe's right to not be known as the man who has lost a testicle. When he is capable, when he is fully aware, she will help him understand that the right path will be to involve others who can help him. She thinks about the scars on his chest. What sort of life has he had? Who abused him? Is this why he never speaks of his parents? Joe is unconscious, so she rolls him onto one side, then the other, maneuvering the bloody sheets from beneath him. She wraps the pieces of flesh she has cut away in the plastic sheet and places it in a plastic bag, then throws the bedsheets, jeans, underwear, and shirt into the washing machine and sets the cycle going. She finds a second plastic shopping bag and begins filling it with all the rubbish from the surgery. She wraps the scalpel blade securely to ensure it can never hurt anybody. She takes off her latex gloves and drops them in the bag too.
zh_text: 喬的人生與衆不同，她不怪他不想當個財富與尊嚴都遭受剝奪的心理障礙人士。她認爲喬有權利不讓其他人知道他失去了一顆睪丸。當他醒過來，完全恢復意識後，她會讓他了解接受其他人的幫助才是正確的作法。她想到他胸口的傷疤。他到底有著什麼樣的過去？是誰虐待他？這就是他不願提起父母的原因嗎？喬不省人事，於是莎莉將他翻向一側，然後又翻向另一側，抽出底下血淋淋的床單。她把剛剛割下來的皮肉包到塑膠床單裡，然後摺成塑膠袋，接著又將被單、牛仔褲、內衣和上衣丟到洗衣機，讓機器開始運作。她又找到一個塑膠購物袋，開始將所有手術時產生的垃圾塞到裡面。她謹慎包裹手術刀片，確保它不會割傷任何人，然後她脫掉乳膠手套，丟入塑膠袋中。

en_text: She puts on another pair, then starts tidying and cleaning the apartment. The dishes piled up in the sink haven't even been rinsed. The food stains on the countertop match the food stains on the table. When she finds a vacuum cleaner, she decides to run it briefly over the floors. None of the noises wake Joe. When the washing machine is finished, she bundles the items into the dryer and sets it going. The paperbacks on the couch are all romance novels. Martin never read anything like this; he only ever read comic books. She finds it odd at first, but encouraging that Joe would read something with more of a story. As she picks up the folders next to the books, the contents of one spill. "What are you doing, Joe?" she whispers to herself. She recognizes the photograph of one of the dead women. She scoops them up, flicks through them, then puts them back into the folder before moving on to the next. Joe has the complete set—the Christchurch Carver's victims. He also has information on the detectives investigating the case. She looks through them, trying to figure out why Joe would have these here. Does he know the women in these pictures are dead?

zh_text: 而來幫我療傷的也是梅莉莎。一定是她。「該死的女人。」我說著睜開雙眼，拉回毯子，靠回枕頭上。我需要休息，不過我不累。我需要想想梅莉莎以外的事情，就算只是分心片刻也好。我伸手到床頭桌上，拿起了那份檔案。

I used to wonder what they were doing at that exact moment. Were they thinking of me?
