Back then the fantasy was in getting away with it—not the killing, but the succeeding. Back then I always believed that I could commit the perfect crime. These days the fantasy has become reality. My testicle is gone and so is my sanity. The former will never come back. I'm holding out hope for the latter. My internal alarm wakes me at seven thirty on Monday morning. An entire week has passed. Just like that. I climb from bed and find myself walking better than I have all week. At the window I stare out my shitty view, which today is even shittier than normal. It looks cold outside.
zh_text: 我回到床上。我少了一顆睾丸，而當我試圖回想怎麼割掉的時候，一開始我想像梅莉莎戴口罩的模樣，然後換成莎莉。我不知道我把口罩放到哪裡去了，還是她們把口罩放到哪裡去了。光明與黑暗，昏迷與甦醒，意識到一切，然後忘記一切。我盡力跳過這種虛實不定的存在，沒有費心去計算時間，以免時間根本不曾流逝。其他時候我會站在泡菜和耶和華之前——甚至不記得我有起身走過去——看著他們游泳，好奇金魚的睪丸被割掉會怎麼樣。他會記得嗎？我的睪丸不見了，理智也跟著消失。前者永遠不會回來，我期待還能找回後者。我的生理時鐘在禮拜一早上七點半的時候叫我起床。一整個禮拜過去了。就這樣。我爬下床，發現自己走路比上個禮拜順暢多了。

en_text: I follow my normal weekday routine. I shower and shave, though it takes slightly longer. I make some toast. I feed my fish. My apartment doesn't smell as bad as I would have thought. The bucket I've been pissing into looks like I've only used it a few times. When I go to make lunch, I find most of the food in my apartment has gone off. Still, I feel like I've gone through the week from hell and come out in pretty good shape considering. The stairs are awkward and I struggle to walk down them, but I make it without any blood appearing on the front of my overalls. The temperature has dropped by half since the last time I was outside. Gray skies above and black clouds far in the distance, none of it looks like it's moving. I have to explain to Mr. Stanley why I haven't seen him for a week. Yeah, Mom's been sick. On the bumpy bus, what remains of my ball sac threatens to tear open. What I need is a man tampon. Or a time machine.
zh_text: 我展開正常的例行公事。沖了個澡，刮了個鬍子，不過花的時間比正常要長一點。我做了些吐司，餵了魚。我的公寓沒有想像中那麼臭。我拿來尿尿的水桶看起來才尿過幾次而已。去做午餐時，我發現公寓裡大部分的食物都不翼而飛。樓梯寸步難行，我努力下樓，在工作服上沒有滲出任何血液的情況下抵達一樓。我必須向史丹利先生解釋為什麼一個禮拜沒搭公車。是的，我媽病了。在顛簸的公車上，我僅存的陰囊差點裂開。我需要男用衛生棉條，或是時光機。

en_text: Mr. Stanley lets me off the bus. I hobble across the road and prepare to start another working week.
zh_text: 史丹利先生讓我下車。我搖搖晃晃地過了馬路，準備展開一天的工作。

en_text: "I heard you were back at work," Sally says, and her face seems to be torn between trying to look both happy and concerned. I am downstairs in the holding cells, throwing a mop back and forth, trying to wipe up all the vomit and piss the weekend drunks have sprayed all over the place. Out of all the things I do here, this has to be the worst. Every month contracted cleaners come in to really give the cells an overhaul, but it's amazing how painted cinder-block walls and cement floors can really soak up the smell, it smells like a zoo, if the zookeepers boxed the animals into smaller cages and never cleared away the shit. I've just spent ten minutes on one particular bad stain that I couldn't say what its ingredients were, and know it will take another ten minutes to finish the job.
zh_text: 「我聽說你回來上班了。」莎莉說，她的表情彷彿糾纏在快樂和憂心之間。我位於樓下的拘留室，前後用著拖把，試圖清理乾淨週末待在這裡的酒鬼所留下來的嘔吐物和排泄物。我在這裡做的諸多雜務裡，這肯定是最噁心的一件。每個月都有承包的清潔工跑來徹底清掃拘留室，不過我實在很難想像煤渣磚牆和水泥地板竟然這麼能夠吸收嘔吐與糞便的味道。

en_text: I take off the face mask that protects me from the God-awful smell. The cells, with their metal front doors and concrete construction, are damn cold to be in even in the middle of summer, and it's not summer anymore, and the frigid air at the moment is making my ball throb. "My mother's okay," I say, knowing she must have heard why I was gone.
zh_text: 我脫掉抵擋惡臭的面具。即使在炎熱的夏天裡，這些有著金屬前門和水泥牆壁的拘留室依然很冷，而此刻冰冷的空氣令我的睾丸不住抽痛。「我媽沒事了。」我說，心知她必定聽說我請假的理由。「什麼？」

en_text: "My mother's okay," I say, knowing she must have heard why I was gone. "Sorry?" "My mother. She was sick all week. That's why I wasn't here."

That's why you had to take the week off." "Yeah. That's what I said," I say, and something in the way she sounds is wrong, oh so wrong. "And she's better now?"
zh_text: 「喔，當然，我懂了。」她說，刻意放低音量，拖長「喔」和「我」兩個音，聽起來神秘兮兮的。好像我們在偷情一樣。「你媽病了。所以你才請假一個禮拜。」「是啊，我剛剛就是這麼說的。」我說，不過她的語氣聽來很不對勁，喔，太不對勁了。「她現在好點了？」

zh_text: 當然。」我說，拖長語音，緩緩點頭，試圖搞清楚怎麼回事。她知道出了什麼事嗎？難道這個智商七十的女人跑到我家來幫我動手術？

en_text: "And how are you, Joe? Are you better now too?"
zh_text: 「那你呢，喬？你好一點了嗎？」

en_text: "I'm coping. Time heals all wounds—that's what my mom says," I say, wondering if my mom had a ripped-off-testicle kind of wound in mind when she said it. "That's right. Look, Joe, remember that if you need anything, if you want me to help with . . . your mother . . . then just let me know."
zh_text: 「我還可以。時間可以治癒所有傷痕——我媽是這麼說的。「說得對。聽著，喬，記住如果你有什麼需要，如果你要我幫助……你媽……跟我說一聲就行了。」

en_text: "That's right. Look, Joe, remember that if you need anything, if you want me to help with . . . your mother . . . then just let me know." Of course the kind of help I really need with my mother isn't the type she would actually be able to offer. Still, if more people were like Sally, maybe the world would be a better place. The problem though is that she sounds like we're both in on the big secret, the one where Joe woke up one morning in a park after having his testicle flattened in a pair of pliers and had to make his own way home.
zh_text: 「說得對。聽著，喬，記住如果你有什麼需要，如果你要我幫助……你媽……跟我說一聲就行了。」當然我需要別人幫我對我媽做的事情絕對不是她所能提供的。儘管如此，如果莎莉這種人多一點的話，或許世界就會變得更好。問題在於她聽起來彷彿我們之間分享了一個大秘密，就是在睪丸被鉗子壓扁後於公園中醒來然後自己回家的秘密。

en_text: "Joe?" However, I can't imagine there ever being a secret both Sally and myself were in on. This is just Sally being Sally. Just trying to help me out with my mother the same way she helps me out by making me lunch. She's just trying to get on the inside track to getting me into bed. "Joe? Are you okay?" zh_text: 「算不上。」你有……去看那些檔案夾嗎？被害女子的照片？那類的東西？我看過會議室牆壁上的照片。就那些了。那些照片很可怕。

en_text: "If somebody forces you to steal because they're hurting you, then it isn't really stealing. And the best thing to do would be to go to the police." I don't know what leap she's just made, but it makes no sense at all. She's rehashing the sort of Christian morality bullshit that somebody has force-fed her. She's no idea what we're even talking about now. She could be saying that killing is bad, that vengeance belongs to God, that using his name in vain is bad, that selling your daughter into slavery isn't frowned upon. All these things are in the Bible and for some reason she thinks we're debating it. She could easily have just told me that drowning the elderly is bad.
zh_text: 「如果有人強迫你偷取那些檔案，那並不算是真的偷竊。最好的作法就是報警。我不知道她怎麼會講成這樣，但是聽起來一點道理也沒有。她在拿別人強行灌輸給她的基督教道德狗屎出來講。她根本不知道我們在講什麼。她可能想說殺人是不好的，復仇屬於上帝，濫用祂的名諱是不好的，將女兒賣給奴隸販子並不是罪。這些都寫在聖經裡，而基於某些理由，她認爲我們在辯論這個。

en_text: She seems to take that as some sort of answer to some half-formed dilemma going on inside her head, because she smiles, tells me she should get back to work, and leaves. Sally disappears, but my paranoia remains, my earlier thought that she could have come to my house is enough to make me nauseous. If Sally did come to my house, then I might have to repay the favor. There are things she might have seen, things I might have told her that would mean a visit to her house in the middle of the night would be in order.
zh_text: 我不知道能說什麼，於是聳了聳肩。她似乎將這個動作視爲腦中某種尚未成型的難題解答，因為她面露微笑，告訴我她該回去工作了，然後離開。莎莉走了，但是我還在疑神疑鬼，光是之前她有可能來過我家的想法就足以令我反胃。如果莎莉真的來過我家，那我或許應該禮尙往來。她可能看到一些東西，一些我或許告訴過她我會在深夜跑去她家造訪的東西。

en_text: I sit on the bunk in the cell I'm cleaning and lean my forehead against the broom handle. Over the following minutes, I slowly convince myself that I'm going crazy. No way could Sally have come around to my apartment. If she had, she wouldn't be able to shut up about it. She would be asking me how my testicle was. She would think that the very fact that she saw me naked meant we were engaged to be married. Sally is too dimwitted to have helped me, too innocent not to have called the police, too in love with me not to have stayed by my side every minute of the week I was laid up in bed. She's too many lots of things. And I can't imagine Sally getting hold of any antibiotics. No, it had to have been Melissa. Which means she is still up to something. Before lunch I spend twenty minutes in the conference room studying the information and swapping my tapes while I clean the windows and wipe down the blinds. I'm reading statements, studying photographs, making sure nobody is watching me. The sky outside the conference room window is getting darker, and as it does it feels like it's getting closer, like the world is closing in on me.
zh_text: 我於正在打掃的拘留室床鋪上坐下，額頭靠著掃帚柄。接下來的幾分鐘內，我慢慢說服自己這種想法太瘋狂了。莎莉絕不可能跑來我家。如果她來過，她不可能不提。她會問我睪丸怎麼樣。她會將看過我的裸體視爲訂婚的象徵。莎莉的智力不足以幫助我，她的天真也一定會讓她打電話報警，而對我的愛則會令她一整個禮拜都待在我的床邊。而且我也無法想像莎莉有辦法取得抗生素。不，一定是梅莉莎。這表示她依然有所圖謀。午餐前，我在會議室裡待了二十分鐘，趁著清理窗戶、擦百葉窗葉的時候研究案情、更換錄音帶。我閱讀證詞，研究照片，確定沒有人盯上我。

en_text: I discover several local prostitutes have been approached in connection with the deaths. Hmm . . . interesting. Questions have been asked about their clients. Is there anybody who has a bizarre fetish? Somebody who enjoys perverse sexual acts? Somebody abusive with unusual requests? It's a feeble and wasted effort. They're hoping that at some point in my life I've vented my sexual aspirations on a whore. I'd never do that. I mean, I'd never do that and keep one alive.
zh_text: 我發現警方偵訊了數名本地妓女。哼……有趣。他們問了些關於她們顧客的問題。有沒有人有奇特的性癖好？喜歡變態性行爲？具有不尋常的虐待傾向？這是一項浪費人力的舉動。他們期望我會在生命中某個時間點上去找妓女發洩性慾。我從不曾這麼做過。我的意思是，我從來不曾在這麼做之後還留下活口。

en_text: Before my workday ends, I successfully get four color photographs, one each of the four men on my list. Schroder and McCoy each have recent photographs in their files, but it's a struggle to get current pictures for the other two—until I realize they've most likely been photographed by journalists and cameramen over the last few weeks. While I vacuum a room upstairs, I use the Internet and search through newspaper sites until I find pictures of a high enough standard I can print out. When I leave work Sally offers me a lift home along with the chance to talk about my mother, and I decline. I forgo my usual bus, and stop at a bank and draw out some cash, figuring I'm going to need it over the next few nights. Melissa took all the cash I was using a few weeks ago, along with my ATM card. Stepping into the bank is like stepping into a small nature reserve. With a few floor-to-ceiling potted plants brightly lit under the glare of halogen lights, and several small ones crammed into most available spaces, it wouldn't be a surprise if there were wild animals living in here. Standing in a line from the counter to the wall is a line of people I don't want to join, but I have no choice. We stand waiting together without daring to make conversation because if any of us did, we'd look like freaks. Eventually the line shuffles forward a few times, and I make it to the teller. She is a tall, masculine woman with large hands who smiles at me a lot, but no amount of smiling would ever get me to sneak through her front door late at night.
zh_text: 一天的工作結束前，我成功地取得了四張彩色照片，我名單上的嫌犯一人一張。施羅德和麥考伊的檔案裡都有近期照片，不過要弄另外兩個傢伙的近期照片就不是那麼容易了——直到我發現他們很可能在過去幾個禮拜裡讓記者和攝影師拍過照片。趁著清理樓上一個房間的時候，我使用網路搜尋新聞網站，找到符合標準的照片列印出來。下班的時候，莎莉說要開車送我，不過被我拒絕。我放棄常搭的公車，前往銀行提領一筆現金，因為今晚可能會需要用到。步入銀行感覺像是步入一塊自然保育區。裡面有幾棵碰到天花板的高大盆栽，由鹵素燈以及其他較小型的燈光提供充足的光線，給人一種就算有野生動物住在裡面也不會令人驚訝的感覺。從櫃檯到牆壁之間站了一排我不打算加入的隊伍，不過我沒得選擇。我們排排站好，不敢交談，因為一旦交談，我們就會看起來像是怪人。隊伍前進了幾次，我終於來到出納員面前。她是個身材高壯的女人，手很大，一直對我笑，不過不管笑成怎樣都不能讓我晚上溜入她家大門。

en_text: From the bank I walk over the road to a supermarket, since most of the food in my house has expired. I walk around, allowing myself to limp slightly now that I'm away from work. It seems strange being here, as if I've slipped into a slice of life that I shouldn't be allowed in, as if the supermarket for serial killers and men who have been assaulted with pliers is the supermarket down the road next to the deli. I stare at beautiful women as I shop, and I begin to feel ill. These women would laugh at me if I attacked them. They would call me Numb Nuts, or maybe even One Nut.
zh_text: 離開銀行後，我穿越馬路前往超級市場，因為我家大部分的食物都過期了。我逛了逛，由於已經遠離工作場所，所以我容許自己跛腳走路。來這裡感覺很奇怪，彷彿我滑入了一個不該允許我進入的生活，彷彿專爲連續殺人魔以及被鉗子夾爆睾丸的男人而設的超級市場就在街尾的熱食店旁。我一邊購物一邊欣賞美女，接著我開始感到不適。如果我襲擊這些美女，她們將會嘲笑我。他們會叫我「麻痺蛋蛋」，或甚至是「獨蛋人」。

en_text: The girl working the checkout smiles at me and asks how my day is going. I want to unzip my fly and show her just how okay it's going. I'm angry as hell. The left one was my favorite. I climb on the bus and the bumpy bus ride threatens to tear my testicle open. When I reach home it takes me five minutes to climb the stairs. Much harder than climbing down them. I enter my apartment. The light on the answering machine is flashing. A sliver of sunlight arcs through the window as part of the sky clears up. At least the place doesn't smell of disinfectant and stale piss. I can smell the food that has started to go off, though. I pull into an alleyway between a couple of shops, the headlights picking out dozens of cardboard boxes, chunks of white Styrofoam, and bags of trash. I try to figure out why Calhoun did what he did, and the answer is actually pretty simple. His problem was that sex with Becky the prostitute couldn't live up to the fantasy he'd imagined. He thought he could quash his desire for rough sex by having it with Becky, but because he was paying her, and she was only pretending to be afraid, it took away the realism. Becky didn't fear for her life, and Calhoun knew that. It may not have sunk in for a few days, or maybe longer, but in the end he was left needing far, far more. Daniela Walker gave him his fantasy. Her skin is so pale she looks as though she could have been locked in the trunk for the last six months. In contrast, her painted lips are a vivid red, the color of blood. I close the trunk.

The same reason she came to my apartment and helped me with the injury. She's playing with me. Toying with me. She's setting something up of which I have no idea at all.

en_text: I'm inside and just shutting my door when a movement to my right stops me. I twist my head to see an old man stepping out of the dark toward me. "My God, is that you, Joe?" He gets a few steps closer, and I give him a casual look up and down, as if I'm out shopping for victims. He looks in his late sixties—his gray hair is combed back at the front, but standing up at the back. His face is a collage of wrinkles that are long and deep. He wears glasses that are broken in the middle, and look to be held together with Velcro dots. They're covered in a thin layer of dust, and I can't pick the color of his magnified eyes. He's holding a hand toward me, not quite pointing, but in a gesture that makes me aware he's about to put his hand on my arm. The sad part is I'm about to let him. He's wearing a flannel shirt and brown corduroy pants. He looks vaguely familiar. I say nothing. I'm in no mood for conversation.
zh_text: 我坐回車上，關上車門，右方傳來一陣動靜，我立刻停止動作。我轉過頭，看見一個老男人步出黑暗，向我走來。「我的天，是你嗎，喬？」他走近幾步，我神態輕鬆地上下打量他，彷彿出門找尋獵物一樣。他看起來年近七十，一頭灰髮梳向腦後，不過後面還是翹起來。他滿臉都是又深又長的皺紋，戴著一副從中斷掉的眼鏡，看來是用魔術貼合起來的。鏡面上有一層薄灰，我看不出放大的眼睛是什麼顏色。他對我伸出一隻手掌，不像是在指我，而是在讓我知道他即將拍拍我的手臂。悲哀的是，我會讓他拍。他身穿法蘭絨襯衫和棕色的燈芯絨褲。他看起來有點眼熟。我一言不發。我沒心情聊天。

en_text: "What are you doing with yourself these days, Joe?" "I sell cars."
zh_text: 「你最近都忙些什麼，喬？」「賣車。」

en_text: "Really? I'm in the market for a car," he says, confusing me since he just said he can't drive anymore, and perhaps he's confusing himself too. I'm desperate to know whether he saw the corpse in the trunk. "Where do you work?" "Umm . . ." I struggle for a name, "Everblue Cars. Heard of it?"
zh_text: 「真的？我正想買一輛車。」他說，由於他剛剛才說不能開車，所以我聽得有點糊塗，或許他自己也有點糊塗。我急著想知道他到底有沒有看到後車廂的屍體。「你在哪工作？」「呃……」我擠出一個名字。「長藍汽車。聽過嗎？」

en_text: Slowly he nods. "Fine establishment, that one, Joe. You must be proud." "Thanks, Walt."
zh_text: 他緩緩點頭。「好地方，那家車行，喬。你一定很驕傲。

en_text: "Yeah." Walt is a witness. Nice old Mr. Chadwick. "Want to take a ride?" "For sale, is it?" "Yep." I take a stab at the price. "Eight grand."
zh_text: 「是啊。」華特是名證人。老好人查德維克先生。「想去兜兜風嗎？」「是賣的嗎，這輛車？」「是啊。」我隨便標個價。「八千。」

en_text: He whistles. Like people do after you've quoted them a price. The whistling is one step away from tire kicking. "Gee, that's cheap," he says, and tries to kick the nearest tire, but misses.
zh_text: 他吹口哨。就像你說出價錢之後人們會有的反應。通常吹玩口哨的人就要踢輪胎了。「天啊，可真便宜。」他說，伸腳去踢最接近的輪胎，不過沒踢中。

en_text: We climb into the car. I do up my seat belt and Walt works on his. He starts whistling again, all the time he's looking at the dashboard, airconditioning, and radio controls. "You know, Joe, I haven't seen your mother since your dad died." I envy him.
zh_text: 我們上了車。我繫上安全帶，華特繫上他的。他又開始吹口哨了。他一直研究著儀表板、空調，還有收音機控制台。你知道，喬，你爸去世後，我就沒有見過你媽了。我真羨慕他。

en_text: "That was a real tragedy," he adds, sounding upset.
zh_text: 「那眞是一場悲劇。」他補充，聽起來很遺憾。

en_text: I find myself nodding. I want to tell him that I thought it was a tragedy too. I want to tell him how it hurt when Dad was no longer with us, how I just wanted him to be alive, but I say nothing. "Yeah," I manage, keeping my voice under control.
zh_text: 我忍不住點頭。我很想告訴他也認爲那是一場悲劇，我想告訴他我爸的死對我造成多大的創傷，我有多麼希望他還活著，但是我什麼也沒說。「是啊。」我擠出這句話，努力控制我的聲音。

en_text: "Did I ever tell you how sorry I was?" I have no idea what in the hell he told me back then. What anybody told me. "You did. Thanks." He opens his mouth, but says nothing. He seems to be thinking. "How are you coping these days?" "I'm over it," I say, not bothering to mention how empty life became without him.
zh_text: 「我有說過我有多遺憾嗎？」我完全不記得他當年跟我說過什麼。不記得任何人跟我說過什麼。「有。謝謝。他張開嘴巴，欲言又止。他似乎在考慮什麼。「那件事情還會影響你嗎？」「已經過去了。」我說，沒有費心提及生活少了爸有多空虛。

en_text: Now it's his turn to start nodding. "That's good, Joe. When a man takes his own life, his family can be a mess for years. Thank God you've come out of it as a nice young man."
zh_text: 這下輪到他點頭了。「那很好，喬。家裡有人自殺時，家人總會低潮一陣子。感謝上帝你能走出陰霾，成爲一個大好青年。」

en_text: I'm still nodding. When Dad killed himself, the only thing I felt like doing at first was joining him. There were hundreds of questions, but the biggest one was Why? Mom knows, I'm sure of it. Just as I'm sure she'll never tell me. The second why is just as important: why did he leave me alone with Mom?
zh_text: 我還在點頭。老爸自殺時，我剛開始唯一想做的事情就是隨他而去。我有數以百計的疑問，但是最大的問題還是在於爲什麼？老媽知道，我很肯定。我也很肯定她永遠不會告訴我。第二個爲什麼也同等重要：他爲什麼把我一個人留給媽？

en_text: "She still got the place in South Brighton?"
zh_text: 「她還住在南布萊頓嗎？」

en_text: I stop nodding. I'm thinking of Dad and feeling depressed. I know Melissa is watching me, but for the moment I don't really care. "Yeah." I start the car. "Shall we take her for a spin?" I ask, needing to change the subject. "Sure, Joe."
zh_text: 我停止點頭。我在想我爸，心情很沮喪。我知道梅莉莎在監視我，不過在這剎那我真的不在乎。「對。」我發動引擎。「我們開出去溜溜吧？」我問，因為我需要改變話題。「當然」喬

en_text: We watch the city go by. Life has wound down in this part of the world. We spot only a few other cars on the road. We pass a service station with a police car parked outside and two officers standing over a man they have handcuffed laying facedown. Walt makes conversation about the car and the weather, and tells me that his dead dog keeps running away. "My God, who would have thought I'd run into Evelyn's son? You know, Joe, I've known your mother more than forty years."
zh_text: 我們看著街景在車外飛逝。這附近的生活步調比較沒有那麼緊湊。一路上只有經過幾輛車。我們路過一座加油站，站外停了一輛警車。華特一直聊著這輛車、天氣，並且宣稱他死去的狗經常逃家。「我的天啊，誰會想到我竟然能遇上愛弗琳的兒子？你知道，喬，我認識你媽超過四十年了。」

en_text: "Really." "We're both single now. Single and old. Isn't life sad?"
zh_text: 「眞的。」「現在我們兩個都單身了。單身又年老。生活不是很悲哀嗎？」

en_text: "Sad," I agree.
zh_text: 「悲哀。」我同意。

en_text: I stop north of the city, turning into a long stretch of road just before the highway where a thousand trees block our view in every direction. Out here, we're all alone. Out here, I can do what I want. "Maybe I'll give your mother a call tomorrow, invite myself around for dinner."
zh_text: 我在城北停車，轉入一條通往高速公路的道路，四周有上千棵樹阻擋我們的視線。在這裡，只有我們兩人獨處。在這裡，我可以爲所欲爲。「或許我該打個電話給你媽，去找她叨擾一頓晚餐。」

en_text: "Maybe I'll give your mother a call tomorrow, invite myself around for dinner." Keeping one hand on the wheel, I reach behind the passenger seat and open my briefcase.
zh_text: 「或許我該打個電話給你媽，去找她叨擾一頓晚餐。」我一手放在方向盤上，另外一手伸到乘客座上打開公事包。

en_text: "No. I'm fine."
zh_text: 「不用，我自己來就好了。」

en_text: "No, I didn't know that, Walt."
zh_text: 「不，我不知道，華特。」

en_text: "Would you mind if I called her? I wouldn't mind getting to know her again." The opportunity knocks so loud I actually drop the knife. Candy's in the trunk of the car, but Walt doesn't know she's there. He couldn't. He's too damn old to make sense of anything even if he had seen her, and he'd be blabbing on about her, asking me a whole bunch of questions. I close my briefcase. If I let Walt live, he's going to spend time with my mother, and that's time she won't be able to devote to me.
zh_text: 「你介意我打電話給她嗎？我想重新認識她。」我腦中靈光一現，興奮得我連刀都握不住了。坎蒂就在後車廂，但是華特並不知情。他不可能知情。他就算有看到她，也已經老到搞不清楚狀況了，而且他一定會喋喋不休地詢問一大堆關於她的問題。我關上公事包。如果讓華特活下來，他就會去跟我媽混，而我媽就不會把那麼多時間花在我的身上。

en_text: The opportunity knocks so loud I actually drop the knife. Candy's in the trunk of the car, but Walt doesn't know she's there. He couldn't. He's too damn old to make sense of anything even if he had seen her, and he'd be blabbing on about her, asking me a whole bunch of questions. I close my briefcase. If I let Walt live, he's going to spend time with my mother, and that's time she won't be able to devote to me. "What are you smiling about, Joe?"
zh_text: 我腦中靈光一現，興奮得我連刀都握不住了。坎蒂就在後車廂，但是華特並不知情。他不可能知情。他就算有看到她，也已經老到搞不清楚狀況了，而且他一定會喋喋不休地詢問一大堆關於她的問題。我關上公事包。如果讓華特活下來，他就會去跟我媽混，而我媽就不會把那麼多時間花在我的身上。你在笑什麼，喬？

en_text: "Nothing. You want to drive back, Walt?"
zh_text: 「沒什麼。你想開回去嗎，華特？」

en_text: "No, son, I'll let you do the driving."
zh_text: 「不，孩子，開車的事情還是交給你吧。」

en_text: "I'll call your mother tomorrow morning," he says, leaning back into the car and smiling at me.
zh_text: 「我明天一早就打電話給你媽。」

en_text: He gives me a knowing nod, his eyes twinkling a little. "Evelyn," he says, more to himself than to me, then he turns and heads up the pathway to his door. I pull away and head south. I turn on the stereo and sing loudly. After ten minutes, I pull the car off to the side of the road beneath a bank of trees. The grass, burned dry from the last few months of hot sun, has been sheltered enough by the trees to keep most of the day's rain off. I study the body again, hoping that I might be able to learn something from it, or more likely, that Melissa has left me a message. I shift the corpse slightly. Deep cuts smile at me. Dark red flesh gleams from beneath thick flaps of skin. I have a good idea what caused the wounds. I wrestle Candy from the car, careful not to get blood on myself, and dump her on the ground, which reveals the murder weapon in the bottom of the trunk. My knife.
zh_text: 我駕車離開，朝南行駛。我打開收音機，高聲歌唱。十分鐘後，我將車開向路旁，停在一排樹下。即使今晚有下毛毛雨，讓上個月烈日曬乾的草地依然在我腳下吱吱作響。我再度打量屍體，希望能夠從中看出端倪，或更有可能的情況是，梅莉莎有在上面留下信息。我慢慢移動屍體。傷口很深，向我微笑。下垂的皮膚下露出深紅色的血肉。我很清楚這些傷口是什麼留下來的。我將坎蒂抬出後車廂，小心不讓血沾到身上，然後將她放在地上，露出躺在後車廂底的兇器。我的刀。

en_text: Or, to be more accurate, a photograph of my knife.
zh_text: 或是，說得更精確一點，刀的照片。

en_text: Seeing this leads me to a couple of conclusions: one, Melissa is definitely stalking me, and two, I'm in serious trouble. The knife has my fingerprints on it, as does my gun. I remove a red plastic container full of gas and set it on the ground.
zh_text: 看到這張照片讓我得出兩個結論：第一，梅莉莎在跟蹤我；第二，我的麻煩大了。那把刀上有我的指紋，槍也一樣。我拿出一個裝滿汽油的塑膠罐，放在地上。

en_text: I dump Candy back into the trunk. Her hands are still tied, her mouth gagged. Both those are my doing. I wonder what she thought when she was desperate for help and a woman came along and opened the trunk. It was the end of things going badly for Candy. It was the end of everything.
zh_text: 我又把坎蒂放回後車廂。她雙手依然緊綁，嘴裡塞著東西。這兩件事都是我幹的。不知道在她絕望無助的時候看到有個女人打開後車廂是什麼感覺。對坎蒂而言，那是苦難的終點。那是一切的終點。

en_text: I decide to leave the trunk open. I shake the container back and forth, listening as the gas inside sloshes around. It's about a quarter full. I use what's there to soak Candy's clothes, then toss the container in there with her. I reach into the car for my briefcase and use a knife to cut away Candy's blouse. Once I pop the gas cap on the side of the car, I stuff the blouse inside, leaving a tongue hanging out.
zh_text: 我決定就讓車廂蓋開著。我搖搖塑膠罐，聽著裡面的汽油晃來晃去。約莫四分之一滿。我浸濕了坎蒂的衣服，將罐子丟到她旁邊。我回車上拿出我的公事包，用刀割下坎蒂的上衣。我打開車身側面的汽油蓋，將上衣塞了進去，留下一點露在外面。

en_text: The car's cigarette lighter does the job. I am most of the way back into town when I remember the cat. There is nobody to see me as I steal my second car for the evening.
zh_text: 我用車上的點菸器點火。差不多要回到城内的時候，我突然想起那隻貓來。我在附近空無一人的情況下偷了當晚第一輛車。

en_text: Jennifer smiles at me when I walk through the door. She looks at me as if we're long-lost friends. "Hi there, Joe," she says, her voice sounding seductive. "Hi."
zh_text: 進門的時候，珍妮佛對我微笑。她看我的樣子彷彿我們是許久不見的老朋友。「哈囉，喬。她說，她的聲音聽來十分銷魂。「嗨。

en_text: I'm picturing how Melissa would look in a studded dog collar when Jennifer brings the cat out in a small cage.
zh_text: 我趁珍妮佛去提裝貓的籠子出來時幻想梅莉莎戴狗項圈的模樣。

en_text: "When I rang to give you an update, you said you didn't want any more cats. How many have you got?" "Last week?" I repeat.
zh_text: 「我打電話去時，你說你不想再養貓了。你到底養了多少貓？」「上個禮拜？」我重複。

en_text: Her smile disappears and is replaced with one of caution. "I called you last week."
zh_text: 她的笑容消失，換上一副謹慎的神色。「我上禮拜有打電話給你。

en_text: "Oh. I was sick last week, really sick. To be honest, I don't even remember you calling. I was in bed all week. I don't know what the hell it was I had, but I was pretty delirious. If you called and I was a bastard or something, I'm really sorry." Though she's the one who ought to be feeling sorry—I'm the one with a missing testicle. Her caution turns to sympathy.
zh_text: 「喔。我上個禮拜生病了，病得很重。老實說，我甚至不記得妳有打電話來。我一整個禮拜都躺在床上。我不知道我到底得了什麼病，不過我神智不太清醒。如果妳打來的時候我表現得很混蛋，我在這邊向妳道歉。」其實她才應該感到抱歉——睪丸不見的人可是我呀。

en_text: "Are you okay now?" "Getting better. The strange part is that I don't even have any cats."
zh_text: 她謹慎的神情轉爲同情。「你現在好點了嗎？」「比較好了。奇怪的地方在於，我根本沒養貓。」

en_text: She smiles, and I wonder why I must keep being nice to people. Why can't I just take her somewhere and do to her what I've been doing to everybody else? "Well, you've got one now. What are you going to call him?"
zh_text: 她微笑，我很納悶我爲什麼一定要跟她這麼客氣。我幹嘛不乾脆帶她前往沒人的地方，對她做出我對其他人所做的事情？好吧，现在你有一隻了。你打算叫他什麼？

en_text: "I haven't really given it any thought. Any suggestions?" "Maybe we could figure one out over coffee?" she offers.
zh_text: 「我沒想過。有建議嗎？」想到的話，我打電話給你。」她說。

en_text: "I didn't know cats drink coffee," I tell her. She smiles, then stops smiling, and looks a little confused. "What do I owe you for the cage?" I ask, figuring it wouldn't look good if I pulled a plastic bag out of my pocket and stuffed the cat inside. I bet the cage is going to add a good chunk to what is already an expensive mammal. "Can I trust you to bring it back?"
zh_text: 「這個貓籠多少錢？」我問，心想如果拿口袋裡的塑膠袋來裝貓的話應該不太好看。我敢說這個貓籠肯定要讓本來就已經很貴的哺乳類寵物加上一大筆額外的開銷。「我相信你會把它帶回來？」

en_text: "I'm a trustworthy guy."
zh_text: 我很值得信任。

en_text: A lift home would be good, since it would give me a chance to test a few things out that haven't been used since my half castration. But my name's on record here, and it wouldn't take long for the police to come.
zh_text: 送我聽起來不錯，因為這樣可以讓我有機會嘗試一些打從我被半閹割後就沒嘗試過的事情。但是我曾在這裡留下紀錄，警方要不了多久就會找上門來。

en_text: The cage moves around beneath my grip. The taxi driver makes some comment on the cat, figuring he can strike up a conversation with me. He figures wrong. When I get home I put the cat in the bathroom and shut the door. When I go to bed, I can hear it crying. Tomorrow I'll buy it some food and myself some earplugs. Then I'll show it around my apartment.
zh_text: 貓籠在我的手中晃來晃去。計程車司機評論那隻貓幾句，以為我想找點話聊。他想錯了。回家之後，我將貓放入浴室，關上房門。上床時，我聽見貓在叫。明天我會買點貓食外帶一副耳塞，然後再帶牠認識環境。

en_text: The following morning my internal alarm clock doesn't let me down. Things are getting back to as normal as they can be for a guy missing his left testicle. I'm still dreaming, though, which is a concern. Last night I was talking to Dad. The dream was disjointed, but I can remember fragments where he was asking me what I was doing. I guess he was asking me because I was stuffing him into the front of the car he was found in. I'd wrapped foam around his wrists, foam and padding, so the rope wouldn't leave bruises. He couldn't wind down the windows or open the doors. He couldn't adjust the air-conditioning or turn off the engine as the carbon monoxide flooded in. He turned blue as he asked me over and over to stop. Mom wasn't there. She was playing bridge down at the local bingo hall. In fact, that was the last time she ever played. He stopped asking me to stop, then told me that he loved me. Then he died. One moment he was my dad. The next moment he was nothing. I'm not growing at all accustomed to dreams and I've woken from this one feeling shaky and ill. Of course I didn't kill my father. I loved him dearly and, like my mother, I'd never have done anything to harm him. Walt mentioning my father's suicide must have given me the imagery. Nobody knows why Dad did what he did. Why he sat himself inside the car parked in the garage and pumped carbon monoxide through the side window with a hose. He didn't even leave a note.
zh_text: 第二天早上我的生理時鐘沒有令我失望，不過我醒來後依然疲憊。對一個失去左睾丸的男人來說，生活已經算是步入常軌。不過我依然會做夢，這倒是令我有點擔憂。昨晚我夢到跟老爸聊天。那個夢沒頭沒尾，不過我依稀記得他問我最近在做什麼。我想他會這麼問是因為當時我正把他塞入他死時的那輛車前座裡。我在他的手腕上裹了一層泡綿，泡綿加襯墊，以免繩子留下瘡痕。他沒有辦法搖下車窗或打開車門。一氧化碳噴入車內時，他無法調整空調或是關閉引擎。他臉色發青，一次又一次地求我住手。媽不在。她去附近的賓果室玩橋牌。事實上，那是她最後一次玩橋牌。他不再求我住手了，然後告訴我他愛我。接著他就死了。前一刻他還是我老爸，下一刻他就什麼也不是了。我完全無法習慣做夢，而自這個夢中驚醒給我一種顫抖與噁心的感覺。當然我沒有殺害我父親。我非常愛他，就像愛我媽一樣，我從來沒有做過任何傷害他的事情。一定是華特提起我爸自殺的關係。沒人知道老爸爲什麼要那麼做。爲什麼要坐到車庫的車裡，自車窗用水管接一氧化碳到車內。他甚至沒有留下遺書。

en_text: I give the cat explicit instructions not to claw the furniture or walls. He doesn't. He looks around for a few seconds before deciding the best way to take a break from being locked inside the bathroom is to hide beneath my bed. I feed my fish, make a mental note to buy some food for the cat, go through the usual routines, then fight the cat back into the bathroom with the aid of a broom. I turn the radio on, listen to the news.
zh_text: 我明確指示貓咪不可抓壞家具與牆壁。牠沒有。牠四下打量片刻，最後決定在被鎖在廁所裡這麼久後，最好的放鬆方式就是躲到我的床下。我餵魚，提醒自己要幫貓買點吃的，做完例行公事，在掃把的幫助下將貓趕回廁所。我打開收音機，聽聽新聞。

en_text: The walk downstairs is easier than yesterday. The bus ride is also easier. The weather a little worse. It's raining steadily. I learn nothing at work except that the people I work with have no Goddamn idea what they're doing.
zh_text: 下樓感覺比昨天輕鬆。坐公車也一樣。除了跟我一起工作的傢伙完全不知道他們在做什麼之外，我在警局一無所獲。

en_text: I eat her sandwiches and take another of the pills. It feels like it goes down my throat sideways, and I don't feel any better for it. I think about my dream, and wonder why I'm having so many these days. I put it down to the fact that at the moment I'm not getting to do all the things other people only fantasize about. A few hours after lunch I'm carrying my bucket and mop when I see her: Melissa, sitting at a desk. For a second, perhaps even two, the world comes to a complete standstill. I can hear blood pulsing in my head, which is a neat trick because I can swear my heart stops beating. She turns to me and winks. I start toward her, then begin to back away, so I end up motionless. I want to look around at the police who are going to start jumping on me, but I can't look away from her. After all she's done to me, there's something about her I can't help but admire. Today she's wearing an expensive light gray suit that makes her look like an overpaid lawyer. Her hair is pulled back neatly, and she is wearing little makeup. She looks like a woman any man would desperately want to believe.
zh_text: 我吃了她的三明治，又吞下另外一顆藥片。感覺好像它神不知鬼不覺地進入我的喉嚨，完全沒有讓我感覺好一點。我又想起我的夢，納悶爲什麼我最近這麼常做夢。我認爲是因為此時我沒有辦法去做那些大部分的人只能幻想的事情。午飯後幾小時，我在拿著水桶和拖把工作時看見了她：梅莉莎，坐在桌子。她轉向我，眨了眨眼。我朝她走去，隨即又向後退開，結果弄到僵在原地。在對我做出那種事情後，我發現她身上有股令我不由自主欣賞的特質。今天她身穿一套昂貴的淡灰色套裝，看起來像是撈過界的律師。她的頭髮整齊後梳，臉上化著淡妝。她看起來像是會讓任何男人樂意相信的女人。

en_text: She flashes a smile at me before turning her attention back to Detective Calhoun. Are they working together?
zh_text: 她對我笑了一笑，接著將注意力轉回到卡爾霍恩警探身上。難道他們狼狽爲奸？

en_text: "Afternoon, Joe. How's it going there?"
zh_text: 「午安，喬，今天過得如何？」

en_text: I jump and turn and see Schroder standing next to me, sipping from a cup of coffee that I haven't made. He's smiling at me. "Fine, Detective Schroder." "You know her?"
zh_text: 我轉頭看到施羅德警探站在我身邊，啜飲著一杯不是我倒的咖啡。「不錯，施羅德警探。」「你認識她？」

en_text: "Huh?" He nods his head toward Melissa. "Looked like you recognized her."
zh_text: 「呃？」他朝向梅莉莎點頭。「看起來好像你認得她。

en_text: I shake my head. "No." He grins. "Just staring, huh? Don't blame you, and don't feel bad for being caught out."
zh_text: 我搖頭。「不認得。」他微笑。「那就只是在看人家了，嗯？我不怪你。」

en_text: He grins. "Just staring, huh? Don't blame you, and don't feel bad for being caught out." "Caught out?" I say. Oh, Jesus, it's come to this, it's finally come to this and my gun is in my office. I can't believe it. Weirdly, I feel like crying.
zh_text: 他微笑。「那就只是在看人家了，嗯？我不怪你。」她知道我是這裡的清潔工嗎？我的工作服顯然說明了這一點，水桶和拖把也是。她在看到我穿成這樣前就知道了嗎？不過我問錯問題了。我真正需要知道的事情在於她為什麼會在這裡。目前為止還沒有人跑來拿槍指我，要我招供罪行。

en_text: "Half the men in here are staring at her." He's right. Half the men in here are staring at her. "Just don't let her catch you," he says, and it's good advice—better advice than he really knows. He disappears back in the direction he came from, as if he'd only shown up to make chitchat. I'm still standing in the same place I was when I saw Melissa, only now I'm feeling more obvious about it. I need to leave. Do I go for my briefcase in case I need to shoot my way out of here, or do I just head for the door now? I carry the bucket and mop back to my office, close my door behind me, and grab my briefcase and at the same time I'm opening it, I remember I don't have my gun anymore. I slump into my chair. I don't know what to do, with a little more distance between Melissa and my remaining testicle, I can think a little clearer. Melissa didn't point me out. That's not why she's here. She's here because, just like my gun, she owns me too. This is her game. She's come here today to make sure I know who's in control. I get out of my chair. I stare down at the city for a few seconds, the people out there moving quickly through the cold. I take one of the knives out of my briefcase. It's small and easy to conceal, but I figure if I'm going down I can take one, maybe two people with me. I slip it into my pocket. When I head into the hallway with the vacuum cleaner, Melissa and Calhoun have gone. They'll be in the smaller of the two conference rooms up here. It's similar to an interrogation room, but with nicer décor, designed to get information from nice people in a comfortable way. There will be tea and coffee and a light lunch, nice music. It's foreplay where the goal is catching a killer. I wish I could be in there listening, and at the same time, I wish I could be a thousand miles away. When I open the door of the main conference room, I see a gaggle of detectives standing around, staring at the board. I expect them to all turn in unison toward me, like I'm a gunslinger entering the local saloon, but only Detective Landry comes over. He's somewhere in his forties. Has those rugged good looks of a movie actor playing a policeman. His clothes are wrinkled, his sleeves are up, and he looks like the sort of guy about to make a breakthrough. He smells of cigarette smoke. "This probably isn't a good time, Joe."
zh_text: 當我拿著吸塵器回到走廊上時，梅莉莎和卡爾霍恩已經不在了。他們進入小會議室。小會議室跟偵訊室很像，不過裝潢好一點，專門用來從好人口中以舒適的方式取得線索。裡面有茶、咖啡、簡餐和好聽的音樂。那是逮捕兇手的前戲。我希望可以進去旁聽，同時我也希望我能身處千里之外。打開主會議室時，我看到一群警探站在裡面，盯著牆上的佈告板。我期待他們會同時轉過頭來看我，好像我是步入酒館的槍手一樣，不過只有艾力克斯·漢森向我走來。他年過四十，如同扮演警察的電影明星般英俊瀟灑。他衣服很皺，衣袖捲起，看起來像個即將突破案情的傢伙。「現在可能不是好時機，喬。」

en_text: "The room's pretty clean. Probably won't need going over for a few more days."
zh_text: 「會議室很乾淨。可能好幾天都不需要打掃。」

en_text: I turn toward the door, fighting the temptation to run. I remind myself that I'm the one in control, that I'm the one running this show, but if that were true, I wouldn't have this God-awful sick feeling in my stomach. Throwing one last glance at the board before I step into the hallway, I see a photograph of a burned car. Christ. I'm learning nothing. I'm out of the loop.
zh_text: 我轉向房門，壓抑著一股想要拔腿就跑的衝動。我提醒自己情況掌握在我手中，是我在主導這場戲，但若果真如此，我心裡就不會有這股超級噁心的感覺。如今真正掌控大局的人是梅莉莎。步入走廊之前，我又瞄了佈告板一眼，看見一張燒毀車輛的照片。天啊。我什麼都不知道。我被排除在外了。

en_text: "Afternoon, Joe."
zh_text: 「午安，喬。」

en_text: "Hi there, Detective Hutton. Looks pretty busy. There something going on?"
zh_text: 「哈囉，胡頓警探。大家好像很忙。出了什麼事嗎？」

en_text: He smiles at me with the same pity in his eyes he always has. "You haven't heard?"
zh_text: 他眼中帶著一貫的同情向我微笑。「你沒聽說？」

en_text: "Heard what?"
zh_text: 「聽說什麼？」

en_text: I feel as though I've just been punched in the stomach, but I force myself to play Slow Joe. Are these people just playing with me? Is this an elaborate trap to call me out? I reach into my pocket and feel for the knife. A guy like Hutton, I just don't think the blade is long enough.
zh_text: 我感覺像是肚子被人揍了一拳，不過我強迫自己扮演智障喬。這些傢伙是在耍我嗎？這是一場精心設計的陷阱嗎？

en_text: "There was another victim last night, Joe. Another prostitute. This time a witness saw him driving away from the alleyway where she was dumped." Jesus, I wonder how Calhoun is feeling now that the woman he paid for sex two months ago has been killed. Is he feeling worse than me? He'll make the connection with the dead hooker, but will he believe it? "Have you caught the bad man yet?"
zh_text: 「昨天晚上又有人遇害，喬，又是妓女。這一次有目擊證人看見他從棄屍的巷子裡倒車出來。」老天啊，我心想卡爾霍恩得知他兩個月前嫖過的女人被殺之後會有什麼感覺。感覺會比我還糟嗎？死妓女會讓他聯想到有人在追查他，但是他會相信嗎？「你們抓到壞人了沒？」

en_text: Hutton shakes his head. "Not yet. The car used was stolen." "You know that already? Wow, you're smart."
zh_text: 胡頓搖頭。「還沒。那輛車是偷來的。」「你已經知道了？哇，你好聰明。」

en_text: "The car was used to dump another body later in the evening."
zh_text: 那輛車後來又被用作棄置另外一具屍體。

en_text: "Another prostitute?" "I can't say too much, Joe." He pauses to take a bite from his chocolate bar, like he needs the energy to come up with the words that he can't tell me. Chocolate-stained teeth begin mincing the confectionery. A few tiny pieces flake onto the collar of his turtleneck. I'm not sure why he doesn't just swallow the whole damn thing in one go.
zh_text: 「又是妓女？」「我不能多說，喬。」他暫停片刻，咬了一口巧克力棒，彷彿他需要能量才能說出他不能告訴我的話。沾有巧克力的牙齒咀嚼口中的零食，一些小碎屑落在高領毛衣的領子上。我不確定他爲什麼不一口吞掉那個可惡的東西。

en_text: "Any suspects?" He shakes his head and keeps chewing. "Better carry on, Joe." "Sure thing."
zh_text: 「有嫌犯嗎？」他一邊咀嚼一邊搖頭。「還是去工作吧，喬。」

en_text: He shakes his head and keeps chewing. "Better carry on, Joe." "Sure thing." I head back to my office. My hands are trembling slightly. Calm down. Calm down.
zh_text: 他一邊咀嚼一邊搖頭。「還是去工作吧，喬。」我回到我的辦公室。我的雙手微微顫抖。冷靜。冷靜。

en_text: It's easy to think, but hard to do. I need to create order from this Goddamn confusion that Melissa has dropped me into. The only problem is I'm coming up with nothing, only more excuses to hurt her. In the end I sneak open my office door and glance into the hallway. It's empty. Could I just leave and follow her? Is it that simple? Will the police let me leave? I wait for thirty minutes, peering out from my office every few minutes or so, watching for Melissa, watching for the police escort to take me away. It doesn't happen, and I start holding out hope that it isn't going to. I grab the vacuum cleaner and let myself be seen. I mooch around the hallway, sucking dust mites and food crumbs from the carpet, biding my time. Occasionally one or two detectives will come from the conference room and head either to their cubicle, or out to the street, but they don't glance at me. Other times they simply come to get coffee. They nod and smile at me without really seeing me.
zh_text: 用想的很容易，真要冷靜很難。我必須在梅莉莎丟給我的爛攤子中理出頭緒。唯一的問題在於我什麼辦法都想不到，只有更多傷害她的藉口。最後我偷偷打開辦公室門，瞄了瞄走廊上的景象。空無一人。我可以就這樣溜出去跟蹤她嗎？事情可不可能這麼簡單？我等了三十分鐘，每隔幾分鐘就從辦公室偷看，等待梅莉莎，等待警方將我逮捕。沒人來逮捕我，於是我心中浮現不會被逮捕的期望。我拿起吸塵器，出去露露臉。我在走廊上徘徊，吸著地毯上的灰塵和食物碎片消磨時間。偶爾會有一兩名警探離開會議室，走回辦公隔間或是離開警局，不過他們沒有看我。有時候他們只是出來倒咖啡的。他們對我點頭微笑，渾然不把我當作一回事。

en_text: All the regulars are gone, or maybe they aren't—maybe they're just waiting around the corner, watching and waiting. Except for Sally. She's always there. Just milling around, asking me how I am, how my mother is, asking me if I would like a lift home.
zh_text: 所有廁所的常客都不見了，或許他們沒有不見，或許他們只是等在轉角，默默監視。除了莎莉。她一直都在我的身邊。糾纏著我，問我日子過得如何，我媽好不好，問我要不要搭便車回家。

en_text: I quickly duck back into my office and watch from the corner of the door. As she stands there, Detective Landry walks from the elevator. In his hand, sitting across the bottom of a clear plastic bag, is a knife. Not any knife, but my knife. One of my favorites. He's carrying it as though he's just found the Holy Grail. Nobody could mistake the look of pride on his face. Melissa and Calhoun head toward him and the elevator, and they pause to talk. I'd love to know what they are saying, and if things go as planned, soon I will. Then Calhoun steps with her into the elevator and the doors slide shut. I rush for the stairwell and race my way to the ground floor, ignoring the throbbing from my groin. And it's worth it, because I'm quick enough to see Melissa as she leaves the building. She's alone now. I head to the door. Nobody puts their hand on my shoulder.
zh_text: 我迅速回到我的辦公室，自門角偷看外面。漢森警探在她等待的時候步出電梯。他手上的塑膠袋裡放著一把刀。不是普通的刀，而是我的刀，我最喜歡的刀之一。沒有人會誤認他臉上的驕傲神情。梅莉莎和卡爾霍恩迎向他和電梯。他們停下來交談。我很想知道他們在聊些什麼，如果一切依照計畫進行的話，我很快就會知道了。接著卡爾霍恩和她一起步入電梯，電梯隨即關門。我衝向樓梯間，急急忙忙來到一樓，完全不顧胯下的刺痛。不過一切都很值得，因為我剛好趕上梅莉莎離開大樓。只剩她一個人了。我走向大門，沒人伸手來搭我的肩膀。

en_text: I turn right. Melissa is heading toward the Avon River, so I take the same route, cross the same road, avoid the same people. The sun has come out overhead, but it doesn't look like it will be for long, and it's not helping me feel any warmer. When Melissa reaches the grassy bank, she turns right and keeps moving, staying parallel to the dark water. I do the same, but keep a good fifty yards behind her. I have to be careful, because if she runs from me, I'm in no condition to chase her. A few moments later she swerves toward a nearby park bench, takes a position sitting at the far end, and looks directly toward me. I stop walking, study the ground like there's something interesting there. I can feel her still looking at me. When I look up again, she smiles.
zh_text: 我右轉。梅莉莎朝向雅芳河走，於是我跟了上去，穿越相同的馬路，避開相同的人群。抵達翠綠的河岸時，她轉向右方，繼續前進，與深色的河水保持平行。我也一樣，不過跟她維持五十公尺的距離。我必須小心，因為如果她逃跑的話，以我的身體狀況絕對無法追趕。幾分鐘後，她突然轉向附近的一張公園長椅，坐在一邊，然後筆直朝我看來。我停止前進，低頭望向下方，彷彿地上有什麼有趣的東西一樣。我感覺到她還在看我。當我再度抬頭時，她面露微笑。

en_text: The long summer is finally coming to an end, but that's okay, because she loves autumn. She can't think of anything better than being outside in a nice nor'west breeze as the leaves are changing color, but as much as she loves it, she dreads the months that are to follow. Winter brings with it a grimy film of depression that settles down over the city and soaks into the buildings and the plants and the people, everything touched by rain and the cold wind and the smog.
zh_text: 這將會是個漫長的夏天，不過沒關係，因為她熱愛夏天。她想不出有什麼能比出門吹吹西北風、身處一群對生命充滿希望的人們之中更美好的事情。夏天就會給她這種感覺。接著冬天到來，將這一切通通奪走，讓整座城市籠罩在沮喪氣息之中，將一切浸泡在雨水、冷風以及煙霧裡。

en_text: Sally is confused. About Joe. About his lies. She understands why he lied about his mother being sick. That was a lie she was happy to go along with, because it protected him. Joe didn't want to be known as the man who had a testicle pulped by a pair of pliers. If something like that had ever happened to Martin, well, she would have wanted somebody like her to have looked out for him. All she can do now is hope the penicillin she gave Joe will help the healing process and fight off any infection. It should. If not he'll have to go to a hospital. He won't have a choice.
zh_text: 莎莉感到困惑，喬令她困惑，他的謊言令她困惑。她了解他為什麼要謊稱母親生病。她很樂意配合這個謊言，因為這樣說能夠保護他。喬不想讓人知道有人拿鉗子夾爆他的睾丸。如果這種事情發生在馬丁身上——好吧，她會希望有個像她這樣的人去照顧他。如今她只能期望她帶給喬的盤尼西林足以幫助他復原，並且避免感染。應該可以。如果不行的話，他就得去醫院。他沒得選擇。

en_text: She had shown up the day he had been attacked, and each of the following three days—on one of those occasions she had found him passed out on the floor. She wanted to go back the next day too, but her father had had a bad fall and she'd been forced to weigh up her priorities. Family had to come first. She'd still gone to work—she had no more sick days— but from there she'd gone straight home and helped with her father. He'd dislocated a hip and broken a collarbone, but he was mending.
zh_text: 她在他遇襲的當天去過他家，之後三天也都有去：其中有一次她發現他昏倒在地板上。後來她還想再去，不過她爸不小心摔倒，於是她被迫必須優先照顧她爸。家人總是優先考量。她還得去上班——她沒有病假可請——不過一下班她就會直接回家，幫忙照顧父親。他髖骨脫臼，還摔斷了一根鎖骨，不過情況逐漸好轉。

en_text: She was going to go back and see Joe on Monday—he still had stitches that needed removing—but he'd shown up at work. They didn't speak directly of the attack. She wants to talk him into going to the police for help, but not at work. She doesn't like the fact that he lied to her about only seeing the crimescene photographs in the conference room. He knows it's stealing, but he's obviously reluctant to open up to her about it. The man with the big smile looks so innocent that she can't imagine him deliberately lying, but the man who smiled at her between the elevator doors two weeks ago, well, that was a different Joe, wasn't it? That was a Joe that looked capable of . . .
zh_text: 她本來打算禮拜一回去探望喬——他的縫線還沒拆除——不過他來上班了。他們沒有直接談論遇襲的事情。她很想勸他去找警方幫忙，不過不能在上班時間。她不喜歡他騙她說只有在會議室裡見過犯罪現場照片。他知道那是偷竊的行爲，不過他顯然不願意對她坦白。她實在很難想像這個臉上掛著無辜大微笑的男人竟然會刻意說謊，不過兩個禮拜前在電梯門口朝她微笑的男人，好吧，那是個截然不同的喬，不是嗎？那是看起來有能力……有能力怎樣？做任何事？

en_text: Of what? Of anything? No. Not anything. But he looked capable of lying. He looked smooth, he looked calculating, as if he knew exactly what was going on. She reminds herself it was a fluke smile, that Joe isn't like that at all.
zh_text: 不。不是任何事。不過看起來像是有能力騙人的樣子。他看起來很冷靜、很精明，彷彿他很清楚周遭所發生的一切。她提醒自己喬只是剛好笑成那樣，他根本不是那種人。

en_text: But why the lies? Every time she stirs around the possibilities in her head, one keeps on coming up to the surface: Joe is being forced to do something he doesn't want to do. Therefore somebody needs to help him, and it's up to her. It's her Christian duty to make sure no harm comes to him. Joe has been nervous and anxious most of the day, more so this afternoon, and she suspects why: the person pressuring him to bring home information has asked him for more. Of course she still can't figure out why the folders would still be in Joe's apartment and not in the possession of the man who attacked him, but she figures it must have something to do with timing. Perhaps Joe forgot to take the folders with him to a meeting and made the man angry. Perhaps those folders aren't at Joe's anymore, but with the man who is threatening him. The only way to know for sure is to keep an eye on Joe. The same way Joe seems to be keeping an eye on the woman who has come to talk to the detectives—which, if Sally is truthful, makes her feel a little jealous. It isn't only Joe keeping an eye on her—it's most of the men in the department.
zh_text: 每當她在心裡盤算種種可能時，一個想法就會不斷浮現腦海：有人強迫喬做一些他不想做的事情。這表示他需要幫助，而只有她能幫他。確保他不會受到傷害乃是她身爲教徒的責任。那天大部分的時間裡，喬看起來都很緊張不安，特別是下午，而她想她知道原因：強迫他帶資料回家的人又要他帶更多資料。當然她還想不透爲什麼那些檔案夾還留在喬的公寓裡，而沒有落入暴徒手中，不過她認爲一定是跟時機有關。或許喬忘記把檔案帶去，結果激怒了對方。或許此刻那些檔案已經不在喬那裡，而是被威脅他的人拿走了。唯一弄清楚此事的方法就是持續關注喬，就像喬在關注那個跑來找警探談話的女人一樣。

en_text: Like everybody else, Sally has heard the rumors flying around the station. This woman has seen something that might bring the case to a close. Perhaps then Joe will be safe.

en_text: Watching Joe watching the woman was unnerving. His fascination was so obvious that at one point Sally was sure he must have known her. But of course he was just learning what he could, so he would have something to tell his tormentor to save him from another attack.
zh_text: 看著喬盯著那個女人給她一種不安的感覺。他專注的程度明顯到讓莎莉覺得他一定認識那個女人。不過他當然只是在想辦法探聽消息而已，好回去告訴折磨他的人，以免再度遭受毆打。

en_text: Standing outside, watching Joe from the corner where he can't see her, she cannot understand why he would have approached the woman, but she will keep on watching until she can finally help Joe out of whatever mess he has got into.

en_text: "Take a seat, Joe." She keeps a tight hold of her smile.
zh_text: 「請坐，喬。」她臉上笑容不減。

en_text: "You still upset with me? Come on, Joe. It's time to move on."
zh_text: 「你還在生我的氣？拜託，喬，人生總要繼續走下去。」

en_text: "Quite the job you have, Joe." I shrug. I see where she's going with this, but force her to carry on.
zh_text: 你的工作不錯，喬。我聳肩。我知道她想說什麼，不過還是讓她繼續下去。

en_text: "The cleaner at the police station. That must allow you access to some privileged information—evidence, reports, photographs. It must be fun seeing where the investigations are going. Tell me, did you ever want to become a cop? Did you try and fail? Or not try because you knew they'd realize what sick thoughts you harbored?"
zh_text: 「警局清潔工。這讓你有辦法接觸一般人無法接觸的資料——證據、報告、照片。觀察調查發展的感覺一定很棒。告訴我，你有沒有想過當警察？你是不是試過，結果失敗了？或是沒有嘗試，因為你知道他們會發現你腦中那些變態思想？」

en_text: "How about you, Melissa? Did you ever try?" "Do you ever try to contaminate the evidence?"
zh_text: 「妳呢，梅莉莎？妳有嘗試過嗎？」「你有試過竄改證據嗎？」

en_text: If this is all she has to say, then I'm not in any trouble. "You're jealous." "Of you?" "Of me working among all those cops, all that information."
zh_text: 如果她想問的只有這些，那我就可以放心了。「妳在嫉妒？」「嫉妒你？」「嫉妒我跟這麼多警察一起工作，能夠取得這麼多資訊。」

en_text: "Of you?" "Of me working among all those cops, all that information." She raises her left hand to her lips and begins rubbing her finger slowly back and forth, the same way she did the other night. She moistens her finger and keeps rubbing. Then she quickly pulls it away, brushes it against her chest on the way down, and rests it in her lap.
zh_text: 「嫉妒我跟這麼多警察一起工作，能夠取得這麼多資訊。」她伸起左手，將手指放入雙唇之間輕輕吸吮，就像那天晚上一樣。她吮濕了手指，然後繼續吸吮。接著她迅速抽出手指，掠過她的胸口，最後放上大腿。

en_text: "We're not that different, you and I, Joe." "I doubt that." "Do you notice the smell in there?"
zh_text: 「我們沒有那麼大的不同，你和我，喬。「你有注意到那裡的味道嗎？」

en_text: "What smell?" "Working there every day, you're probably used to it. But there's this smell in there. Smells slightly like sweat and damp blood, but it's power. Power and control."
zh_text: 「什麼味道？」你每天都在警局工作，或許已經習以爲常。那裡有股味道。有點像汗，有點像血，不過那是權力的味道。權力與支配。

en_text: "It's the air-conditioning." "It was fun in there today, Joe. I got to see something you see every day. Seems like menial work for somebody like yourself."
zh_text: 「那是空调的味道。」「今天在警局很有趣，喬。我有機會見識你每天都能看到的東西。那份工作對你這種人來說似乎有點低賤。」

en_text: "It was fun in there today, Joe. I got to see something you see every day. Seems like menial work for somebody like yourself." "I do it for the love of the job."
zh_text: 「今天在警局很有趣，喬。我有機會見識你每天都能看到的東西。那份工作對你這種人來說似乎有點低賤。」「我做這份工作是因為我熱愛這份工作。

en_text: "Does it pay well?"
zh_text: 「薪水優嗎？」

en_text: "Does it need to?" "You know what confuses me?" she asks.
zh_text: 「需要優嗎？」「你知道最讓我困擾的是什麼嗎？」

en_text: "Several things?" Her smile stretches. "How you can afford an expensive gun, nice clothes, a good watch, yet you live in a rat hole of an apartment." I hate the fact that she's been in my apartment. I hate the fact that this is the woman who tidied up my messy wound. No way in hell am I going to thank her for that. "I have a good accountant."
zh_text: 「有很多地方讓妳困擾？」她微笑擴大。「就是在有能力購買昂貴手槍、上好服飾、精美手錶的情況下，你卻依然住在那種破爛地方。」我不喜歡她到過我家這個事實。我不喜歡幫我療傷的就是這個女人。我打死都不會向她道謝的。「我有個高明的會計師。」

en_text: "It pays the bills."
zh_text: 足以支付帳單。

en_text: "What's your point?"
zh_text: 「妳到底想說什麼？」

en_text: "My point is you must have some money stored away." "I have a couple of hundred dollars. Why?"
zh_text: 我想說你一定藏了不少錢。「我是有幾百塊錢。幹嘛？」

en_text: "Bullshit, Joe. How much you got?" "I just told you."
zh_text: 「狗屁，喬。你到底有多少錢？」「我剛剛說了。」

en_text: "No you didn't. It's time you were honest with your partner, Joe."
zh_text: 「不，你沒有。你該對你的夥伴坦白，喬。」

en_text: "What?" I ask, and suddenly I know what game we're playing. "You heard," she says.
zh_text: 「什麼？」我問，我突然知道我們在玩什麼遊戲了。「你聽到了。」

en_text: "Obviously I didn't."
zh_text: 「顯然沒有。」

en_text: She rolls her head back and laughs. Hard. This really pisses me off. Nobody's laughed at me like that since those days at school when the laughter accompanied the words Numb Nuts everywhere I went. Other people are looking around. Nothing I can do but wait her out. Finally she finishes. "We're partners, Joe, whether you like it or not. Especially after what I've just done for you."
zh_text: 她仰頭大笑。笑得很用力。這下真把我給惹毛了。自從學校那段走到哪裡都被人一邊嘲笑一邊叫我「麻痺蛋蛋」日子以來，我再也沒有被人這樣笑過了。旁邊的人轉頭來看。我什麼都不能做，只能等她笑完。最後她終於笑完了。「我們是夥伴，喬，不管你喜不喜歡。特別在我爲你做了那件事後。」

zh_text: 「什麼事？」

zh_text: 冷靜點，大傢伙。我描述的是另外一個人的長相。「爲什麼？」我知道答案：因爲她要錢。「爲什麼不呢？」

en_text: "Stop being so damn evasive," I say.
zh_text: 不要一直逃避問題。我說。

en_text: "I can imagine. You know," she says, "it was nice to go in there and talk to the detectives, to see for myself just how smart they really are, or, in this case, just how smart they aren't. en_text: "I'm not sure there's anybody like you and me," I say.
zh_text: 我不確定世界上還有像妳和我這種人。」我說。

en_text: "So why did you do it? Why go in there?"
zh_text: 「那妳爲什麼要那麼做？爲什麼要去警局？」
