en_text: Sure. It isn't the only thing that goes without saying. Obviously I'm going to kill this woman at some point. I just need to do my homework first. That's something I'm good at. Life's all about homework. And I have until Friday at five o'clock to get my assignment done. She starts telling me the rules of her game. I'm to charge the phone when I get home because she'll be in touch. She reminds me that she still has my gun, which has my fingerprints on it. It can be used as a future murder weapon. She tells me she wiped my fingerprints off the knife before telling the police where they could find it, but it doesn't brighten this nightmare. After she walks away, I stare at the water, drumming my fingers against the top of my briefcase while watching the birds. I tap some rhythm that I've never heard before. It seems my life is following that rhythm. Some of the ducks look back at me. Perhaps they want money too.
zh_text: 當然。這並非唯一不需要提醒的事情。顯然我必須找機會殺死這個女人。我只是得先做點功課。這是我很擅長的事情。人生就是不斷地做功課。而這份功課得在禮拜五五點之前做完。她開始說明她的遊戲規則。我回家後必須將手機充電，因為她會跟我聯絡。她提醒我槍還在她手中，上面還有我的指紋。那把槍未來可能成爲謀殺兇器。她說她在告訴警方上哪兒去找我的刀前已經抹除了刀上的指紋，不過這並沒有解除這場惡夢。她離開後，我注視著河面，一邊看鳥一邊用手指敲打公事包。我敲著我從未聽過的節奏，我的生活彷彿都跟著這個節奏在走。有些鴨子回應我的目光，或許牠們也想要錢。

en_text: One hundred thousand dollars is an amount I can't fully comprehend, and I already know I'll never be able to raise it. Does Melissa know that too? Even if by some miracle I could get the money, nothing is stopping her from asking me for more in another year, or another month, or even another day.
zh_text: 十萬塊是一筆超過我理解範圍的大錢，我也很清楚我絕不可能籌到這筆錢。梅莉莎是不是也知道這一點？就算奇蹟出現，我弄到了這筆錢，誰知道她會不會在一年後又來煩我，或是一個月後，甚至是隔天。

en_text: The bus driver is some bored forty-year-old guy who wears a hearing aid and yells Hello at me as I get on, and Have a nice day when I leave, even though the day is winding down. When I get home the light on my answering machine is flashing. I push it, only to hear my mother's voice, insisting I go around there for dinner tonight. When she insists, it's best I go. She also tells me Walt Chadwick called and asked her out for dinner. She's accepted, and tells me of their entire phone call until my machine eagerly runs out of tape. When I open the bathroom door the cat races out, and I feel bad because I'd actually forgotten about him. I take a shower, clean myself up, and dress in tidy clothes, hoping Mom won't be able to find anything in my appearance to complain about. I put the cat back into the bathroom when I finish, making him a promise that I'll pick up some food later on tonight. I steal a car and park a block away from Mom's house. The sound of the beach brings a smile to my face. I imagine walking down there and going for a swim. I don't imagine hard enough to get wet.
zh_text: 公車司機是個四十來歲的無趣男子，戴著助聽器，在我上車時對我大喊哈囉，又在我下車時大聲祝我有個愉快的一天。當我到家時，答錄機的燈閃個不停。我按下按鈕，聽到我媽的聲音堅持要我今晚過去吃飯。每當她堅持時，我最好還是過去一趟。她也告訴我華特·查德維克打電話來約她吃飯。她同意了，然後把電話裡的內容通通講一遍，直到我的答錄機迫不及待地用光錄音帶爲止。我打開浴室門，那隻貓立刻衝出，我覺得有點過意不去，因為我完全忘記牠的存在。我沖了個澡，梳洗乾淨，然後換上整齊的服裝，希望媽沒辦法挑剔我的打扮。弄好之後，我把貓放回浴室，向牠保證晚上會帶吃的回來。我偷了輛車，停在距離我媽家一條街外的地方。海灘的聲音令我面露微笑，我想像自己在海灘上漫步，以及下海游泳的樣子。不過我並不想當真弄濕自己。

en_text: I'm halfway to the door when Mom opens it and comes outside. She looks better than I've seen her in years. Before I can even say anything, she's hugging me. I hug her back—while subtly shielding my crotch—to stop her from clipping me over the ear. "I'm so happy to see you, Joe."
zh_text: 快到門口時，老媽開門出來。她看起來比過去幾年更有精神。在我開口之前，她將我一把抱住。我也抱著她——巧妙地擋住胯下——以免她抱得太緊。「真高興見到你，喬。」

en_text: She pulls away from me, but keeps her hands on my shoulders. "Walt's taking me out to lunch tomorrow. You know, I haven't seen Walt since the funeral, and your father's been gone six years now."
zh_text: 她鬆開我，不過雙手還是搭在我的肩膀上。「華特明天要帶我出去吃午飯。你知道，葬禮過後我就沒有見過華特，而你爸已經去世六年了。」

en_text: "Eight years, Mom." "Time does fly," she says, then leads me inside.
zh_text: 「八年了，媽。」「時光飛逝。」她說，然後帶我進去。

en_text: It flies when you're having fun. I can't see how it could have flown for Mom, though. "So where are you going?" I ask. "He hasn't told me. Said it's a surprise. He's picking me up around eleven o'clock."
zh_text: 時光會在人快樂的時候飛逝。不過我看不出媽的時間爲什麼會飛逝。「你們要上哪兒去？」我問。「他沒告訴我。說是驚喜。他會在十一點左右過來接我。」

en_text: "He hasn't told me. Said it's a surprise. He's picking me up around eleven o'clock." "That's good."
zh_text: 「他沒告訴我。說是驚喜。他會在十一點左右過來接我。」「那很好。」

en_text: "I'm going to go like this." She twirls around to show me her dress, an ugly thing with long sleeves that looks like it's been made from recycled sackcloth, then dipped in blood. "What do you think?" "I can't remember the last time you looked so good, or so happy, Mom."
zh_text: 「我打算穿這樣。」她旋轉一圈，讓我看清楚她的衣服，醜得要命，袖子看起來像用回收麻布做出來後再拿去泡血。「你覺得如何？」「我想不起來上次看妳這麼開心、這麼美麗是什麼時候，媽。」

en_text: "You're saying I never look happy?"
zh_text: 「你是說我一直都不開心？」

en_text: "I'm not saying that at all."
zh_text: 「我完全不是那個意思。」

en_text: She frowns. "So, you're saying I never look any good, then."
zh_text: 她皺眉。「那你是說我一直都不美麗了？」

en_text: "I'm not saying that either."
zh_text: 「我也不是那個意思。」

en_text: "Then what are you saying, Joe?" she snaps. "That I don't deserve to be happy?" "I'm not trying to say anything," I say, "other than you look really nice. I'm sure Walt will be thrilled." I manage to say the right thing, because her face breaks out in a smile. "You think so?"
zh_text: 那你是什麼意思，喬？」她大聲道。「我沒資格過快樂的日子？「我什麼意思都沒有。」我說。「除了妳看起來很美。我敢肯定華特會很開心的。」我終於說對話了，因為她臉上露出一絲微笑。「你這麼認爲？」

en_text: "He'd be crazy not to think so."
zh_text: 「他要不開心的話肯定是瘋了。」

en_text: "A problem? With what?"
zh_text: 「意見？什麼意見？」

en_text: "And I'm only going to lunch with Walt. I'm not marrying him. I'm not asking you to call him Dad." "I know that."
zh_text: 「而我只是跟華特去吃個午飯。我不是要嫁給他。我不是要你叫他爸爸。」「我知道。」

en_text: She leans forward, and instead of hitting me, she hugs me again. "We have you to thank for this, Joe," she whispers. "If it wasn't for you, he would never have called." She dishes dinner. Instead of meatloaf, she's cooked up one of the chickens she bought on special last week. It's too damn big for two people, but she'll throw half of it into the fridge as leftovers. Thankfully she's cooked the chicken to perfection. It's one thing my mother manages to get right. It's juicy and full of flavor, and chicken fat starts dripping down my fingers.
zh_text: 她湊上前來，不是要打我，而是又來抱我。「這都得要歸功於你，喬。」她低聲道。「要不是你的話，他絕對不會打電話來。」她端出晚餐。今天不吃烤肉餅，而是上禮拜特價的雞肉。那隻雞大到兩個人根本吃不完，不過她會把剩菜丟回冰箱。幸虧她燒得一手好雞。那是我媽唯一做對的事情。那隻雞香嫩多汁，雞油自我的指尖滴落。

en_text: "I'll ring you tomorrow night, Joe, and tell you all about our lunch." "Uh huh."
zh_text: 「我明天晚上打電話給你，喬，告訴你午餐的事情。」

en_text: "Maybe this weekend the three of us can go out for dinner. Would you like that?" "Sure. That'd be nice," I say, unable to think of anything worse. I clutch at a napkin Mom gave me. She's always saying I'm a sloppy eater. She takes the empty plates and begins to clean up. I wrap some chicken into a napkin and put it into my briefcase for the cat. My hands are covered in chicken fat. "I'm just going to wash my hands, okay, Mom?"
zh_text: 「嗯哼。」「或許這個週末我們三個可以共進晚餐。你想要嗎？」「當然。那樣很好。」我說，完全想不出比這更糟糕的事情。我接過媽遞來的一條餐巾。她總是說我吃相很難看。她清空餐桌，開始洗碗。我拿餐巾包了點雞肉，放進公事包給貓吃。我的手上都是雞油。

en_text: "Good boy, Joe."
zh_text: 「好孩子，喬。」

en_text: I walk to the bathroom, eating a piece of chicken on the way. Stepping past the toilet brings images of her sitting in there with her nightgown hitched up around her waist, her glasses resting on the tip of her nose as she puts a few more pieces of her jigsaw puzzle into place. I crouch to my knees and hang my head, focus my eyes on the bath mat. The nausea starts to fade. When I turn on the bathroom light, my hand slips from the switch. I pull back the shower curtain. Mom has one of those combined shower baths, but she always uses the shower. I try to turn on the tap, but my hands keep slipping off it, so I crouch down and begin smearing the chicken fat at the end of the bath instead. I spend a minute spreading it out, covering a good-sized area. It comes off my fingers easily enough, and off my palms. It's clear too, so Mom won't notice the mess. The only way she'll see it is if the angle and light are just right. I eat the rest of the chicken. It's cold now. I grab the tap, and this time it turns easily enough. I wash my hands, then head back to the kitchen.
zh_text: 我前往浴室，邊走邊吃一塊雞。走過馬桶就讓我想到她穿著沾了大便的睡衣坐在上面，戴著眼鏡拼拼圖的模樣。我蹲在地上，垂頭喪氣，注視地毯。噁心感開始消失。打開浴室燈時，我的手在開關上滑了一下。我拉開浴簾。媽的浴室有淋浴又有澡盆，不過她總是用淋浴的。我試著打開水龍頭，不過我的手一直滑開，於是我蹲下去，把雞油擦在澡盆裡。我花了一分鐘的時間塗抹均勻，把澡盆弄得油油的。雞油輕易離開我的手指及掌心。油是透明的，所以老媽不會發現。除非角度跟光線剛好才有可能看見。我吃掉剩下的雞塊。雞已經冷了。我握住水龍頭，這一次輕鬆轉開。我洗了洗手，然後走回廚房。

en_text: "Walt was so nice on the phone, Joe." Walt. I'm regretting letting him go. "He seemed nice, Mom."
zh_text: 「華特在電話裡很有禮貌，喬。」華特。我有點後悔放過他了。「他似乎不錯，媽。」

en_text: I sit at the dining table while she finishes off the dishes. I offer to dry them, but she says no. I keep watching her, wondering how this could be the woman who gave me life. How can she think I'm gay? What have I done to this woman to make her possibly think that? I'm her son, and she won't even give me the benefit of the doubt.
zh_text: 我坐在餐桌上等她清洗餐盤。我說要幫忙擦乾，不過她拒絕了。我一直看著她，懷疑我怎麼可能是這個女人的。她怎麼會以為我是同性戀？我對這個女人做了什麼事情居然讓她以為我是同性戀？我是她兒子，而她竟然不由分說就認定我是同性戀。

en_text: I'm not gay, Mom. I'm not gay. She drones on about Walt for another hour or so before finally letting me leave. As I stand on the doorstep, surrounded by night and the sound of the beach and by the muggy air touching my damp skin, I glance up at the stars, all of them overlooking my mother. One day her spirit will be floating up there, finding Heaven and finding God. She'll be off to talk to Dad again.
zh_text: 我不是同性戀，媽。我不是同性戀。她語氣單調地講了一小時華特的事情，然後終於讓我離開。當我站在門口台階上，身處夜色、海灘的聲音以及悶熱的空氣中時，我抬頭望向星空，它們全都在看顧著我媽。有一天，她的靈魂將會飄上天空，找到天堂，找到上帝。到時候她就能再度跟老爸聊天了。

en_text: I start grinning. Both God and Dad are going to be in for a hard time. I give her a hug before I go. I'll miss her.
zh_text: 我開始微笑。到時候上帝和老爸的日子就不好過了。我離開前抱了她一下。我會想念她的。

en_text: I park the same stolen car a block from home. Friday is quickly approaching and . . . Jesus Christ! I drop my briefcase and run over to the goldfish bowl. Some of the knives slip out of their restraints and they sound like drum cymbals being smashed. I put both hands onto the glass bowl. The water inside is murky. A few dozen scales are floating on the surface. I thrust my hand in and grope for either of my fish and, while I'm searching, I find them with my eyes. One is in front of my bed. The other near the kitchen. Each is covered in bloodless scratches. Melissa's message is obvious. I make my way over to Pickle when the cat runs out from beneath the bed, hooks the dead fish in its claws, fires it across the room, chases it, gets it in its mouth, then runs back toward the bed. The fish falls from its mouth, but the cat keeps on running, either knowing it's been spotted and is about to be in a world of trouble, or still thinking it has the fish in its mouth. Either way, it's running as if its leg was never broken, and I realize that Melissa hasn't done this at all.
zh_text: 我將同一輛偷來的車停在我家一條街口外。禮拜五很快就會來臨，而……耶穌基督啊！我丢下我的公事包，衝到金魚缸前。幾把刀滑出刀套，聽起來像是銅鈸砸爛的聲音。我雙手捧著玻璃魚缸。裡面的水十分混濁。幾打魚鱗漂在水面上。我伸手進去尋找我的魚，而在我摸索的同時，我看見了他們。一隻在我床前。另外一隻在廚房附近。兩隻身上都有不帶血的傷痕。梅莉莎的意思十分明顯。我朝向泡菜走去，那隻貓突然衝出床底，伸爪去抓死魚，將他撞到另外一邊，跟著連忙追上，將魚一口叼起，然後朝向床鋪奔回。魚從貓嘴裡滑落，不過牠繼續奔跑，要嘛就是知道牠被我盯上而且麻煩大了，不然就是以爲魚還在嘴裡。無論如何，牠跑得一副好像腳從來沒有斷過的樣子，我終於了解這件事情根本不是梅莉莎幹的。

en_text: "Fucking cat," I yell, striding over to Pickle and kneeling down next to him. He looks dead. I pick him up—he's cold, but fish are cold anyway, right? I carry him over to the fishbowl and drop him in, hoping I have him back there in time. I pick up Jehovah, and carry her over and drop her in. Pickle is already floating on his side. A few seconds later, Jehovah joins him.
zh_text: 「天殺的貓。」我吼道，大步走向泡菜，跪倒在他身邊。他看起來已經死了。我撿起他——身體冰冷，不過魚本來就很冰冷，不是嗎？我帶他回到魚缸，放他進去，希望還來得及。我也撿起耶和華，帶她回到水中。泡菜已經側身漂在水面上。片刻過後，耶和華也加入他。

en_text: I swirl them around in the water, pushing them forward into a forced swim, and then I press on their little chests, and even though it seems none of this is of any use, I persist for another ten minutes before finally giving up. I whirl around and face the bed. This fucking expensive cat has killed my two best friends. I storm over, grip the edges of the bed, and lift it up on its side. A whole bunch of crap falls onto the floor. The mattress slides off and so do all the sheets. My groin is starting to hurt, but not as much as my heart. The cat looks up at me with shock, its head is tilted and its eyes wide open. When I lean down to pick it up, it backs away. Its ears are pricked back and it looks ready to kill me. I lean forward and try to stomp on its back, but it sees this and stops just before me, forcing me to stretch forward to correct my aim, and as I do, my groin screams out in pain. I stomp on the floor where the cat has just been, and the shooting pain in my phantom testicle drops me to my knees.
zh_text: 我伸手在魚缸裡轉圈，強迫他們自動游泳，然後我輕壓他們的小胸口，儘管這些作法看起來都毫無用處，我還是又搞了十分鐘才終於放棄。我轉過身去，面對床鋪。這隻貴得要命的貓害死了我最好的兩個朋友。我衝上前去，抓起床緣，用力掀開。一大堆東西掉到地上。床墊滑落，所有床單也一樣。我的胯下又痛起來，不過完全比不上我的心痛。貓神情驚恐地抬頭看我，腦袋微側，雙眼圓睜。我彎下腰去抓牠，牠後退。牠的耳朵向後豎起，一副準備殺我的模樣。我身體後傾，試圖踩牠的背，不過牠察覺我的動作，在我面前止步，迫使我必須向前修正這一腳的落點，而這麼做的同時，我的胯下傳來劇痛。我一腳踩在那隻貓原先的位置，那顆鬼睪丸所帶來的劇痛令我跪倒在地。

en_text: Puss stops in the center of the room and sits down. He looks at me silently. His ears are no longer pricked back. I loosely cup my remaining testicle. Okay. Time to change tactics.
zh_text: 貓咪停在房間中央坐下。牠沉默地看著我。耳朵不再豎起。我輕輕捧著僅存的睪丸。好吧，該是改變策略的時候了。

en_text: "Here, kitty. Come on, fella. I just want to pet you." I start clicking my Goddamn fingers because it seems to be the sort of thing that cats like. I keep clicking them, and in my mind a movie plays with me in the leading role, wringing the stupid cat's neck. The cat must be watching the same movie, because it won't come near me. I make my way toward my briefcase. Both the cat and I look at the knife I pull out, and both of us know what it can do. It knows I'm about to test the adage and see just how many ways I can skin the little bastard. I can see the reflection of my eyes in the blade. For a few seconds I just keep looking at them, and all I can think of is how I have my father's eyes. Thinking of Dad makes me feel suddenly sadder at losing those I love, and then I get angry at the cat for making me feel sad.
zh_text: 「來吧，貓咪。過來，小夥子。我只是想拍拍你。」我開始彈我天殺的手指，因為那似乎是貓咪會喜歡的動作。我一直彈著手指，腦中播放一部電影，我是電影裡的主角，正在掐死那隻蠢貓。那隻貓肯定在看同一部電影，因為牠不肯靠近我。我走向我的公事包。貓跟我一起看著我拔出的那把刀，我們也都很清楚那把刀能做些什麼。牠知道我打算測試一下那句諺語，看看我能用多少方法剝掉那個小混蛋的皮。我可以在刀面上看見我雙眼的倒影。接下來幾秒內，我就這麼看著它們，腦中唯一想到的就是我的眼睛多像我爸。想到老爸就讓我突然間對於失去所愛感到更加悲哀，接著我又爲了讓我悲哀而更氣那隻貓。

en_text: "Good boy. Come on." I keep clicking my fingers. The cat meows. Then I throw the knife. I'm quick. The knife is quick. The cat's even quicker. The blade digs into the floor exactly where he'd been sitting a split second earlier. Then he turns his back on me and slowly walks back over to the bed. I'm making my way to the knife when the phone rings. I don't want to answer it. All I want to do is kill this Goddamn cat. My testicle hurts like hell. The phone keeps ringing, and ringing.
zh_text: 「好孩子。過來。」我不停彈著手指。貓叫了一聲。接著我射出飛刀。我動作很快。刀飛得很快。不過貓閃得更快。刀刃插入片刻之前牠所坐的地板。跟著牠轉身背對我，慢慢走回床下。我正要過去拔刀的時候，電話鈴突然響起。我不想去接。我一心只想殺死那隻可惡的貓。我的睾丸痛得要命。電話繼續響，不停響。

en_text: I pick up the knife and throw it toward the cat, and the cat darts forward a second later without a knife protruding from him. He looks back up at me.
zh_text: 我拔起刀，射向貓，片刻過後，貓向前一閃，沒有中刀。牠回頭看我。

en_text: "I'm going to kill you, you little bastard."
zh_text: 「我一定要殺了你，你這個小混蛋。」

en_text: The cat hisses at me.
zh_text: 貓對我嘶嘶叫。

en_text: The phone keeps ringing. It's giving me a headache. Ring, ring, fucking ring. Why isn't the machine picking it up?
zh_text: 電話繼續響。聽得我頭都痛了。鈴，鈴，媽的鈴。答錄機為什麼沒有接聽？

en_text: I pick up another knife, then carefully make my way to my feet. The pain in my groin is going. I walk slowly over to the phone. It has stopped ringing and the answering machine is recording a message. The volume is turned down and I can't hear it. I interrupt the message.
zh_text: 我拔出另外一把刀，小心翼翼地站起身來。胯下還在痛。我緩緩走到電話旁。鈴聲已經停了，答錄機正在錄製訊息。聲音調低了，所以我聽不見。我打斷錄音。

en_text: "Hello?" I say, hoping that my goldfish are the only things I am losing today, but my gut instinct is that something has happened to Mom. That premonition is back, riding my inner thoughts. Why must life be so cruel to those I love? And why must those I love betray me? I took the cat in and gave it a home, and in return it has done this to me. "Joe? Hi, this is Jennifer."
zh_text: 一哈囉？」我說，希望金魚是我今天唯一失去的東西，不過我的預感告訴我說媽出事了。那股預感乘著我的內心思緒回來了。爲什麼生活要對我所深愛的人們如此殘酷？而我所深愛的人們又爲什麼會要背叛我？我收養那隻貓，給牠一個家，結果牠竟然這樣回報我。「喬？嗨，我是珍妮佛。」

en_text: Jennifer? How does she know my mother? "What can I help you with, Jennifer?" I hear myself asking. "You're not going to believe this, but we've just found the owner of the cat!"
zh_text: 珍妮佛？她怎麼會認識我媽？「有什麼事嗎，珍妮佛？」我聽見自己問道。「你不會相信這種事的，不過我們剛剛找到那隻貓的主人了！」

en_text: She sounds excited. I look over to my bed. The cat is still sitting there. I take aim with the knife. "Really." This means my mother is still alive and well. Thank God! "Really! Isn't that exciting?"
zh_text: 她聽起來很興奮。我看向我的床。那隻貓依然坐在那裡。我舉刀瞄準。「真的。」這表示我媽還好好活著。感謝上帝。「真的！這不是很棒嗎？」

en_text: "Really." This means my mother is still alive and well. Thank God! "Really! Isn't that exciting?" "The cat isn't here anymore," I say, wondering how hard I need to throw the knife to pin him to the floor. "What do you mean?"
zh_text: 「真的。」這表示我媽還好好活著。感謝上帝。「真的！這不是很棒嗎？」「那隻貓已經不在我這裡了。」我說，計算著我要丟多大力才能把貓釘在地板上。「什麼意思？」

en_text: "I gave him away to one of my neighbors." "Can't you get him back?"
zh_text: 「我把他送给我的鄰居了。」「不能要回來嗎？」

en_text: "Well, the thing is it kind of ran away." I'm still talking, but hardly listening to her or even to myself. My brain's on automatic. I can't take my eyes from the Goddamn cat, and all I can think about is Dad. Dad killing himself. Dad being found locked inside his car. "You're kidding," Jennifer says, and for the first time she doesn't sound like she's desperate to see me naked. I look from the fishbowl to the cat.
zh_text: 「這個，問題在於牠跑掉了。」我還在說話，不過幾乎沒在聽她講話，甚至也沒聽我在講些什麼。我的腦子在自行運作。我沒辦法將目光自那隻天殺的貓身上移開，不過我腦中想的卻只有我爸。老爸殺了自己，老爸死在上鎖的車裡。你在開玩笑。」珍妮佛說，這是第一次她聽起來不像是想要把我剝光的樣子。我看向魚缸，然後又看回那隻貓。

en_text: "It gets worse," I say. "Worse? Did you say worse? How?"
zh_text: 「還有更糟糕的。」「更糟？你說更糟？」

en_text: "Well, it didn't just run away. It ran out into traffic." No way in hell is she getting the cat back. It represents too much. Melissa betrayed me. Dad betrayed me. I won't be beaten by an animal with a brain a tenth the size of mine.
zh_text: 「這個，牠不光只是跑掉而已。牠直接跑到馬路上去。」我絕對不會讓她把貓要回去。牠在我心中代表重大的意義。梅莉莎背叛我。爸背叛我。我絕對不會敗在一隻腦袋只有我十分之一的動物手上。

en_text: "Is this for real, Joe? Or are you trying to keep the cat?"
zh_text: 「你是說真的嗎，喬？還是只想留下貓？」

en_text: "If you don't believe me, you can come and dig the damn thing up out of the yard!"
zh_text: 「如果你不相信我，妳可以把那隻可惡的東西從花園裡挖出來！」「沒有必要……」

en_text: "There's no need—" "I hate meatloaf!" I scream, and she hangs up on me without another word. Guess I won't be seeing any more of Jennifer.
zh_text: 「我恨烤肉餅！」我大叫，她二話不說掛斷電話。看來我再也別想看到珍妮佛了。

en_text: Rather than throwing the knife, I decide to take another crack at being nice to the cat in hopes of getting near it. I glance at my fishbowl. The murky water is dead still. This is what I get for trying to be a good person, a caring person. "Come on, pussycat. Come and see Joe."
zh_text: 我決定別丟飛刀，再來試試扮演好好先生，想辦法接近牠。我看向我的金魚缸。污濁的水完全靜止。這就是我嘗試當個好人、關懷動物的下場。「來嘛，小貓咪。來看看喬。」

en_text: "Come on. Come on. That's a good boy." I'm nearly there. I start to reach out with the knife. I'm going to teach it a lesson it will never forget. It moves into a standing position. "Come on. It's okay." Then the bastard runs. I bring the knife down hard and fast, but miss as it scoots around me. It heads toward the kitchen.
zh_text: 「來嘛，來嘛。真是個好孩子。」我只差一點了。我開始提起刀。我要好好教訓教訓這個傢伙。牠立起身來。

en_text: I throw the knife at the cat as it skids on the floor, changes direction, darts past my briefcase, and heads for freedom. This time the blade sails just over the cat's head and sticks into the door. He stops in the doorway, looks over at me, gives a meowing sound that makes me want to spend the next twelve hours stomping the life out of him, and then he's gone. I get to my feet, race to the door, and look out into the corridor. If I had the ability, I would run after it, but my groin is throbbing and possibly bleeding. I close the door, slump onto the sofa, and stare at the goldfish bowl. Pickle and Jehovah are still floating on the surface. I can't tell who is who. And as I stare, my eyes mist over. I allow myself to cry. There's no shame in crying. I will find that cat. I will find it and kill it. I swear. I get up and move into the kitchenette. The night is young, and even though I'm suffering from setbacks, I need to push myself forward. My eyes are blurry from tears and sore from being rubbed. I'm shivering even though it has to be ninety degrees in here. I hang up the phone, pull the bed back onto its legs, and tidy up.
zh_text: 我在牠打滑轉彎，衝過我的公事包，朝向自由邁進的時候射出飛刀。這一次刀掠過貓的腦袋，插在門板上。牠在門口停步，回頭看我一眼，發出一聲讓我很想花十二個小時把牠踩扁的貓叫，然後消失在門後。我起身衝往門口，看著門外的走廊。跑得動的話，我一定會去追牠，但是我的胯下在抽痛，很可能有流血。我關上門，癱坐在沙發上，楞楞地看著金魚缸。泡菜和耶和華依然浮在水面上。我無法分辨誰是誰。看著看著，我的視線開始模糊。我容許自己哭泣。哭泣並不丢人。我會找出那隻貓。我會把牠找出來殺掉。我發誓。我起身步入小廚房。時間還早，儘管遭受挫敗，我還是必須勇往直前。我的雙眼因為淚水而模糊，也因爲揉太用力而痠痛。室溫起碼三十度，不過我還是渾身發抖。我掛上電話，將床放回原位，整理床單被單。我唯一能做的就是繼續過活。泡菜和耶和華會希望我這麼做的。

en_text: I pour the murky water from the fishbowl down the sink. Dad keeps coming into my thoughts, and I wish he'd just leave me alone. I scoop my goldfish into a clear plastic bag, then tie it shut before heading downstairs. In the front lawn of this apartment complex—and the word lawn is being generous—I pull aside some of the weeds, then use my hands to dig a hole. I put the plastic bag inside, then scoop dirt back over it. I could easily have flushed Jehovah and Pickle away, but I did not want to insult their memories by having their bodies float around for eternity with pieces of shit. I pat the dirt down nice and tight before saying some words over the piece of ground where my friends lie. My eyes fill with tears. I swear revenge on their grave. I look for the cat, and though I can't find it, I can feel its eyes on me. After digging the dirt out from beneath my nails, I manage to get into bed early, which is the only good thing to happen to me all night. I dream of death, but of whose, I can't be sure.
zh_text: 我將魚缸中的濁水倒入水槽。老爸不斷進入我的思緒，我真希望他能讓我靜一靜。我將我的金魚放入透明塑膠袋裡，綁好後走向樓下。站在這棟公寓大樓的花園裡，說花園純粹是好聽，我清開一片雜草，用手挖了個坑。我將塑膠袋放進去，然後把土撥回坑裡。我可以隨手將耶和華和泡菜放到馬桶裡沖掉，但是我不希望他們的屍體永遠和屎尿漂在一起。我將土壓實，然後朝我朋友長眠的地方說了幾句話。我眼中盈滿淚水。我在他們的墳前發誓一定要報仇。我尋找那隻貓，雖然找不到牠，但是我可以感覺到牠的目光。在清完指甲縫裡的土後，我提早上床睡覺，這就是今晚唯一發生在我身上的好事。我夢到死亡，但是死的是誰，我不確定。

en_text: Sally wouldn't mind living on a street like this. Every night she would leave her window open, listening as the ocean crashed against the shore. Every summer morning she could go for a swim before heading to work. She's sure the people living out here must be more laid back, more relaxed. Martin would have loved living out here, she thinks. He used to love the beach. Yesterday afternoon, she stayed by the corner of the police station just out of sight watching while Joe talked to the woman. She fought with the idea of approaching Joe and asking him straight out what was going on; she was also regretting the chance she'd passed up to look through Joe's briefcase. If the opportunity arises again, she will take it. Then she drove to the graveyard and, while standing above the grave of her dead brother, she concentrated less on grieving and more on Joe. She wanted to know, no, needed to know what was going on. She decided she couldn't wait. She apologized to Martin, promised him she would return the following day, and drove toward Joe's apartment. She was going to confront him. She had to, if she had any chance of helping him. Anyway, his stitches would need removing, and she had to give back the copy of his key she'd had made.
zh_text: 莎莉不介意住在這樣的街上。住在這裡的話她會每晚不關窗，聽著海浪打在沙灘上的聲音。每個夏日早晨她都可以趁上班前先去游泳。她認爲這裡的人必定都很悠閒，都很愜意。馬丁一定會喜歡住在這裡的，她想。他喜歡海灘。昨天下午，她待在警局的牆角偷看喬和那個女人交談。她壓抑著一股想要直接跑去問喬的衝動；她同時也很後悔自己當初沒有把握機會偷看喬的公事包。如果再度遇上這種機會，她會動手。接著她駕車前往墓園，站在死去弟弟的墳墓上時，她沒有花很多心思哀悼，反而都是在想喬。她很想知道，不，她必須知道究竟是怎麼回事。她認爲自己等不及了。她向馬丁道歉，保證隔天會再回來，然後開車前往喬的公寓。她打算直言相詢。她非這麼做不可，如果還想幫助他的話。反正他的縫線也該拆了，而且她也得要歸還她打的那把公寓鑰匙。

en_text: Only she didn't make it all the way there.
zh_text: 只不過她根本沒有開到他的公寓。

en_text: She drives her car slowly down the street, checking every few mailboxes, watching the numbers climb. Most of the houses look as though they're only a coat of paint away from being charming character homes. When the door she wants opens not long after she knocks, she knows immediately she has the right place. The resemblance is obvious. "I'm sorry, but I'm not buying," the woman says, and starts to close the door.
zh_text: 次日，她緩緩沿著馬路前進，沿途查看信箱，看著門排號碼數目轉變。大部分的房子看起來都像只要再上一層油漆就能展現迷人風格的房子。當希望開啓的門在她敲過片刻之後開啓之時，她立刻知道自己來對地方了。這個女人跟喬長得太像了。一很抱歉，但是我不買。」那個女人說，接著開始關門。

en_text: "I'm not selling anything," Sally quickly says, but the door doesn't slow down. "My name's Sally. I work with Joe, and I was hoping—" "Well, why didn't you say so," Joe's mother says, swinging the door open nice and wide. "I've never met any of Joe's friends. I'm Evelyn. Please, please, come inside. Would you like a drink? A Coke perhaps?"
zh_text: 「我不是來推銷的，」莎莉立刻說道，但是對方關門的速度並未減緩。「我叫莎莉，是喬的同事，我是希望……」「哎呀，怎麼不早說呢？」喬的母親說道，立刻敞開大門。「我從來沒有見過喬的朋友。我是愛弗琳。請、請、快請進。要喝東西嗎？或許來瓶可樂？」

en_text: "Sure. That'd be nice."
zh_text: 「當然。那太好了。」

en_text: "Why . . . thank you," Sally says, and nobody has ever said that to her before.
zh_text: ……謝謝妳。

en_text: "So what time is Joe getting here?" Evelyn asks. "Joe's coming here?"
zh_text: 「那麼喬什麼時候過來？」愛弗琳問。「喬要過來？」

en_text: "That's why you're here, isn't it? You're meeting Joe? It's a bit late for dinner, but I suppose I can still whip something up. Perhaps I'll call him and see if he's on his way."
zh_text: 「妳是來找他的，不是嗎？妳跟他約在這裡？現在吃晚餐有點晚了，不過我可以弄點東西。或許我可以打電話看看他過來了沒。」

en_text: Joe's mother pauses and the edges of her mouth turn downward. "I don't follow, dear."
zh_text: 「我不懂，親愛的。」

en_text: "About Joe? Whatever for?"
zh_text: 他媽皺眉。「喬的事？爲什麼？」

en_text: From the moment Sally looked through Joe's personal file earlier in the day to get his parents' address, she knew the questions his mother was going to ask. "I, well, there were a few things I wanted to talk to you about. I have some . . . concerns." Evelyn starts nodding, slowly, as if she is suddenly saddened by Sally's possible concerns. "I know what you mean, dear."
zh_text: 打從今天稍早莎莉從喬的個人資料中得知他父母的地址後，她就知道他媽會問這個問題。「我，呃，我有些事情想跟你談談。我有點……擔心。」愛弗琳開始點頭，慢慢點頭，彷彿她突然爲了莎莉所擔心的事情而悲傷起來。「我了解妳的意思，親愛的。」

en_text: Evelyn starts nodding, slowly, as if she is suddenly saddened by Sally's possible concerns. "I know what you mean, dear." "You do?"
zh_text: 愛弗琳開始點頭，慢慢點頭，彷彿她突然爲了莎莉所擔心的事情而悲傷起來。「我了解妳的意思，親愛的。」「妳了解？」

en_text: "I have concerns of my own," she says, the downturned features of her face softening. "Tell me, do you like my son?"
zh_text: 「我自己也有點擔心。告訴我，妳喜歡我兒子嗎？」

en_text: Evelyn starts nodding. "I always thought more women would like him, but he doesn't seem to have any interest in them. He's . . . special, you know."
zh_text: 我一直認爲會有其他女人喜歡他，但是他似乎對女人不感興趣。他有點……特別，妳知道。

en_text: "Oh? Your brother is that way?"
zh_text: 「喔？妳弟弟也是那樣？」

en_text: "He . . . is," she says, not saying was, because was has a finality about it that she doesn't want to think about right now.
zh_text: 「他……是。」她說，沒說「以前是」，因為「以前是」有種已成定局的感覺，而她此刻不願多想那種感覺。

en_text: "And you like Joe." "I like Joe a lot," Sally says.
zh_text: 「而妳喜歡喬。」我很喜歡喬。

en_text: "I like Joe a lot," Sally says. "That's good, dearie," Evelyn says, and she pops open the Coke she got for Sally and hands it over. "I like hearing that. It means there's still a chance for Joe."
zh_text: 我很喜歡喬。「那很好，親愛的。我喜歡聽妳這麼說。我是說喬還有機會。」

en_text: "That's good, dearie," Evelyn says, and she pops open the Coke she got for Sally and hands it over. "I like hearing that. It means there's still a chance for Joe." "But these concerns, well, I don't really know where to start." "We've already started, dearie."
zh_text: 「那很好，親愛的。我喜歡聽妳這麼說。我是說喬還有機會。」「但是我所擔心的事情，嗯，我不知道該從何說起。「我們已經開始說了，親愛的。」

en_text: "How long has Joe been able to drive?" "What was that, dear?"
zh_text: 「喬會開車多久了？」「什麼，親愛的？」

en_text: "Well, it doesn't, not exactly. But I saw him driving last night, and—" "He was coming to see me. He's such a good boy." "I know. It's obvious Joe has a big heart. He's really such a lovely guy. But I didn't know he could drive." "You didn't know he could drive?" Evelyn asks, sounding surprised. "I thought you said you work with him."
zh_text: 「這個，是無關，沒有直接關係。不過我昨晚有看到他開車，而且……」「他是來看我的。他是個好孩子。」我知道。喬的心胸寬大。他真是個很窩心的人。只是我不知道他會開車。「妳不知道他會開車？我以爲妳說他是同事。」

en_text: "I do work with him."
zh_text: 「我是他同事。」

en_text: Does Joe tell her he drives the police cars around? It would be the sort of big-kid thing he'd do. She doesn't want to spoil the illusion for Evelyn. It's bad enough just being here, invading his privacy. Even now she's fraught with guilt, and scared about how Joe will react. By trying to help him, she'll likely end up hurting him, and he'll likely end up hating her. "Sure. I was just curious as to how long he has been able to do it, that's all." Evelyn gives the statement a dismissive shrug. "I don't know," she says. "Years, I imagine. But what I'm more interested in is you, Sally. I take it you're not married?"
zh_text: 開警車嗎？難道喬告訴她說他開警車？這聽起來像是會做的。她不想戳穿愛弗琳的幻想。光是來這裡刺探喬的隱私就已經夠糟糕了。就連現在她也覺得滿心罪惡，並且深怕喬得知後的反應。試圖幫助他的結果很有可能會傷害他，而他最後也很可能會討厭她。「當然。我只是好奇他會開車多久了，如此而已。」「談談妳自己吧，莎莉。我想妳應該還沒結婚？」

en_text: Sally smiles. "No, no, not married," she says, and takes a mouthful of Coke.
zh_text: 「不，不，還沒結婚。」

en_text: "Do you have family? Any other brothers and sisters? And what do you do with Joe? Are you his receptionist? Do you clean the cars? Are you a cleaner?" "I live with my parents," she says, wanting to get through this part quickly so she can get back to talking about Joe. "I don't clean the cars, and I don't think Joe does either."
zh_text: 「妳有家人嗎？其他兄弟姊妹？妳在那間公司是做什麼的？妳是他的櫃檯小姐嗎？妳洗車嗎？妳是清潔工嗎？」「我跟父母同住。」她說，一心只想盡快結束這個話題，回去談論喬。「我不洗車，我想喬也不洗車。」

en_text: "No, of course he doesn't. Why would he?"
zh_text: 「當然不洗。他爲什麼要洗？」

en_text: Sally shrugs in reply. Why would a cleaner have a receptionist?
zh_text: 莎莉聳肩回應。清潔工要櫃檯小姐幹什麼？

en_text: "What do you do then?" Evelyn asks. "At work, I mean."
zh_text: 「那妳是做什麼的？」愛弗琳問。「工作，我是指。

en_text: "Well, I'm a maintenance worker. I kind of keep things in order."
zh_text: 這個，我是維修工。我算是維持工作場所一切的運作。

en_text: "Oh, that sounds very interesting, Sally. You don't see many female mechanics. Do you want to sell cars one day?" "Sell cars?" "Yes. Do you want to sell them?"
zh_text: 「喔，聽起來非常有趣，莎莉。女性維修工不常見。妳希望有一天也能賣車嗎？」「賣車？」「是啊。妳想賣車嗎？」

en_text: Maybe selling cars is a dream of Joe's. "I guess I've never thought about it." She picks up her drink and takes another large swallow. Speaking to Joe's mother is turning out to be just as difficult as some of the conversations she has had with Joe. "The thing is, I came here to talk about something I think might be happening." "Between you and Joe? Oh, that would be marvelous!"
zh_text: 或許賣車是喬的夢想。「我想我沒想過這個問題。」她拿起飲料，喝了一大口。跟喬的母親交談幾乎和有時候跟喬交談一樣困難。「重點在於，我是來談一些我認爲此刻正在發生的事情。」「妳和喬？喔，那眞是太好了。」

en_text: Sally leans back, struggling not to sigh. Suddenly she can't go through with it. Joe has created a world for his mother to see him in, and no doubt it's taken a long, long time. She could destroy all of that with some careless words. No, she is best to end this. There are no answers here as to why Joe can drive. No answers as to who attacked him. She takes another mouthful of drink, trying to get through it quickly, wanting to get out of here.
zh_text: 莎莉靠向椅背，壓抑著想嘆氣的衝動。突然之間她發現自己談不下去了。喬在他母親面前創造了另外一個世界，毫無疑問這花了他很長很長一段時間。她只要一不小心就可以摧毀這一切。不，她最好快點結束這次會面。這裡找不到喬能開車的原因。找不到襲擊喬的人的身分。她又喝了一口飲料，試圖盡快喝完，想要離開這裡。

en_text: "I knew Joe would find somebody."
zh_text: 「我就知道喬會找到對象的。」

en_text: "He really is something," Sally says, unsure of what else to say. She takes another mouthful. Only another mouthful to go. "After his father died, well, I was unsure how that would affect him, you know what I mean? I thought it might mess him up a little. Make him a little odd."
zh_text: 「他真的很特別。」莎莉說，不確定還能說什麼。她又喝了一口。只剩一口就喝完了。「在他父親死後，唉，我也不確定會對他造成什麼影響，妳知道我的意思嗎？我以爲那會打亂他的生活。讓他變得有點怪。」

en_text: Sally nods. She didn't know Joe's father had died.
zh_text: 莎莉點頭。她不知道喬的父親死了。

en_text: "Joe became quiet. Withdrawn. Not long after, he moved out. Do you know, I've never been to his house? I worry about Joe. I suppose that's the job of a mother." "I worry about him too." Sally finishes off her drink. "Well, I'd best be going."
zh_text: 「喬變得沉默、孤僻。沒過多久，他就搬出去了。妳知道我從來沒有去過他家嗎？我很擔心喬。我想這是母親的責任。」「我也擔心他。」莎莉喝完飲料。「我最好先走了。

en_text: "But you only just got here."
zh_text: 「但是妳才剛來。」

en_text: "I know. Next time I'll stay longer. I just wanted to come by and say hello." "You really are a nice young girl." Evelyn walks her to the door and opens it. The night has cooled off in the fifteen minutes she has been here. She thinks it's going to start raining again. "Did Joe tell you about Walt?"
zh_text: 我知道。下次我會待久一點。我只是想要過來打聲招呼。「妳真是個好女孩。」愛弗琳陪她走到門口，打開屋門。過去十五分鐘裡，外面的氣溫降低許多。「喬有跟你提過華特的事嗎？」

en_text: "Walt?"
zh_text: 「華特？」

en_text: Sally stands in the doorway with her arms wrapped around her body, listening as Evelyn recounts the story of Walt. When it's over, she thanks Joe's mother, then walks down the path to her car. She grips the steering wheel, but doesn't start the engine. According to Evelyn, Joe is a car salesman. Joe was out test-driving a car when he ran into her old friend Walt.
zh_text: 莎莉站在門口，雙手緊抱自己的身體，聽著愛弗琳重複華特的事情。講完之後，她向喬的母親道謝，然後走向她的車。她握著方向盤，但是沒有發動引擎。根據愛弗琳所言，喬是個汽車銷售員。喬在外出試駕的時候遇上了她的老朋友華特。

en_text: According to Evelyn, Joe is a car salesman. Joe was out test-driving a car when he ran into her old friend Walt. She clutches the crucifix around her neck. Joe has created a fictional world to keep his mother happy. What else has he created? Joe is more than he seems and, in a way, that frightens her.
zh_text: 根據愛弗琳所言，喬是個汽車銷售員。喬在外出試駕的時候遇上了她的老朋友華特。她握著脖子上的十字架。喬爲了讓他媽高興而創造了一個虛構世界。他還創造了什麼？喬不像外表那麼單純，而就某方面而言，這一點讓她害怕。

en_text: The next morning my internal alarm wakes me into what is another glorious Christchurch morning—according to some old guy giving the forecast on the radio. Looking out the window shows something different: gray skies and dark storm clouds on the horizon, which make me think the forecaster must be crazy or drunk. There is some condensation on the window and the floor is cold. I stare at the coffee table before leaving for work. There is a tin of fish food on it and no dead cat. I leave my apartment and head downstairs and out into the first frost of the year. The lawn looks crunchy, and there are leaves filling the gutters. I'm shivering a little when I hand Mr. Stanley my bus ticket, and today he punches it. I wonder if this is an omen. I want to tell him about my goldfish, and I don't know why. I don't even know if he would care. When he drops me off opposite my work, we exchange waves.
zh_text: 第二天早上，我的生理時鐘帶我進入一個陽光普照的基督城早晨——根據某個老頭在電台裡的天氣預測。不過窗外的景象可不是這麼說的——灰濛濛的天空和地平線上陰沉沉的烏雲都讓我覺得報氣象的老頭不是瘋子就是酒鬼。我出門上班前盯著咖啡桌看了一會兒。桌上擺了一盒魚飼料，不過沒有死貓。我離開我的公寓，將公車票交給史丹利先生，今天他有剪票。我在想這是不是什麼不好的預兆。我想告訴他我的金魚出了什麼事，我也不知道爲什麼。我甚至不知道他在不在乎。在警局對面放我下來時，我跟他互相揮手道別。我下了公車，步入雨中。中午太陽就會出來了。我敢保證。

en_text: The day doesn't suggest that it's going to get much warmer. I keep my hands buried in my pockets as I make my way across the road. Sally catches me by the elevator. We make inane conversation up to my floor, but mostly Sally seems preoccupied, and then she is gone. I'm unable to gain access to the conference room, so I end up doing what I'm paid to do. I keep an eye on Detective Calhoun when he is around. I try to figure out just how he's feeling, but I don't know him well enough to see if he's going through a personal crisis. I also keep an eye out for Melissa, but she doesn't show. I vacuum and clean and wipe and do the general workday things that bring in the big janitorial bucks. Nobody treats me any differently. Nobody gives me the sort of look they'd reserve for a serial killer.
zh_text: 這就是基督城的天氣——一天之中能夠體驗五個可惡的季節。莎莉在電梯裡遇上我。我們在到我的樓層前閒聊了幾句，不過莎莉似乎心事重重，然後她就離開了。我不能進入會議室，只好去做我應該做的工作。卡爾霍恩警探在警局裡的時候，我會特別注意他。我很想知道他此刻心裡是什麼感覺，不過我跟他沒有熟到能夠看出他有沒有面臨心理危機的地步。我也有注意梅莉莎，不過她沒出現。我吸地、掃地、擦窗，做著那些賺取優渥工資的例行工作。沒有人改變對待我的態度。沒有人以看連續殺人魔的目光打量我。

en_text: The station doesn't have the same buzz about it as yesterday, when everybody thought the case was about to bust wide open. Even the conference room is empty. I step inside and take a look around. The composite picture Melissa helped them with is on the wall. Dark, bushy hair; cheekbones that can't be seen, let alone felt; lots of stubble. A flat nose, big eyes, high forehead. The cold, calculating expression on his face looks mean, as though the person in this picture was born to be a criminal. The picture in no way represents how I actually look. My hair is finer, swept back, and kept reasonably short. It's dark, which is the only similar thing, but I have high cheekbones with no flab, and my eyes are thinner too. And stubble? No way. I'm lucky if I need to shave once a month. I grin at the picture. It doesn't grin back. On the table with the folders is the knife. Shrouded inside a plastic bag, sitting inside a cardboard box, it has already been studied for fingerprints, blood, and DNA. If my fingerprints were found on it, I would know by now. All employees in this building have been fingerprinted. It's standard. Melissa wasn't lying. It isn't standard for all of us to have given DNA samples. I grip the handle tightly, feel it beneath the thin plastic. This knife was stolen from me in circumstances I can never possibly forget. This knife was there the night I suffered my greatest indignity, my greatest pain, and experienced my greatest hatred. I quickly put it back down. It isn't mine anymore.
zh_text: 警局裡不像昨天那樣籠罩在一股所有人都認爲即將破案的興奮氣氛中。就連會議室也空無一人。我走了進去，好好打量一番。梅莉莎描述給他們的拼貼照片就貼在牆上。濃密的黑髮，臉頰肥到看不見也感覺不出，很多鬍碴。扁平鼻，大眼睛，高額頭。老謀深算的表情看起來十分奸詐，彷彿照片中的人天生就是罪犯。這張照片跟我一點也不像。我的頭髮柔順，梳向腦後，而且很短。它是黑色的，這是唯一相似之處，不過我的頰骨很高，沒有贅肉，眼睛也沒那麼大。至於鬍碴？不可能。幸好我的鬍子少到一個月只要剃一次就好。我看著照片咧嘴而笑。如果照片算是我的鏡中倒影，他沒有回應我的笑容。跟檔案夾一同放在桌上的是一把刀。包在一個塑膠袋裡，放在一個紙箱子中，已經驗過指紋、血跡和DNA。如果上面有找到我的指紋，這時我應該已經聽說了才對。警局中所有的雇員都有記錄指紋。這是標準程序。梅莉莎沒有騙我。至於留下DNA樣本那就不是標準程序了。我緊握刀柄，感覺包在塑膠袋下的刀。這把刀是在我永遠不可能忘記的情況下自我手中被人奪走的。我遭受此生最大屈辱、最大痛楚、激起最強烈的恨意的那晚，這把刀就在現場。我很快就把刀放回去，它已經不屬於我的了。

en_text: The second whore who died, Candy number two, is still to be identified. I don't need to take any information away with me, but I find myself collecting what I can anyway, more as mementos than anything else. I also take the tape from the recorder in the potted plant. I'm back in my office when Sally knocks at the door and comes in.
zh_text: 第一名死者，坎蒂一號，身分依然有待鑑識。我不需要帶走任何資料，不過我發現自己還是盡力蒐集，有點像是紀念品性質。我也拿走了盆栽裡的錄音帶。回到我的辦公室後，莎莉敲門進來。

en_text: "Sure is a cold day," she says, but the switch has been flicked to automatic now, so she doesn't really know what she is saying. She looks out the window. Looks at the ceiling. At the floor under the bench. Finally her eyes rest on my briefcase. "I forgot to make you lunch today. I'm sorry, Joe."
zh_text: 「天氣真好。」她說，不過她的開關此刻轉到「自動」模式，所以她並不清楚自己在說些什麼。她看看窗外。看看天花板。看看工作台下的地板。最後她的目光停留在我的公事包上。「我今天忘了幫你做午餐。對不起，喬。」

en_text: "Don't worry about it."
zh_text: 「不必介意。」

en_text: She keeps staring at my briefcase, and I guess she's figuring I'd like her more if she went out and bought the same one. She's trying to figure out whether I'd be impressed or devastated if she bought one that was better. The truth is she probably isn't thinking anything at all. She is frowning slightly, which suggests something is going on inside her mind, but the way her face is slightly scrunched up suggests the only thing happening in there is a whole lot of confusion. It's as if she wants to ask me a really big question, but has no idea what that question even is.
zh_text: 她一直盯著我的公事包看，我認爲她是在想如果她跑去買個一模一樣的，我就會更喜歡她。或者是在考慮如果她買了一個比我的好的公事包，我會開心還是不爽。事實上，她很可能什麼都沒在想。她微微皺眉，這表示她有心事，不過她臉上皺成一團的模樣顯示她內心極度困惑。那感覺像是她想要問我一個很嚴重的問題，偏偏又不知道是什麼問題。

en_text: "Well, thanks for dropping by. I got a lot of work I ought to get started on."
zh_text: 「好了，謝謝妳過來看我。我還有很多工作要做……」

en_text: This seems to snap her out of it. The switch inside of her doesn't go to on, because that isn't one of the positions. Other than off and automatic, she only has barely functioning, and she goes into that mode now. "I'll see you later on, Joe." "Oh. Okay then," I say, trying to singsong the three words. She heads out of my office but doesn't close the door. I have to get up and do it myself.
zh_text: 這話似乎令她回過神來。她體內的開關沒有轉到「開啓」，因為根本沒有這個選項。除了「關閉」和「自動」外，她只有「勉強運作」模式，而此刻她就進入了這個模式。「喔，好哇。」我說，努力讓這句話聽來像用唱的一樣。她離開我的辦公室，但是沒有關門。我得要起身自己去關。

en_text: I listen to the tape from the conference room. Lots of different theories, none of them right. The police are freaking out because they think I'm escalating. They think soon it'll be only a few days between my victims. Hell, maybe they're right. It's too early to tell. The Everblue Motel is one of those dives you see in movies where bad things happen to unlucky people who just happen to be staying there the same night as some escaped mental patient. It's not far from town, but far enough for the land to be cheap, like those living nearby.
zh_text: 我聽了會議室的錄音帶。很多不同的理論，沒有一個正確的。警方驚慌失措，因為他們認爲我開始加速犯案了。要不了多久我的犯案間隔就會縮短爲數日。見鬼了，說不定他們猜對了。現在還看不出來。長藍汽車旅館就是你會在電影裡看到的那種倒楣鬼剛好跟逃出精神病院的瘋子同時過夜並且發生慘劇的地方。那裡離城區不遠，不過地租便宜，就像附近的住戶一樣。汽車旅館的房間排列成L狀，油漆斑剝，窗沿龜裂，雜草枯黃，灌木垂死。走道上的裂縫裡積滿鏽色的積水。我在停車場裡看到十來輛車，從最便宜的爛車到中產階級家庭轎車都有。或許今天妓女有禮拜三折扣日的活動。幾台破爛的超級市場推車躺在地上，圍繞在雜草和菸屁股中。霓虹招牌發出惱人的吱吱聲。

en_text: The motel is an L-shaped stretch of rooms with old paint and chipped windowsills, opposite brown grass and half-dead shrubs. The cracks in the sidewalk are full of rust-colored water. I count a dozen vehicles in the parking lot, ranging from the cheapest of the cheap to the most average, middle-class family sedan. Maybe it's discount Wednesday for the hookers. A few corroding shopping carts are lying on their sides, surrounded by weeds and cigarette butts. The neon sign is making a loud buzzing noise. I park outside the office. Long ribbons of thick plastic cover the doorway, the type you'd find if you traveled back twenty years and entered a dairy. I brush them aside and make my way in. The room smells of latex and cigarette smoke. The walls and ceiling are stained. The carpet is patterned with cigarette burns.
zh_text: 我將車停在辦公室外，步入炎熱的夜晚中。今天一整天越來越熱。每隔十秒左右我就會感到有滴汗水自我腋下滑落。門上垂著長長的塑膠布簾，就是在二十年前乳品製造廠裡看到的那種。我撩開它們，進入辦公室。裡面瀰漫著一股乳膠和香菸的味道。牆壁和天花板上都是污垢，地毯上隨處可見菸頭燙出來的痕跡。櫃檯後方的男子看來四十幾歲，禿頭，過胖，直視著我，一副不信任我的模樣。彷彿他認爲我會扯下他的彩色塑膠門簾然後奪門而出。他身穿一件印有「種族歧視乃是最新潮流」字樣的汗衫。

en_text: The guy behind the counter must be in his forties. He's bald and overweight, and he stares directly at me as if he doesn't trust me. As if he thinks I'm going to grab his multicolored plastic ribbons from the doorway and take off. He is wearing a T-shirt that says Racism is the New Black. I flash some police identification that isn't even mine—sometimes all you need is a policeman's business card with a name and no photo and it can open any door—and he shrugs and hardly glances at it. When I ask to look through the guest book, he spins it around and tells me to go ahead. His fingernails, long and dirty, flick the pages open toward the date I indicate. Then he uses them to scratch at his barren scalp. He gets tiny pieces of skin stuck under them, and then he starts to pick them out. They drift onto the guest book, and he brushes them off with his hand. We make miniature conversation as I look through the book. He has dealt with police before, so he says, and even rented a room once to a murderer. Of course, he didn't know the man was a murderer at the time. That hadn't come out until the guy was caught. Fascinating. I tell him so. I search through the dates, looking for the room Calhoun used. Of course, it won't be beneath his name, but I look nonetheless. My finger scrolls past lots of people called John Smith, and others with names like Ernest Hemingway and Albert Einstein. The Everblue seems a popular place for dead people, because even Abraham Lincoln has stayed here. I turn the guest book back around so it faces Mr. Greasy. Slap the photograph of Detective Calhoun down on top of it. "You recognize this guy?" "Should I?"
zh_text: 我秀出一份根本不是我的警察證件——有時候只需要一張有名字沒照片的警察名片能就讓任何門爲你而開——他聳了聳肩，看都不看那張證件一眼。當我要求看看住客登記簿的時候，他把登記簿轉過來，叫我隨便看。他又長又髒的指甲將登記簿翻到我指定的那一天。接著他又用那些指甲去搔他的光頭。指甲上刮下了小小的頭皮屑，然後他開始挖出那些頭皮屑。它們飄到櫃檯上，他用手拍開它們。我們在我翻閱登記簿的時候隨口閒聊幾句。他曾與警方打過交道，他如此宣稱，甚至曾經把房間租給一名殺人犯。當然，當時他並不知道對方是殺人犯，那要等到那傢伙被捕之後才知道。「厲害厲害。」我對他說。我翻閱登記簿，找尋卡爾霍恩住過的房間。當然，他會使用化名，不過我還是要找。我的手拍滑過很多名叫約翰·史密斯的人，還有像是厄尼斯·海明威和亞伯特·愛因斯坦之類的名字。我將登記簿轉回去面對油垢先生。把卡爾霍恩警探的照片丟在上面。「認得這傢伙嗎？」「應該認得嗎？」

en_text: "Yeah, you should." He takes a close look at it. "Yeah, I remember him. He came in a few months ago."
zh_text: 對，應該認得。他細看那張照片。「是啊，我記得他。他幾個月前來過。

en_text: "Out of all the people who come in here, you remember this guy? Why's that?"
zh_text: 「這裡這麼多人來來往往，偏偏你就記得他？爲什麼？」

en_text: "I sure as hell remember the mess he made, and the noise he made while he was making it." "You sure this guy did that?"
zh_text: 「我打死都記得他所留下的爛攤子，還有他在搞的時候發出的噪音。「你確定是這傢伙幹的？」

en_text: He shrugs again. "Does it matter?" I guess it doesn't. I don't bother thanking him. Just nod, and leave. My next stop is a direct contrast to the Everblue. The Five Seasons Hotel is closer to the center of town, among a handful of hotels, most around ten years old. Land isn't cheap here. It just looks it. I park the stolen car three blocks away and take my briefcase with me. The evening is getting darker and colder. There's going to be another frost. The hotel is ugly. I don't know quite how to describe it as anything other than an artistic dream turned nightmare. Architects using braille to draw their plans. Painters using materials from the seventies. It looks like a lava lamp. It's fifteen stories high—not huge, but big enough when your major color is lime green. Spotlights around the foundation light it up at night. The hotel would look more in place in Disneyland as some scary ride. Amazingly, it's a five-star.
zh_text: 他再度聳肩。「有差別嗎？」我想是沒差。我沒向他道謝。只是點頭離開。我的下一站與長藍旅館有著天壤之別。五季旅館接近市中心，座落在幾家旅館之間，大部分都只有十年歷史。這裡的地可不便宜。只是看起來很便宜而已。我將偷來的車停在三條街口外，帶著公事包下車。夜還不深，不過陽光依然炙烈耀眼。我汗流不止。這間旅館很醜。除了藝術家的美夢化爲惡夢之外，我不知道該如何形容這個地方。建築師根本是用盲人點字法去繪製設計圖的。畫家則採用了七〇年代的顏料。整棟旅館看起來像是一盞熔岩燈。十五層樓高，佔地不廣，不過在以萊姆綠作爲主色的情況下看起來並不算小。由地面打上去的聚光燈令它在黑夜中耀眼生輝。這棟旅館看起來比較像是迪士尼樂園雲霄飛車裡的裝飾。驚人的是，它竟然能被評爲五星級。

en_text: What's also amazing is that police personnel from out of town are put up here. It's taxpayers' money going to good use. I already have a picture in my mind of what the interior will look like, but I quickly find I'm completely wrong. The walls are varnished wood, giving the foyer a strange type of antique look. A chandelier hangs from the ceiling with a million reflections of light. The carpet, a deep red color, is plush enough to sleep on and be comfortable. Where the carpet ends, checkered black-and-white linoleum takes over. The foyer is large enough to chase somebody around in for a good minute or so. The air is cool, and slightly scented. Could be jasmine, or lilac, or one of those other incense aromas that men all over the world have no idea how to distinguish from others.
zh_text: 同樣驚人的地方在於從外地調來支援的警方人員竟然安排入住這種地方，真是善用納稅人的錢。我心中浮現一幅旅館內部的模樣，不過很快就發現我猜錯了。牆壁採用亮面木板，讓大廳有種奇特的古意。天花板上的吊燈反射著百萬點光芒。深紅色的地毯厚到能讓人舒舒服服地躺在上面睡覺。地毯盡頭接著黑白格子的油布。大廳大到足夠讓人追逐好一陣子。室溫涼爽，還帶有一點香味。可能是茉莉香，或是紫丁香，或是全世界的男人都不知道有何差別的那堆香味之一。

en_text: I book and pay for a room with cash, then I sign my name in the guest book the same way it was on the cards. She asks me for a credit card she can swipe in case I make any extra purchases, and I tell her I'm a cash only kind of guy, and don't own one. She nods and smiles, and says that that's fine, then adds that they'll lock the minibar so I can't access it. She puts me in room 712. I grab my key, which is actually an electronic card so could pose a problem. I thank her, wondering if I'll ever see her again. She thanks me, and no doubt has a similar thought.
zh_text: 我付現入住了一個房間，拿出偷來的信用卡和提款卡作爲身分證明。然後我在登記簿上簽下卡片上的簽名。由於我預先支付現金，信用卡不需要過卡。就算失主有掛失，旅館也不會發現。七一二號房。我拿起我的鑰匙，一張可能會造成問題的磁卡。我謝謝她，心想不知道還有沒有機會再見到她。她謝謝我，一定也在想著同樣的問題。

en_text: A porter with barely enough personality to get by in life rides with me to the seventh floor. I have no luggage, but he comes along anyway. He seems depressed, and I figure it must be because he's over a hundred years old and is still a damn porter. My legs take me to the twelfth room. He takes the key off me, puts it into the lock, and the mechanism pops open with the same sound as a latch on a briefcase. He opens the door, then stands there like it's well within his Goddamn right to take a tip off me. Like he's just earned ten bucks for making this trip and providing no conversation. I give him five and he doesn't thank me. I close the door and head to the windows. My eyes take me out to the city beyond. I decide to relax a bit. With my shoes off and my feet breathing in the air-conditioned room, I struggle to believe, or perhaps don't want to believe, that outside this hotel I have a life that consists of mayhem and confusion and very little else.
zh_text: 一名勉強算是有點表情的服務員跟我一同前往七樓。我沒帶行李，不過他還是跟過來了。他神情沮喪，我猜是因為他已經超過一百歲了還在幫人搬行李的緣故。我徒步走到第十二個房間。他取過我的鑰匙，插入鎖孔中，電子鎖立刻傳來如同公事包開鎖的聲音。他打開房門，然後站在旁邊，一副有權收小費的模樣。彷彿他一言不發地跟我上來就可以賺十塊錢一樣。我給他五塊錢。他沒有道謝。我關上房門，走向窗口。我望向窗外的城市，太陽逐漸消失在眼看就要下雨的烏雲後方。我決定先放鬆一下。脫掉鞋子，讓雙腳在有空調的房間裡呼吸，我努力相信，又或許是不願相信，自己在這間旅館外的生活除了暴行與混亂外幾乎一無所有。

en_text: The room is divine, the sort of place that gives me the motivation to become rich just so I can live here. You could stay at the Everblue for about a week and still pay less than you'd pay for this place for one night. The large window makes the view of Christchurch seem nicer than I've ever seen it, and combined with its height and the fact it's been raining, it even makes Christchurch look cleaner. The bed is so comfortable I'm afraid if I lie down I may never get up. I check out the minibar: one look at the prices and I think it's ironic that I'm the one being called a criminal. None of the items are accessible as the door to the minibar has been locked. The kitchen is filled with expensive appliances I have no idea how to use. The TV is a big screen with a remote control that has a hundred buttons. I take the gamble and lie down on the bed. I end up spending forty minutes staring at the ceiling, allowing my mind to visit other places it hasn't been in weeks, catching up on old fantasies that include the woman from the vet, and thinking of new ones that include the receptionist downstairs, before finally using the phone to call home and check my answering machine. A moment later I'm listening to a man from the veterinary clinic, reminding me that I have a cat cage that doesn't belong to me. I don't need to wonder why Jennifer didn't call. I'll return the cage when all this is over. The second caller identifies himself as Doctor Costello. He leaves a phone number where I can contact him. He says it's urgent. Says Mom's in the hospital. He leaves no other details. My hands are shaking and I struggle to hang up the phone. Has something happened to Mom? Of course it has. She wouldn't be in the hospital otherwise. Please God . . . Please let her be okay.
zh_text: 這房間棒透了，就是那種會讓我想要變成有錢人以便住在裡面的地方。在長藍汽車旅館住上一個禮拜都還不及在這裡住一晚。大窗戶外的基督城看起來比我印象中要美好許多。床舒服到會讓我害怕一旦躺下去就再也起不來的地步。我翻了翻迷你吧台：標價足以嚇死心臟不夠力的人。廚房裡擺滿了我不知道該如何使用的昂貴器具。還有一台遙控器上有上百個按鈕的大螢幕電視。我決定冒險上床躺一躺。結果我盯著天花板看了四十分鐘，任由思緒飛奔到已經幾個禮拜不曾去過的地方，回想從前的幻想，創作全新的幻想，最後才拿起電話打回家去聽答錄機留言。片刻過後我聽到一個獸醫診所的男人打來提醒我要歸還不屬於我的貓籠。我不需要猜測爲什麼不是珍妮佛打的，我會在這一切結束之後歸還貓籠。第二通電話是位名叫寇斯特羅的醫生打來的。他留下一個聯絡電話。他說是緊急情況。說老媽人在醫院。他沒有交代其他細節。我雙手顫抖，努力掛上電話。難道媽出什麼事了嗎？當然出事了。不然她不可能在醫院裡。拜託，上帝……千萬保佑她沒事。

en_text: I punch in the number (I wrote it down on a complimentary Five Seasons pad with a shaky hand while listening to the message), and the phone starts ringing. I end up talking to a woman at a Chinese restaurant for about a minute, trying to ask how my mother is while being given the day's specials, until I realize I've dialed the wrong number. I slam the phone down and suck in a deep breath, but it doesn't calm my nerves. My hands are shaking violently, and I have to use both of them to dial. I close my eyes and begin to imagine a world without Mom, and as I imagine it, tears begin to well in my eyes.
zh_text: 我撥打醫生留下的號碼（我邊聽留言邊拿五季旅館免費提供的便條紙抄下號碼），聽著電話鈴響。結果我跟一個中國餐館的女人講了一分鐘，我詢問我媽的病情，她介紹今日特餐，然後我才發現我打錯電話了。我用力掛上電話，深吸一口氣，但卻完全無法冷靜下來。我的手掌劇烈顫抖，我必須雙手並用才能撥號。我閉上雙眼，試圖想像沒有老媽的世界，在想像的同時，我的淚水奪眶而出。

en_text: I simply won't imagine it.
zh_text: 我就是不願去想像。

en_text: A woman at Christchurch Hospital answers the phone and tells me I've just called Christchurch Hospital. I appreciate her insight. I ask for Costello and a long minute later he comes to the phone, bringing with him a deep, concerned voice. "Ah, yes, Joe. Listen, it's about your mother."
zh_text: 基督城醫院裡有個女人接起電話，我說要找寇斯特羅，然後等了好一會兒，他才接起電話，傳來了深沉又關切的嗓音。「噢，喬啊，聽著，這事兒和你媽有關。」

en_text: "Please don't tell me anything's wrong with her."
zh_text: 別告訴我她哪裡出了問題。

en_text: "Well, actually, nothing is wrong with her," he says, and for some reason I can't explain I feel disappointment. "You can speak to her yourself. She's right here." "But you're at a hospital," I say, as if I'm accusing him of something— perhaps of being a doctor. "Yes, but your mother's fine."
zh_text: 「呃……其實她平安無事啦，你可以自己跟她說，她就在這。」「但你來電說是緊急狀況。」我說，有如對他的指控。「是沒錯，但你媽沒事。」

en_text: "Then why didn't she call me?" "Well, she's fine now, and since she's not going home tonight, this was the only way she could speak to you. She said the only way of getting hold of you was if I called. She's quite an insistent woman, your mother," he says, without any humor.
zh_text: 「那幹嘛打給我？」「應該是說，她現在沒事了。但今晚她還是得住院。她想跟你說說話，她還說唯一方法，就是看我打不打這通電話。你媽挺固執的呢。」他說話毫無幽默感可言。

en_text: "What was wrong with her?" "I'll let you talk to her."
zh_text: 「那她到底怎麼了？」「我讓你自己跟她說。」

en_text: The line goes quiet as the phone changes hands. A mumbling of voices and then, "Joe?" "Mom?" "This is your mother." "What's wrong? Why are you in the hospital?"
zh_text: 電話換手的同時，話筒的另一端安靜下來，接著有個含糊的聲音說道：「喬？」「媽？」「是啊。「怎麼了啊？妳怎麼會在醫院咧？」

en_text: "What's wrong? Why are you in the hospital?" "I chipped a tooth."
zh_text: 「是啊。「怎麼了啊？妳怎麼會在醫院咧？」「我有顆牙齒斷了。」

en_text: "I've been to the dentist, Joe."
zh_text: 「喬，我去過了。」

en_text: "It's Walt."
zh_text: 「因爲華特。」

en_text: "He's sick?" I ask, perhaps a little too hopefully. "He broke his hip." "Broke his hip? How?"
zh_text: 「他摔傷屁股了。」「摔傷屁股？怎麼摔的？」

en_text: "Broke his hip? How?" "He slipped in the shower."
zh_text: 「摔傷屁股？怎麼摔的？」「洗澡時滑了一跤。」

en_text: "He slipped in the shower." "What?"
zh_text: 「洗澡時滑了一跤。」「什麼？」

en_text: "He was having a shower, and he fell. Broke his hip. I had to call an ambulance. It was scary, Joe, yet exciting too, because I've never been in an ambulance. The sirens were loud. Of course, Walt kept on crying. I felt so bad for him, but he was so strong. The ambulance driver had a mustache." Uh huh. Uh huh. "You were at his house when he was showering?"
zh_text: 「那時他人在洗澡，然後跌了一跤、摔傷了屁股，我還得叫救護車呢。喬，當時超恐怖的，但也很刺激，因為我這輩子從沒搭過救護車。沒錯，華特哭個不停，我替他感到非常難過，但他也真的非常堅強。對了，救護車的司機留有小鬍子喔。」嗯哼、嗯哼。所以他洗澡時你在他家？

en_text: "Don't be silly, Joe. I was at home."
zh_text: 「喬，少扯了，我在自己家。」

en_text: "Why did he call you?" "He didn't need to call me. I was already at home. It was me who called the ambulance."
zh_text: 「他爲什麼打給妳啊？」我在家，他大可不必打給我，我只是打電話叫救護車。

en_text: "Yeah, but why didn't Walt call?" I ask, somewhat confused—perhaps not as confused as I'd like to be, because there is a scenario being built here. "Because he was in the shower," Mom says.
zh_text: 「我知道，只是華特爲什麼不自己打啊？」「因爲他在洗澡啊。」

en_text: "Then how did he call you?"
zh_text: 那他又是怎麼打給妳的？

en_text: "I was already there, Joe. What are you getting at?"
zh_text: 「喬，我人就在現場，你到底懂不懂？」

en_text: "I'm not sure," I answer, happy to let it go. "We were getting ready to go out, so we decided . . ." She pauses, but I've already heard her mistake. "He decided to take a shower."
zh_text: 「不太懂。」我回答，很開心岔開話題。「我倆原本準備一起出門，所以決定……」她稍作停頓，但我已從她話中聽出事有蹊蹺。「是他決定洗個澡。」

en_text: "He was at your house? You had a shower with him?" "Don't be so rude, Joe. Of course I didn't."
zh_text: 他在妳家，然後妳和他一起洗澡？「喬，別這麼失禮，我當然沒這麼做。」

en_text: Images start going through my mind. I squeeze my eyes shut. I'd tear them out if it'd help. The images don't budge. I'm sweating like a pig. I push my fingers at my closed eyes and thousands of colors appear—like in the chandelier downstairs—and I try to follow the colors with my eyes as they float across my mind. I'm happy to believe they didn't take a shower together. If she says so, then I'm happy to believe it. Happy to forget she said we instead of he. Happy to forget this entire conversation. She just has to tell me that . . . "So, Mom, how did you chip your tooth?"
zh_text: 我腦海中開始浮現畫面，於是硬把雙眼閉上——撐開眼皮有所幫助我才會撐開——此時那些畫面動也不動。我汗流浹背，用手指壓起眼皮，接著眼前浮現了有如花式吊燈那般數以千計的斑斕色彩。隨著它們掠過我的腦海，我這才試圖用目光追隨起色彩的痕跡。我樂於相信他們並未共浴。她都這麼說了，我也就樂於相信、樂於遺忘她說的是「我倆」以及這從頭到尾一整段的對話。她只須告訴我……「媽，所以妳是怎麼摔斷牙齒的？

en_text: "So, Mom, how did you chip your tooth?" "It happened when Walt fell over."
zh_text: 「媽，所以妳是怎麼摔斷牙齒的？「華特跌倒時摔斷的。」

en_text: "What?" "It happened when—" "I heard you, Mom," I say, trying to squeeze my eyes closed even tighter. "But I thought you said you weren't taking a shower together."
zh_text: 「啊？」「就在……」「妳不是才說你們並沒一起洗澡嗎？」

en_text: "Well, Joe, we're adults. Just because we were taking a shower together doesn't mean anything of a sexual nature was happening. Just because in this day and age young people can't keep their hands off each other doesn't mean we were acting just as immorally. We're pensioners, Joe. We can't afford to leave hot water running all day. So we took a shower together. Now don't you go making a big deal out of nothing." "So how did you chip your tooth? He knocked you over?"
zh_text: 「喬，我們都是成人了。喬，我們現在是領老人年金、靠政府救濟，成天打開熱水流個不停我們可負擔不起，所以才會一起洗澡。」「那妳究竟是怎麼摔斷牙齒的？被他撞斷的嗎？」

en_text: I open my eyes, because if they're open, I see this lovely hotel room wall and not my mother taking a shower with some old guy. I don't want to question her. She has explained things in enough detail for me, yet the question has left my mouth before I could stop it. I didn't want to ask— God knows I didn't. Eyes open, I see a couple of chairs, some paintings, and I can see the hotel room door. Maybe I should run for it. "No, no, he kicked me in the mouth. His foot slipped out from beneath him, and the heel of his foot kicked me in the mouth."
zh_text: 我睜開雙眼，因為我這麼做，眼前所看到的就是旅館客房漂亮的牆壁，而不是自己的老媽正和某個老傢伙一起洗澡。由於她已經向我解釋得相當清楚，我並不想有所質疑，只不過後來我還是脫口而出。睜開雙眼的我看到的是幾張椅子、幾幅圖畫還有房門。也許我應該衝出門外、問個明白。「不是、不是，是他踢到了我的嘴巴。他滑了一跤，然後腳跟正好踢中了我的嘴巴。」

en_text: Don't ask, Joe. Just don't ask. "But how did his foot reach so high?" "Oh, I wasn't standing. I was kneeling. I was . . . um . . . well, it just happened, Joe, okay? He kicked me in the mouth."
zh_text: 喬，別問，就是別問……「他的腳怎麼能舉得那麼高？」「噢，當時我不是站著，而是跪著，我……呃……好啦，喬，事情就是這樣好嗎？他就是踢到了我的嘴巴。」就是這樣？哪樣？天啊，別告訴我……

en_text: It just happened. What just happened? Oh God, please don't show me. . . . Only my mind does show me. My entire shirt is wet. I become so scared that she might confirm exactly what she was doing that the moment she starts talking again I put the phone down and run to the bathroom, reaching the bowl only just in time. A hiccup, a convulsion of my stomach, the taste of bile. Vomit explodes from me in a roar and splashes into the water, while drops of water and puke flick onto my face and roll down onto my chin. I keep coughing it up until I have no more to cough, but I keep coughing anyway, watching it form a yellowish soup in the bottom of the toilet. As my body shudders, all I can picture is my mother in the shower. My throat quickly becomes raw, and my stomach shrinks into a small ball of pain. I can taste blood as it drips off my lips and plinks into the syrup below. There is something floating in there that looks like one of my dead goldfish.
zh_text: 我閉上雙眼，敞開心胸。我害怕她可能會一五一十地解釋起自己當時正在幹嘛，所以擔心到整件襯衫都濕了，然後就在她又開始說話的當下，我放下話筒，直奔浴室，及時跑到了馬桶邊。打嗝，胃抽筋，膽汁的苦味……我吐得唏哩嘩啦，自馬桶反濺而出的水珠和嘔吐物就這麼彈上我的臉頰、滑至我的下巴。我瘋狂反胃，直到咳不出來，同時望著馬桶座底形成了一碗黃湯。隨著身子不住哆嗦，我所能想像的就是媽正在洗澡的畫面。我瞬間感到喉嚨灼疼，胃因疼痛而縮成一團，就連雙唇滴下鮮血、悄悄落入黏稠的黃湯時，我都還嚐得到血腥味，而且某樣東西就在湯裡載浮載沉，看來有如我其中一條死去的金魚。

en_text: My mind is spinning and I feel light-headed. I reach out and slap the lever and the mess that surely couldn't have come out of me, but did anyway, is flushed away. It hasn't stopped flushing before I kneel back over the bowl, trying to throw up once again. Now I'm only gagging. Blood clots land in the water and spread out into rose petal shapes. I flush, but the toilet hasn't regained pressure, so the petals don't disappear. They just swirl around the edges of the bowl. Strands of drool hang from my bottom lip. They stick to the rim of the bowl, and they stretch when I lean back, eventually breaking. The tops of the strands swing down onto the black linoleum. Thinking about the thousands of people who have sat here and pissed and shat is better than thinking about Mom and her broken tooth.
zh_text: 我感到天旋地轉、頭昏眼花，緊接著伸出手去、扳下把手，於是那些亂七八糟、不可能是我所造成但我確是始作俑者的玩意就這麼被水沖了走。就在我重新跪到馬桶邊、試圖再次嘔吐之前，馬桶的水還沖個不停，但我現在只是乾嘔而已。一團團的血塊就落在水中，攤成了玫瑰花瓣的形狀，我又沖了次水，但這次馬桶尚未回壓，花瓣沒被沖掉，而僅在馬桶的四周來回打轉。我下唇牽絲的口水甚至緊黏在馬桶邊緣，在我向後靠時一如披薩起司那樣拉長延伸，最後才斷裂甩回，落至鋪起黑色油布的地面。想到成千上萬的人曾坐在這裡尿尿拉屎都要比想到老媽和她斷掉的牙齒來得好。

en_text: When I was in the faggot's house, I tried thinking of other things to take my mind away from what was going on, and in the process I thought about Dad and what he would say. Bending over the toilet, I start to remember something I saw. Something Dad was doing. I wasn't supposed to be home. I can't remember why, but what I can remember is coming home early and finding . . . Oh God.
zh_text: 以往我在柴房時，我都會試著想想其他事情、轉移當下的注意力，然後就在我這麼做的過程中，我想到了老爸，還有他會怎麼看待這件事。當我在馬桶邊彎著腰的同時，我記起了某件自己曾經目睹的事，某件老爸曾經做過的事。當時我本來不該在家，但我忘記爲什麼了，就只記得那天我提早回家，然後發現……噢，我的老天。

en_text: I start to gag, but I have nothing left to cough up except blood. I keep my eyes closed so I don't have to see the red water below, but behind my eyes the memory is playing. Images of Mom and Walt in the shower fade in and out, replaced slowly with images of Dad in the shower. Only he's in there with somebody else. Who? And why in the hell did I walk into the bathroom when I heard the damn shower going in the first place? That somebody else was another man.

zh_text: 「不知道。好啦，老媽，我得走了。

"That he was gay." I have no idea what she's on about. It's as if she's picking up on another conversation somewhere, perhaps a faulty phone connection. "Seriously, Mom, I really have to go. I'll talk to you soon."
zh_text: 就是她老哥是同性戀。她好像打算來個不清楚的三方通話、聊起別的話題，我壓根就聽不懂她在說些什麼。「媽，我真的得走了，再打給妳。」

en_text: I don't wait for a response. This time I hang up. I walk to the window and look out at the city. I want to jump out and crash into the sidewalk below. My mind is churning with images of my mother and Walt, but they're only shadows now. The day is winding down. Daylight is being replaced by streetlights and headlights. Hardly anything happens on a Wednesday night. Garbage trucks are rolling up and down the streets, taking away the trash left by shop owners and businesses. I wipe at the tears running down my face with no idea why I'm even crying. Finally I start to focus on why I'm here. I turn on the hotel room light, then start to make myself familiar with my surroundings, doing what I can to forget about my mother. It's a distraction, but it works. I go back into the bathroom. I flush the toilet and spray some air freshener about the place. Only the distraction ends up pissing me off. It makes me think of what I have at home, or, more accurately, what I don't have. en_text: I open my briefcase and take out a cleaning rag to remove my fingerprints from the knife. This isn't essential, but it's better to be safe than jailed. I slip on a pair of latex gloves, clean the knife once again, then slip it into a plastic bag from my briefcase. I grab the list of phone numbers from my briefcase. Look up Detective Inspector Calhoun's and dial it from the cell phone Melissa bought me. Since it's a prepay, if the number shows up on Calhoun's caller ID display, it can't be traced back to me. Because of the latest break in the case, many of the detectives are putting in extra hours, and from what I can make out Calhoun is one of them. After six rings I'm beginning to doubt he's there. If he isn't at his desk the phone automatically switches through to his mobile, which these guys carry with them every moment of the day. Finally he answers. Look out at the city. "Tonight's point, or moral, is that I know you have a sexual dysfunction that you attempt to put right by using prostitutes, and that that dysfunction has led to murder." Rather than denying anything, or abusing or threatening me, he says nothing. We both stay that way for almost half a minute. I know he's still there: the sound of the open phone line hums loudly.

en_text: "Ten grand." "When?"

en_text: "I can't risk being seen paying somebody off. How about somewhere more secluded?" "Like where?" I ask, knowing he would ask this. I can imagine exactly what he's thinking. His speedy answers are proof of that. He's suddenly inside that game he told me he didn't have time for. Like chess, he's setting me up, but again like chess, I can see it coming. I'm half a dozen steps ahead of the guy. Nobody's going to have ten thousand dollars on them, ready to make a payoff in thirty minutes, and nobody is going to want to make that payoff a few hundred meters from the police station in which they work. But he's seeing an ideal opportunity to eliminate me as a risk. Because I've sprung this on him pretty quickly, he hasn't had long enough to think it through properly. He thinks he's doing a pretty good job. Being clever. Being smarter than me. But I've been thinking through this all day. He's going to ask for somewhere way less public and much more secluded.
zh_text: 「我不能冒著被撞見付款的風險，要不要約在隱密一點的地方？」「像是？」我完全可以想像他在想些什麼。他回答得如此神速便是鐵證。這人已頓時置身於先前口口聲聲說著沒空跟我玩起的遊戲之中。這就有如下棋，他佈好了局、等我上鉤，然而下棋就是這樣，我總是能洞燭機先、看出端倪。比起這個傢伙，我棋高一著啊。沒人會在身上備好一萬塊現金，而且還在半小時內付清。他正找起最佳時機除掉我這個眼中釘。正因為事出突然、嚇了他一大跳，他並沒充分的時間好好思考。他自以為做得很好，甚至比我高招，但卻萬萬沒有料到我策劃了一整天呢。

en_text: Good question. I'm surprised he's asked this, considering he can't afford to fuel me with any suspicion that he's preparing to kill me. Again, I've been thinking about this all day knowing he had no choice but to ask it. "For ten grand, I'll give you both the photographs and negatives of you at the Everblue. I'll give you the negatives and photographs of you leaving Daniela Walker's house on the night she died. And on top of that, if I wanted more money, I'd be asking for more. en_text: "Ten o'clock then." He hangs up without waiting for a response. He's realized I'm cleverer than he first thought, I'm clever enough to have photos of him from the crime scene, and he'll wonder how this is even possible. It'll take him a while, but in the end he'll conclude that I'm lying. I look at my watch. I have more than three-quarters of an hour not to show up. Plenty of time not to do several things. Plenty of time not to kill. I reach down and scratch at my testicle through the padding, realizing it isn't my remaining testicle that has me in discomfort, but the missing one. The itch is where the skin is mending. Melissa left me some disinfectant and some talcum powder. I grab them from my briefcase and sit down on the edge of the bed. I remove the padding—it pulls at the hairs and I have to stifle a scream—then clean the area and sprinkle on the talcum powder. By the time I'm done, my testicle looks as though it's been dusted for fingerprints. I replace the padding and lie down on the bed and focus on not falling asleep. The problem is the bed is so comfortable I'm wondering if I can somehow steal it.
zh_text: 「那就十點吧。」他沒等我回話就把電話掛了。他了解到我比他預想的還要聰明，聰明到握有他在犯罪現場的照片，他甚至還會納悶我是怎麼辦到的。這會花上他一點時間，但他終究會得出結論，發現我唬弄他。我看了一下錶，這四十幾分鐘內我不必現身，這麼長的時間內我啥都不做。誰都不殺。我手向下摸，隔著敷料搔起睾丸，了解到讓我不舒服的不是剩下的那顆睾丸，反而是不見的那顆。癢的感覺主要來自長出新皮膚的部位。我站起身子，望過浴室找起塗抹的東西，後來才在藥櫃裡找到一小瓶消毒藥水。就在我取下敷料——取下時扯到陰毛還得憋住尖叫——正打算輕輕上點藥水時，我看到了一罐爽身粉，那也許是前一位房客所留下來的。上完爽身粉後，我的睪丸彷彿撒上了採指紋的藥粉。我更換敷料，爬回床上，希望自己至少可以放鬆到入睡就好，這張床實在太過舒適，舒適到我心想能否就這麼把它偷走、佔爲己有。

en_text: The graveyard is mostly deserted. It's late to be out here, but Sally wanted somewhere quiet to think. She parks next to a car that has a guy inside it slowly drinking from a bottle wrapped in a paper bag. He looks at her and she can see pain in his eyes and for a moment she wants to help him, to tell him that things will get better, but she isn't so sure it's true, not for this guy. She's seen him out here before, and she's seen him around the police station a few times too, talking mostly to Detective Schroder. She thinks he used to work there. She doesn't know his story, and doesn't want to ask. She makes her way to her brother's grave. Long blades of grass, those close to the gravestones missed by the lawn mower, are bending under the weight of the dew. Other than going to church, she feels like the cemetery is the closest place to God. Last night, rather than having some of her questions answered, Sally was only led further down the path of her confusion. No, further into the world of Joe's fiction. Just how much is he lying about? Did he attack himself? She thinks about the blood on the stairs at his apartment building. If Joe attacked himself, he must have done it outside. It doesn't seem likely. As unlikely as Joe driving? She knows she needs to confront him. She was going to today at work, but she'd become scared. She didn't want to lose Joe. Though, really, that has probably already happened. Maybe his mother hasn't told him yet of her visit, but she soon will.
zh_text: 天色漸亮，墓園中一如既往杳無人煙，野草狹長的葉身——也就是除草工在墓碑旁所遺漏的那些野草——隨起暖風擺盪。與其上教堂，她覺得墓地才是最接近上帝的地方。隨著有些問題不得而解，昨晚莎莉一頭栽進了自己困惑的思緒，噢不，應該是一頭栽進了喬所虛擬的世界。喬究竟撒了多少謊？還有他是否曾經自殘？她想起了他公寓樓梯上的血跡。要是喬曾自殘，那麼一定是在外自殘，但這似乎不太可能。就像他不太可能開車那樣？她很清楚自己得和他當面對質。今天她還得上班，但她感到非常害怕，她並不想失去喬——即便此事可能早已成真。也許他老媽還沒告訴他她來過，但她遲早會說。

en_text: She wipes the back of her hand across her face, streaking the tears across her cheeks. Her breath is forming a mist in front of her face. She doesn't want to let Joe down.
zh_text: 她滿臉淚痕，用手背擦起臉頰。她並不想讓喬失望。

en_text: The same way you let down your brother?
zh_text: 就像妳不想讓弟弟失望那樣嗎？

en_text: The tears start to come more freely. Nobody blames her for what happened to Martin, at least that's what they say, but she knows they do. She certainly does. Her parents must do. As for Martin and God, well, one day she'll find out. She pulls out a tissue from her pocket and dries her face. Across the graveyard, mist looks as though it's seeping out of the ground. Fog is hanging around the gravestones but doesn't have the strength to climb any higher. By the time she gets back to her car her legs feel damp. She turns the heater on to full as she drives to Joe's apartment. The hot air dries her legs and her face. Sometimes on the way home from seeing her dead brother, she can't stop the tears. She parks in the same spot she parked in the first time she came here. She grabs the first-aid kit from the backseat. She will help Joe by removing the stitches before she will help him by confronting him. Nobody appears as she makes her way up to the top floor. The small splotches of blood are still on the stairs. Some of them have been smeared to the size of a watch face. She knocks, but nobody answers. A cat appears at the end of the hallway and walks down to her. It has a slight limp. She squats down next to it and starts petting it.
zh_text: 淚珠又開始不聽使喚、滾滾滑落。沒人因為馬丁的遭遇責怪過她——至少他們是這麼說的——但她很清楚大家覺得她難辭其咎，就連爸媽也這麼覺得。呃……至於馬丁爲何就這樣走了，她總有一天會找出箇中原由。她從口袋抽出了一張衛生紙，擦乾眼淚，過了一會兒才驅車前往喬的公寓。她搖下車窗，吹進車裡的風幫忙吹乾了臉頰。天候開始轉涼，隱隱透露出下雨跡象的厚重雲層已準備遮起豔陽。有時在探視亡弟後回家的路上，她的眼淚就這麼撲簸簸地掉個不停。她把車停在第一次來此的位置，並從後座抓起急救箱。在即將幫他、和他對質之前，她會先替他拆線。她在通往頂樓的一路上不見半個人影。樓梯上一坨坨小小的血跡依稀可見，其中幾坨還抹成了時鐘表面的大小。她敲了敲門，但沒人應門，然後有隻小貓出現在走廊的盡頭，逕向她走來，走起路還有點一跛一跛的，於是她蹲在小貓身旁，輕輕拍起了牠。

en_text: "Hey, little one, aren't you just the cutest?"
zh_text: 「嘿，小喵喵，你眞是可愛。」

en_text: The cat meows as if to agree, then starts purring. She knocks on the door again, still hunched down next to the cat. Joe doesn't answer. Is it possible he has passed out again? Or been attacked? She knocks louder. Most likely he isn't home, but what if he is? What if he is lying on his bed, bleeding, the other testicle removed? She reaches into her first-aid kit, where the copy of Joe's key has been since the day she had it cut. She stands up and inserts it into the lock. She realizes the chances are higher that she's looking for an excuse to enter rather than Joe being in trouble inside. This realization doesn't stop her from turning the handle and pushing the door open.
zh_text: 小貓彷彿有所回應，「喵」了一聲，並開始發出「呼嚕嚕」的滿足聲。她又敲了敲門，仍舊弓身蹲在小貓身旁。喬沒應門耶，他會不會又暈倒了？還是又自殘了？她又敲得更用力些。他比較可能是出門去了，不過要是他在家？要是他正流血躺在床上，然後這次是另一顆睾丸不見了？她把手伸進急救箱，自她上次替喬割除睾丸後，喬的備用鑰匙就一直放在急救箱裡。於是她站起身子，把鑰匙插入門鎖。

en_text: "Joe?"

Joe doesn't answer, because Joe isn't home. She closes the door behind her. The cat sits down on the table next to the goldfish bowl. The bowl is empty. Did Joe not feed them? Has he bought a cat to replace them? His clothes are scattered across the floor again, though this time there aren't any patches of blood on any of them. The pile of latex gloves she had made has become smaller. There are dishes in the sink, exposed food on the table. The bed is unmade, and has possibly been that way since the attack. Would Martin have lived like this?
zh_text: 喬不在家，因此並沒人應話。她關起身後的門，小貓則跑去坐在桌上，而桌旁正好有個金魚缸，裡頭空無一物。喬不養魚了嗎？還是現在換成養貓？他的衣服再次散落一地，只不過這次每件衣服上都毫無血跡，她所用過的那疊橡膠手套看起來也少了些。洗碗槽裡堆著碗盤，桌上也擺著食物，連床也沒鋪，很可能就停留在她上次來到這裡的模樣。今天要是換作馬丁，他平時的生活習慣也是這樣嗎？

en_text: Sally starts to walk around the apartment. This isn't right, being here, but whatever's happening to Joe isn't right either. Happening to Joe? She looks through the folders he has brought home from the police station—there are extra ones now. The photos are disgusting, and she can bear only to look at them for a few seconds. She replaces them. Why would Joe have these here?
zh_text: 莎莉開始在公寓四處走動。等等，來到這裡並不合理，而此時喬的遭遇也同樣不合情理。喬的遭遇？她開始翻起他從警局所帶回來的資料夾，如今資料夾多了好幾個，而且裡頭的照片慘不忍睹，她看了幾秒無法忍受，把它放往別處。喬怎會把這些東西擺在這裡？

en_text: Perhaps a more important question would be what he'd say if he came home and found her looking around his apartment. Yes, it's best that she goes. She is about to pick up the cat when it races under the bed.
zh_text: 也許更重要的問題在於，他要是一回到家就發現她正在他公寓裡東看西看，他會作何反應。沒錯，離開才是上策。就在她正要抱起小貓的同時，牠火速地往床底下竄。

en_text: "Come on, little one, come on. You can't stay under there."
zh_text: 「嗨，小東西，出來囉，別躲在床下。」

en_text: But the cat thinks that it can. When she gets onto her hands and knees and looks under the bed, the cat is right in the middle. Next to it is a small piece of paper. Curious, Sally reaches under and grabs it.
zh_text: 但小貓就是覺得可以躲在床下。當她趴下身子往床底探去，小貓就在正中央，旁邊還有一張小紙。莎莉出於好奇，伸手往床底一抓。

en_text: It's a ticket from a parking building. The time and date printed across it are several months old. It doesn't make sense to still have the ticket, because the ticket gets handed back on the way out of the parking building so the guy in the booth knows how much to charge you. She reaches under the bed and puts the ticket back on the floor. She clicks her fingers for the cat, which a moment later is purring in her arms. She carries it into the hallway, sets it down, then heads back outside.
zh_text: 那是一張停車大樓的票卡，上面印的日期、時間已經是好幾個月前。因為大家在開出停車大樓時，都得把票卡交給收費員才能結算費用，所以票卡這時還留在手上實在相當奇怪。她又伸手進床底，放回票卡。她朝著小貓在地面敲起指尖，沒一會兒牠就願意走出床底、到她懷裡「呼嚕嚕」叫個不停。最後她抱牠走到走廊，放下，才轉而向外走去。

en_text: I get in the elevator. Just as the doors are closing, a maid comes out from a nearby room, almost like fate intended it. I slap at the open door button on the inside panel, and step back into the hallway. The maid smiles at me as we cross paths. She looks in her fifties, has the worn-out look of a mother who has maybe six kids and has to clean up after hundreds of adults forty hours a week. Her black hair is dyed, and she looks so thin that if I picked her up and threw her into the wall, she would land in a thousand pieces. I smile and nod back, then turn and watch as she comes to a stop a few doors down.
zh_text: 我進到電梯。就在電梯關門的同時，有個清潔婦從附近房間走了出來，就像註定好的一樣。我用力拍起電梯樓層板上的開門鍵，轉而走回走廊，和她相互照面。那清潔婦對我一笑，看來大約五十好幾，一臉滄桑，彷彿膝下有六個孩子嗷嗷待哺，還得在數百名房客離開後奮力打掃、一個禮拜工作四十小時。她染了頭黑髮，身形瘦弱，薄如紙片，要是我抱起她往牆上一砸，她很可能會被我砸成一堆肉屑，落至地面。我也微微一笑，點頭回應，接著才轉過身子，望著她走過幾道房門後停下腳步。

en_text: I reach my arm over her shoulder before she even knows I'm there, and pull it tightly across her throat, using my other hand to support the back of her head. I tighten both arms slightly to slow down her breathing. She, of course, is starting to struggle, but quickly stops when I suggest it isn't in her best interest. She stops fighting, and I'm wondering if she's gone through this before. Maybe that's why she's got six kids.
zh_text: 她還沒意識到我在那之前，我就已經使出「鎖頸」的招式，伸出一隻手繞過她的肩膀、扣住她的咽喉，同時用另一隻手撐住她的後腦勺。我雙手微微使力，壓迫她的呼吸。起初她當然想要掙脫，但在我暗示這樣只會對她不利的當下，她很快就停止掙扎。我心想，她以前是不是有過類似的經驗，或許那就是她生了六個孩子的原因。

en_text: I don't want to do anything to her. Not sexually, anyway, because she's old enough to be my mother. Here she is, just doing her job—a low-paying, demeaning job like my own—and suddenly it could cost her her life. Well, I'm going to give her a chance to hang on to it. For now.
zh_text: 我並不想傷害她，至少不是肉體方面，因為她實在老到足以當媽。她就在這，像我一樣從事這種低收入又下三濫的工作，甚至可能登時斃命，所以我打算給她機會幹下去。

en_text: I tell her to shut up or she's going to die. Then I tell her to keep facing ahead, that if she turns, if she tries to see me, she will die. From my voice she knows I'm not bluffing.
zh_text: 我叫她安靜，否則就要她的命；我還告訴她不要回頭，要是回頭、試圖看我是誰，我一樣會殺了她。從我的語氣聽來，她知道我不是嚇唬人的。

en_text: I ask for her key card. She lowers her hand to her waist and unclips it from her waist, and hands it to me. She knows it isn't worth dying for. She's thinking I can steal all the towels and free soap I want from any room I want. With my arm still around her throat, I tuck the key card into my pocket, lead her forward, and push her onto the bed. When I straddle her back, she doesn't complain, doesn't cry out. She's a quick learner. Then again, I also threatened to kill her husband and her kids.
zh_text: 我要她給我鑰匙，於是她放手，解下扣在腰上的鑰匙給我。爲了鑰匙喪命得不償失，這一點她了然於胸，同時心想我如今能從任何一間房裡偷走所有毛巾和免費肥皂了。我一手扣住她的咽喉，一手把鑰匙塞進口袋、把她推到床上。當我跨坐在她背上，她既沒喊痛，也沒大叫——她學得很快。接著我又開始威脅要殺掉她的老公和孩子。

en_text: I use a sheet to bind her arms and legs, another to cover her eyes. I tell her to keep still for twenty minutes, because I'm going to be back. Perhaps even sooner. If she's gone, I'll find her and kill her. If she's still here, I'll let her go. I don't want to create a crime scene. I can't afford any attention coming this way. Satisfied she isn't going anywhere in a hurry, I head into the corridor, wheel the cart into the bedroom so nobody will see it, then close the door.
zh_text: 我先拿起一條床單綑綁她的手腳，再拿起另外一條蒙住她的雙眼。我要她待著別動，因為我會在二十分鐘內回來，甚至更快。要是我回來後發現她已經逃跑，我就會找到她、幹掉她；要是她還在這裡，我則會放她走。我並不想把這房間搞成犯罪現場，也禁不起人人留意起這裡在搞什麼鬼。由於她並沒打算趕往別處，我放心地朝走廊走去，唯恐他人撞見，我甚至還把清潔車推進房裡才關門離開。

en_text: I put the key card into the lock of Detective Robert Calhoun's room. He'll be waiting for me, probably getting pretty impatient by now. I figure he'll give me maybe another ten minutes. Even if he's leaving now, he still has to drive into town. I've plenty of time to go through his room. I close the door behind me, shutting myself into complete darkness, then reach into my pocket and pull out the small flashlight I've brought along, then realize there's no point in sneaking around, and turn on the lights. The kitchen's bigger than mine, and Calhoun has a larger range of utensils, pots, and cutlery. I see he made himself a sandwich before leaving for work.
zh_text: 我把門卡插進了羅伯特·卡爾霍恩警探的房間。他很可能已經心浮氣躁，但他還是會等我，而且我猜會多等個十來分。即便他才剛剛離開，他也還是得開進市區，所以我有相當充裕的時間搜起他的房間。我關起身後的門，把自己困在一片漆黑之中，然後把手伸進口袋，掏出了那把隨身攜帶的小型手電筒。這裡的廚房比我那裡還大，餐具、鍋具也比我還多。我還看到他在上班前替自己做了個三明治。

en_text: In order for the police to get cheap rates, they need to do their own housecleaning, which includes dishes. Calhoun is a man in his fifties away from his wife, which means the dishes at the moment are stacked high and haven't been washed in about a week. He'll probably live off junk food for a few days before he'll wash them. I pull out my knife and set it on the bench next to its twin, making sure they're indeed identical.
