Satisfied, I wrap them into separate plastic bags, careful not to smudge Calhoun's fingerprints. I slide the bags into my pockets—mine in the left, Calhoun's in the right. Perfect.
zh_text: 警方爲了拿到比較優惠的住宿費，他們得自行打掃房間，包括洗碗。卡爾霍恩已經五十好幾，老婆又不在身邊，這意味著碗盤大概有一個禮拜沒洗、如今早已堆積如山。在他洗好碗盤之前，他很可能有好幾天要吃垃圾食物度日了。我掏出那把刀子，放在長椅上同一款刀子的旁邊，確認這兩把的確一模一樣。我感到非常滿意，將刀放入個別的塑膠袋，過程中小心翼翼，深怕抹去了卡爾霍恩的指紋。我把兩個袋子塞進口袋，我的刀放在左邊，卡爾霍恩的則放在右邊。

en_text: I look through his drawers, his suitcases. Even though he's been here more than a month, he's hardly unpacked. I find a collection of pornographic magazines, a pair of handcuffs (standard issue—though not for police), and a leather gag with a rubber ball in the center to keep people quiet. I consider taking it with me, but it's probably not wise. Anyway, I'm happy with my own technique. There are other sex toys, many of which I've never seen. The man's a real deviant, and I begin to admire him. The door automatically locks behind me when I leave.
zh_text: 天衣無縫。我搜遍了他的抽屉、公事包，即便他已在這住了一個多月，行李還是像剛剛打包那樣放得整整齊齊的。我還找到一整套的色情雜誌、一副手銬（標準尺寸——但算不上警方的標準尺寸）、中央放了橡膠球好教人無法開口的皮製口銜。我當下想要順手牽羊、帶走口銜，但這或許是不智之舉。總之，我對自己的技術還算自豪。這裡還有其他情趣用品，很多都是沒見過的。這男人真是變態，這下我開始仰慕他了。離開時，我身後的門自動上鎖。

en_text: It looks like the maid has struggled to escape from her bindings, but has failed. Pretty much what I expected. I move into the kitchen and find a third identical knife, which I put into a different plastic bag. Back in the bedroom, I tell the maid to shut up and to keep facing away from me. Then I untie the sheets, put my arm over her shoulder, and hand her a thousand dollars. This will definitely buy her silence, and I still consider myself up a grand after not paying Becky the other night. Plus it's good not to make another crime scene. I feel her eyes scanning over the money, her mind already spending it. I can see her thinking what she has to do to earn more. I tell her to stay where she is for another five minutes. If she understands, she's to nod. She nods vigorously while still looking at the money. I toss her key card onto the bed (a hard decision because I could have a fun time going from room to room), turn my back, and walk away, closing the door behind me. She's probably thinking that unless there's a report of a crime, there's no reason for her to tell anybody what happened. The knife from Calhoun's room feels heavier than the one I took there, even though it's identical. His fingerprints are weighing it down. Sometimes it's embarrassing to be so competent. Back in my room, I put my knife back in the kitchen, then clean the one I got from the room with the maid, slipping it back into a bag.
zh_text: 看來那個清潔婦一直想要掙脫，只不過未能成功。這全都在我預料之中。我挪動身子，進到廚房，找到了第三把一模一樣的刀子，再把它放進不同的塑膠袋裡。我回到房間，叫清潔婦乖乖閉嘴、背對著我，然後替她鬆綁、架起她的脖子，最後才交給她一千紐幣，這樣她保證會守口如瓶。我也在想那晚既然沒付錢給貝琪，那麼我是不是可以多貼給清潔婦一千塊錢。附帶一提，再搞出個犯罪現場可是大大不妥。我感覺到她正把錢從頭到尾掃過一遍，在她心裡，她已經在想怎麼花了；我也看得出她正在思考該怎麼做才能賺得更多。我又叫她在原地待個五分鐘。要是她懂我的意思，她就會點頭。於是她用力點頭，仍盯著錢看。我把她的鑰匙扔到床上（我真的是痛下決心才這麼做，因為有了這把鑰匙，我就可以逛起一間間房，樂在其中），轉身走開，關起身後的門。我口袋裡的刀子要比我從房裡拿來的那把還要重——即便它們根本就一模一樣。是卡爾霍恩的指紋，就是他的指紋增添了刀子的重量。人要是太過能幹也不太好。回房後，我把刀放回廚房，然後擦乾淨自己從清潔婦那間房所拿走的那一把，再接著滑入塑膠袋裡。

en_text: I'll go out tonight and do some window-shopping. There won't be any homework involved, because I can't base spontaneity on homework. Tonight should be fun.
zh_text: 今晚我會外出逛逛櫥窗。有所計畫就會少了隨機行動的樂趣。今晚應該會很好玩。

en_text: The biggest crime in Christchurch—apart from fashion and Old English architecture, glue-sniffing, too much greenery, bad driving, bad parking, lack of parking, wandering pedestrians, expensive shops, the winter smog, the summer smog, kids riding skateboards on sidewalks, kids riding bikes on sidewalks, old guys yelling Bible passages at anybody passing by, stupid policemen, stupid laws, too many drunks, too few shops, barking dogs, loud music, puddles of urine in shop doorways in the morning, puddles of vomit in the gutters, and the gray décor—is burglary. Burglaries occur every few minutes. Mostly thanks to teenagers who will grow up to become armed offenders who shoot people to get enough money to buy their daily prescription of drugs. Up there with burglary is car theft. Cars are stolen almost as often as homes are broken into. Therefore, you'd think more people would have car alarms. But they don't. They prefer to spend their money on expensive car stereos, which end up in cheap pawnshops. Therefore, stealing another car is not difficult. Not when you know how. Not when you're as good at it as I am. I'm driving around the outskirts of town in my new car, a Ford something or other, browsing for merchandise, looking for somebody who'll take my liking, or perhaps a house that looks reasonably unsecured, when it comes to me. An idea. As I know from experience, spontaneous ones are sometimes the best. I have to remind myself that sometimes they're not. My briefcase sits on the passenger seat, loaded with knives, scissors, and a pair of pliers. The briefcase is the toolbox for the modern serial killer. I head toward one of the nearby movie-theater complexes, which seem to be springing up all over the city at the rate of about one a year. I park this car among the many others. Here I wait, idly scratching at my crotch, flicking the window wipers every thirty seconds or so to clear the view. The flow of people is interrupted by the sessions starting and stopping and by the slow, the gossiping, and the disabled taking the longest to make their way to their cars. Finally, I spot the perfect victim. In her thirties, I guess. Long blond hair, high cheekbones, shiny wheelchair. I figure a person like this has nothing to lose, so killing her won't really be a crime—hell, she won't even feel half the things I'm planning to do to her.
zh_text: 除了時尚與老舊的英式建築、吸食強力膠、綠化過甚、危險駕駛、癟腳停車、停車一位難求、行人亂走、店家昂貴、冬夏起霧、小孩子在行人步道溜起滑板並騎起自行車、老人朝著任何一個路過的行人朗誦《聖經》的章節、白痴的警察、荒唐的法律、太多醉漢、太少店家、小狗亂叫、吵雜的樂聲、店家一早開張門口就有一窪窪的小便、排水溝浮起一攤攤的嘔吐物、灰色裝潢以及其他亂象之外，基督城裡最普遍的犯罪就是搶劫，而且每幾分鐘就會發生一起搶劫案。這多半要感謝那些即將長大成人、變成武裝小組最後卻爲了湊錢去買醫生每天所開出的藥而開槍殺人的青少年。然後僅次於搶劫的就是偷車。車子被偷幾乎和民宅遭闖一樣普遍。因此，你應該覺得會有不少人裝汽車警報器吧，但事實不然，與其裝汽車警報器，人們寧願花錢去買原先價格高昂最後卻淪落到廉價當鋪的汽車音響，也因此歹徒要再偷起其他車並非難事，特別當你已經知道怎麼偷、和我一樣擅長的時候，這更是不成問題。我開著那輛福特之類的新車在郊區兜風，看看有沒有什麼可買。此時我靈光一閃。根據以往的經驗，突如其來的靈感有時才是最棒的，但我得提醒自己偶爾也有例外。我那只裝滿刀子、剪刀和鉗子的公事包就放在乘客座上，它是連續殺人魔的工具箱。我朝著所在地附近其中一家綜合電影院駛去，這城市裡的綜合電影院以一年一家的速度如雨後春筍般蓬勃成長。我在諸多車子之間停好車，等著，然後懶散地搔著胯下。人潮被前往觀影和結束觀影的觀眾所打斷，行動緩慢的、邊走邊聊的還有不良於行的人都花了超久時間才順利找到自己的車。最後，我找到了那屬於我的完美獵物，她有著長長的金髮、高顴骨，並坐在亮晶晶的輪椅上，我猜她大概三十來歲。我想，這樣的人已經一無所有、不會再去計較什麼得失，所以殺掉她算不上是犯罪吧——她根本就沒察覺我打算對她下手。

en_text: I watch as the breathing corpse courageously makes her way into her car, using her arms to transfer her weight from the chair to the driver's seat. Then, with a skill only cripples can acquire, she swings the chair onto the roof of her car and clips it down. Amazing. It will be the last time she ever does it.
zh_text: 我看著那個行屍走肉大刺刺地往車子方向去，用雙臂把身體的重量從輪椅挪到駕駛座，還秀了一手殘障人士才可能具備的技能——把輪椅甩上車頂、扣上，眞不可思議。這可是她最後一次這麼做了。

en_text: I follow her home. The Ford is a late model and handles nicely. I turn on the air-conditioning and listen to the stereo. Quite the relaxing drive. I pull up outside a house a few down from hers, and give her twenty minutes to get inside and get herself settled. I'm guessing she lives alone. First, she's a cripple and nobody would want to love her; second, if she has a partner, then he would have been with her at the movies. Until now I never considered there was a use for the disabled, the retarded, and the crippled. The house has a single story—can't expect more for somebody in her condition. The garden is poorly looked after. The wheelchair ramp leading to the front door has a welcome mat at the bottom of it. I walk up just after eleven o'clock. Fumble with the lock. For somebody who lives inside a wheelchair, she has poor security. Life's like that. Those most prone to being attacked—the old, the weak, the beautiful—generally have maybe a chain across their door and a safety lock. Not much. Not much at all to somebody like me. The first port of call is the kitchen, where the appliances are all at waist level. I open her fridge and examine the contents. I do this not because I'm hungry, or thirsty, but because I've done it at many of the other victims' houses. The fridge offers nothing exciting to choose from. It appears she's a vegetarian. I don't get vegetarians.
zh_text: 這輛新型的福特非常好開，我一邊開車，一邊打開空調、聽著音樂，十分享受。一路跟蹤她回家後，我把車停在離她家不遠處，還給了她二十分鐘進到屋裡安頓自己。我猜她是一個人住，爲什麼呢？第一，她是殘疾人士，這種人沒人想愛；第二，要是她有男友，他們應該會一起看電影才對。截至目前爲止，我還沒想到殘疾、殘障還有智障人士有何用處。那間房子只有一樓——像她這樣的人，別期待太多——庭院也是雜草叢生，無人照料。一開始通往大門的無障礙坡下擺了一張「歡迎光臨」的鞋墊。就在十一點過後，我向上走去，摸起門鎖。對於一個住在屋裡還得靠輪椅才能生活的人，她實在是安全堪慮。人生就像這樣。像是年長、弱小和漂亮這種比較容易遭到襲擊的人或許普遍都會拴上門鏈、裝起安全鎖，但不太管用，特別是對我這樣的人完全沒用。首先我在廚房停留，那裡的廚具設備全都高及腰際。我打開冰箱，檢查裡頭的東西。我之所以這麼做，並不是因為餓了或是渴了，而是因為我在許多其他被害人的家裡也會這麼做。冰箱裡沒什麼出人意表的食物可選。她好像吃素，但我不是。

en_text: I select a carton of milk, drink directly from it, and set it down in the middle of the table. I wipe my arm across my mouth to get rid of the milk mustache, then make my way down the wide, uncarpeted hallway to her bedroom. No time for mucking around. Don't want to risk having her scream. So it'll have to be straight in there, and straight into it.
zh_text: 我選了紙盒包裝的牛奶，直接喝掉後放在桌子中央。我還擦了擦嘴，讓牛奶不致沾上鬍鬚，才徑自走往那條寬廣、沒鋪地毯且通往她房裡的走廊。這次襲擊得要速戰速決，沒時間讓我瞎搞。我可不想冒險讓她尖叫，所以得直接進去、直接搞定。

en_text: I'm in her room and subduing her before she's even aware of what's happening. I stop hitting her when a sudden searing pain appears in my hand. It feels like my little finger has been broken. I pray it hasn't, figuring that since God didn't help me out with my testicle, He owes me one. I just hope He's in a good mood. I won't need to worry about binding the woman's legs. No point. Just her hands. I use the cord from her phone next to the bed. She isn't going to be needing it. When I have her secure, I start massaging my finger. Feeling begins to seep back into it, and I breathe a sigh of relief. God loves me after all.
zh_text: 我進到她房裡，在她還沒意識到發生何事之前就先將她制伏，然而就在我的手感受到一陣突如其來的燒灼、小指有如斷掉之時，我停了下來，暗暗祈禱這不是真的，同時心想上帝既然沒有保住我的睪丸，祂應該還欠我一次呀。我只能希望祂現在心情不錯、願意幫我。我不必擔心要綁起這女人的雙腳，完全不用，只要綁起她的雙手就行了。她都快用不著床邊的電話線了，於是我先用電話線綁緊她的雙手，再按摩自己的手指。隨著手指慢慢回復知覺，我鬆了一口氣，心想上帝終究還是眷顧我的。

en_text: The padding on my testicle will stop me from doing what I'd normally do, but at least I can do us both a favor and save us some time. Careful not to get my hands too bloody, I use the knife I cleaned last night and, when I'm done, I pack it away and take out the one with Calhoun's fingerprints on it. The risk of smudging the prints now that the victim is dead is minimal. Even so, I'm careful when I slip the blade into one of the already open wounds. When I'm finished, I go through her cupboards and drawers, and end up borrowing some gear that she won't be needing anymore. I'm about to leave when I hear a humming coming from her living room. It's a fish tank. I stand silently and watch perhaps two dozen fish moving back and forth in the blue light. Immediately I think of Pickle and Jehovah. Immediately I wish I had picked another woman to have killed and not a fellow fish lover. The temptation to select two fish from this tank to keep is powerful, but I know I can never replace the two I've lost. No. The emptiness in my life must remain—at least until I've had the chance to mourn. The joy of having two new fish will only taste like ashes.
zh_text: 睪丸上的敷料讓我無法像平常那樣靈活，但我至少可以幫忙彼此，替大家省點時間。爲了避免雙手弄得太過血腥，我小心用起昨晚擦過的那把刀子，在完事後把它裝進另一個袋子，再拿出沾有卡爾霍恩指紋的那一把。既然被害人已經死了，抹去指紋的風險也就變得微乎其微。即便如此，我在把刀送入已被劃開的傷口時依舊不敢大意。搞定之後，我把她的樹櫃、抽屜整個看過一遍，最後借走了一些她永遠都用不著的家用品。就在我打算離開時，我從她家客廳聽到了「嗡嗡嗡」的低鳴聲——是魚缸。我默默站著，看著二十幾條魚在藍光下來回悠游。我頓時聯想到泡菜和耶和華，衝動地想從魚缸裡挑走兩條，但我很清楚自己絕不可能找到取代他們的魚。不可能。我得繼續維持生命中的空虛，至少維持到我有哀悼的機會爲止。養兩條新魚所帶來的喜悅只不過曇花一現。

en_text: I stay feeling pretty bad for killing Little Miss Cripple as I'm leaving her house. She loved fish, and I loved fish. We lived alone with them. They were our friends. We were their gods. Before she was just a person I didn't know, but now she's somebody I can relate to. In another life, maybe we could have been friends. Or even more. I leave the front door open, figuring her body will be found quicker that way by a concerned neighbor or late-night burglar. The best I can do for her now is to hope she has a nice funeral. Before walking to my car, I check if I've got any blood on me. A few dark spots have flicked onto me, but they're close to impossible to see on my dark overalls.
zh_text: 實際上，在殺了殘廢小姐之後，我覺得很糟。她這麼愛魚，而我也愛魚。我們都獨自和魚一起生活，魚等於是我們的朋友，然後我們就是他們的神。從前我對她一無所知，現在卻和她有所交集。來生我們也許可以結爲好友，甚至不止這樣。我開著前門，想藉此讓關心的鄰居或深夜的搶匪快點發現她的屍體。現在我所能爲她做的，就是盼她入土爲安、一路好走。在我走到車子之前，我檢查身上是否沾有血跡，結果發現衣服上濺到了幾處深紅的血斑，只不過血斑和我一身打扮的顏色十分相近，不可能看得出來。

en_text: I drive directly to the hotel, make sure no policemen are around, then go to my room. Safely inside, I clean down the actual murder weapon, soak it in some bleach for ten minutes that I took from work, then roll it back into the plastic bag. Ideally I'd like to put it back where I got it, but this isn't an ideal world. I'll dump it elsewhere.
zh_text: 我直接把車開到旅館，很快地巡視一遍，確定四周沒有警察這才走進房間。房裡非常安全，於是我先把實際的兇器擦乾淨，再放回塑膠袋裡。原本我想得很美，想把刀放回原處，但這世界可沒我想的這麼美，於是我打算把刀扔在別處。

en_text: I remove the pad from my testicle, knowing that I'll have to replace it soon. I sit on the edge of the bed first and examine my genitals in the mirror. I'm expecting to see this black, infected thing that will probably see me either in the hospital or in a morgue. What I see is wrinkled skin covered in dry blood and talcum powder, and as I dab it away with a damp corner of the towel, I see that Melissa's work has been effective. The area is inflamed from all the scratching, and on closer examination, I see why it has been so itchy. The stitches are overdue for removal.
zh_text: 我取下睾丸上的敷料，清楚自己很快就得換藥。我先是坐在床緣，對著鏡子檢查著生殖器。我原本預期會看到呈現黑色、受到感染然後不是讓我住院就是喪命的部位，但如今我所看到的是一片皺巴巴又覆蓋起乾掉血跡和痱子粉的肌膚，而且在我用毛巾沾濕的一角擦去血跡和痱子粉的同時，我發現梅莉莎的包紮已經有所成效。整片傷口雖然因我抓個不停而發炎，但只要湊近一看，就會發現傷口之所以一直很癢只是因為我拖了太久沒拆線。

en_text: I don't want Melissa making another visit to help me out, so I head into the bathroom and grab the small sewing kit that's wrapped up in a matchbook-size box next to the soaps. With a towel beneath me on the bed, ever so slowly I use the needle to tug at the stitches, loosening them enough to then use one of my smaller knives to cut them. My whole groin, the base of my stomach, and the tops of my thighs start to hurt, but the pain is tolerable—the hardest part is knowing what will happen if I slip. But I don't slip, and each thread vibrates through my body as I draw it through and away from the skin. I wonder if this wouldn't be a better procedure if I were drunk, but decide that it probably wouldn't be—not at the prices I'd have to pay to access the minibar. My sac begins to bleed, but only lightly.
zh_text: 我不希望梅莉莎再來探望我、幫忙我，所以我走進浴室，抓起昨晚在上痱子粉時所看到的剪刀和鑷子。我坐在床上，底下鋪著一條毛巾，然後即便動作極其緩慢，我還是用鑷子拉起縫線，剪了一刀。刹那間我整個胯下、胃下和大腿根部都開始疼痛，但那種痛還能忍受。隨著我從皮膚拉出線來，一條條的縫線都牽動著我的肉身。我心想自己要是醉了，過程中是否就會舒服一點，但我後來判斷可能不會——醉了只會把傷口弄得更糟，這種代價我可付不起啊。我的陰囊開始流血，但只是輕微出血。

en_text: I clean up and take a long shower. The nozzle is directional and I can control the pressure of the spray. It's wonderful. My groin feels better, and I wonder why I didn't become a surgeon instead of a cleaner. After half an hour, I climb out and towel myself down. All the blood is gone—both the cripple's and mine. The throbbing has gone too and, better still, so has the itching. I'm recovering. I will never be the same, but I'm recovering nonetheless. I collapse between the cool sheets and close my eyes.
zh_text: 我清理之後沖了好久的澡。蓮蓬頭是活動式的，所以我能控制出水的水壓。真是太棒了，這下我的胯下好多了，我心想自己幹嘛去當清潔工，我大可以去當個外科醫生呀。半小時後，我踏出浴缸，從頭到尾把身體擦乾。如今不管是殘障小姐還是我，全身上下都已經看不到任何血跡，肌膚的表面也不再抽動，更棒的是，就連搔癢的感覺也消失得無影無蹤。我癱倒在涼爽的被單之間，然後闔上雙眼。

en_text: The next day is work as usual. The old guy giving the forecast earns his pay by getting things right. I guess he's looking out the window at the frost rather than reading off the report in his hand. My biggest concern is running into Detective Calhoun. I use the stairs rather than the elevator, scratching at my crotch the entire way down. In the foyer a bunch of tourists is being given directions by the doorman in English, which they are having trouble understanding. A few taxi drivers carrying luggage to and from taxis. People checking in. People checking out. No Calhoun. I look outside. The storm clouds last night weren't bluffing. Every surface I can see is wet.
zh_text: 隔天又是一如既往的工作日。那個老傢伙又透過準確的天氣預報掙得了薪資。我猜他正望出窗外、看著太陽，而不是流利地朗讀他手上的報告。我選擇爬起樓梯，不搭電梯，以防自己撞見卡爾霍恩。門廳裡一堆觀光客正在向警衛問路，但他們對於警衛所說的英文有如鴨子聽雷、有聽沒懂。有些計程車司機正把行李搬上搬下。人們登記入房、退房，就是不見卡爾霍恩的蹤影。

en_text: I check out of the hotel. I keep looking around so often that the hotel clerk must think I'm paranoid. There aren't any extra charges. The clerk asks me if I've had a pleasant stay, and I tell him I have. He asks me where I'm from, and I realize I can't say Christchurch, because then I'd look like an idiot. Who the hell spends a few nights in a five-star hotel in their own city? I tell him I'm from up north. He asks me exactly where, and I suddenly understand why he is asking all these questions—he is hitting on me. I tell him Auckland, and he tells me he is from Auckland too. He tells me it's a small world. I tell him it's not small enough, and he has to think about this for a few seconds until he realizes that in my small world he wouldn't even exist. I can actually see his thought process as his smile slowly disappears. I walk to work. It's one of those nothing kind of days, where it could end up being sunny or could end up raining but you just don't know and don't really care. I'm feeling good about a whole lot of different things, among them that my testicle isn't itching this morning. Sally is on my floor when I get to work. She looks me up and down. She seems distracted. "Do anything exciting last night?" she asks.
zh_text: 我一邊辦理退房，一邊不斷地東張西望，飯店的櫃檯人員鐵定覺得我是個偏執狂。由於我沒什麼額外的住房費用，所以信用卡不見了也無所謂，只要直接簽名、毋須再過卡一次。櫃檯人員問我房間一切還好嗎，我說都很好，他還問我是從哪來的，我驚覺自己可不能回答是從基督城來的，因為這樣聽起來挺白痴的——誰會在自己居住的城市花起大把鈔票選個五星級旅館住上好幾晚啊？於是就說是從北方來的，而就在他問起確切的地點時，我突然了解他之所以問這麼多，全是因為他煞到我了。我說我是從奧克蘭來的，他就說他也是從奧克蘭來的，還說這世界真小、我倆真有緣。後來我說這世界還不夠小，他還得思考一會兒才聽懂我口中的小小世界根本就沒有他的存在。隨著他慢慢斂起笑容，其實我看得出他在想些什麼。我走路上班。今天風和日麗，所有截然不同的事物都讓我覺得很棒，其中之一就是今早我的睪丸不癢了。我到班時，莎莉正在清理我的樓層，整個人看似心不在焉。「昨晚忙了什麼新鮮事嗎？」

en_text: Here we go again, back to people's fascinations about what other people do with their time. "Not much. Just stayed at home and watched TV." "Sounds nice," she says, then walks off.
zh_text: 我們又開始上演每早的戲碼。「沒什麼，就待在家裡看電視而已。」「聽起來很不賴啊。」她一邊說，一邊走開。

en_text: I begin my day with cleaning the toilets on the first floor. The body of the crippled woman is found. Tragic, apparently. Inhumane too, people are saying. A disgraceful country we must be living in, according to the news. Where will it end? people keep asking, but nobody asks me. In my office, I use a felt marker to darken the spots of blood on my overalls and make them look like ink stains. While the stressed-out detectives look for the killer, I sit in my office and make a call with the cell phone. I sit with my chair against the door just in case Sally comes along and tries to come in.
zh_text: 我以打掃起二樓的盥洗室揭開今天的序幕。那個殘障女人的屍體已經被人發現。人們顯然不是說「眞慘」，就是「禽獸不如」，新聞報導還會用起「我們居住的國家眞是何其醜陋」的字句，人們甚至會追問起「這種事何時才會告一段落？」但就是沒人會來問我。我在辦公室拿起麥克筆畫起連身工作褲上的血跡，讓它們顏色加深，看來像是墨點。就在警探備感壓力、加緊絹兇的同時，我就坐在辦公室裡，拿手機撥起電話。唯恐莎莉一路跟來、試圖闖進辦公室，我拿椅子抵住門邊，然後坐在上面。

en_text: Detective Calhoun answers. I apologize for not meeting him two nights ago. He tells me exactly what he thinks of me. We exchange a few more pleasantries before agreeing to meet once again, this time at six o'clock tonight, at the Walker house. Reluctantly, he agrees. Without thanking me, he hangs up. After lunch, I listen closely to find out if the detectives are plotting to stake out the Walker place. Nobody makes any reference to it. Calhoun has kept the information to himself. That means he's sticking with his game plan of killing me. Then suddenly everything around the station gets even busier. I don't get the details, but enough to know another body has been found this morning—this one nothing to do with me. Some guy has gotten himself killed in a pretty nasty way at a church somewhere here in town. So the workload is doubled because now they have the dead woman in the wheelchair, and the dead guy at the church, and what they really need is twice as many cops. Every half hour or so I run into Sally, but she doesn't seem in the mood for talking. She'll look at me from the end of a corridor or stairway, and she'll stare at me with this look on her face that suggests she is lost, but not once does she come up to me and make the sort of inane conversation that makes me want to scream. I must admit I miss the lunches she makes, and I make a mental note to suggest my hunger to her so it may inspire her to start making them again.
zh_text: 卡爾霍恩偵緝督察接起電話。我爲昨晚爽約道了歉，他也確實地告訴我他是怎麼看待我這個人。我們互開了對方幾個玩笑後，才說好再碰一次面，這回訂在今晚六點，地點選在沃克家。他心不甘情不願地答應了，緊接著掛上電話，連句謝謝也沒說。午餐過後，我仔細監聽，打算找出偵絹督察是否密謀派人監視渥克屋，結果發現完全沒人提及此事，看來卡爾霍恩眞的是守口如瓶。這也意味著他死守著獨自幹掉我的遊戲計畫。我大概每隔半小時就會撞見莎莉，但她似乎沒心情聊天，都只在走廊底或樓梯口一臉茫然的看著我、盯著我，而不像往常那樣找我聊些白痴到只想讓我尖叫的內容。我得承認自己非常想念她所替我準備的午餐，於是我提醒自己務必向她暗示我對餐點的渴望，這樣她才會受到鼓舞，再次爲我備餐。時間緩緩流逝，如今已是下午四點半，我可以忙裡偷閒了。我回到辦公室，又打了通電話，這次同樣是打到警局，並要求和重案組的人通話。當我一說手上握有情報，電話就直接轉給了卡爾·史卓德。

en_text: Four thirty rolls along, and with it, the chance to enjoy my day. Back in my office I make another cell phone call, this one also to the police station. I ask to speak to somebody in homicide. When I say I may have some information, I'm transferred directly to Carl Schroder's phone. I skip the part where I'm supposed to give him my name, telling him I know how these things work, and although I'm willing to help, I'm not prepared to testify in court for reasons I don't want to discuss, but which mostly involve my own safety. He disagrees with my fears, but doesn't push it, probably because ninety-five percent of calls he gets are from crackpots. Regardless, he sounds desperate to know what I know. I tell him it isn't what I know, but what I've found. I give him directions to the trash dumpster three blocks away from last night's crime scene. When asked how I found it there, I answer by telling him I saw a man dropping it off, and once I learned of the murder today, I decided to call them.
zh_text: 我跳過了自報姓名的那部分，告訴他我很清楚他們是如何蒐證，還有我雖然樂於幫忙，但並不打算爲了自己不想討論的原因出庭作證，其中多半也是基於人身安全考量。他對我的憂慮不以爲然，卻並未對我施壓，或許因爲他所接到電話中有九成五都是瘋子吧。無論如何，聽他的口氣，他還是迫不及待地想要得知我手上的情報。我告訴他我手上的情報不是從別人那兒聽來的，而是自己發現的，還向他明確指出昨晚犯罪現場的三個路口外有個大型的垃圾箱。當他問及我怎會發現在那有個垃圾箱，我說自己曾經親眼目睹有個男人把東西往裡頭一丟，然後今天一聽到發生謀殺案就決定報警。

en_text: Sure. Why not? I give a brief description of Calhoun before hanging up on more questions. It's nothing like the picture of "me" hanging in the conference room.
zh_text: 當然啦，有何不可？我概述了卡爾霍恩的特徵，而且在他來不及問起更多時就把電話給掛了，這可不像會議室掛起「我的」照片那樣可以讓他問個不停。我離開辦公室，看到史卓德偵緝督察就坐在辦公桌旁。他看著我，只不過兩眼無神，然後在我還沒走到門邊就一口氣跳了起來、抓起鑰匙，一路衝往卡爾霍恩警探的辦公室。他倆先是互相討論，之後才火速移往出口。

en_text: I slip on a pair of latex gloves and put my hands under the mattress, searching for the parking ticket I kept as a memento months ago. Only I can't find it. I bury my arms in until I'm up to my shoulders, swirling them around, searching, searching . . . but it's gone.
zh_text: 我戴上橡膠手套，雙手伸進床墊下，摸起自己在幾個月前留下來作紀念的停車卡，但這會兒卻怎麼也找不到。我連兩隻手臂都伸了進去，左右掃過一遍，到處找呀找，但就是找不到……票卡不見了！

en_text: Why would she even look here?
zh_text: 她怎會連床墊下都看呢？

en_text: But I already know why. People hide things under their mattresses all the time. It was stupid of me to hide the ticket there. But then I remember flipping the bed when trying to get hold of that stupid cat. I get down on my hands and knees and look under it, and sure enough, there's the ticket. I put it in my briefcase, then take off my gloves. After walking a few blocks, I use the usual mode of illegal transport to make my way to the house where I'm meeting Calhoun. Each of us is intending to kill the other, though, supposedly, neither of us knows that. By the time I get there it is five forty. I'm sure I've beaten Calhoun because he has a long day dealing with the dead.
zh_text: 這下我知道原因了。人們老愛在床墊下藏東西，我眞是笨到不行，居然還把票卡藏在那裡。我掀起床單扔到地上，將床墊靠在牆上，然後繼續找，必須確認票卡眞的不在那裡才行。我趴下身子，往床底一探，結果……有了！我在鋪床的當下才想到票怎會跑到床底。在我試圖弄死那隻可惡的貓時，我曾翻過床來靠在牆上。拿到票後，我把它收進公事包才取下手套。在走過幾個街口之後，我東彎西拐、抄起捷徑，採用自己一貫方式前往即將和卡爾霍恩碰面的那間屋子。雖然我倆都企圖殺掉對方，但對方大概不知情。我一到那裡的時間是五點四十分。我很肯定自己已經打敗卡爾霍恩，因為史卓德一心覺得他和那把殺人兇器脫離不了干係。我猜，我的時間綽綽有餘。

en_text: I park several blocks away and walk. The night is as cold as the morning, and I fear winter may end up being just as long as summer. When I reach the house, I suddenly have this fear that maybe the residents have moved back in and family life is under way again. I suck in a few deep breaths. No, if anybody was living here, I'd have heard about it by now.
zh_text: 我把車停在幾個路口外，下車步行。今晚和今早一樣暖和，輕柔的微風教我渾身放鬆。當我到了屋前，我突然擔心起這裡的住戶也許已搬了回來，重新展開屬於他們的家庭生活。我用力吸了幾口氣。不對。這裡要是早有人住，我應該已經聽說了。

en_text: I use my skills to unlock the front door and use my foot to close it behind me. I stand still in the hallway and listen for sounds of life. No one here. The bedroom seems the place to be, since it has the most history now, so I head there first. I open my briefcase and, regretting the lack of a firearm that could end this whole drama quickly, I pull out a hammer. Under the circumstances it's the best I can do. But looking at it, the hammer seems the wrong way to go—too easy to end up putting a hole in his skull and killing him. I head to the kitchen to look for something better. I return to the bedroom, now the proud owner of a large frying pan. It's nonstick. I sit on the bed and watch the hands on my watch tick around, waiting for Detective Calhoun to arrive.
zh_text: 我開了前門的鎖，然後用腳往後一蹬，把門踢上。我仍舊站在走廊，確認屋裡是否有人聲。沒人。既然臥房截至目前爲止歷史最爲輝煌，那麼那裡似乎是最妥當的地點，於是我逕向臥房走去，打開公事包，並掏出了一把大榔頭——少了槍真是可惜，不然事情就能速戰速決——在這種情況下，我充其量只能做到這種地步。但我要是下手太重，很可能會敲破他的頭顱，所以我決定到廚房找找有否較好用的器具。後來我回到臥房，手裡有了一只大煎鍋，眞令人自豪。我坐在床上，一邊望著錶上的指針滴滴答答，一邊默默等著卡爾霍恩警探的到來。

en_text: She's sick of not knowing. Sick of the questions. Sick of being sick. At four fifteen, Sally leaves work. She doesn't need to justify leaving early. Others here know her father is in bad shape and that she wants to spend time helping him. Not that anybody would notice—it's been a very active day in the world of a homicide detective. She's always hated days like this, and hates that they come around so often. At four twenty, when she reaches the parking building, Henry isn't here. She isn't sure whether she ought to be disappointed or flattered that he must only show up at four thirty for her. She doesn't know whether to feel used or wanted.
zh_text: 她對被人蒙在鼓裡感到厭煩、對問題感到厭煩，就連對厭煩本身也感到厭煩。四點十五分莎莉就下班了。她毋須爲自己早退找起正當的理由，因爲人人都知道她老爸身體欠佳，然後她想花時間照顧他。四點二十分，當她到了停車大樓，亨利不在。關於他得在四點半就現身等她這事兒，她不定自己是該暗暗失望，還是受寵若驚；也不知道是該覺得被人利用了，還是被人需要。

en_text: She drives past the police station, does a U-turn, and finds a parking spot on the opposite side of the road. Four thirty arrives, but Joe fails to. She can never remember him not leaving exactly at four thirty. Has he left already?
zh_text: 她開車經過警察局，迴轉，然後在對面路邊找到了停車位。都已經四點半了喬還沒來。她記得喬總是準時四點離開。不知道他離開了沒？

en_text: She waits another five minutes. Still no Joe.
zh_text: 她又等了五分鐘，還是不見喬的蹤影。

en_text: Just what are you doing? Planning on following him around? Still trying to help him?
zh_text: 妳在幹嘛？打算跟蹤他？還是試著幫他？

en_text: Exactly. She wants to see if he's meeting anybody. Perhaps the woman he spoke to earlier in the week, the witness from the police station. Five minutes later, she starts the car and, disappointed, pulls away. She wasn't comfortable about waiting anyway.
zh_text: 沒錯。她想看看他是不是正在和誰約會。也許他約會的對象就是他在禮拜一、禮拜二講過話的那個女人，也就是目擊證人。五分鐘後，她啟動引擎，開車上路。對於等人這事兒，她沒什麼耐性。

en_text: She's at a red light when she sees Joe in the rearview mirror on the sidewalk. The lights turn green. She doesn't know what to do. A car behind her starts tooting. By the time she turns around, Joe's already disappeared. He's probably already on the bus.
zh_text: 當她等起紅綠燈，她從後照鏡看到了喬，此時燈號轉綠，她不知如何是好，後面車子也開始按起喇叭，而待她迴轉成功，喬早已消失得無影無蹤。他很可能已經搭上公車。

en_text: She starts driving to the graveyard, but a few minutes later she finds she's not actually going in that direction, but back toward Joe's apartment. She needs to talk to him away from the station. She hopes talking doesn't turn into confronting. She parks down the street and decides to wait twenty minutes at the most. He arrives in half that time.
zh_text: 她開始開往墓園，但過了一會兒，她總覺得自己得去見喬一面，於是就把車停在喬公寓外的街上，決定最多等個二十分鐘。結果過了十分鐘喬就出現了。

en_text: She waits in the car imagining the outcome of their talk and trying to figure out whether she should go and knock on his door, or just drive away. Plus sits waiting to see if anybody else is coming to see him, and all that waiting takes the decision to talk to him out of her hands because Joe is only in his apartment for a few minutes before coming back out. He starts walking away from her. She begins to follow him. By the time she rounds the corner, he's turning left down another street. She slows down a little. She has never followed anybody before, and she suddenly realizes she isn't very good at it. She inches her car closer to the corner, and is about to go around it when Joe appears from the left, driving through the intersection. In a different car from the one she saw him in last time. She keeps pace with him, trying to keep a car between them, until he slows down in an upper-class area and pulls over to the curb. Sally keeps on driving, watching him in the rearview mirror. He climbs out and walks to the end of the block, his briefcase swinging slightly back and forth with his momentum.
zh_text: 她坐在車裡，不確定是該當面叫住他，還是靜觀其變、看看會不會有人來這看他。做出決定是不容易，但喬只要再次現身，過沒多久她也就毋須爲此憂心。他走得離她越來越遠，她則跟蹤起他。就在她拐了個彎後，他又在另一條街上左轉，於是她放慢速度。她從沒跟蹤過別人，現在才突然領悟自己對這種事並不擅長。她緩緩開往那個轉角，越開越近，再拐個彎就會看到喬出現在左手邊、正要開車經過十字路口。他這次開的車和她上次所看到的並不相同。她跟起他的車，直到他在某個高級地段放慢速度然後把車停在路邊。莎莉繼續開著，透過後照鏡盯著他看。他跨出車門，逕往街區走了進去，公事包則隨他一前一後微微甩動。

en_text: She follows him to a two-story house, where he heads up the path and disappears from sight within the alcove of the front door. Something about the house is familiar, but she can't figure out what. And if it were something as innocent as meeting a friend, why would Joe park a short distance away? Why not just up the driveway? People who park a few blocks away are normally people who are having affairs, she thinks. Parking a few blocks away is definitely an affair kind of thing to do, but Joe isn't an affair kind of guy. He's not a . . . a what? Well, he's not a sexual kind of guy. He's Joe. He's like her brother. Only Joe can drive and sneak around and can steal and lie.
zh_text: 她跟蹤他到了一間兩層樓的房子，他正往屋前的小徑走去，隨後在前門的凹處消失蹤影。這房子感覺非常熟悉，但她就是想不起來，況且喬若只是要來見個朋友、如此單純，那他幹嘛不停在附近或者車道那邊就好？

en_text: Ten minutes pass. Twenty. After a while, Sally starts to realize she's whispering a prayer. She wants Joe to reappear and carry on; she wants him to be okay. Maybe something bad is happening to him, and all she's doing is sitting out here and waiting, letting the bad things happen to Joe the same way she let the bad things happen to Martin five years ago. "Stupid, stupid, stupid," she mutters, hitting the palm of her hand against her forehead.
zh_text: 十分鐘過去了。緊接著二十分鐘。過了一會兒，莎莉意識到自己正在默默禱告，希望喬能再次現身、處理之後的事，也希望他能平安無事。或許此時他正遭遇不測，但她只是坐在外面枯等，眼巴巴地看著喬就和五年前的馬丁一樣遭遇不測。「妳真是笨、笨、笨死了！」她一邊咕噥，一邊用掌心打起額頭。

en_text: Then, a few minutes later, a car pulls into the driveway and a man climbs out. She's slightly too far away to recognize him, but, like the house, something about the man is familiar. He moves quickly to the front door and steps inside.
zh_text: 又過了一會兒，有輛車停進車道，然後有個男人下了車。她距離那人太遠，以致完全認不出他是何方神聖，但就和這間房子一樣，那男人感覺也非常熟悉。他迅速走到前門，踏進屋裡。

en_text: Calhoun starts to turn as I make my way from behind the bedroom door. He raises his arm to protect himself from the swinging frying pan. He's able to get his elbow in the way; the pan cracks into it, then deflects into his chest. He staggers backward, and I stumble forward, crashing into him. We both drop to the ground, and then he's reaching into his jacket for his gun. My mind's racing so fast that I have time to comprehend that I'm failing, time to ask why he never had his gun in his hand in the first place, time to speculate that he wanted me to trust him first so that he could learn what I knew. I make my way to my knees as he leans upward, and I can see the surprise in his face because he knows who I am, but that knowledge doesn't make him any less desperate to kill me. I crash my head forward, connecting with his forehead and hurting myself as much as him, but at least his hand falls away from the gun. Lights flare behind my eyes—a hundred, no, a thousand of them—all at once and all in the same shade of white, but then the reds start to filter through, but compared to the pain I've known lately, this is nothing, and I'm quickly able to recover. I wobble back and the room spins only a little. I know Calhoun must be feeling the same way, just as I know I can't give him a second chance. I'm still holding the frying pan, and I quickly decide to use it.
zh_text: 我從臥房門後走上前，卡爾霍恩轉過身來舉手擋格，保護自己別被揮來的煎鍋擊中。他用手肘擋在中間，煎鍋於是打歪，「砰」一聲斜斜滑進了他的胸前。他踉蹌而退，我則向前絆了一跤，整個跌在他身上。我倆雙雙摔落在地，接著他掏出槍來。我的思緒跳躍得如此之快，以致我有充分的時間知道自己快要摔倒，也有充分的時間問他怎沒一開始就持槍在手，更有充分的時間推測他希望我一開始就信任他，那麼他才能從我口中套出情報。在他坐起身子的同時，我正曲膝跪在地上，還能看見他因為得知我是誰而流露出驚訝的神情。但知道歸知道，他要致我於死的念頭依舊不減。我以自己的頭撞向他的頭——我有多痛他就有多痛——把槍撞掉了。我眼冒金星，而且是上百個金星，不止，應該有上千個吧，它們突然以相同金色的形狀出現在我的眼前，只不過後來漸漸轉成紅色。我搖搖晃晃，向後傾倒，房間彷彿開始天旋地轉。就在我知道自己不能再給他逮到第二次機會的同時，我知道卡爾霍恩一定也和我有著相同的感受。我仍手握煎鍋，於是當機立斷，決定再次善用手上的利器。

en_text: When I look at him, there are two Detective Calhouns, two bedroom doors, two of everything. I shake my head and the room keeps spinning, but the images begin to form into one. I roll my body, raise my heavy arms, and swing the pan against the side of his head. It connects with his cheekbone and jaw, possibly breaking the former and maybe dislocating the latter. He falls back to the ground and doesn't move. Exhausted, I let the pan fall to the floor. I roll him onto his front and bind his hands behind him, then tie his legs. When I try to open his mouth, I discover I've dislocated his jaw. Since I need to make conversation with him later, I grip hold of his mouth and try to move it back. Nothing happens. I tap it with the hammer—softly at first, then harder—and after a few blows it clicks back into place. I open his mouth and place the egg inside, then change my mind. I won't risk the egg slipping to the back of his throat while he's unconscious and killing him. I use a pair of the husband's underwear to gag him instead.
zh_text: 當我盯著他看，我看到的是什麼東西都有兩個影子。我甩了甩頭，房間還是天旋地轉，只不過多重影像開始慢慢合而爲一。我轉了個身，舉起沉重的雙臂，拿煎鍋朝他側臉揮去。鍋身就打上他的顴骨和下巴，前者可能已經碎裂，後者或許也已易位。被我這麼一揮，他又摔倒在地、動也不動，我則是精疲力盡，手上一鬆，煎鍋就這麼落至地面。我替他翻了個身，先反綁他的雙手，再綑起他的雙腿。當我試圖撐開他的嘴巴，我才發現他的下巴已經被我打歪。既然稍後還得和他對談，我得先撐住他的嘴巴，試圖接回下巴，但眼見這麼做無濟於事，我這才拿大榔頭敲了起來。起初我輕輕敲，後來越敲越重，而且在重重敲了幾下之後，下巴才「喀」一聲接回原處。我撐開他的嘴巴，放了顆蛋，卻隨即改變主意——我可不能冒險在他昏迷不醒時讓蛋滑下他的喉嚨然後將他噎死。於是我轉而拿起一條男主人的內褲當綁嘴布，好讓他開不了口。

en_text: By the time Calhoun wakes up I have him sitting in a chair I've brought up from the dining room. I've used rope to secure him to it and, because the chair has metal legs, even if he can somehow tip it over it won't break. I wrap duct tape around his legs and reinforce them to the chair, and run more tape around his arms. Unless he's Harry Houdini, he won't be going anywhere. I crouch in front of him. He's staring at me, as if the face he saw before being knocked out couldn't possibly be the one he's seeing now. How is it possible that Joe—Joe the cleaner, Joe the fucked-up retard—is doing this to him? Can it be that the man they've been looking for has been working for them all this time?
zh_text: 待卡爾霍恩悠悠轉醒，我讓他坐在我從飯廳所拿來的椅子上，再用繩子加以固定。因為四個椅腳都是金屬，所以不管他用什麼方法把椅子翻轉過來，椅腳都斷不了。除了繩子，我還用膠帶把他的雙腿纏在椅子上，並在手臂多繞了好幾圈。除非他是逃脫大師胡迪尼，否則他根本就動彈不得、哪兒也去不了。我跏在他的面前，他則盯著我看，彷彿他正盯著的這張臉，不可能就是他被打昏之前所看到的那張臉。喬，清潔工喬，去他媽的智障喬居然有辦法對他幹起這種事？他們一直在找的那個人難道一直以來都在替他們工作？

en_text: I nod, confirming that yes, it is not only possible, but better than possible. He grunts, either to confirm his surprise, or to ask me why, or perhaps to test the gag in his mouth. Whatever the reason, he can't sustain much of a noise. The pain in his jaw must be killing him. Blood hangs off his bottom lip. I want to tell him it's nothing compared to having a testicle torn off, but I don't want anybody else knowing about that.
zh_text: 我點了點頭，確認答案就是「對，他不但有辦法，而且是很有辦法」。他「哼」了一聲，不是要證實自己非常驚訝，就是要問我幹嘛這樣，又或者只是想測試一下鄉嘴布管不管用。無論如何，他的下唇滴起鮮血，下巴鐵定也痛得要命，他可承受不了發出更多的噪音。我很想告訴他，比起一顆睾丸被人扯掉，這根本就不足爲道，但此事我並不想張揚。

en_text: He grunts, either to confirm his surprise, or to ask me why, or perhaps to test the gag in his mouth. Whatever the reason, he can't sustain much of a noise. The pain in his jaw must be killing him. Blood hangs off his bottom lip. I want to tell him it's nothing compared to having a testicle torn off, but I don't want anybody else knowing about that. "You killed her, didn't you?" "Uh-uh." He shakes his head. "I didn't ki' any'ody." "Yes, you did."
zh_text: 他「哼」了一聲，不是要證實自己非常驚訝，就是要問我幹嘛這樣，又或者只是想測試一下鄉嘴布管不管用。無論如何，他的下唇滴起鮮血，下巴鐵定也痛得要命，他可承受不了發出更多的噪音。我很想告訴他，比起一顆睾丸被人扯掉，這根本就不足爲道，但此事我並不想張揚。「是你殺了她吧？」「呃啊……」他搖了搖頭，「偶耶欸額啊（我誰也沒殺）。」才怪，就是你殺的。」

en_text: This time, shaking his head, he repeats himself. Almost. "No. No, I didn't, you cwasy fasdid." I think he has just called me a crazy bastard. Perhaps I am. Perhaps that's my problem. I test his theory by standing up and punching him in the stomach.
zh_text: 這次他一邊搖頭，一邊盡可能地重複說著：「惡惡，偶額噁，以惡恨幹、哼個（不不，我沒有，你這混蛋、瘋子）。」我想，他剛是在罵我混蛋、瘋子。也許我眞的是。也許這就是我的毛病。我透過站起身子、一拳打在他的胃上證明他的論點。

en_text: Will you look at that? He was right. Only I'm a bastard who needs to make a deal.
zh_text: 你看到了嗎？他說得很對，只不過我是個需要交換條件的混蛋。

en_text: "I'm going to take off your gag," I say, leaning forward once more. "You know the drill. If you don't, then assume it. Any sound," I say, raising the knife to his mouth, "has an unpleasant ending for you. Nod if you understand." I'm still being a bastard, because I'm holding the tip of the blade directly beneath his chin, so as he nods, he keeps pricking himself. I ensure this by raising the knife higher every time his head rises. In the end, he nods with his eyes. I use the knife to cut his gag. It falls away and hangs around his neck like a collar.
zh_text: 「我打算拿掉你的鄉嘴布。」我說，再次向前傾身。「你知道電鑽吧？要是你不知道那是什麼，那就想像一下。要是你敢出聲，」我說，在他嘴邊舉起刀子，「就會死得非常難看。聽懂就給我點點頭。」我還是一副混蛋欠扁的德行，因為我就這樣拿刀抵住他的下巴，讓他在不停點頭時把刀給刺進肉裡。他每每抬起頭來，我就把刀頂得更高、確定我是認真的，最後他只好上下移動眼球代替點頭。我拿刀劃破鄉嘴布，它應聲而斷，有如領子那般掛在他的頸上。

en_text: "Better?"
zh_text: 「好多了吧？」

en_text: "You can talk, you know. That's the point of removing the gag."
zh_text: 「你可以說話了。」

en_text: It's a stupid question, but I answer it anyway. "Of course I do." "Now, do you understand that it's bad to do this? It's bad to tie people up. Especially policemen." "I'm not a moron."
zh_text: 「當然知道。」「你知不知道自己現在這麼做很糟糕？把人家綁起來很糟糕，尤其當那人是個警察。」「我可不是笨蛋。」

en_text: He tilts his head slightly as he takes this information in, and slowly he starts to do the realizing he needs to do. He comes to the conclusion that I'm not Slow Joe, but Angry Joe. I'm Superintelligent Joe.
zh_text: 他聽進我的話後側了側頭，逐漸了解到我可不是智障喬，而是憤怒喬、天才喬！

en_text: "No, I can't blame you, but you can stop sucking up, Bob." "You haven't crossed the line here yet. If you let me go, I can forget this ever happened. We can both carry on with our normal lives. Once you do something, though, once you hurt me, there's nothing I can do to help you out. You understand that, right? If I'm dead, I'm useless, right? Okay? You're obviously an intelligent guy, I'm sure you understand. And I'm sure you know a useless dead cop means trouble for you, Joe, and neither of us wants any trouble, right?" he says, which is his way of assuming that neither of us wants a dead cop. "We both know that. It's just too much hassle. So how about you untie me, huh? Untie me and we can discuss any concerns you have. We can talk about what you want."
zh_text: 「對，不能怪到你的頭上，但是鮑伯，你能不能不要這麼機車？」趁你還沒失控，要是你放我走，我可以當作什麼都沒發生，我倆可以繼續過著日常的生活。不過，要是你對我不利、動我一根寒毛，那我可就饒不了你。這你懂吧？我要是死了，那也就毫無用處了不是嗎？你顯然聰明絕頂，也相當清楚一具沒用的警官屍體其實相當麻煩。喬，無論你我，我們都不想惹上麻煩，也都不想處理屍體吧？我們都很清楚……所以，放開我如何？先替我鬆綁，我們可以談談你想要什麼、有什麼考量。

en_text: "Don't you want to know what we're going to be talking about?"
zh_text: 「你不想知道我們接下來會談些什麼嗎？」

en_text: "No guesses as to who I am? Other than Joe the Janitor?"
zh_text: 「除了我是工友喬，你不猜猜我的真面目嗎？」

en_text: He's sweating so much I'm starting to worry that he might be able to slip out of the knots and that the duct tape will just run off him in long, silver streaks. "Do you know who I am?"
zh_text: 他汗流浹背，我開始擔心他或許可以藉此掙脫打好的結，不然就是黏好的長銀色膠帶會這麼從他身上鬆落。「你知道我是誰嗎？」

en_text: "Come on, you do know. I'm the Carver."
zh_text: 「拜託，你一定知道，我是『基督城屠夫』呀。

en_text: This, of course, is all bullshit. Bullshit that is taught to these guys when they become cops. He's trying to negotiate with me, but he has nothing to bargain with. He knows that, but what else can he do? He keeps using my name, trying to relate to me, trying to make me see him as a real person.
zh_text: 這些全是狗屁，全是這些傢伙在當上條子之後學到的。他正試著和我談判，但他手上什麼籌碼都沒有，這他非常清楚，但他還能怎樣呢？他不斷地稱呼我的名字，試著和我拉近關係、要我把他當成活生生的人來看待。

en_text: "Let's make a few assumptions. First of all, let's assume I'm telling the truth. Secondly, let's assume I'm not about to let you go. Thirdly, let's assume you don't cooperate with what I want. Do you know what happens then?" He nods. Assumptions are something that cops aren't supposed to make. They're supposed to use facts, not maybes. However, Calhoun has been to some of the crime scenes. He can safely assume what will happen to him without needing any further evidence. All he has to do is swap, inside his mind, his own body for that of one of the women.
zh_text: 「現在先做幾個假設。第一，假設我說的是實話；第二，假設我並不打算放你走；第三，假設你並不怎麼合作。你知道接下來會怎樣嗎？」他點了點頭。條子是不應該預先假設、先入爲主的。他們應該結合事實，而非單憑猜測。然而，卡爾霍恩曾到過幾處命案現場，他可以不靠進一步的探證，就信心滿滿地爲接下來的遭遇作好假設。在他心裡，他很清楚自己所能做的就是一命抵一命，拿自己的身體去交換其中一個被他謀殺的女人。

en_text: "Good. Then let's get a few of the ground rules out of the way. First of all, you're all alone. Help isn't coming, and you have no way to escape. However, don't let this get you down. You've probably figured out that if I wanted you dead, you'd be dead already, right?"
zh_text: 一很好，我們開門見山，直接說明幾項基本的遊戲規則吧。第一，你單槍匹馬、孤立無援、無從逃脫。不過先別失望，因為你很可能已經猜到我若要殺你，你應該早就死了，對吧？

en_text: "Because if you agree to what I want, which is most likely, you'll not only get out of here with your own life, but you'll get paid an income for surviving."
zh_text: 「你要是答應我的要求——目前這看起來可能性較大——你不但可以活著離開這裡，還會因為保住性命而賺到一筆。」

en_text: At this, he slowly starts nodding—at the word income, not life. Suddenly he not only survives, he becomes richer. This is sounding like a pretty good deal to him. He's already paying for more hookers and he doesn't even know yet how much he's earning.
zh_text: 就在我說到「錢」，而非「活著」的當下，他慢慢點起頭來。突然間，他不但可以活命，還會變得更加富有。對他而言，這筆交易聽起來挺吸引人。他砸在嫖妓上的錢越來越多，而且都已經到了這種地步，他居然還不知道自己到底有多少收入。

en_text: "The second thing is that I ask the questions, and you answer them truthfully. Failure to do so will jeopardize both aspects of the first ground rule. Any questions?" He opens his mouth, but nothing comes out. Yes, he understands. Perfectly.
zh_text: 第二就是我問什麼，你都要老實回答，否則就會危害到雙方在第一項遊戲規則下的立場。懂了嗎？他張口欲言，卻無言以對。懂，他完全懂。

en_text: "I suppose you want to know how much money and what you need to do for it?"
zh_text: 「我猜，你想知道自己得怎麼做，以及會拿到多少錢吧？」對，我洗耳恭聽。

en_text: "Please." "Twenty thousand dollars, and it's simple to earn. You don't need to kill anybody for it, because you'll be leaving that to me."
zh_text: 「兩萬紐幣。很好賺吧？而且你誰都不必殺，只要交給我就行。」

en_text: He nods at this. Thinks twenty grand isn't a lot of money to get tied up for, but it's better than getting tied up and shot. Twenty grand is a lot of money to earn for doing nothing. This is the part of the plan he likes. The part of the plan I knew he would like.
zh_text: 他點了點頭，心想才爲了兩萬紐幣就被人綁成這樣眞不划算，不過遭人綑綁總比中彈來得好，而且自己什麼都沒做就可以賺到兩萬紐幣，這也算是相當可觀了。他喜歡這部分的計畫，而我也清楚他會喜歡。

en_text: "I don't want anybody to die," Bob starts, as if he really means it, and as if I'd really care even if he did. People dying isn't a relevant factor for him, or for me. Under other circumstances—better circumstances, he'll be thinking—we could have laughed at his joke. What is relevant is Daniela Walker. I lean back on my elbow. If I smoked, now would be the time to casually light up an expensive cigarette. If I were an evil mastermind, now would be the time I started petting my white Persian cat. But I'm just a cleaner with no goldfish to feed. An average, everyday Joe. If I had my mop, then maybe I would stroke it. If I had my metal bucket, I could beat out a rhythm. All I can do is turn the knife over and over in my hands, watching him watching the blade.
zh_text: 「我並不想鬧出人命。」鮑伯劈頭就這麼說，彷彿他是認真的，彷彿這若是他的真心話我就會非常在意那樣。無論對他或是對我，有沒有鬧出人命和我倆毫無關係，而真正和我倆有關的，其實在於丹妮耶拉·沃克這個人。我撐起手肘向後靠。要是我有抽菸的習慣，現在將會是信手燃起一根高檔菸的好時機；要是我是邪惡組織的首腦，現在也會是輕撫那隻白色波斯貓的好時機。但我只不過是一個沒有金魚可養的清潔工，只不過是大家日常所見的喬。要是我有抹布，我很可能會拿來擦地；要是我有金屬水桶，我很可能會敲敲打打、演奏起打擊樂。但我現在所能做的，就只是把玩著那把刀，看他盯著刀鋒。

en_text: "Come now, Bob, you've killed before. I don't see how you can feel bad about somebody else dying." "I haven't killed anybody." I shake my finger back and forth. "No, no, no. I said no lying. Do you remember what I said would happen if you lied?" He nods. He remembers.
zh_text: 「鮑伯，拜託，你又不是沒殺過人，我看不出來你會因爲出了人命而難過。」「我誰都沒殺。」我來回晃動手指。「錯、錯、錯，我說過要誠實。記不記得我說過不誠實會怎樣？」他點頭，他記得。

en_text: "Good. I know of a couple of ways we can do this," I say, reaching into my briefcase and rummaging around. "I can start by using these," I pull out a pair of sharpened gardening shears, "on your fingers. For every answer I don't want to hear, I'll remove one finger."
zh_text: 「那好。我知道要是你不誠實，我們可以有幾種處理方式。」我說，把手伸進公事包，東摸西找。「這個，」我掏出了一把磨好的園藝剪，「我可以用這剪斷你的手指。凡是聽到不想聽的答案，我就剪掉一根。」

en_text: Actually, I won't. I'm not going to remove any of them, but as long as he believes I'm going to, that's all that really counts. This is where his assumptions are going to lead him astray. I watch his face as he studies the gardening shears. It takes no effort to imagine how they can wrap around any one of his fingers, how the blades can sink through his flesh, and how with a little bit of extra effort I can get them to snap through the bone. His imagination already has all his digits scattered across the floor behind his chair. I'm capable of this. Melissa would be too. And so is he.
zh_text: 實際上我不會這麼做，也沒打算剪去他半根手指，但只有讓他以為我會照做，他才會說起真話，也才會覺得自己太過異想天開。我看著他的臉，他正仔細端詳園藝剪，不費吹灰之力就能想像刀刃是怎麼夾住他的任何一根手指，刀鋒是怎麼劃進他的肉，而我又是怎樣輕輕鬆鬆地「卡」一聲就把骨頭給剪了斷。他已經開始想像自己一根根的手指就這麼慘遭毒手，散落在椅子後方的地面。我辦得到，梅莉莎辦得到，就連他自己也辦得到。

en_text: The three of us have all killed.
zh_text: 我們都殺過人。

en_text: "You did kill her, didn't you?" He nods.
zh_text: 「她是你殺的吧？」他點了點頭。

en_text: He shrugs. "I'm still not sure."
zh_text: 他聳了聳肩。「我也還沒找出原因。」

en_text: "Would you like me to help you understand why?"
zh_text: 「那要不要我告訴你原因？」

en_text: He does the wise thing and nods.
zh_text: 這次他學聰明了，點了點頭。

en_text: He says nothing. I think about the indications in the pathology report that said Daniela had previous injuries. If she'd left her husband, she'd still be alive. And somebody else wouldn't be. Calhoun surely would have found somebody else.
zh_text: 他不發一語。我想起了病理解剖曾明確指出丹妮耶拉·沃克在死前便已傷痕累累。要是她離先生而去，現在還能保住一條小命，然後死的會是別人——卡爾霍恩鐵定會找別人下手。

en_text: I look at him. My speech hasn't made any impact. If it's true, and I believe most of it is, then he isn't going to let me know. This annoys me, but not enough to jump up and cut his throat. I sit and wait. "You're new in the city," I continue, "so the opportunity to act out is irresistible. You know her address and learn the pattern of her movements. Her husband's at work, her children are away at camp, so what could be better? Before you attack her, you decide to frame the husband, because what possible candidate could look any more attractive as her killer? Then you answer the question. One person fits the bill perfectly, and that person is me. So what do you do? You frame me for a murder I didn't commit, and to be honest, Bob, I never really appreciated it. But you're lucky, because you're being given the chance to change the way I feel about you. You can either leave this house a richer man, in terms of both money and character, or you can leave inside a body bag on your way straight down to hell. Of course, needless to say, punishment down there will be eternal, and eternity, Bob, is a very long time."
zh_text: 我看著他，剛剛的話一點影響力都沒有。要是我說的是事實——我相信八九不離十——他也不會讓我知道，我是覺得很煩，但還不至於跳起來劃破他的喉嚨。我靜靜坐著、等著。「你對基督城還不熟，」我繼續說，「所以不禁想逮住機會上演一齣戲。你拿到了她的地址、掌握了她的行蹤，等到她先生去上班、小孩參加校外露營，這不就是你的大好時機嗎？在你攻擊她之前，你決定要栽贓給她先生，因為你想，還會有誰比她先生看起來更像兇手呢？於是你找起答案，發現有個人百分之百可以勝任，那人就是我，所以你幹了什麼好事？我根本沒殺人，你卻栽贓給我，坦白說，鮑伯，我一點都不感謝你，但因為你一直都有機會改變我對你的觀感，所以你真是好狗運。今天，你可以活著離開這間屋子、一夜致富，也可以命喪黃泉、不得好死。

en_text: I start wondering what I'm talking about. Hell? Who gives a damn about Satan? The limp-wristed, red-skinned motherfucker is a figment of the Christian imagination, designed solely as a deterrent for killers, thieves, rapists, liars, hypocrites, and mime artists—yet a lot of bloody good that's done. "Whether you rot in hell or not isn't my concern. What is my concern is what you did to poor Daniela Walker. From what I've learned, and from being here," I spread my arms out to encompass the room, "I've come to some expert and insightful conclusions."
zh_text: 當然，到了地獄你將受盡折磨，這不用我說。我開始納悶自己到底在說些什麼，地獄？撒旦？那個懦弱無能、紅色皮膚的軟腳蝦完全是基督教所想像出來的虛構人物，純粹設計用來嚇阻小偷騙子僞君子殺人犯強暴犯或是默劇演員之類的，只不過最後卻一點鳥用也沒有。「我在乎的不是你會不會在地獄遭到酷刑，而是你對可憐的丹妮耶拉·沃克做了什麼。一路下來，」我張開雙臂，作勢包圍整個房間，「我推論出一些專業又深入的結論。」

en_text: "Good for you."
zh_text: 「算你厲害。」

en_text: I smile. "You broke into her house during the late afternoon, climbed upstairs while she was showering, and waited for her in the bedroom. In this bedroom." It's a familiar scenario.
zh_text: 我莞爾一笑。「你在傍晚闖進她家，趁她入浴時上樓，然後在臥房等她。就這間臥房。」這個場景好熟悉。

en_text: "She had no chance. After all, you had the element of surprise on your side, as well as being bigger and stronger. Her fear, her imagination, made her react, but not quickly enough to escape you. You struggled with her, managed to force her onto the bed, and she managed to reach to the bedside table and clutch at the only weapon she could find." I point to the table for effect. "She fought with you and managed to stab you with the pen she'd been using to fill in her crossword puzzles. The wound wasn't deep, but it was enough to piss you off. You tossed it away, then got back to business. Except the pen was your mistake, Bob, but you know that, don't you? At the time, after you killed her, nothing else mattered. The pain was gone, as was any concern of being caught. The pen was the furthermost thing from your mind. Until you came back. Then it became the biggest thing on your mind, and it was only a matter of good luck that you were able to swap it unnoticed. At least unnoticed by everybody except me."
zh_text: 「她毫無勝算。和她比較起來，你又高又壯，嚇人的本事可是掌握在你的手裡。她的恐懼、想像力都激起本能反應，但不足以快到逃過你的手掌心。你和她發生扭打、打算逼她床上就範，她則打算爬到床頭櫃、抓起任何能夠取得的武器。」爲了增添效果，我手指櫃子。「你們大打出手，她拿起玩塡字遊戲的鋼筆朝你身上一刺，傷口雖然不深，卻足以讓你抓狂，於是你抓起筆向外一扔，才接著辦起正事。但你栽在那支筆上了。鮑伯，你自己也很清楚吧？就在你殺了她的當下，什麼都已經不再重要。你不再感到疼痛，也不再擔心自己會不會被抓，當時你根本就沒想到那支筆。直到回來之後，那支筆才成了你心中的一塊大石，而你只能企盼自己走運、可以趁人不注意時把換掉筆，對，你的確趁別人不注意時成功偷天換日，但你完全忘記還有我。」

en_text: "What is it you want?"
zh_text: 「你到底想怎样？」

en_text: I shake my head. "Bob, Bob, Bob. I thought we had an understanding. You know you're not allowed to ask the questions." "Just tell me what you want."
zh_text: 我搖了搖頭。「我還以爲我們已經達到共識。你應該很清楚自己不准發問。」「你只要告訴我你想怎樣。」

en_text: "That's another question."
zh_text: 「你還問？」

en_text: "No, it isn't. It's a request." "And that's a lie." I hold up the gardening shears. "You're just asking for it, aren't you?"
zh_text: 「我沒問，我只是拜託你。」「那就是你不老實了。」我舉起園藝剪。「這可是你自找的。」

en_text: He shakes his head. "No. I swear."
zh_text: 他搖頭。「沒有，我真的沒那意思。」

en_text: "What about Daniela? Was she asking for it?"
zh_text: 「那丹妮耶拉呢？那也是她自找的嗎？」

en_text: Bob's face is wet and he's looking down into his lap. We're both sweating. It's not warm outside, but somehow this house is still retaining the heat from the summer. The windows have been closed for three months now, so the air is stale and tastes like bad meat. I move over to the window. Open it slightly. Suck at the air outside. The smell, the thick air, the pressure on my skin—it is similar to my apartment the week I spent in bed with a bleeding ball and a bucket full of piss. I'd got used to the feeling, but it is a great relief to be rid of it now.
zh_text: 鮑伯臉上汗如雨下，往下看起大腿。我倆都是揮汗如雨。那天晚上很熱，而臥房的窗戶仍舊緊閉。截至目前爲止，這裡已經三個月沒開窗，所以空氣帶了股腐臭味，聞起來就像壞掉的肉。我挪身窗邊，開了點窗，吸了一口外頭的新鮮空氣。那種氣味、滯悶的空氣、我皮膚所感受到的壓力……剛剛我雖然已經習慣這種感覺，但如今可以解脫眞是讓我鬆了一大口氣。這地方和我花了一個禮拜與血流不止的睪丸、整桶小便待在床上的那間公寓頗爲類似。

en_text: He tilts his head to look at me. He looks sorry, but he's sorry to have been caught, not sorry for killing Daniela Walker.
zh_text: 他側頭盯著我看，一臉遺憾，卻是對自己被人逮到感到遺憾，而不是對殺了丹妮耶拉感到遺憾。

en_text: The air seems to be getting stickier by the minute. I don't reply to his answer. I just sit still, silently reasserting my dominance over this man. The room is cooling. Somewhere, Melissa is dreaming about her money. Somewhere nearby a dog is barking. Some place further away the police are coming closer, if they've not done so already, to discovering a match for the fingerprints on the murder weapon they found in the dumpster.
zh_text: 此刻的空氣感覺起來更爲滯悶。我並沒回應他的答案，只是靜靜坐著，再次宣稱這男人如今可是任我擺佈。房裡泛起了點涼意。此時梅莉莎正在某處幻想著她的錢，然後警方要是沒發覺那把曾被他們遺漏的兇器上沾有符合嫌犯的指紋，那麼他們可能也正朝這兒來。

en_text: Bob is now a condemned man. He's effectively on death row. It's just that nobody has told him. His family, especially his wife, will have to live with the stench of blame. How can she justify not knowing what a monster her husband really is? Or how does she explain that she knew and never did anything about it? I've been wondering whether Bob has an alibi for several of the killings. He was in Auckland for the first few. However, because of the seriousness of this horrific series of murders, the police will work their way around any small inconsistencies, and when nobody else shows up dead, they will be satisfied with labeling Calhoun the Christchurch Carver. I've learned enough from cleaning their hallways to know that they're so hard-pressed for a suspect, they'll keep their mouths shut, never mention all the DNA evidence that never quite matched up, and if a few more bodies show up every now and again they'll use a copycat defense. It'll keep them happy, and the media, and the country. It'll even keep me happy.
zh_text: 鮑伯現在已被定罪，即將執行死刑，只是沒人告訴他。他的家人，尤其是他太太，她將得活在衆人的辱罵之下。她要如何證明自己對於枕邊人是個禽獸一無所知？還是她要怎麼解釋自己明明知情，卻袖手旁觀、不爲所動？我一直在想，在鮑伯犯下的幾次謀殺案中，他是否都具備有效的不在場證明。前幾次案發時他人在奧克蘭，然而，有鑑於這次連續謀殺案駭人聽聞、案情嚴重，警方將在矛盾處動些細微的手腳，一旦沒再出現其他被害人，他們就會樂於替卡爾霍恩貼上標籤，把他當成基督城屠夫。我一直都在替他們打掃走廊，久到足以得知他們結案壓力很大，大都選擇乖乖閉嘴，絕口不提DNA根本不合的事，然後要是一年內又發生了幾起命案，他們就會辯稱兇手是在模仿先前的殺人模式。這麼做會讓他們開心、媒體開心、國人開心，甚至讓我開心。

en_text: "Okay, Bob, explain how killing her was an accident."
zh_text: 「好，請你解釋一下是怎麼失手殺了她吧。」

en_text: He looks up. Stares into my eyes. He shrugs, then he looks down at the floor, then he shrugs again. He seems really unsure. "I followed her home, to talk to her, right?" he says, still looking down. "I wanted her to charge her husband with assault, 'cause the guy's a real asshole, right? Shit, you probably saw him. Stuck-up, arrogant bastard. So full of himself, sure that he's above the law, that it's his right to beat the crap out of his wife. So I follow her home to tell her she's making a mistake, and when I get here, I find that she's home alone."
zh_text: 他抬起頭來，和我四目交接。「爲了跟她聊聊——就只是聊聊——我先跟蹤她回家，要她控告自己先生家暴，因爲那傢伙眞是窩囊廢。那混蛋白大高傲、自以爲是、完全以自我爲中心、認爲自己把太太打到屁滾尿流全都是他身爲丈夫的權利而且絕對和『犯法』沾不上邊，也因此我才會跟蹤她回家、告訴她她錯了，然後一到這裡，我才發現原來她獨自在家。

en_text: "It wasn't your job, Bob. You were here to work on my case alone."
zh_text: 「鮑伯，這不關你的事，你搶走了我的案子。」

en_text: He sighs. "I know. I know that, but, well, it just happened." "Did you know she was going to be home alone?"
zh_text: 「我懂、我懂，不過……呃……事情就是這樣嘛。「你知不知道她接下來會單獨在家？」

en_text: "Not really."
zh_text: 「不太確定。」

en_text: "That sounds like a yes to me, Bob."
zh_text: 「這聽起來像是你知道。」

en_text: "I suspected."
zh_text: 我想過有這可能。

en_text: "Which is why you followed her, right? Because you could only talk to her while she was alone. Having her husband in the same room wasn't going to make for a useful conversation."
zh_text: 「那才是你跟蹤她的原因吧？因爲你只能在她獨自一人時才能和她說得上話。」他試圖聳一聳肩，礙於全身遭我綑綁，只能微微一動。

en_text: "You guess so. Okay, then what happened?"
zh_text: 是吧？好，那接下來呢？

en_text: "Considering whether to kill her or not?" He shakes his head. "Nothing like that."
zh_text: 「心想自己該不該殺掉她吧？」「沒這回事。」

en_text: "What then?" "I don't know. I just sat there, watching the house, thinking about the best way to convince her of what she needed to do. Finally, when I went to the door and knocked, there was no answer. I was going to leave . . ." he says, but doesn't finish the sentence. "But you stayed," I tell him. "I stayed," he says. "For some reason I couldn't tell you, I stayed."
zh_text: 「不然咧？」「我不知道。我只是坐在那裡，望著房子，思考著說服她最佳方法。最後當我走到門邊敲了敲門、屋裡沒人應門而正打算離開時，不知怎麼搞的，我就是留在原地。」

en_text: "Because you saw an opportunity."
zh_text: 「因爲你找到機會了。」

en_text: "No," he says. "It wasn't like that. I was worried. What if she wasn't answering because her husband was home beating her up for not having dinner on the table or for not cleaning his shoes or whatever excuse the piece of shit needed? Anyway, I checked the door and it was locked, but I had some keys on me designed for picking most house locks, so I used them."
zh_text: 「因爲我很擔心。我擔心她之所以沒來應門，全是因爲她老公爲了桌上沒晚餐、鞋子沒擦或是什麼鳥事就把她痛打一頓。總之，我檢査了一下門，發現門是鎖著的，但我握有幾把設計來打開多數門鎖的萬用鑰匙，於是用它開了鎖。

en_text: I know the keys well. I also know that domestic abuse isn't about a man who is in love with his wife too much; it's about a man who is in love with the ability to control her.
zh_text: 我很清楚那種鑰匙，也很清楚家暴的來由不是男人過度迷戀自己的太太，而是過度迷戀那種控制的能力。

en_text: "I checked around the kitchen, the living room, looking for her."
zh_text: 「於是我在廚房和客廳東看西看，找起她人在哪。

en_text: "Did you call her name?" "No."
zh_text: 「你有叫她嗎？」「沒有。

en_text: He shakes his head. "That wasn't it at all. I didn't want to let the husband know I was there, in case he was home and hitting her. I wanted to catch him in the act." "That's pretty lame, Bob."
zh_text: 他搖了搖頭。「不盡然，她先生要是正在毒打她，我可不想讓他知道我就在那。」「這理由不充分。」

en_text: "She was upstairs sitting on the bed. Sobbing." "Which is why she didn't answer the door, I suppose?"
zh_text: 「她人在樓上，坐在床邊，正在啜泣。」「我猜那就是她為何沒去應門。」

en_text: If he sees the irony, he doesn't let it show.
zh_text: 他若聽得出我是在調侃他，也不會表現出來。

en_text: "Pretty soon she couldn't see my way of thinking, my way of understanding."
zh_text: 她很快就無法理解我的思考和理解方式。

en_text: "The correct way, you mean?" "Yeah. Do you know what it's like, Joe, to know you're absolutely right about something—I mean, beyond any doubt—but you can't get somebody else to agree with you? It's not that they don't understand, or that they don't want to. They've become so used to doing the wrong thing that there couldn't possibly be another way."
zh_text: 「也就是你心目中的『正確方式』吧？」是的，我的意思是，當你在某方面的見解鐵定沒錯，但卻無法說服別人認同你的那種感覺。別人不是不懂，或是不想懂，而是他們對於錯事已經習以爲常，覺得事情不可能還有其他出路。

en_text: "Yeah. Do you know what it's like, Joe, to know you're absolutely right about something—I mean, beyond any doubt—but you can't get somebody else to agree with you? It's not that they don't understand, or that they don't want to. They've become so used to doing the wrong thing that there couldn't possibly be another way." "Get back to the point, Bob."
zh_text: 是的，我的意思是，當你在某方面的見解鐵定沒錯，但卻無法說服別人認同你的那種感覺。別人不是不懂，或是不想懂，而是他們對於錯事已經習以爲常，覺得事情不可能還有其他出路。「鮑伯，請你回到重點。」

en_text: "We ended up disagreeing, pretty quickly actually, and then we were arguing. In the end she started screaming at me to leave. I asked her to calm down, but she wouldn't. Then she tried to call the police, so I had to stop her. She slapped me, so then I hit her back. Next thing I knew she was dead and I was standing over her naked body." He stops talking. We both listen to the silent room. Peaceful, but still warmer than I'd like. I believe most of his story, but he's left something out. "Next thing you knew," I repeat. "I didn't mean for it to happen."
zh_text: 「結果我們各持己見，很快就發生爭執，最後她開始尖叫、要我離開。我要她冷靜下來，但她不肯，還企圖報警，所以我得阻止她。結果我被她摑了一巴掌才還手，然後等到我意識到怎麼回事的時候，她已經死了，而我就站在她赤裸裸的屍體旁。」他不再說話。我倆都聆聽著這間萬籟俱寂的臥房，很平靜，也很炎熱。大部分他所說的我都相信，但有件事他漏掉沒說。

en_text: "A touching story, Bob," I say, reaching to my eyes with an imitation hanky, wiping away pretend tears. "It seems you've gone for a classic defense strategy. Do they teach you that at training college, or did you pick it up being a cop? See, Bob, what you've done here is extremely common. You've shifted all the blame onto the victim. She's the one who disagreed, she's the one being unreasonable, and she's the one who hit you. If she'd refrained from doing any of those things, then she'd still be alive today. Am I right?" No answer.
zh_text: 「鮑伯，這故事眞感人。」我說，作勢拿起手帕，擦去假裝流下的淚水。「你聽起來似乎上過經典的防衛策略課程喔。你是在培訓院學的，還是當上警察之後才會的？你現在的所作所爲太老套了，你把所有的錯全推給了被害人：是她和你意見不合、是她自己不合情理、是她先動手打你，要是她忍住不做以上那些事情，那她到了今天就還能保有自己的小命。我說的沒錯吧？他默不作聲。

en_text: "Am I right, Bob?" Again the shrug. "I don't know."
zh_text: 「我說的沒錯吧？」他又牽強地聳了聳肩。「我不知道。」

en_text: Again the shrug. "I don't know." "Come on, Bob, you do know. It's the whole domestic abuse scenario over again. She deserved to be punished, didn't she, because she stepped out of line. If she'd done what she was told, if she'd simply obeyed, then she'd be living the contented and happy life. But she didn't, so you killed her—not that you remember doing so. That's the second common phase here, Bob. How many killers have you put away who've told you they don't remember anything? How many have told you that if it weren't for the crazy way this or that particular female acted, then none of this or that would have happened? Now tell me what really happened."
zh_text: 他又牽強地聳了聳肩。「我不知道。」「你明明就很清楚，整個家暴的場景再度上演。你覺得是她活該。要是她乖乖聽話，她就會活得心滿意足、幸福快樂。但她就是不聽，所以你就索性把她殺了——但你已經忘了。鮑伯，這太老套了。在你辦過的案子裡，有幾個殺人犯告訴過你他們記得過程？有幾個殺人犯告訴過你要不是這女人發瘋似的這樣或那樣，事情就不會這樣或那樣了？現在你給我說清楚到底怎麼回事。」

en_text: "That is what happened." "Yeah, most of it probably did, but I'd bet my life on it . . ." I pause, create dramatic effect, then change my mind. "No, I'd bet your life on it that you do remember killing her, and were aware of every second of it."
zh_text: 事情就是這樣。「是啊，或許八成就是這樣，但我敢打賭……」我稍作停頓，營造出戲劇性的效果，接著改變主意。「不對，我敢打賭你明明就記得殺了她，還對每分每秒的經過一清二楚。」

en_text: "Yeah, most of it probably did, but I'd bet my life on it . . ." I pause, create dramatic effect, then change my mind. "No, I'd bet your life on it that you do remember killing her, and were aware of every second of it." "I can't remember."
zh_text: 「是啊，或許八成就是這樣，但我敢打賭……」我稍作停頓，營造出戲劇性的效果，接著改變主意。「不對，我敢打賭你明明就記得殺了她，還對每分每秒的經過一清二楚。」「我沒辦法記住。」

en_text: He sounds like a whining child. "There's no such word as can't, Bob." I lift the gardening shears to prove my point. He says nothing until I start to rise. "Okay, okay." He'd have his hands out in a defensive gesture if he could, waving them in the air like a maniac. "I do remember."
zh_text: 他聽起來就像個哀嚎的孩子。「鮑伯。」我舉起園藝剪，證明我的論點他悶不作聲，直到我站起身子。「好好好，」他要是可以，就會像個瘋子伸出手在空中揮舞，做出一副「我怕了你」的手勢。「我記得。」

en_text: "Okay, okay." He'd have his hands out in a defensive gesture if he could, waving them in the air like a maniac. "I do remember." "Oh? And what do you remember?" I don't need to know this for my plan to work. I'm just interested, as a fellow participant in this game of life and death.
zh_text: 「好好好，」他要是可以，就會像個瘋子伸出手在空中揮舞，做出一副「我怕了你」的手勢。「我記得。」「喔？那你記得什麼？」我其實不必知道這些就能執行這項計畫，但如今既然身爲這場生死遊戲的參賽者，我就是很感興趣。

en_text: "Oh? And what do you remember?" I don't need to know this for my plan to work. I'm just interested, as a fellow participant in this game of life and death. "We argued, like I told you, and she picked up the phone and threatened to call the police. So I hit her, and once I did that, I knew there'd be no way to shut her up."
zh_text: 「喔？那你記得什麼？」我其實不必知道這些就能執行這項計畫，但如今既然身爲這場生死遊戲的參賽者，我就是很感興趣。「如我剛剛所說，我們發生爭吵，然後她拿起電話、威脅我要報警，結果我出手打她，而我一旦出手，也就明白自己再也無法讓她安靜下來了。」

en_text: "Come now, Bob. She's a domestic-abuse victim. She's used to keeping her trap shut when a man hits her." "Not this time. She told me I was going to lose my job for what I'd done, and she was right too, so I hit her again, this time harder. Then I shoved her onto the bed and . . ." He stops, either to think of what to say next, or to invent it. "Well, I needed to make it look like she was one of your victims, Joe."
zh_text: 「拜託，她是家暴的受害者，一旦被人打了，必然習慣乖乖閉嘴。」「這次不是這樣。她說我將失去工作，這聽起來挺有道理，於是我又出手打她，這次打得更重，然後再把她推到床上……」他就此打住，不是在想接著怎麼說就是故事怎麼編。「呃……喬，我得讓這看起來像是你下的手。」

en_text: "I had to make it look real," he says, and he says it in a defeated tone, not the kind of tone somebody who stands by their work would use.
zh_text: 「我得讓這看起來像是眞的。」

en_text: "Pure power. Isn't that the answer, Bob? Isn't that what we all look for?" "What do you want from me?"
zh_text: 「單純的權力？這不就是答案嗎？這不就是衆人苦苦追尋的？」「你想從我這得到什麼？」

en_text: "That's a question, Bob."
zh_text: 「鮑伯，問題就在這裡。」

en_text: "I don't give a shit, Joe. Just tell me what you want, or fuck off. You're wasting my time, you little asshole." I'm not shocked at his sudden outburst. Over the last hour, I've touched several nerves. Before all of this is over, a knife is going to touch several more. "The requirement is simple. All you need to do is listen."
zh_text: 「喬，我什麼都不想管，你只要告訴我你想要怎樣，否則拉倒。你一直在浪費我的時間！」對於他突如其來的情緒爆發，我並不震驚。先前的一小時裡，我一直都在試探他的底限，搞得他戰戰兢兢、如履薄冰。「我的要求很簡單。你只要乖乖聽話就好。

en_text: "That simple, huh?" "That's right."
zh_text: 「喔？就這麼簡單？」「就這麼簡單。」

en_text: "Bullshit," he says. "What do I have to listen to?"
zh_text: 放你媽的屁！我會有什麼話要聽！

en_text: "A confession."
zh_text: 「告解。」

en_text: "Yours?" "Funnily enough, no. But it's your job to be my security, my insurance if you like. You knew from the moment you saw my face I was either going to kill you or make a deal. Well, here's the deal, Bob. I will give you twenty thousand dollars, in cash, tomorrow night, to listen to a confession. That's all you have to do. Just sit and listen and remember. Do you think you can handle that?"
zh_text: 「你要告解？」「這就妙了，不是我要告解。你如果願意，你的工作就是當我保鏢、保護我的安全。從你看到我臉的那一刹那，你就很清楚我不打算殺了你，想是跟你交易。所以鮑伯，現在交易來了。明晚我會給你現金兩萬紐幣，要你聆聽告解。你只要乖乖照做，只要坐著、聽著然後牢牢記住就行了。你覺得自己辦得到嗎？

en_text: "Then what? You let me go, is that it?" "That's it."
zh_text: 「然後？然後你就會放我走了嗎？」「對。」

en_text: "And what's in it for you?" "My freedom. Yours too."
zh_text: 「這麼做究竟對你有什麼意義？」「這攸關我的自由，還有你的自由。」

en_text: "And if I refuse?" "I'll kill you. Right now."
zh_text: 「那我如果拒絕呢？」「那我現在就會幹掉你。」

en_text: "You're not really in a situation to ask for anything, Bob." I stand and walk over to him.
zh_text: 「你現在的處境沒資格要求。」我站起身子，向他走去

en_text: "Joe? What the hell are you up to?"
zh_text: 「喬，你到底要做什麼？」

en_text: "Shut up, Bob." I continue pulling on the chair, and it makes scuff marks across the carpet, but finally I manage to get Calhoun into the bathroom. "I'm afraid you'll have to spend the night here." "Why?"
zh_text: 「閉嘴。」我一直拉著椅子，隨著它在經過的地毯留下磨痕，我還是努力地把卡爾霍恩拉到浴室。「恐怕你得在這裡過夜。」「爲什麼？」

en_text: "Safer that way."
zh_text: 「這樣比較安全。」

en_text: "For who?" "For me."
zh_text: 「對誰？」「對我啊。」

en_text: I pull out some duct tape. "Anything else before I seal you up for the night?" "You're a real psycho, Joe, do you know that?"
zh_text: 我拉開膠帶。「在我貼上你的嘴巴之前，你還有什麼要說的嗎？」「喬，你是個心理變態！你自己知不知道？」

en_text: I run the tape across his mouth. Then I head back into the bedroom and take the parking ticket from my briefcase. I squat down behind Bob, grab the skin on the back of his hand, and start twisting until he unclenches it, then I push his fingertips against the ticket.
zh_text: 我用膠帶貼住他的嘴，回頭走進臥房，從公事包拿出了那張停車卡，接著蹲在鮑伯後面，抓住他的手背肌開始扭轉，直到拳頭鬆開，再把他的指紋按在票卡上。

en_text: With nothing else to do, I head toward home and toward the end of another long night. Another phase completed.
zh_text: 閒來無事，於是我往自家住處、另一個漫漫長夜的盡頭而去。另一個階段又完成了。

en_text: She doesn't know this is where she is driving to until she pulls up the long, twisting driveway lined with beautiful trees, which is ironic because she wanted to come here earlier and found herself driving in a different direction. She can't park in her usual spot because the church has become a crime scene, so she parks out on the street and uses a smaller entrance to walk through.
zh_text: 直到她把車停在細長、蜿蜒又種滿了美麗行道樹的車道後，她才知道自己正開往何處。她把車停在陰暗處，下了車，一腳踩上了綠油油的草坪。距離天黑還有一小時，她打算就耗在這裡。

en_text: Sally makes her way to her brother's grave and crouches down next to it, not over it. She's always careful about that. She has a whirlwind of scenarios racing through her head, but she can't comprehend any of them, and the ones she can almost grasp keep floating away from her. Joe and the second man had been inside for at least an hour. She had been relieved when Joe came out okay, and tempted to follow him, but she was more curious about who the second man was. She'd waited another half hour, but he hadn't shown up. Most likely he lived there. She starts brushing her hands back and forth through the grass, letting the soft textures tickle her palms. The grass is wet. She had written down the address before leaving. What she would do with that information she wasn't sure. Probably just leave it scrawled across the notepad in her front seat for the next few weeks before balling it up and tossing it out. Joe driving different cars. Joe with files at his house. Joe with a missing testicle. Joe secretly meeting people.
zh_text: 莎莉一路走到弟弟墳前，趴在墓碑旁，而非墓碑上。她向來對此小心翼翼。此時她腦海中快速地湧現一個個的畫面，但就是沒一個她搞得清楚，而那些差點搞得清楚的卻「咻」一聲就不見蹤影。喬和之後來的那個男人在屋裡至少待了一個小時。當喬安然無恙地走出屋外，她鬆了口氣，打算跟蹤他，但這時她比較好奇的反而是之後的男人究竟是誰。於是她又等了半小時，只不過那人並沒出現，他很有可能就住在那。她來回摸起地面的草坪，讓草兒柔細的質地搔觸著掌心。她在離開前記下了地址。她到底留著這些連自己都不確定是什麼的資訊幹嘛呢？也許就只是把它寫在前座的筆記本上，擺在那幾個禮拜，之後再揉成紙團扔掉。喬這次開的車不一樣。喬的家裡放著資料夾。喬有一邊的睪丸沒了。喬偷偷摸摸和別人碰面。

en_text: Well, okay, Joe went to somebody's house, the same way she's gone to other people's houses. Gone there and had coffee, played some cards, killed some time, ate some dinner. What is so suspicious about that? Nothing. Except Joe parked two blocks away and left in a different car. Plus the house—somehow she knows that house. "So what do I do, Martin?"
zh_text: 好，這麼說吧，就像自己去別人家裡喝杯咖啡、打打牌、消磨時間、用個晚餐那樣，喬也同樣會去別人家裡，所以這有什麼可疑的呢？除了喬把車停在兩個路口外、開了另一輛車子離開還有那間房子以外——不知怎麼她就是認得那間房子——其實沒啥大不了的吧。「馬丁，我該怎麼做？」

en_text: If her brother could reach out from his grave and offer her some advice, it wouldn't be Do nothing. It was her doing nothing that had got Martin killed five years ago. It has been her lack of responsibility, her laziness, her unawareness. She was doing nothing five years ago when she should have been doing something. She should have been doing anything to stop Martin from being hit at forty miles an hour in a thirty-mile zone. It wasn't the school's fault. It wasn't even really the driver's fault. It was her fault. She knows some people would blame God, and she suspects her parents split the blame between her and Him.
zh_text: 要是她弟弟可以爬出墳墓給她一點建議，那麼他的建議會是「什麼都別做。」五年前，她就是懶惰、沒責任感、毫不留神、什麼都沒做才會害死馬丁。五年前，當她原本應該有所行動的時候，她什麼都沒做。她原本應該有所行動，好讓馬丁不致在速限五十五公里的地區被時速六十五公里的車撞上。這不是學校的錯，也不是司機的錯，而是她的錯。她知道有人會說是造化弄人，但她懷疑自己爸媽除了覺得造化弄人，也覺得她難辭其咎。

en_text: That's why her mother flinches when she puts an arm around her. That's why her parents didn't try to convince her to stay at nursing school, and allowed her to give up her career to help them pay the bills. It was difficult not to hate God. It was His fault for making Martin intellectually handicapped. It was easy to lay blame with her, though. It was her fault that Martin had run out into traffic. Her fault for forgetting how excitable he could be when she finished her studies early and got the chance to pick him up from school. She'd rung home to say she could pick Martin up. Her mother had told her not to worry, but Sally had gone ahead and worried. She loved the look on Martin's face when he stepped out of school and saw her waiting there for him. The rules were always simple. Her parents had told Martin a thousand times. He was never to cross the road. And she knew the rules too. She was never to park across the road and wait for him there; she either parked on his side of the road, or she walked over. Her parents reminded her time and time again, but the problem when people remind you so often is that you start to ignore it. The words go in, but they don't settle anywhere. The other problem was she was late. Only by two minutes. How many times has she remembered the route she took to his school that day? A red light there that could have been green. A person towing a trailer ahead of her at twenty-five instead of thirty miles an hour. A pedestrian crossing with people taking their time to cross it. It all added up, and in the end it came to two minutes. It all added up the same way all the ages in the graveyard add up and divide to get an average of sixty-two. Just simple mathematics combining to end a life.
zh_text: 那也是她在抱住媽媽時身體猛地一縮的原因，也是爸媽沒試著說服她待在護校，而讓她放棄自己的事業、替他們還債的原因。不怨天尤人很難。要不是造化弄人，馬丁也不會生來就是智障，但把錯推到她的頭上總是比較容易。大家覺得馬丁衝到路上都是她的錯；忘了她去學校接他然後他會有多麼興奮也是她的錯。她打過電話回家，說她能去接他下課。媽媽雖然要她不用操心，但莎莉已經操起心來。她愛極了馬丁在走出學校、看到她就在那等他的表情。規則一向非常簡單。爸媽已經告訴馬丁不下數次，不准他過馬路，而她也明白這項規則，所以她從來不會把車停在馬路對面、在那等他；她只會把車停在他那一邊，或者走路過去接他。爸媽不斷耳提面命、再三叮嚀，但問題就在於人家要是太常提醒你，你就會開始左耳進、右耳出，充耳不聞。另一個問題則在於那天她遲到了，只遲到兩分鐘。當天她開到學校前方的路——她不知回想起多少遍了——那裡的紅燈應該是綠燈才對。她前方有人以時速四十公里，而非五十公里的速度開著吊車。行人和其他人慢慢過著馬路。這一切的一切兜在一起，便讓事情有所耽擱，結果慢了兩分鐘；這一切的一切兜在一起，便有如把墓園裡的所有年齡加總，加以平均，就能得出了「六十二」的平均數字。數學何其容易，結合起來便足以結束一條寶貴的生命。

en_text: She'd pulled up outside the school two minutes later than she should have. She'd opened her car door two minutes after she should have opened it. And Martin had seen her from across the road. It all came down to mathematics, basic physics, and human dynamics. Martin getting excited. Martin running over the road to meet her while she was getting out of her car. Martin getting in the way of an object moving much faster than he was, weighing much more than he did. She'd run to him and knelt by his side. He was alive, but that had changed two days later. She'd let her brother down when he'd needed her most.
zh_text: 她把車停在校外，只不過慢了兩分鐘打開車門，馬丁就已經看到她在馬路對面。所有一切都可拆解成數學、基礎物理學還有人體動力學。馬丁非常興奮，在她準備下車時，他等不及要穿越馬路找她，結果被某個速度比他快、重量比他重的物體迎頭撞上。她跑向他，跪在他身旁，當下他還活著，但兩天後事態急轉直下——他走了。就在弟弟最需要自己的時候，她讓他失望了。

en_text: She won't let Joe down. He needs her. He needs somebody to look out for him, to protect him from whatever madness he's got himself involved in.
zh_text: 這次她不會讓喬失望。他需要她、需要某人替他留意，並保護他免於陷入那無法自拔的狂亂。

en_text: For fuck's sake! On the floor directly outside my apartment door is Pickle. Or Jehovah. It's too damn difficult to tell. I spin around, looking for the fluffy bastard that did this, but it's gone. I crouch down, and touch my dead fish with my finger. It feels rubbery.
zh_text: 就在我公寓門外的地上，我看到了泡菜——還是耶和華？眞的分辨不出。我繞了一圈，想找出是哪隻臭貓幹的好事，但就是遍尋不著。我蹲下身子，用手指碰觸我死去的魚，沒想到摸起來挺有彈性的。

en_text: "Come on, pussycat. Come on."
zh_text: 「來呀，小貓，過來呀。」

en_text: It starts toward me, covers half the distance, stops, turns back toward the fish, stops, then turns back toward me. It meows. I tighten my grip on the knife. Then it moves slowly back to the fish, picks it up softly between its teeth, and carries it toward me. It stops a few feet away, lowers the fish to the floor, then takes a few steps back. Once again it meows. I get on my hands and knees so I can slowly crawl forward. I keep the blade of the knife ahead of me. And then I understand what it's doing. It's offering my fish back to me. It meows again, but this time it is more of a whispering whine.
zh_text: 牠向我走來，走到一半之後停下腳步，回頭往金魚走去，然後停下腳步，再轉身向我走來，發出了喵喵叫。我把刀握得更緊，小貓又慢慢朝金魚移動，輕輕啣起金魚朝我走來。牠就停在約莫一公尺外，把魚放在地上，然後向後退了幾步，又喵了幾聲。爲了慢慢往前爬，這次我趴在地上，直讓刀鋒朝外。後來我弄清楚牠在幹嘛了——牠正試著把魚還我。牠又開始喵喵叫，不過這次比較像是叨叨細語。

en_text: "There's a good boy," I say in my friendly voice, happy to lull it into believing I no longer have any urge to see it skinned. "Come on, fella. I'm not going to kill you, boy. I'm not going to break your neck."
zh_text: 「這樣才乖。」我用友善的聲音說著，樂於引誘牠相信我沒有看著牠遭人宰殺的衝動。「過來呀，小夥子，我不會殺你，更不會扭斷你的脖子。」

en_text: Then the bastard starts purring.
zh_text: 然後這隻混蛋小貓開始發出「咕嚕咕嚕」的滿足聲

en_text: And me? What do I do? I start petting the damn thing. I'm tickling it beneath its chin as if it's just the greatest little cat in the world.
zh_text: 那我呢？我該怎麼做？我開始摸起這隻小王八，把牠當成世上最棒的小貓那樣搔起牠的下巴。

en_text: I look to the floor where my two dead goldfish are. I'm going to have to bury them again. I tighten the grip on my knife, then use the tip of it to start scratching the top of the cat's head. It tilts its face sideways to get a better scratching position for itself.
zh_text: 我看著那兩條金魚所葬身的地面——這下又得替牠們收屍了。我把刀握得更緊，用刀尖輕輕摩擦起小貓的頭頂。牠一左一右側著頭，好替自己找起哪個姿勢磨起來比較舒服。做的就是用力一刺，然後這隻被我救過一命的小貓就……

en_text: All I have to do is thrust down, and this little cat that I saved will . . . Saved. Now that's the key word. I saved this thing, I spent money on it, I brought it into my home, it repaid me by killing my goldfish, and after all of this I'm saving it again. Saving it by not killing it. I put the knife away. Under the observing eyes of the cat, I put the two goldfish into an evidence bag. I will bury them later. Back inside I sit down on the sofa. The cat jumps onto my knee and I keep petting it. After a few minutes it falls asleep. Before I go to bed, I stare at the coffee table and wonder if I will buy any more fish. Maybe when all of this is over. Without them, I feel like a piece of my life is missing. I feel empty. Though not as empty as I felt yesterday. When I wake the next morning, I'm sweating and the cat's on the end of my bed. I've had another dream. I can remember Melissa. We were together somewhere, I think a beach or an island, and I realized I'd formed a misconception about our violent relationship. Rather than killing her, I was lying with her, both of us enjoying the sand, the sound of the sea, and the sun. It was as though we were having a good time.
zh_text: 救過一命。這成了關鍵。我救過他，在牠身上砸錢，帶他回到我家，結果牠以搞死金魚來回報，然後即便如此，我也還是手下留情、饒他不死。刀子被我放到一邊去。那隻貓看著我把兩條金魚放進證物袋。我打算晚點再埋金魚。我回到屋裡，坐上沙發。小貓跳上了我的膝蓋，接受我不斷輕撫，沒幾分鐘後就沉沉入睡。就寢前，我盯著咖啡桌，心想要不要再去買魚。也許等一切告一段落再說吧。少了魚，我總覺得自己的人生有如遺失了一角，感到非常空虛，但比不上昨天。我隔天醒來，小貓就睡在床尾，而我則是冷汗直流。我又做了個夢，夢裡的梅莉莎和我待在某處——海邊還是小島吧——然後我領悟到自己誤會了這段暴力的兩性關係，於是沒動手殺她，反而躺在她的身旁，和她雙雙享受起沙灘、豔陽與海浪聲，彷彿共度起美好的時光。

en_text: A nightmare. The smell of the sea comes with me from the dream and lingers in the room for a few minutes. I get away from it by climbing into the shower. I wash away the night, the tackiness, and the dregs of the dream. When I come out, the cat's sitting on the kitchen floor cleaning itself. I find something in the fridge that looks like meat and the cat seems happy enough to believe it.
zh_text: 海的氣味隨我由夢境進入現實，在房裡流連片刻。爲了將這拋諸腦後，我踏進浴室沖澡，沖去了前一晚身體的濕黏以及夢的殘渣。我一出浴室，小貓就坐在廚房地上替自己洗澡。我在冰箱找到像是肉的玩意兒，小貓似乎也樂於相信。

en_text: Before leaving for work, and after making myself some toast, I check through the briefcase and study my assortment of tools. More importantly I check to make sure the Glock I took from Calhoun is fully loaded. It is. All fifteen rounds ready to react to the tip of my finger pulling in the mechanical trigger. The first cartridge ready to be introduced to the chamber, ready to be struck by the firing pin, the powder inside ready to be ignited. The gas, the pressure, the explosion. The power.
zh_text: 上班前，我先替自己烤了吐司，才把公事包從頭到尾檢查一遍，研究起各式各樣的工具。更重要的是，我之所以檢查，全是爲了確定我從卡爾霍恩取得的葛拉克手槍已經裝滿子彈。沒錯。裡頭的十五發子彈隨時等我用指尖扣起扳機。彈匣裡的第一枚彈藥只要上膛，經撞針一敲，就能引燃火藥。氣體、壓力，接著爆炸。

en_text: It takes less than a quarter of a second for the trigger finger to obey the command of the shooter. Milliseconds later, the firing pin is hitting. For the whole cycle to progress from nerve impulse to firing of the cartridge, I'm looking at a third of a second. The bullet travels at nearly a thousand feet per second. The target can be dead in less than a second. I place the gun back in the briefcase. Let the cat out of my apartment. Go to work.
zh_text: 火藥。要食指恪守射擊手所接收的指令只不過是零點二五秒，而阻鐵釋放彈簧、透過彈力驅動撞針的時間則是更短，需要零點零零五秒。在這近零點三秒內，我聚精會神，好目睹人體從神經受到刺激、帶動制動器扣下扳機、直到發射彈藥的整體流程。子彈速度每秒高達三百公尺。目標可能不到一分鐘就遭擊斃。我把槍放回公事包，讓小貓走出公寓，接著上班去。

en_text: The place is a madhouse.
zh_text: 這地方是瘋人院吧。

en_text: I step into a flurry of detectives and officers. The buzz is much bigger than any of the previous days. The men have their sleeves rolled up, their ties loosened. Conversations are spilling from every corner, every cubicle, every office. Excitement hangs in the air like a half-deflated balloon. I don't hear any full conversations as I make my way through the clusters of people to my office, but I pick up on several snippets. "How long have you known him?"
zh_text: 我走進了警官和警探的一陣慌亂中，人們嘰嘰喳喳要比前些日子還要大聲。男人捲起衣袖，鬆開領帶。每個角落、每個隔間、每個辦公室都能聽見人們從那發出聲音、正在談話。興奮之情有如洩了氣的氣球掛在半空中。雖然我一路走往辦公室、穿過群聚人潮時所聽到的對話都不完整，但還是零碎偷聽到一些。「你認識他多久了？」

en_text: "I heard his son killed himself." "Has anybody checked his hotel?"
zh_text: 「聽說他兒子自殺了。「有人去過他的旅館喔？」

en_text: "Where else can he be staying?"
zh_text: 「不然他還能住哪？」

en_text: "And you knew him."
zh_text: 「你不是認識他？」

en_text: "And you were working with him."
zh_text: 「你不就和他同部門？」
